entry.summary: FlowErase-OPD erases multiple unsafe concepts from flow-matching text-to-image models by distilling several single-concept erased models into one LoRA using on-policy distillation, with a retention teacher to preserve unrelated generation quality. It targets the underexplored multi-concept erasure setting.

entry.title: Vision Meets WiFi: Physics-Grounded Estimation of Volumetric Mechanical Properties

author.name: Ali Bahri, Hongliang Li, Soufiane Lamghari, Jie Chuai, Zhitang Chen

entry.summary: ViWi estimates per-voxel Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, and density by combining vision with WiFi sensing, using object-centric material slots so voxels of the same material share consistent estimates. The WiFi signal helps disambiguate objects that look alike but differ physically.

entry.title: Circuit Fine-Tuning for Compute-Efficient Transformer Adaptation

author.name: Uri Z. Kialy, Gil Ben-Artzi

entry.summary: Circuit Fine-Tuning repurposes mechanistic circuit discovery, normally used to explain trained models, to choose which modules to fine-tune before training begins, using attribution against a near-zero-initialized probe head. The goal is compute efficiency rather than parameter count, since parameter-sparse adapters still pay full-model training cost per step.

entry.title: 4D-WAM: Infusing Spatiotemporal Awareness into World Action Models through Trajectory Fields

author.name: Lishan Yang, Wenxuan Song, Xi Wang, Pingyue Sheng, Zheng Fang, Ziyang Zhou, Junjie He, Haodong Yan, Jiayi Chen, Nan Sun, Qiao Sun, Lingqiao Liu, Yan Wang, Yuxiang Gao, Feras Dayoub, Haoang Li

entry.summary: 4D-WAM is a model-agnostic training strategy that injects 3D trajectory field information into world action models via representation alignment, using motion alignment across adjacent frames plus a complementary spatiotemporal objective. It closes the gap between 2D pixel-space video prediction and the 3D space in which robot actions actually occur.

entry.title: JEPA-WAM: Learning Vision-Language-Action Policies with Joint-Embedding World Modeling

author.name: Yihan Lin, Jiawei He, Shifeng Bao, Chen Zhao, Yang Li, Xiaobo Wang, Yan Wang, Cheng Chi, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: JEPA-WAM builds a world action model inside a pretrained V-JEPA latent space, coupling latent transition prediction with continuous action generation through a shared predictor and predicting a spatially structured joint current-future target that preserves patch-level correspondence. It avoids the deployment cost of pixel-space video generation while keeping predictive representations aligned with those used for control.

entry.title: MetaSpace: Metamorphic Testing for Spatial Cognition in Embodied Agents

author.name: Gengyang Xu, Dongwei Xiao, Yiteng Peng, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Applies metamorphic testing to embodied agents, generating semantics-preserving transformations of scenes and queries to probe spatial cognition without relying on hand-annotated VQA pairs or coarse task-success metrics. The aim is to expose latent spatial reasoning failures that success rates hide.

entry.title: SurgLAT: Surgical Latent Attention Tracking for Depth-Aware Robotic Laparoscope Control

author.name: Rulin Zhou, Qiujie Song, Yujie Ma, An Wang, Wanhao Liu, Guoheng Ma, Yidu Wang, Guankun Wang, Xingrong Diao, Jiankun Wang, Chaowei Zhu, Xianming Liu, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Proposes an online framework for autonomous laparoscope control that models the surgeon's operative intent as a latent, temporally evolving attention state rather than a fixed physical target. It combines a frozen DINOv3 encoder, a state-conditioned spatial token mixer, and a selective causal latent memory that fuses short-term motion with long-horizon intent.

entry.title: TongGuOCR: A Layout-Aware and Token-Augmented OCR Framework for Chinese Historical Documents

author.name: Zhongheng Zhou, Yi Sun, Huiguo He, Yuyi Zhang, Peirong Zhang, Yulin Fang, Dezhi Peng, Minghui Liao, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: Presents an OCR framework for Chinese historical documents combining layout-aware preprocessing that builds locally coherent recognition blocks with token-augmented recognition to handle rare characters and nontrivial reading orders. The goal is to unlock scanned heritage collections for full-text search and computational analysis.

entry.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning

author.name: Keyang Zhong, Kuo Wang, Peng Liu, Quanlong Zheng, Junlin Xie, Zhijia Liang, Yanhao Zhang, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: Introduces a recovery-aware agentic framework for reasoning over hours-long egocentric video that evaluates intermediate tool observations and adaptively trades off zooming into a region versus switching regions. This addresses error propagation caused by rigid zoom-in strategies in chain-of-tool-thought video agents.

entry.title: Your Prompt Is Not the Only Prompt: How Much Do LLMs Weight Structured-Output Schema Descriptions?

author.name: Sin-Ying Lin

entry.summary: This study asks whether label definitions for classification should live in the system prompt, user prompt, or JSON schema descriptions when using structured output. Across ten configurations from two vendors, schema placement was not consistently better and sometimes lagged system prompts by over ten points, yet incorrect schema instructions still hijacked behavior when they conflicted with prompts. Practical guidance for anyone using schema-constrained extraction pipelines.

entry.title: LLM within MCP Matters: Measuring Inefficient Resource Utilization Driven by LLMs

author.name: Minhan Cho, Soyoung Park, Kihyeon Jeong, Byeongkyu Jeon, Daejin Choi, Jinyoung Han

entry.summary: A 54,000-trial measurement across 24 models from three vendors on a production legal-information MCP server tests whether clients actually use reference data embedded in server instructions instead of redundantly calling search tools. A diagnostic condition removing the competing tool shows failures stem from model choices rather than missing information, wasting tokens and latency. Practical guidance for MCP server design and client behavior.

entry.title: Time Present and Time Past: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Temporally Evolving Document Understanding

author.name: Mahbub E Sobhani, Md. Faiyaz Abdullah Sayeedi, Fahmid Hasan Chowdhury, Md Adnan Arefeen, Farig Sadeque, Md. Faizul Bari, Swakkhar Shatabda

entry.summary: TIDE is an expert-verified benchmark of over 3,000 questions on 644 official customs instruments where the correct answer depends on which version of a regulation was in force at the queried date. Unlike prior temporal QA sets that treat time as an annotation, it directly tests version resolution across amendments, replacements and reversions. This targets a failure mode that matters for legal, tax and documentation assistants.

entry.title: SDDBMs: Soft Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models

author.name: Shiyi Qi, Kun He, Mingmou Liu

entry.summary: Soft Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models relax the hard endpoint conditioning used in diffusion bridges, which forces the terminal distribution to a point mass and makes drift coefficients ill-conditioned near the boundary. By regularizing the terminal constraint the authors obtain better-behaved transports for image-to-image translation and restoration. A clean theoretical fix to a known numerical pathology.

entry.title: The Scaffolding Matters More Than the Interface: A Controlled Comparison of MCP and CLI Tool Use Across Seven Agent Scaffoldings, Five Language Models, and One Software Task

author.name: Marc Alier Forment, Mar\'ia Jos\'e Casa\~n Guerrero, Francisco Jos\'e Garc\'ia-Pe\~nalvo, Juanan Pereira

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of tool access via the Model Context Protocol versus an ordinary command line, run across seven agent scaffoldings and five models on one fixed multi-step git task, with completion verified by inspecting repository state rather than trusting agent self-reports. The dominant cost driver was the scaffolding, not the tool interface, contradicting practitioner claims that differ by an order of magnitude. A refreshingly rigorous answer to a contested engineering question.

entry.title: ComboShoppingBench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Budget-Constrained Basket Shopping with Coupons

author.name: Adrian Li, Kelong Mao, Yudong Guo, Heming Xia, Xinwei Yang, Lirui Luo, Jace Wong, Pu Yao, Sulong Xu, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: ComboShoppingBench evaluates agents on constructing budget-constrained baskets of complementary items in a simulated commerce and takeout environment, checking coupon validity, store requirements, delivery fees, and payment correctness rather than exact product matches. Designed so open-ended solutions remain verifiable.

entry.title: verdi: retrieval is not transfer for continual world model optimization

author.name: Junyu Wu, Shiqin Nie, Youyi Kou, Baohua Yin, Guocai Yao, Qingyu Chen, Jingheng Ma, Shiji Zhou, Hongyong Song, Mingchen Zhuge, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that retrieved optimization strategies for tuning pretrained world models are only hypotheses, not transferable knowledge, until validated on the target model, and builds verdi, a continual research agent that gates reuse behind target-side experimental validation. Aims to stop optimization know-how from being rediscovered per campaign.

entry.title: NeuroPilot: An Agent-Driven Smart Pipeline for Processing, Quality Control, and Managing Neuroimages

author.name: Yiyao Chen, Yucheng Li, Jungong Tong, Shaoqi Wang, Kunhao Zhou, Ziquan Wei, Monica Murea, Marissa DiPiero, Tingting Dan, Guorong Wu

entry.summary: NeuroPilot is a multi-agent system that packages neuroimaging standardization, preprocessing, and quality control into LLM-invokable skills, with an agent orchestrating workflows across heterogeneous infrastructure. Aims to replace brittle project-specific scripts and manual QC.

entry.title: Geometry Beats Estimated Depth: RGB-Only Multi-Camera 3D Tracking under Sim2Real

author.name: Abdullah Naeem, Anav Katwal, Ayon Dey, Noman Khan, Md Tamjidul Hoque

entry.summary: A controlled AI City Challenge study comparing a geometry-first RGB-only multi-camera 3D tracking pipeline against monocular-depth pseudo-LiDAR under synthetic-to-real transfer. Concludes that cross-view geometric consistency, not monocular depth accuracy, governs Sim2Real performance.

entry.title: LGNNIC: Acceleration of Large-Scale GNN Training using SmartNICs

author.name: Liad Gerstman, Aditya Dhakal, Dejan Milojicic, Avi Mendelson

entry.summary: LGNNIC offloads preprocessing and communication-heavy steps of distributed graph neural network training onto SmartNICs co-located with remote memory nodes to relieve inter-node network congestion. Targets graphs too large for a single CPU-GPU node.

entry.title: From Product Search to Preference Articulation: The Economics of Agentic Commerce

author.name: Lingxiu Dong, Kaiwen Luo, Fasheng Xu

entry.summary: Builds an economic model comparing manual product search against delegating discovery to an AI agent that screens a broad catalog through noisy representations of consumer preferences, with preference complexity as the key parameter. Finds manual search collapses beyond a complexity threshold while agentic search shifts effort toward articulating preferences.

entry.title: RippleKV: Cross-Layer KV Cache Allocation via Perturbation Propagation

author.name: Dongjie Xu, Kai Qian, Julius, Weijie Shi, Yuxuan Sun, Minghua Tang, Fenglei Jin, Hanchi Dong, Jiajie Xu

entry.summary: Allocates KV cache budget across transformer layers by injecting norm-adaptive perturbations into each layer value cache and measuring the resulting KL divergence at the output, giving a direct sensitivity estimate instead of proxies like depth or attention statistics. Targets memory-bound long-context inference.

entry.title: LibraSpec: Dynamic Diffusion-Based Speculative Decoding via Marginal-Gain-Driven Optimization

author.name: Zexun Lin, Yuan Feng, Junlin Lv, Kevin S. Zhou, Xike Xie

entry.summary: Reformulates dynamic speculative decoding length selection as expected-speedup optimization for diffusion-based drafters, arguing that with parallel block drafting the question changes from how many tokens will be accepted to how many are worth verifying. Uses marginal-gain reasoning to choose verification depth per round.

entry.title: RL-Native Distillation: Exploiting Scored Trajectories for Few-Step Image Generation

author.name: Yuhan Li, Fangao Zeng, Sicong Kang, Mengfei Xu, Hao Zhou, Wei Li, Pipei Huang, Bingbing Ni

entry.summary: REST merges reward alignment and few-step distillation for text-to-image diffusion into one stage by treating the reward-scored trajectories produced during RL as distillation supervision for a decoupled student. This avoids losing reward gains during a separate compression phase.

entry.title: Can Coding Agents Solve Repository-Level Issues with Rendered Code? An Exploratory Study of Visual Representations

author.name: Weijie Liang, Yuanfeng Song, Xing Chen, Caleb Chen Cao, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Tests whether rendering source code as images can serve as operational context for agentic repository repair on SWE-bench Verified, with controlled settings separating exploration from structured repair. Finds prompt-token savings that do not scale linearly with nominal visual compression, and largely preserved but not improved repair performance.

entry.title: Temporal Misgrounding in Legal RAG: A Versioned-Corpus Benchmark for French Tax Law

author.name: Rose Cymbler, Daniel Guez, Laurent Fabre

entry.summary: Defines temporal misgrounding, where legal RAG retrieves the currently in-force version of a statute when an earlier or future version applies, and builds FiscalQA Pro from 32,436 versioned French tax code articles spanning 1938 to 2031 with expert-reviewed temporal reasoning questions. Reports that no evaluated model recovered the date-applicable answer closed-book.

entry.title: MADBench: A Benchmark for Modality-Aware Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Yanqiu Li, Yang Xiao, Jisheng Bai, Bin Chen, Hong Jia, Ting Dang

entry.summary: MADBench separates speech forgery from background-audio forgery in deepfake video, arguing that the two acoustic streams come from different generative mechanisms and leave distinct artifacts. It provides a benchmark for modality-aware audio deepfake detection where speech and ambient sound can be manipulated independently over authentic video.

entry.title: Illusion or Integrity? Geometrical Consistency Metric for AIGC Video Quality Evaluation

author.name: Yifei Xue, Yuanchen Fei, Hao Zhang, Chenzhi Nie, Tie ji, Yizhen Lao

entry.summary: Proposes measuring geometric consistency across frames of generated video as a quantitative proxy for physical plausibility, complementing existing metrics that focus on visual appeal and text alignment. The benchmark aims to give video generation models a measurable signal for adherence to physical law.

entry.title: From Benchmark Performance to Tool Deployment: Human-in-the-Loop Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mike Szklarzewski, CJ George, Gavin Smithson, Christopher Stokes, Dakota Fulp, William M. Jones, Benjamin Wynn, Alexander Ur, Agit Yesiloz, Clint Kallenbach, Mark Swartz, Nathan DeBardeleben, Sharmistha Chakrabarti

entry.summary: Evaluates nineteen unsupervised anomaly detection models on a difficult real manufacturing dataset with reflective surfaces and subtle defects, finding performance far less stable than on standard academic benchmarks and highly sensitive to preprocessing. A consensus audit indicates that the quality of supposedly nominal training data itself affects deployment outcomes.

entry.title: LLM-Based Embeddings for Program Analysis and Optimization

author.name: Calvin Higgins, Marco Alvarez

entry.summary: Applies embeddings from a language model pretrained on compiler intermediate representation to program analysis tasks by chunking programs, embedding chunks independently, and aggregating. Combining source-level and intermediate-representation embeddings cuts algorithm classification error to about 1.5 percent, a notable improvement over prior representations.

entry.title: SAGE: SLO-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Production RAG Systems

author.name: Muhammad Faizan Raza (Luna), Shuo (Luna), Yang, Satish Mahadevan Srinivasan

entry.summary: SAGE learns to choose how many passages to retrieve per query in production retrieval-augmented generation, using cheap features from an initial retrieval and imitation learning from an oracle that approximates the best latency-quality tradeoff. The aim is to stop over-retrieving for easy queries and under-serving hard ones under strict tail-latency and cost targets.

entry.title: Stateful CARS: Exact Cross-History Reuse for Policy-Constrained LLM Agents

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Md Najmus Swaqeeb, Abu Sa-Adat Mohamed Moon-Im Al Ahsan

entry.summary: Studies exact sampling from a language model conditioned on a hard stateful validator for tool-using agents, reusing certificates of invalidity across different action histories. The method freezes a bank of state-continuation schemas per attempt, removes trajectories containing certified-invalid continuations, and uses a residual transform to keep samples exactly distributed.

entry.title: Path-dependent Discrete Amortized Inference

author.name: Tiago da Silva, Esmeralda S. Whitammer, Salem Lahlou

entry.summary: Shows that the Markov assumption in amortized samplers for discrete compositional objects causes state aliasing that limits expressivity and hampers credit assignment. The fix is to lift the underlying Markov decision process with a learnable latent dynamical system so the policy can condition on the entire construction history.

entry.title: In-Context Density Estimation for Tabular Data

author.name: Patryk Marsza{\l}ek, Jacek Tabor, Marek \'Smieja

entry.summary: ICED is a transformer pretrained once on a synthetic prior that performs energy-based density estimation in context, reading an arbitrary tabular dataset as input and returning an unnormalized density without per-dataset fitting. This targets the shared foundation of anomaly detection, out-of-distribution detection and data augmentation on tabular data.

entry.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes

author.name: Laiqiao Qin, Tianqing Zhu, Longxiang Gao, Wanlei Zhou

entry.summary: Argues that prompt-injection detectors cause widespread over-refusal because aligned models can often withstand injections depending on the instruction and model. BASIS uses prefill attention probes to predict whether the model would actually be breached, shielding selectively instead of blanket-refusing.

entry.title: Wiener Representation Filtering for VLM Hallucination Suppression

author.name: Ameen Ali, Tamim Zoabi, Lidor Brami, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free, post-hoc edit in a vision-language model's language-backbone representation space to suppress object hallucination, modeling hidden states as a mix of truthful and hallucination-linked components. A one-time offline covariance calibration yields a Wiener-style filter that is folded directly into existing weights, requiring no gradients.

entry.title: Differentiate the Solver, Not the Equation: Reverse-Sweep Adjoints for Block Implicit Simulation

author.name: Lei Shu, Ying Jiang, Kui Wu, Yin Yang, Leonidas Guibas, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces solver-level differentiation for implicit simulators, differentiating the finite computation that actually ran rather than the converged equation or an unrolled tape. When the solver is built from block implicit updates, its discrete adjoint is obtained by a reverse sweep of block adjoint updates, avoiding global Jacobian assembly and depth-growing memory.

entry.title: Logarithmic-Free Moment and Generalization Bounds for Uniformly Stable Algorithms

author.name: Thanh Nguyen-Cung, Binh T. Nguyen

entry.summary: Answers an open question from prior work by proving moment and generalization bounds for uniformly stable algorithms without the extra logarithmic factor in the sample size. The result tightens a classical route to generalization guarantees for stable learners.

entry.title: High-Capacity Generalized Hopfield Networks

author.name: Victor Galitski

entry.summary: This theoretical paper generalizes Hopfield associative memory so that neurons and memories live on Riemannian manifolds, specifically symmetric spaces of special unitary groups, and shows nearly an order-of-magnitude capacity gain over vector networks starting at dimension three. A Lie-algebraic mapping to an auxiliary Hilbert space lets the nonlinear geometric constraints be handled with linear algebra and replica analysis.

entry.title: Reconfigurable Structural Robotic Assembly: Interlocking 3D Aggregations with Self-Aligning Compound Nested Lattice Modules

author.name: Alexander Htet Kyaw, Miana Smith, Paul Richard, Neil Gershenfeld

entry.summary: Presents a discrete building-block system in which geometric intelligence is embedded in the material itself: nested cuboctahedral-octahedral lattice modules that give robots defined grasping surfaces, passive self-alignment, and screw-releasable snap-fit joints for reversible 3D assembly. The work reframes robotic construction as co-design of material and robot rather than pushing all difficulty into sensing and control.

entry.title: Compiling and Benchmarking Task-State Horizons for Embodied Agents

author.name: Meiqi Wang, Shichao Li

entry.summary: Defines task-state horizon as the span of evolving task-relevant world states an embodied agent must track, and introduces RoboGraph, a compiler that turns state-transition dependencies into executable symbolic task graphs for benchmarking. It argues existing long-horizon benchmarks conflate action-sequence length with genuine state-tracking difficulty.

entry.title: SLIM-0.5B: Learning Action-Grounded Predictive Latents for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jingkai Wang, Zihan Tang, Gu Zhang, Mingyu Cao, Jiapeng Chen, Jingjiao Zhao, Xiansheng Chen, Pengwei Wang, Lemao Liu, Dejing Dou

entry.summary: SLIM is a compact half-billion-parameter latent interaction policy that learns action-grounded predictive latents capturing both action-conditioned future transitions and the actions explaining observed transitions, rather than carrying a large multimodal backbone or predicting pixels. The argument is that continuous manipulation needs compact transition representations, not open-domain semantics, at every control step.

entry.title: An AI Scientist that Doesn't Drift: Taste, Structure, and Falsifiable Findings in a Quadruped Navigation Research Loop

author.name: Yiwen Zhang, Eloise Zeng, Jaeha Lee, Tony Yue Yu

entry.summary: Builds an autonomous LLM research loop for quadruped navigation generalization that resists metric drift through an immutable experiment card pairing predictions with outcomes, role-restricted subagents, and a preference oracle encoding the human researcher's taste. The design prevents falsified hypotheses from being retroactively rewritten.

entry.title: An Agentic AI Framework Overcomes Fundamental Limitations of Large Language Models for Glaucoma Detection from Fundus Photography

author.name: Jalil Jalili, Hossein Taghizad, Anuwat Jiravarnsirikul, Christopher Bowd, Akram Belghith, Raheleh Kafieh, Christopher A. Girkin, Sally L. Baxter, Robert N. Weinreb, Linda M. Zangwill, Mark Christopher

entry.summary: Builds an agentic clinical pipeline in which an LLM makes an initial glaucoma assessment from fundus photos, calls specialized deep learning tools for image quality, classification, and disc-cup segmentation, then reflects to integrate tool outputs. Evaluation uses Gemini 2.5 Flash and a GPT-5.4 mini variant on two public datasets under cropped and uncropped conditions.

entry.title: Locating Failure in Multi-Page Visually Rich Document Understanding: An Empirical Attribution

author.name: Lewei Xu, Yihao Ding, Zihan Xu, Daniel Yitian Su, Daochang Liu, Siwen Luo, Yifan Peng, Wei Liu

entry.summary: Attributes errors in multi-page visually rich document understanding to three isolated failure modes: representation, evidence selection, and reasoning, intervening on each while holding the others fixed. Findings include that vision is necessary but does not replace text extraction, missing pages cap accuracy while distractors are cheap, and reasoners still fail to integrate evidence supplied across pages.

entry.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: Are Embodied VLMs Ready for Safety-Critical Scenarios?

author.name: Gabriele La Malfa, Nitay Alon, Emanuele La Malfa, Reuth Mirsky, Stefan Sarkadi

entry.summary: Extends a theory-of-space evaluation framework into a goal-driven pipeline measuring whether vision-language models explore competently, build reliable spatial memory, and make hazard-aware decisions under partial observability. It asks whether decisions rest on physical evidence or are corrupted by visual-language priors and whether memory patterns resemble human cognition.

entry.title: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception

author.name: Zejun Xu, Taiyi Chen, Jin Li, Yongtong Gu, Qi Cheng, Aixuan Lv, Shuai Zhu, Pengfei Zhu, Kaichen Yang, Boyu Sun, Yixian Yang, Mulong Xie, Xin Liu, Dagang Li, Xiaoteng Ma, Hongru Wang

entry.summary: CAP is a benchmark for browser agents emphasizing two overlooked difficulties: complex interactions with rich user interfaces and perception of dynamically rendered visual content, especially in tasks that span multiple websites. Sites are abstracted into structured cards and recomposed into scalable cross-site tasks. It targets the gap between end-to-end success metrics and the actual mechanics of real browsing.

entry.title: Reproducing and Stress-Testing Two Approaches to LLM Reasoning Reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation and Logic-Representation Editing

author.name: Minhan Cho, Jimin Kweon

entry.summary: An independent reproduction and stress test of two published methods for improving LLM reasoning reliability, one aggregating token probabilities with self-consistency at inference and one editing hidden states along a separated logic subspace. The authors extend both to new domains and models, noting that the original evaluations were author-run and one method shipped no code. Reproduction work like this is scarce and valuable for calibrating claims.

entry.title: SkillSentry: Reliable Skill Execution for LLM Agents via Runtime Assurance

author.name: You Lu, Xinyu Huang, Bihuan Chen, Xin Peng

entry.summary: SkillSentry defines a domain-specific language for runtime guidance and monitors skill execution to catch procedure deviations and incorrect steps, improving consistency when agents follow reusable skill documents across repeated or similar tasks. Frames agent unreliability as a runtime assurance problem.

entry.title: MMArch: Benchmarking Multimodal Reasoning Grounded in Architectural Evidence

author.name: Chenxu Du, Kang An, Tengyue Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Xinqi Yang, Yuanchi Zhu, Hebao Zhu, Ziliang Wang, Faqiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: MMArch is a 1,212-item short-answer benchmark for architecture and civil engineering built entirely from peer-reviewed paper figures, requiring models to combine distributed visual evidence with governing engineering principles rather than merely read drawings. Uses a planner-writer generation pipeline plus blind adversarial audit and expert review.

entry.title: CircuitReason-1k: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Visual-to-Symbolic Reasoning inElectrical Circuits

author.name: Xinqi Yang, Kang An, Tengyue Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Chenxu Du, Yuanchi Zhu, Hebao Zhu, Ziliang Wang, Faqiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: CircuitReason-1k benchmarks long-horizon visual-to-symbolic reasoning on 1,000 authentic textbook circuit problems, each requiring symbol grounding, topology recovery, model selection, coupled equation formulation, and unit or sign consistency, with reference worked solutions. Includes an evidence-first pipeline and a reasoning-oriented taxonomy.

entry.title: Representation Matters in Longitudinal Affective Computing

author.name: Igor Matias, Maximilian Haas, Eric J. Daza, Matthias Kliegel, Katarzyna Wac

entry.summary: Studies how to map dense daily wearable sensor histories onto sparsely labeled affect and cognition outcomes, comparing level summaries, absolute change, and proportional change representations across 21 outcomes in a year-long study of 82 adults. Frames the label-cadence mismatch as a temporal representation choice.

entry.title: COMEX: A Composition-Grounded Benchmark and Learning Framework for Explainable Aesthetic Image Cropping

author.name: Rui Yang, Wei Zhou, Dingyong Gou, Xiaohui Cui, Cong Li, Yinyin Gong, Yipo Huang, Jiliang Zhao

entry.summary: COMEX reformulates explainable aesthetic image cropping as joint crop, composition category, and composition-grounded explanation prediction, with a 33,161-quadruple benchmark built via image expansion and an input-output reversal pipeline. Moves explanation from post-hoc text generation to a structured aesthetic reasoning target.

entry.title: Compositional Cross-Modality Translation via Whole-Volume Multitask Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Daniele Molino, Alessio Zoboli, Camillo Maria Caruso, Valerio Guarrasi, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: Decouples volumetric anatomical priors from cross-modality mapping by pretraining a large 3D variational autoencoder and then learning conditional flow matching in that latent space, enabling whole-volume, multi-task medical image translation with a single model. Avoids the usual per-task, per-patch pipelines.

entry.title: DoGMA: A Central-Dogma-Guided Foundation Model for Multi-Omics Alignment and Multi-Task Learning in Oncology

author.name: Junfei Ling (Institute of Medical Robotics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Bangzheng Pu (Institute of Medical Robotics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Bingsen Xue (Institute of Medical Robotics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Tianle Li (Institute of Data Science, The University of Hong Kong), Ruying Hu (Oriental Pan-Vascular Devices Innovation College, University of Shanghai for Science and Technology), Cheng Jin (Institute of Medical Robotics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

entry.summary: Introduces a pan-cancer multi-omics foundation model whose Transformer mixture-of-experts uses directed attention biases reflecting the central dogma, so information flows in biologically plausible directions rather than freely bidirectionally. Claims better transfer across cancers, tasks and missing-modality settings.

entry.title: Beyond Tables: Doc2DB-Bench for Relationally Faithful Document-to-Database Construction

author.name: Zhuowen Liang, Zhengxuan Zhang, Jiayang Wang, Jiazhuo Chen, Nan Tang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for converting long heterogeneous documents into normalized relational databases rather than flat tables, testing whether extracted facts form a valid database instance with keys, entity identities, cross-table relations and integrity constraints. Motivated by finance, healthcare and compliance workflows that need SQL-backed reasoning.

entry.title: On-Device Multi-Species Malaria Detection with Uncertainty-Calibrated Slide-Level Aggregation

author.name: Idaya Seidu, Ahmed Tahiru Issah, Charles B. Delahunt, Carine Mukamakuza

entry.summary: Develops a deployable on-device malaria microscopy pipeline co-designed with a national health center, adding clinically required features usually omitted in the literature such as stopping criteria to limit image acquisition, human-in-the-loop review, and uncertainty-calibrated slide-level aggregation across species. Emphasizes clinical constraints over raw accuracy.

entry.title: REVEAL: A Rubric-Guided Agent for Explicit Evidence Sufficiency Verificationin Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Caijun Yan, Yang Zhou, Meixing Shi, Haoran Sun, Yichen Li, Yuxiang Cai, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: Presents a rubric-guided agent for long-video question answering that explicitly verifies whether retrieved evidence is sufficient before answering, instead of stopping at the first semantically relevant clue, and replaces fixed-length chunking with adaptive event-aware retrieval. Targets missing temporal, causal and fine-grained action evidence.

entry.title: 360CityArena: A Realistic Virtual Urban Navigation Benchmark for Embodied Agents

author.name: Kenta Watanabe, Atsuyuki Miyai, Mizuki Takenawa, Kiyoharu Aizawa, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Introduces a photorealistic urban navigation benchmark built from six hundred 360-degree video segments covering eighty-five streets of a Tokyo district, with one hundred seventy-five hand-crafted tasks spanning environment understanding, path reasoning and spatial reasoning. Aims to close the realism gap in outdoor embodied agent evaluation.

entry.title: How Do Large Language Models Judge Social Attraction? Evidence from Theory-Grounded Persona Ratings Across Multiple LLMs and Humans

author.name: Hasan Mahmud, Khawaja Abaid Ullah, Mohammad Javad Khojasteh, Jamison Heard, Prabu David

entry.summary: Tests whether language models can act as valid judges of social attraction using theory-grounded persona profiles rated by 34 models and compared against human raters. Models were internally stable across repeated runs and agreed on the intended three-tier ordering, though with systematic level shifts between models.

entry.title: Agentic Harnesses: LLM-Driven Verification Layers for Robot Autonomy

author.name: Rohan Bhagra, Mahantesh Halapannavar, Uddhav Bhattarai

entry.summary: Proposes inserting a language-model verification layer between robot planning and execution that judges whether proposed actions are permissible, using an ensemble of judges with chain-of-thought reasoning. The motivation is that planning models optimize for user goals and can propose unsafe, unethical, or adversarially induced actions.

entry.title: Beyond Aggregate Calibration: Decomposing Income-Conditional Recall Disparities in Automated Credit Default Prediction

author.name: Sai Srikar Boddupalli

entry.summary: Shows on a large consumer-lending sample that confidence-based data curation disproportionately flags high-income defaulters as label noise, and that the resulting model has a nearly seventeen point recall gap between high- and low-income borrowers who actually defaulted. Sequential feature blinding is used to isolate where the disparity originates.

entry.title: Conversation as Measurement in Clinical Encounters: Observable Phase Structure, Partially Observable Patient State

author.name: Lily Chen, Ted Mau, Michael Gensheimer, Brian Anthony Nuyen, Nancy Jiang, James Zou

entry.summary: Studies observability, meaning whether a target quantity is actually recoverable from conversational transcripts alone, using clinical encounters where patient-reported outcome measures give an external anchor for patient state. Distinguishes limits of the conversational signal itself from annotator error, and finds conversation phase structure is observable while patient state is only partially so.

entry.title: Reducing Pretraining-Generation Mismatch in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiaocheng Lu, Huabin Liu, Song Guo, Jianguo Li

entry.summary: Identifies a mismatch in native diffusion language model pretraining, where prompt and continuation tokens are corrupted together, undermining the clean-prefix conditioning that prompted generation relies on. Proposes a continued-pretraining objective that combines autoregressive prefix supervision with unshifted suffix denoising by changing only attention, corruption, and label construction, without needing an autoregressive decoder.

entry.title: The Judge Knows When It Knows: Calibrated Abstention for LLM-Based A/B-Test Prediction

author.name: Tyler Dooskin, Squoosh Technical Staff

entry.summary: Six weeks of pre-registered experiments test whether a multimodal LLM judge can predict real web A/B test winners from screenshots, finding agreement near chance once statistically unreliable labels are removed. The authors also show that a large fraction of industry ground-truth labels come from non-significant tests and that the model matches the unreliable labels better, indicating shared prior rather than prediction.

entry.title: FlexSplat: Flexible Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting without Point Cloud Correspondence

author.name: Amir Sabbaghziarani, Hanting Ye, Maria Gorlatova, Yi Ding

entry.summary: FlexSplat performs feed-forward novel view synthesis from uncalibrated object-centric image sets by jointly training a geometry transformer that predicts camera parameters and depth alongside a Gaussian decoder. Depth-guided parameterization and multi-view deformable cross-attention aggregate all views into one consistent set of Gaussian primitives.

entry.title: What Irregularity Costs: CUDA C++, Rust, and Triton on a Hash-Blocked GPU Workload

author.name: Petr Korolev (Spacial Intelligence Labs)

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks the same hash-blocked TSDF fusion kernel implemented in CUDA C++, Rust via a CUDA binding, and Triton, deliberately choosing an irregular workload with open-addressed hashing, compare-exchange insertion, and contended scatter. On the regular stage all three are comparable, while on the irregular stage Triton is more than an order of magnitude slower than the other two.

entry.title: WA-SpecDec: World-Aware Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zikang Wen, Yuning Zhang, Dong Yuan

entry.summary: WA-SpecDec speeds up autoregressive vision-language-action inference by making speculative-decoding acceptance thresholds state-dependent: world-model signals tighten tolerance near contact and relax it in free space. This replaces scene-agnostic fixed token-distance tolerances that treat identical deviations as equally safe everywhere.

entry.title: Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents

author.name: Ao Ding, Hongzong LI, Shiqin Tang, Li Zhang, Liang Chen, Xuyang Chen, Zi Liang

entry.summary: Introduces a diagnostic framework for studying how long-term agent memory evolves when new experiences reinforce, revise, or contradict stored memories, rather than only how memories are retrieved. Findings indicate benign accumulation is relatively harmless while conflicting or authority-differing memories cause failures.

entry.title: CausalNav: Reliability-Certified Causal World Models for Control under Physical-Parameter Shift

author.name: Yiyao Zhang, Diksha Goel, Hussain Ahmad, Shixun Huang, Jun Shen

entry.summary: Presents a controller that builds a signed, action-conditioned causal transition graph over identified state variables, simulates candidate intervention sequences at deployment, and only accepts the resulting advice when a predictive-reliability certificate and two decision gates all pass, otherwise reverting to a base controller. It is compared against nine controlled world-model baselines under physical parameter shift.

entry.title: Counterfactual Benchmarking and Training for Factuality Consistency and Order-Robust Grounded Reasoning in LLMs over Heterogeneous Knowledge

author.name: Shibo Chu, Yuze Liu, Tiehua Zhang, Zhishu Shen, Lianghua He, Haofen Wang, Zhijun Ding

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of over ten thousand QA pairs grounded in tables, text, and knowledge graphs, each built from an explicit counterfactual reasoning chain so that answer correctness, chain accuracy, and sensitivity to input ordering can be scored jointly. Fourteen open and closed models are evaluated.

entry.title: The Authority Expectancy Effect in Multi-User Conflict

author.name: Eunna Lee

entry.summary: Studies how social authority signals such as occupation, institutional documentation, and relational congruence interact with severity-based triage in LLM judgments across resource allocation, fault attribution, and dispute mediation. The authors find restructuring effects not explained by simple additive reweighting of authority cues and formalize this as an authority expectancy effect.

entry.title: Lingjing: A Simulation Testbed for Multi-Agent Embodied Tasks in Open-Ended Cities

author.name: Xiaohe Li, Yiru Wang, Junhao Fan, Mingyuan Liu, Jie Huang, Kaixin Zhang, Jiahao Li, Chen Qian, Zide Fan

entry.summary: Presents a simulation platform for heterogeneous embodied multi-agent coordination in reconstructed open-ended cities, synchronizing multiple physics engines and exposing shared physical and structured urban state through a Gym-like interface. It supports drones, ground robots, and vehicles with user-defined ReAct agents in single or multi-agent modes.

entry.title: SodaMem: Evidence-Grounded Temporal Graph Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: Fengrong Wan, Chengcan Wu, Ningtao Lyu

entry.summary: Proposes an agent memory system that extracts typed fact events with mandatory provenance spans, records mention time, occurrence time, and validity with supersedes and contradicts edges, and answers queries through a planner-reader loop that gathers citable evidence first. It targets currency and ordered temporal reasoning that flat retrieval diaries handle poorly.

entry.title: CORDA: A Benchmark for Hierarchical Harm-Centric Moral Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Siddarth Singh, Victoria Williams, Simon Rosen, Ebenezer Gelo, Helen Sarah Robertson, Ibrahim Suder, Benjamin Rosman, Geraud Nangue Tasse, Steven James

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 90 moral dilemmas testing whether LLMs can prioritize among conflicting harm-centred principles when no option is cost-free, rather than merely selecting acceptable answers. It builds on a morality chains formalism spanning trolley cases, medical trade-offs, and resource allocation.

entry.title: OBLIVION: Workflow-Level Operational Skill Unlearning for Deployed Agents

author.name: Zhengyang Shan, Xu Qian, Jiayun Xin, Kun Li, Yue Zhang, Minghui Xu

entry.summary: OBLIVION frames a new problem it calls operational skill unlearning: after a capability is revoked from an agent registry, the agent may rebuild it from archives, transcripts, schemas or memory. The paper provides a benchmark modeling episodes as source-to-sink workflows plus a defense that erases residual carriers coherently across surfaces. It reframes unlearning as a deployment and tooling problem rather than a weight-editing one.

entry.title: Not Worth Another Token: Marginal Value Estimation for Efficient Deep Research Agents

author.name: Harshitha Kolukuluru, Reshma Ashok, Kirat Arora, Evan William Ciccarelli, Nischal Ashok Kumar, Lunyiu Nie, Franck Dernoncourt, Samyadeep Basu, Ryan A. Rossi, Nedim Lipka

entry.summary: A study of when to prune accumulated context in deep research agents, comparing heuristic scorers against a learned value model at pre-retrieval, post-retrieval and pre-synthesis stages. The main finding is that where pruning happens matters more than the scoring rule, with early pruning giving the best cost-quality tradeoff. Relevant to controlling token cost and noise in long-horizon research pipelines.

entry.title: Can Open-Weight Models Compete on Financial Text Comprehension?

author.name: Jan Sp\"orer

entry.summary: An updated financial text comprehension benchmark of nearly 3,000 question-context-answer triplets over 495 annual reports, expanded to twenty models from ten providers including several open-weight Chinese models and a proprietary Alibaba flagship. Anthropic's Opus model leads on accuracy while a Google model has the lowest hallucination rate, so open-weight parity on generic benchmarks does not fully transfer to this task. Note that all models discussed here were already generally available well before this evaluation.

entry.title: SymDiag: Explainable Diagnosis for LLM Reasoning via Neuro-Symbolic Verification

author.name: Wenyao Cui, Huaping Zhang, Yongyi Huang, Qiuchi Li, Jian Xu, Cheng-Lin Liu, Chunxiao Gao, Juan Wang, Baohua Zhang

entry.summary: SymDiag translates natural-language chains of thought into symbolic constraints and runs step-level satisfiability and entailment checks, turning reasoning verification into localized failure diagnosis rather than a scalar score or subjective judge critique. It aims to say where a derivation breaks and why, even when the final answer happens to be right. Relevant to faithfulness measurement and process supervision.

entry.title: From Relevance to Execution Utility: Reward-Aware Dynamic Execution Gating for Skill-Based LLM Agents

author.name: Liang He, Jingbo Wen, Hongyu Gu, Hao Li, Haoyu Wang, Yixiong Chen, Kangning Cui, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: RADEG inserts a lightweight learned gate between skill retrieval and skill execution for LLM agents, predicting whether executing a retrieved skill bundle is actually worth its rollout cost rather than merely whether it is topically relevant. The surrogate is retriever-agnostic and trained to estimate execution utility.

entry.title: Entropy-based Code Adversarial Translation for Real-world Repository Migration

author.name: Yushun Tang, Yisen Cao, Zhicheng Chen, Lin Peng, Junkang Mao, Fengyi Song, Yantao Jia

entry.summary: ECAT is a multi-agent framework for migrating whole Android repositories to HarmonyOS, framed as adversarial minimization of a code entropy metric between a generator and a discriminator that emits file-level directives and needed skills as text gradients. Targets the long-horizon failure of repository-scale translation.

entry.title: EmoPatient: An Emotion-Directed Patient Simulator for Realistic Palliative Care Communication Training

author.name: Yining Wu, Tianshu Du, Jinrui Fang, Chi Zhang, Sonal Admane, Ying Ding

entry.summary: EmoPatient is an LLM patient simulator for palliative care communication training that adds an Emotion Director agent estimating emotional state and emitting turn-level signals for intensity, regulation, and expression. It targets the shortcoming that most simulators hold patient emotion static.

entry.title: Temporal Generalization in fNIRS-Based Autism Classification: A Cross-Time-Window Transfer Benchmark

author.name: Marios Petrov, Sahana Vinayak, Targol Bakhtiarvand, Moses Smith Guddah, Adham Atyabi, Frederick Shic, Kevin A. Pelphrey

entry.summary: Formalizes cross-time-window transfer for fNIRS-based autism classification, noting that optimal observation windows differ per subject due to hemodynamic variability, and benchmarks three vision architectures with zero-shot and eight adaptation strategies under leave-one-subject-out evaluation. Treats window misalignment as a distribution shift problem.

entry.title: Hit Selection Using SSMD-Based Machine Learning Performance Metrics in High-Throughput Screening Assays

author.name: Xiaohua Douglas Zhang

entry.summary: Derives closed-form relationships between the strictly standardized mean difference effect size and classification metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, and AUROC, enabling metric estimation in single-replicate high-throughput screening where empirical estimation is infeasible. Provides a model-based route to evaluate hit selection under extreme data sparsity.

entry.title: Prompt Embedding Probes (PEP): Hallucination Detection in LLMs from Hidden States

author.name: Zakhar Mrykhin, Valentin Malykh

entry.summary: Introduces Prompt Embedding Probes, which augment standard linear probes on frozen LLM hidden states with a few learnable prompt embeddings to detect hallucinated answers. Tested on TriviaQA, GSM8K and MedQA with Qwen3 models, including pre-generation prediction and cross-model transfer settings.

entry.title: $\texttt{DisMorph}$: learning to disentangle technical distortions from true biological change

author.name: Jingru Fu, Kathleen E. Larson, Douglas N. Greve, Bruce Fischl, Malte Hoffmann

entry.summary: Proposes a deformable registration framework trained purely on synthetic data that separates scanner-induced geometric distortions such as gradient non-linearity from genuine biological change in longitudinal brain MRI. Aims to remove a systematic bias in morphometric measures of aging and neurodegeneration.

entry.title: VTO: Visual Tool Orchestration for Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Rui Wang, Yeteng Wu, Xianling Zhang, Mengshi Qi

entry.summary: Introduces a process-supervised reinforcement learning framework for video anomaly detection in which a multimodal agent learns to orchestrate visual tools dynamically, with intermediate rewards to prevent the premature stopping caused by outcome-only signals. Targets generalization across diverse real-world surveillance scenarios.

entry.title: Dramarrator: Object-Based Audio Editing for Audio Drama Production from Books

author.name: Karim Benharrak, Oriol Nieto, Bryan Wang, Zeyu Jin, Amy Pavel

entry.summary: Introduces an authoring tool that converts books into audio dramas by extracting story elements as editable objects, generating linked speech, sound effects and music, and composing a multi-track timeline so a single edit propagates across dependent assets. Addresses the ripple-edit problem that makes generative audio production labor-intensive.

entry.title: SuperNeuroMAT: An Efficient Matrix-based Simulator for Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Prasanna Date, Kevin Zhu, Shruti Kulkarni, Ashish Gautam, Chathika Gunaratne, Robert Patton, Tyler Nitzsche, Ian Mulet, Zachary Johnson-Scott, Addison Helms, Duncan Rowden, Simon Weston, Maryam Parsa, Catherine Schuman, Thomas Potok

entry.summary: Releases an open-source matrix-based spiking neural network simulator that models leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics with dense and sparse execution modes, simulating tens of thousands of neurons on commodity laptops and outperforming four established simulators. Lowers the barrier to neuromorphic experimentation.

entry.title: Epistemic Transfer in AI-Assisted Verification: A Framework and Evaluation Protocol

author.name: Christoph Trattner

entry.summary: Defines epistemic transfer, the question of what a person can still do unaided after using an AI verification assistant, and separates it from correction effects, trust and human-AI team performance. Proposes two measurable quantities, a transfer effect and a tool-removal cost, plus an evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Not All Visual Tokens Are Equally Safe to Remove:Consequence-Sensitive Visual Token Compression

author.name: Jingbo Wen, Liang He, Mingyu Cao, Haoyu Wang, Minxuan Hu, Kangning Cui, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: Argues that visual token compression in VLMs wrongly assumes all errors cost the same, and proposes allocating visual compute per request according to the downstream consequence of an error. Uses offline calibration of consequence-specific error-budget curves and then allocates budgets at inference.

entry.title: Software Engineering for and with GUI Agent

author.name: Shengcheng Yu, Yuchen Ling, Junyang Xing, Quan Zhou, Chunrong Fang, Zhenyu Chen

entry.summary: Surveys 336 GUI-agent papers from 2018 to April 2026 through a software engineering lens, arguing that GUI agents are closed-loop software systems coupling model reasoning with perception, execution feedback, recovery, and human oversight. Organizes the landscape, architectures, evaluation practice, and engineering gaps around five research questions.

entry.title: VeinCast: Physics-Guided Dynamic Field Graphs with Graph-Conditioned Fusion for Global Medium-Range Weather Forecasting

author.name: Zhisheng Chen, Jinhan Li, Yuxuan Li, Yuan Gao, Hao Wu, Zheng Lu, Jinlong Du, Kun Wang, Bo An

entry.summary: VeinCast forecasts 69 atmospheric fields using a physics-guided dynamic field graph that mixes predefined inter-variable relations with state-dependent top-K residual edges, then conditions Earth-window attention and latent fusion on that graph context. Positions itself between purely data-driven models and hard equation-level constraints.

entry.title: Test-Time Augmentation for LLMs: When Input Diversity Beats Output Diversity at Matched Compute

author.name: Nikita Kozodoi, Zainab Afolabi, Jack Butler

entry.summary: Compares test-time augmentation, which perturbs the input via rephrasing, lexical edits, or visual transforms, against self-consistency, which samples multiple reasoning paths, under matched inference compute. Asks whether input-side diversity converts compute into accuracy more efficiently than output-side diversity.

entry.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training

author.name: Zehao Chen, Gongxun Li, Tianxiang Ai, Yifei Li, Zixuan Huang, Wang Zhou, Tao Huang, Fuzhen Zhuang, Xianglong Liu, Jianxin Li, Deqing Wang, Yikun Ban

entry.summary: WDL-OPD stabilizes on-policy distillation, where each update changes both the policy and the states used for the next update, by co-training an anchor policy that generates rollouts and an auxiliary policy evaluated on the same states, matching a geometric mixture of their distributions to a frozen teacher via reverse KL. Shows freezing the auxiliary recovers a known anchor-plus-contrast target.

entry.title: MixFormer: Linear Transformer with Mixture of Memory Experts

author.name: Yu Guo, Lei Duan

entry.summary: MixFormer is a linear-attention transformer that maintains multiple memory experts, routed mixture-of-experts style, plus a time-aware linear attention with learnable exponential decay and positional bias to update memory states. Aims to overcome the limited input adaptivity and fixed memory capacity of state space models on ultra-long sequences.

entry.title: Finite Constant Frontiers and Auditable Regret Certificates for Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Abu Sa-Adat Mohamed Moon-Im Al Ahsan, Md Najmus Swaqeeb

entry.summary: Proposes a constant-aware protocol for comparing average-reward reinforcement learning regret bounds, since published guarantees differ in probability mode, structural parameters, and logarithmic normalization. It derives an explicit finite lower-bound certificate for communicating Markov decision processes that improves the published leading coefficient.

entry.title: Support Selection Beyond Smooth DAG Exactness: Completion Geometry,Score Margins, and Selective Certificates

author.name: Rui Wu, Zongyuan Chen, Hong Xie

entry.summary: Examines what smooth acyclicity constraints used in continuous structure learning can and cannot tell you about which edge to change, showing that at a DAG boundary the response to a support change has an order set by the smallest cycle completion. It constructs many cyclic manifolds where popular smooth-constraint methods provide no ranking signal.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Diagnostic of Rank Collapse in Post-Norm Decoder Transformers

author.name: Xingjian Wang, Qingyu Han, Xiaodong Luo, Yin Zhang

entry.summary: Provides a two-stage mechanistic explanation of why post-normalization decoder transformers suffer rank collapse, treating token similarity as a scalar state variable. At initialization causal attention behaves like a prefix-averaging operator that raises token similarity with depth, and the analysis explains why training dynamics fail to reverse this.

entry.title: OpenVisTool: An Open Recipe for Synthesizing Instructive Visual Tool-Use Trajectories

author.name: Changhao Xiang, Shilin Zhang, Zheng Ma, Kanzhi Cheng, Ruize Ma, Yi Feng, Jianbing Zhang, Zhi Wang, Zhen Wu, Xinyu Dai, Lewei Lu

entry.summary: OpenVisTool challenges the standard recipe of distilling visual tool-use from teacher trajectories filtered only by answer correctness, arguing that strong teachers often reach correct answers without needing their tool calls. The result is students that learn tool calls as decoration rather than as grounded evidence, motivating an open framework for synthesizing genuinely instructive trajectories.

entry.title: A Mean-Field Framework for Inference-Time Distributional Control of Diffusion Models

author.name: Samuel Howard, Nikolas N\"usken

entry.summary: Provides a mean-field framework for steering diffusion models at inference time toward distribution-level rewards, such as matching population statistics or encouraging diversity, rather than only per-sample rewards. It extends principled particle-reweighting targeting of tilted distributions to the distributional case where naive reward-gradient guidance lacks guarantees.

entry.title: SurveyReview: A Reviewer-Aligned Benchmark for Survey Evaluators

author.name: Yuheng Zhang, Yuanchun Wang, Fanjin Zhang, Ruyu Zhao, Juanzi Li, Jie Tang, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: Builds a reviewer-aligned benchmark for evaluating automatically generated survey papers, based on 675 annotated surveys and over 1,600 structured peer-review reports. Provides a framework for quantifying how well LLM-as-a-judge evaluators agree with real human reviewers, addressing the evaluation bottleneck as survey generation becomes automated.

entry.title: Commitment Before Realization: When Classifier-Free Guidance Becomes Unnecessary in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Fan Zhou, Weitian Wang, Tim Van de Cruys

entry.summary: Analyzes when classifier-free guidance actually helps during masked diffusion language model decoding by comparing eventual constraint-satisfaction probability under continued guidance versus base-only continuation. Finds guidance dependence is strongly prompt-specific and usually concentrated early, and defines a commitment horizon after which guidance can be switched off with no loss.

entry.title: Thinking vs. NoThinking: Towards Interpreting Reasoning Mechanisms of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Bo Cheng, Qiaolin Lu, Yi Chang, Yuan Wu

entry.summary: Applies top-K sparse autoencoders to a distilled reasoning model's intermediate representations to contrast explicit chain-of-thought mode with direct answering across three math difficulty levels. Reports that thinking mode uses sparse, high-intensity features supporting verbal deduction largely independent of problem difficulty, whereas non-thinking mode behaves differently.

entry.title: Multilingual Emotion Neurons in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Xiutian Zhao, Philipp Koehn, Bj\"orn Schuller, Berrak Sisman

entry.summary: Performs a neuron-level interpretability study of large audio-language models to test whether emotion is encoded through language-specific correlations or language-agnostic units, introducing a consistency-regularized fusion method to identify multilingual emotion neurons. Across four models and twelve typologically diverse languages, per-language emotion neurons overlap minimally, motivating the fused identification approach.

entry.title: Unsure but Certain: Uncovering the Representation-Confidence Gap in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Saurabh Yadav, Badri Narayana Patro, Vijay Srinivas Agneeswaran

entry.summary: Shows that diffusion language models internally detect corrupted or noisy input text with high accuracy while their externally reported confidence stays near maximum, so answer ranking degrades toward chance as accuracy falls. Names this the representation-confidence gap and shows standard calibration transforms remove the surface symptom without restoring correct ranking.

entry.title: Tevatron-Elastic: A Unified Abstraction for Training Elastic Retrievers and Rerankers

author.name: Yu Wang, Shengyao Zhuang, Xueguang Ma, Zongyu Wu, Jimmy Lin, Vivek Srikumar, Zhichao Xu

entry.summary: Provides a unified training abstraction for elastic retrievers and rerankers, bringing layer reduction, token pruning in upper layers, and shorter embeddings under one interface with a simple schedule specification. Makes previously separate efficiency techniques composable and portable to new backbone models.

entry.title: PragMatch: Separating Pragmatic Incongruity from Cross-Modal Mismatch in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhanna Mukhametsharip (Saarland University, Germany), Vera Demberg (Saarland University, Germany, Max Planck Institute for Informatics, Germany), Varsha Suresh (Max Planck Institute for Informatics, Germany)

entry.summary: PragMatch is a 3,000-pair controlled benchmark that separates genuine pragmatic incongruity in sarcasm from simple image-text mismatch, using literal and hard-negative constructions derived from an existing sarcasm dataset. Systematic masking identifies shortcut cues that vision-language models exploit instead of reasoning about intent.

entry.title: EvoTrustRAG: Evolution-Aware Conflict Attribution and Evidence Handling for Reliable Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Xi Nie, Hongwei Li, Shenghao Wu, Wenshu Fan, Qiyang Song, Wenbo Jiang

entry.summary: EvoTrustRAG reframes retrieval conflicts by asking why evidence disagrees, distinguishing legitimate knowledge evolution, malicious manipulation, and genuine uncertainty rather than just picking a winner. The training-free framework attributes conflict origin from observable context and adapts evidence handling accordingly.

entry.title: The Voiceprint Fallacy: Why Voices Are Not Unique Biometric Imprints

author.name: Tianle Yang, Cuiling Zhang, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu, Phil Rose

entry.summary: A critical review arguing that the popular notion of a voiceprint as a stable, unique biometric analogous to a fingerprint is scientifically unsupported, given the dynamic and context-dependent nature of speech. It revisits the history of voiceprint identification and reconsiders what should count as speaker-identity evidence.

entry.title: AnchorFold: A Focus-Then-Fold Framework via Recursive Attention Propagation for Efficient Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Haoyu Zuo, Yibo Yan, Xin Zou, Shuliang Liu, Yi Cao, Mingdong Ou, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: AnchorFold compresses the document-side index of multi-vector visual document retrievers by first selecting important patch anchors via recursive attention propagation over self-attention graphs, then folding remaining patches into them. It is training-free and aims to beat both pruning and merging under aggressive compression.

entry.title: HSMLA: Hierarchical Softmax Multi-scale Linear Attention for Efficient Vision Transformers

author.name: Dong Liu, Yanxuan Yu, Renata Borovica-Gajic, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: HSMLA combines ReLU-based linear attention for global context with selective softmax refinement on important local regions and multi-scale tokens from depthwise convolutions. It reports several-fold inference speedups on dense prediction tasks including CT organ segmentation and pathology slides while maintaining accuracy.

entry.title: HeatCast: A Benchmark for Neighborhood-Scale LST Forecasting across 124 U.S. Cities

author.name: Jesus Guerrero, Isaac Corley, Leon Najafirad, Maryam Tabar, Paul Rad

entry.summary: HeatCast provides a Landsat-based benchmark for forecasting land surface temperature at 30 meter resolution across 124 US cities from 2013 to mid-2025, with fixed splits, auxiliary spectral and climate-zone layers, and a reference evaluation harness. Baselines include a CNN-LSTM and a transformer-based spatiotemporal model.

entry.title: XClipGS: Exact Half-Space Clipping for Medical Volume Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zhongpai Gao, Benjamin Planche, Meng Zheng, Anwesa Choudhuri, Chaoyi Zhou, Terrence Chen, Ziyan Wu

entry.summary: XClipGS derives a closed-form operator for rendering half-space-clipped Gaussians in medical volume splatting, showing the ray integral factorizes into the usual 2D footprint times a conditional Gaussian CDF. It separates the render-time clipping problem from the problem of supervising interior anatomy never seen during external-view training.

entry.title: Advantage-Guided Gate: Reshaping Open-Ended Reasoning for Vision-Based Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Ling Lin, Yang Bai, Congcong Zhu, Jiangming Shi, Meng Wang, Yang Long, Jingrun Chen, Ling Shao, Huazhu Fu

entry.summary: This framework treats multimodal step-by-step spatial reasoning as a finite-horizon decision process and uses Monte Carlo value estimates over a reasoning tree to supply intermediate supervision. Step-level and trajectory-level advantage gates then select high-value reasoning steps and prune deviations that would otherwise compound into errors.

entry.title: Ego-OSCAR: Egocentric Open source Stereo CAptuRe System

author.name: Gunjan Paul, Senthil Palanisamy, Satpal Singh Rathore, Pratyush Kumar Patnaik, Shubhanshu Khatana, Abhishek Anand

entry.summary: Ego-OSCAR is an open-hardware head-mounted stereo-inertial capture rig costing under 200 dollars per unit, built from off-the-shelf parts and 3D-printed components with a synchronized global-shutter stereo camera and IMU. The authors release the full software stack plus roughly 550 hours of synchronized egocentric stereo video.

entry.title: Learning How the World Evolves: Extrapolative Video World Models via Latent Dynamics Reasoning

author.name: Haodong Li, Shaoteng Liu, Tianyu Wang, Chongjian Ge, Sihui Ji, Jiahan Zhang, Xin Lin, Haolin Lu, Zhe Lin, Manmohan Chandraker

entry.summary: Latent Dynamics Reasoning reformulates video world-model rollout as explicit kinematic integration in a structured latent space, numerically integrating lower-order dynamics and learning only the higher-order residual. Evaluated on controlled physics worlds, it targets extrapolation beyond the training distribution rather than pixel plausibility.

entry.title: Diminishing Returns of Intelligence: The Non-Linear Relationship Between LLM Scale and User Perception in Short-Duration Open-Ended Social Human-Robot Interactions

author.name: Amanda Rasille R{\o}n Volf, Morten Roed Frederiksen

entry.summary: A within-subjects study with nineteen participants finds that driving a robot face with a 30B parameter vision-language model produced no significant gain in perceived intelligence, naturalness, enjoyment, or humor over 8B and even 4B variants during brief open-ended social interactions. The result suggests sharply diminishing perceptual returns to model scale in short human-robot encounters.

entry.title: On Democratizing ASI to Preserve Civil Liberties

author.name: MichaelDickens

entry.summary: An essay arguing that even a fully solved alignment problem leaves a structural risk: superintelligence concentrates power so severely that liberal democracy and individual civil liberties survive only at the discretion of whoever controls the system. The author examines whether broadly distributing access to advanced AI could preserve autonomy, while maintaining that a development pause remains preferable.

entry.title: Towards an Argumentative Foundation for Evaluative AI

author.name: Xiang Yin, Tim Miller, Nico Potyka, Antonio Rago, Francesca Toni

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that computational argumentation should serve as the formal backbone for Evaluative AI, a decision-support paradigm that presents competing hypotheses with supporting and opposing evidence instead of a single recommendation. The authors sketch a research agenda for explainable and contestable, human-centred decision support systems.

entry.title: Who Verifies the Benchmark? Decentralizing Trust in Large Language Model Evaluation

author.name: Sahil Pardasani, Madhusudan Singh

entry.summary: Argues that vendor-reported LLM benchmark results run on an honor system and proposes decentralizing verification of evaluation claims. It also examines identity-aware bias in LLM-as-a-judge setups, where judges score responses partly by the source model rather than answer quality, citing market reactions to unverified capability claims.

entry.title: Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework

author.name: Abhishek Panwar, Maheep Singh, Saksham Bansal

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid architecture that embeds deep recursive latent computation inside a pretrained transformer's semantic representations, aiming to internalize reasoning without emitting long chains of explicit tokens. It targets the observation that tiny recursive models excel at symbolic puzzles but lose natural language coherence.

entry.title: Persuasive and Compliant Tendencies Predict Group Decision-Making in Humans and Language Models

author.name: Wenwen He, Wenke Huang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: The paper introduces a questionnaire framework to measure how persuasive versus compliant language models are, then tests those traits in a Werewolf-style social deduction game with asymmetric information. Stronger persuasion did not improve group outcomes, while compliance-oriented models showed steadier cooperative advantages. Relevant for understanding social dynamics as models increasingly deliberate with humans and each other.

entry.title: StructReward: Efficient Structured Process Rewards for Self-Correcting Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Yifan Li, Ruxin Sun, Tongzhou Zhao

entry.summary: StructReward provides dense step-level rewards for multimodal reasoning RL by representing solutions as structured step sequences and aligning them, avoiding separately trained verifiers, chain-of-thought annotation, or expensive online LLM judging. The goal is process-level supervision at roughly outcome-reward cost. It targets a known bottleneck in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

entry.title: TrustRoboReward: Preference-Ordered Isotonic Score Editing for Multi-Paradigm Robot Reward Models

author.name: Yidong Wang, Yan Zhan, Ziteng Feng, Zhenyu Cui, Ziyi Zhou, Renzhao Liang, Jiaxuan Zhu, Zilei Yang, Yiran Zhao, Zhongkuan Mao, Bo Jia, Hanchu Ni, Chenggang Xie, Biao Liu, Yi Zhang, Yong Dai, Xiaozhu Ju, Wei Ye, Shikun Zhang

entry.summary: TrustRoboReward builds a robot reward model that supports pointwise progress scores, pairwise preferences and video question answering at once, fixing the inconsistency that arises when these supervision types disagree. It uses preference-ordered isotonic editing of scores so pairwise and pointwise signals stay coherent for downstream RLHF or DPO training. Reward models are a stated bottleneck for embodied reinforcement learning, so consistency here matters.

entry.title: Understanding Calibration and Truncation Error Propagation in Training-Free Low-Rank Compression for LLMs

author.name: Mohanad Odema, Gabrielle De Micheli, Dayin Gou, Nilesh Malpeddi, Prathamesh Vaste, Jacob Song

entry.summary: The paper analyzes two overlooked errors in training-free low-rank LLM compression: calibration activation errors compounding layer by layer, so compression-time representations diverge from inference-time ones, and the false assumption that layer importance rankings survive compression. It proposes a simple training-free correction addressing both. Relevant to anyone deploying rank-reduced models without retraining.

entry.title: ForestBench: A Unified Graph Framework for Evaluating Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Guo Chen, Ziwen Li, Reed Li, Yu Lu, Haibo Shi, Bingbing Xu, Junjie Huang

entry.summary: ForestBench converts heterogeneous multi-agent execution traces into a common collaboration-graph representation so different multi-agent methods can be compared under one metric panel, using verified-success reference graphs instead of an LLM judge. This avoids both outcome-only scoring that discards collaboration structure and judge variance. Useful infrastructure for a fragmented subfield.

entry.title: Branch2Skill: Efficient Skill Evolution Through Reasoning Trees

author.name: Yanwei Ren, Haotian Zhang, Likang Xiao, Jiaxing Huang, Jiayan Qiu, Baosheng Yu, Quan Chen, Liu Liu

entry.summary: Branch2Skill extracts dense supervision for skill improvement from a single Monte Carlo tree search reasoning tree, using sibling branches to distinguish genuine skill gaps from early reasoning errors that would otherwise contaminate single-trajectory feedback. This avoids repeated rollout-diagnose-update cycles and their token cost. It is a plausible efficiency win for self-evolving agent skill libraries.

entry.title: DualCert: A Solver for the Traveling Salesman Problem with Constraint-Coupled Learning

author.name: Yancheng Song, Yongzhi Qi, Wei Qi, Zuo-Jun Max Shen

entry.summary: DualCert couples learned guidance for large traveling salesman instances directly to the constraints discovered during search, defining each learned transition on a KKT manifold formed by degree equations and strictly satisfied subtour-elimination constraints. The goal is neural guidance that cannot violate combinatorial feasibility.

entry.title: SafeSceneReason: A Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Connecting Industrial Hazards with Accident Knowledge

author.name: Yuanchi Zhu, Kang An, Tengyue Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Chenxu Du, Xinqi Yang, Hebao Zhu, Bokai Zhao, Tianyu Liang, Ziliang Wang, Faqiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Weiyang Shi, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: SafeSceneReason is a multimodal benchmark and training corpus for industrial safety reasoning that goes beyond detecting workers and protective equipment to assessing compliance, explaining accident mechanisms, and recommending prevention, grounded in occupational accident investigation knowledge. Built from two complementary scene-centric and knowledge-centric pipelines.

entry.title: Emotion2Skill: Model-Internal Emotion Signals for Adaptive Skill Selection and Evolution

author.name: Bohan Lin, Hejia Geng, Xinyi Xie, Heng Zhou, Qinghua Xing, Bo Liu, Chen Zhang, Yudong Zhang

entry.summary: Emotion2Skill extracts internal linear emotion directions from an LLM and uses them as an additional signal for choosing and evolving skills in a skill-based agent, on the premise that these representations causally influence behavior. Moves interpretability findings from post-hoc analysis into agent decision-making.

entry.title: DSLE: A Learning Environment for Dark Souls Boss Encounters

author.name: Derin Gezgin, Jim O'Connor, Tanner Goodwin, Gary B. Parker

entry.summary: DSLE turns all 22 boss encounters of a commercial action game into a containerized Gymnasium-style benchmark with real-time combat, high-dimensional visual input, and sparse terminal rewards, where each step is an actual action against the running game. Defines a five-boss representative subset and evaluates random, expert-system, and evolutionary baselines.

entry.title: Evaluation of Motivational Interviewing Counsellors with Task-Aware Multi-Stage LLM-Based Simulated Clients

author.name: Jiading Zhu, Xinyu Cindy Wang, Thomas Nguyen, Yan Qing Lee, Osnat C. Melamed, Peter Selby, Jonathan Rose

entry.summary: Evoke-Sim builds task-aware simulated clients for evaluating motivational interviewing counsellors in smoking cessation, structured around the evoking stage with a three-phase conversation flow and a reveal policy controlling information disclosure. Aims to align simulator behavior with the therapeutic task rather than generic chat.

entry.title: Open-World Hierarchical Perception: Taxonomic Abstraction over Class-Agnostic Proposals for the Safe Handling of Out-of-Vocabulary Road Objects

author.name: Felix Schaller

entry.summary: Extends hierarchical taxonomic abstraction for autonomous driving perception to the open-world setting by attaching it to class-agnostic region proposals, so out-of-vocabulary road objects can be coarsely classified or flagged rather than mislabeled or dropped. Reports a feasibility study of three open-world signals.

entry.title: CFD-Guided Detection of Concept Drift in Multimodal Physiologic Signals

author.name: Farouk Ganiyu Adewumi, Timothy Oladunni, Rochak Ghimire, Kosisochukwu Ogbuanya, Sanaa Reeves, Sandy Akoy

entry.summary: Proposes a physiologic stability framework that decides whether a cardiovascular model should keep, revise, or flag its prediction by comparing internal model change against measurable signal change across ECG, PPG, and respiration. Evaluated on PTB-XL and synchronized BIDMC and MIMIC waveform cohorts.

entry.title: DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Asaad Althoubi

entry.summary: Formulates KV cache eviction as a sequential decision problem and trains a lightweight policy network with REINFORCE using a per-step KL-divergence reward that penalizes drift from the full-cache output distribution. Positioned against heuristic eviction methods that rely on static attention or positional cues.

entry.title: DeepFreqMark: End-To-End Learnable Frequency-Domain Watermarking with Spherical Attack Simulation for Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Chen-Hsiu Huang, Mario K\"oppen, Ja-Ling Wu

entry.summary: Proposes DeepFreqMark, an end-to-end learnable frequency-domain watermark for latent diffusion images that replaces handcrafted latent-noise patterns with a neural message encoder and decoder. It sidesteps expensive DDIM inversion during training by simulating attacks with spherical linear interpolation in latent space.

entry.title: Don't Scroll Back: Missing-Evidence Memory for Streaming Dialogue Summarization

author.name: Hyangsuk Min, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Formalizes streaming dialogue summarization, where a system must summarize the latest window using a fixed-budget selective memory over unbounded history. Argues the bottleneck is whether memory recovers evidence the current window presupposes, and proposes ReMEMBER plus a benchmark that separately scores evidence recovery and its reflection in the summary.

entry.title: ELBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Education-Facing Large Language Models

author.name: Yilin Jiang, Xiaorong Zhu, Fei Tan, Zicheng Zhang, Kaiyi Huang, Yang Yu, Zexuan Fei, Yiming Luo, Keqian Li, Hao Hao, Aimin Zhou, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: ELBench proposes a combined benchmark that scores education-facing language models on four axes at once: general ability, safety under sensitive prompts, basic instructional usefulness, and higher-level pedagogical cultivation. The argument is that existing evaluations test these properties separately, so no single score reflects whether a model is actually deployable as a tutor or teaching assistant.

entry.title: Modern Backbones Improve Multi-task DETR for Mammography Classification and Lesion Localization

author.name: Dinh Tan Nguyen, Quang-Hien Kha, Le-Hoang Nguyen, Minh-Toan Dinh, Xuan-Huy Nguyen, Dac Phu Ho, Cao Truong Tran, Sai Ho Ling, Lan T Ho-Pham, Liem Pham, Nguyen Quoc Khanh Le

entry.summary: Benchmarks modern vision backbones inside a multi-task detection transformer that jointly predicts exam-level malignancy and localizes lesions in mammograms, across a public cohort and a biopsy-confirmed cohort. Newer backbones such as ConvNeXtV2 and a DINO-style vision encoder clearly beat older residual networks, while a Mamba-based vision backbone lagged.

entry.title: Data-Driven Fire-Zone Segmentation for Improved Short-Term Wildfire Prediction

author.name: Nicolas Caron, Christophe Guyeux, Hassan Noura, Benjamin Aynes

entry.summary: Argues that for short-term wildfire prediction how the map is discretized matters more than which forecasting model is used, replacing uniform grids with unsupervised fire zones derived from historical ignition patterns via watershed detection and clustering.
