Across six French departments and six models, the segmentation approach improved overlap scores by a few points at negligible compute cost.

entry.title: Tracing sources of epistemic uncertainty in deep learning predictions: homo- and hetero-scedastic linearized estimators

author.name: Pierre Nodet, Thomas George

entry.summary: Adapts two classical statistical estimators, in homoscedastic and heteroscedastic variants, to attribute deep-network predictive uncertainty to distinct sources such as noise versus locally scarce data. Scaling relies on recent approximations of the Fisher information matrix.

entry.title: Adaptive KappaSharp: Condition-Number Shaping for Preferential Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Ketong Shao, Jialu Wang, Xuekai Pei, Ali Mesbah

entry.summary: Shows that the standard acquisition strategy in preferential Bayesian optimization creates isolated components in the comparison graph, making the likelihood Hessian structurally rank-deficient regardless of the surrogate model choice. The proposed adaptive method shapes the condition number to fix this without wasting comparison queries.

entry.title: The Neural Division of Labor: Biologically-Inspired Modular Architectures for Robust Neuromorphic Computing

author.name: Maksim Bazhenov, Serafim Grubas, Vakhtang Putkaradze

entry.summary: Proposes a Decomposable Spiking Neural Network that structurally separates classification pathways into independent experts trained with a bio-inspired push-pull loss, avoiding globally entangled weights. It reports parity with dense networks on MNIST-scale and CIFAR benchmarks using roughly ten times fewer parameters while reducing catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Neural Message Passing on Structural Interaction Graphs for Fully-Inductive Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Omer Yom Tov, Avigdor Gal

entry.summary: SIGIL maps any attributed graph into a fixed-dimension representation space by lifting it to a structural interaction graph whose nodes are feature dimensions and whose typed edges encode feature alignment across connectivity orders. This targets the input heterogeneity that blocks fully inductive transfer and graph foundation models.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Agent-Specific Preference

author.name: Ni Mu, Yao Luan, Yiqin Yang, Qing-Shan Jia

entry.summary: MAGPIE replaces hand-designed global rewards in multi-agent RL with per-agent preference models supplied by dedicated experts, and proves that optimizing these decentralized preferences converges to a Nash equilibrium policy. This targets heterogeneous teams where a single scalar objective cannot capture diverse desired behaviors.

entry.title: Efficient Test-Time Scaling for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xuan-May Le, Minh-Tuan Tran, Ling Luo, Uwe Aickelin, Dinh Phung, Trung Le

entry.summary: SCALER makes test-time scaling for language-model time series forecasting cheaper by first predicting a coarse global shape with a lightweight transformer and then having the LLM refine residual tokens in a coarse-to-fine loop. This reduces tokens processed per refinement step while preserving trend and seasonality over long horizons.

entry.title: Real Data Closes Synthetic-to-Real Gap in Optical Chemical Structure Recognition

author.name: Yani Guan, Dengpan Dong, Zi Wei, Shuang Luo, Dan Hannah, Yumin Zhang, Kang Xu

entry.summary: Systematically fine-tunes twenty-one optical chemical structure recognition models to show that a small fraction of real labeled depictions dramatically closes the gap between near-perfect synthetic-render accuracy and very poor real-document performance. The starting vision-language recognizer scores above ninety percent on synthetic renders but below sixteen percent on patent and journal benchmarks.

entry.title: DreOPD: Degraded-Reference Extrapolative On-Policy Distillation for Flow-matching Models

author.name: Mingfeng Lin, Chengfei Cai, Lin Xu, Yuxiang Wei, Liang Han

entry.summary: DreOPD adapts flow-matching image generators to downstream tasks by combining on-policy distillation with reward extrapolation, using deliberately degraded references so the teacher signal points beyond simple imitation. It aims to keep the dense, stable supervision of distillation while capturing the task-specific gains of reinforcement learning.

entry.title: From Objectives to What Models Learn: A Landau Theory of Invariant Learning

author.name: Pinli Wang, Yue He, Peng Cui

entry.summary: Applies a Landau free-energy analysis, borrowed from phase transition physics, to invariant learning objectives, deriving low-order coefficients that act as signatures predicting distinct regularization behaviors. The framework explains phase-boundary shifts, mode elimination, residual feature loading and collapse along the regularization path.

entry.title: When Do Task Vectors Interfere? Mapping the Validity Boundaries of Weight-Space Composition

author.name: Chencheng Zhu, Xiaoyang Li, Taotao Cai

entry.summary: Empirically maps when adding fine-tuning task vectors in weight space produces predictable functional changes, distinguishing parameter geometry from functional geometry using a first-token predictive-distribution interaction ratio. On a 1.5B model, combining code and safety vectors is markedly more non-additive than a matched code and math control, and only on some prompt distributions.

entry.title: Tracking the Best Strategy in an Extensive-Form Game

author.name: Stephen Pasteris, Rahul Savani, Theodore Turocy

entry.summary: Gives an efficient bandit algorithm for repeated extensive-form games against an oblivious adversary that bounds switching regret against comparator sequences of mixed strategies. The bound scales with the number of switches, the depth of information sets traversed and the action count, with low per-trial computational cost.

entry.title: Auditing Medical Vision-Language Models on Chest Radiographs: Estimating Reference Agreement Across Institutions

author.name: Pengyang Yu, Yiou Wang, Zhongping Dong, Sahraoui Dhelim, Chun-Mei Feng, M. Tahar Kechadi

entry.summary: Audits three generative vision-language models on chest radiographs across three institutional corpora and six findings, generating over 345,000 finding-level predictions. The key question is whether agreement with one institution's reference standard can be estimated at a receiving site from a small local label budget, given that these interfaces expose no confidence scores.

entry.title: Preserving Item Semantics for Free: Rethinking Token Initialization in LLM-Based Generative Recommendation

author.name: Donald Loveland, Liam Collins, Bhuvesh Kumar, Danai Koutra, Neil Shah

entry.summary: Shows that adding semantic item IDs to an LLM recommender's vocabulary as randomly initialized Gaussian tokens throws away the continuous geometry those IDs encode, forcing the model to relearn item relationships from interactions. The authors propose geometry-preserving initialization as an essentially free improvement to generative recommendation.

entry.title: MDB-Link: Hierarchical Schema Linking for Multi-Database Text-to-SQL

author.name: Beiyu Xu, Zhenyu Wu, Jiaoyan Chen, Riza theresa Batista-navarro

entry.summary: MDB-Link tackles text-to-SQL when the target database is unknown among many, using global column retrieval, evidence aggregation to shortlist databases, and budget-aware LLM reranking for table and column selection. With a mid-size open model it beats a prior schema-linking baseline on several multi-database benchmarks.

entry.title: DevIntent: How Much Does LLM-Generated Code Violate Developer Intent?

author.name: Susana Haing, Natan Vidra, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: DevIntent introduces an Intent Violation Rate metric and a 49-problem pilot benchmark where implicit constraints are stripped from prompts and encoded as hidden tests. Two frontier models pass over 92 percent of stated tests yet violate unstated developer intent in more than half of problems, revealing a systematic bimodal failure pattern.

entry.title: EgoTrack3D: A Modular Framework for Egocentric 3D Object Tracking

author.name: Jan Kulik, Bjarni Dagur Thor Karason, Yung-Hsu Yang, Boyang Sun, Marc Pollefeys, Xi Wang

entry.summary: EgoTrack3D builds and maintains a dynamic 3D object representation directly from egocentric RGB video by lifting 2D masks into a global frame and associating tracks with point-based motion scoring and voxel merging. It targets rapid viewpoint change and occlusion, which break static-scene assumptions in prior scene-graph methods.

entry.title: Agentic AI-powered flexible fiber-bundle endoscopy for high-resolution NIR-II fluorescence imaging in vivo

author.name: Yanzhao Shi, Yuanhua Liu, Sixin Xu, Wayne Jason Li, Yuyuan Chen, Danyang Xu, Zhisheng Wu, Hanze Yu, Ian Yu-Hong Wong, Simon Ying-Kit Law, Hongjie Dai, Liangqiong Qu, Feifei Wang

entry.summary: Reports an optical-computational co-designed fiber-bundle endoscope for near-infrared-II fluorescence imaging in vivo, pairing ultrathin bundle optimization with AI reconstruction to remove honeycomb artifacts and core crosstalk, plus an agentic control layer. It targets a decades-old resolution limit in flexible clinical endoscopy.

entry.title: VLZip: Unified Visual and Textual Compression for Interleaved Long-Context Modeling

author.name: Yuqi Zhang, Cheng Chen, Yuyu Guo, Wenjie Yang, Lingchen Meng, Peng Di, Hang Yu, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: VLZip compresses both image and text segments of ultra-long interleaved multimodal contexts into layer-specific soft prefixes injected into decoder hidden states, shortening attention sequences without pruning tokens outright. It notably treats textual context compression as equally important as visual token reduction.

entry.title: Beyond Global Editing: Per-Instance Disentangled Subspaces for Training-Free Hallucination Mitigation in LVLMs

author.name: Ali Cheraghian, Hamidreza Dastmalchi, Hamed Barzamini, Morteza Saberi, Mojtaba Golzan, Shafin Rahman, Hossein Rahmani

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free hallucination mitigation method for large vision-language models based on per-instance disentangled subspace edits of internal representations, rather than a single global edit direction. It argues model editing is more stable and cheaper than decoding-time interventions for suppressing text that does not match the image.

entry.title: LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection

author.name: Renshan Zhang, Haoyang Meng, Yixiao He, Rui Shao, April Hua Liu, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: LookAgain makes GUI grounding a closed loop: predicted coordinates are treated as revisable hypotheses that the model reflects on using newly gathered visual evidence, rather than frozen single-shot outputs. It targets known failure modes on small targets, dense control clusters and out-of-distribution interfaces.

entry.title: Perception Before Supervision: Self-Contained Visual Distillation from Counterfactual Blind Spots

author.name: Shravan Venkatraman, Omkar Thawakar, Ritesh Thawkar, Abdelrahman Shaker, Rao Muhammad Anwer

entry.summary: CVPD is a self-contained visual self-distillation method for multimodal LLMs that finds visual blind spots by comparing how zooming into versus removing a region changes the answer distribution, then uses those contrasts as dense token-level supervision. It avoids external annotations, tools or stronger teacher models.

entry.title: JUMP-lite: Compact, reproducible benchmarking of cell representations

author.name: Al\'an F. Mu\~noz, Johan Fredin Haslum, Runxi Shen, Anne E. Carpenter, Shantanu Singh

entry.summary: JUMP-lite is a curated 116 GB subset of the 115 TB JUMP Cell Painting resource, about a thousand times smaller while preserving phenotypic diversity, released alongside an open framework for reproducible model deployment and a benchmark of five cell-representation methods. It aims to make systematic comparison of image-based profiling models feasible for ordinary labs.

entry.title: AdaDexGrasp: Adaptive Dexterous Grasping via 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Fusion

author.name: Xirui Liang, Jiaqi Liang, Jingkai Xu, Yuran Wang, Ruochong Li, Yuanpei Chen, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Wei Zhan, Ruihai Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a dexterous grasping framework that fuses 3D object geometry with per-finger tactile signals into a single representation supporting grasp generation, feasibility prediction, and post-contact refinement. The aim is human-like adaptation after contact, which most vision-only grasping pipelines lack.

entry.title: GWM-VLA: Geometry-Aware Latent World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Learning

author.name: Yanping Zhao, Hang Yu, Yiwei Wang, Chen Ye, Siyu Tian, Di Zhang, Qingjun Wang, Qian Chen, Junqiao Zhao, Chen Ye, Guang Chen

entry.summary: GWM-VLA adds a geometry-aware latent world model to vision-language-action policies, jointly aggregating multi-view observations, predicting target views conditioned on global context, and grounding shared latent actions with robot action supervision. The goal is robustness of manipulation policies under visual and environmental distribution shift.

entry.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing

author.name: Arjun S. Lakshmipathy, Jonathan P. King, Ethan Zuo, Rohit Satishkumar, Hongyi Chen, Jeffrey Ichnowski, Dan Ding, Zackory Erickson, Nancy S. Pollard

entry.summary: Presents a capture and transfer pipeline for contact-rich robot-assisted bathing that uses contact regions as the core processing primitive, and releases a dataset of bathing demonstrations performed by trained clinicians on human subjects. The dataset then informs the design of transfer methods for sustained physical human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Skills in Weights, Memory in Code: Hybrid Learning for Memory-Dependent Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yunhao Zhao, Zhenyang Ni, Haoyang Chen, Ruohan Zhang, Qi Zhu

entry.summary: HyMeS splits memory-dependent manipulation into low-level motor skills learned by gradient-based imitation and high-level memory management acquired by a coding agent that writes and maintains explicit state in code. This lets a Markovian VLA policy handle non-Markovian tasks that require reasoning over long interaction histories.

entry.title: Marginally Useful: Formalizing the Information Gap in Conformal Prediction

author.name: Peter Cotton

entry.summary: Shows that for a single-shape residual predictive system, the log-score regret against the oracle equals the mutual information between the residual and the input, a quantity conformalization cannot reduce because it depends on the predictor shape class rather than calibration. The decomposition formalizes why distribution-free marginal coverage should not be read as evidence of forecast quality.

entry.title: Langevin dynamics along the zero set of real-analytic potentials

author.name: Martin Larsson

entry.summary: Studies Langevin diffusion with a large inverse-temperature parameter for nonnegative real-analytic potentials, deriving a limiting evolution confined to the zero set that is partitioned into strata by the local learning coefficient and its multiplicity. The limiting dynamics are shown to be strongly biased toward more singular, higher-dimensional strata.

entry.title: TelemetrySuffBench: Is Agent Telemetry Sufficient for Failure-Origin Diagnosis?

author.name: Yuxuan Zhu, Peng Pu

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled benchmark that separates whether an agent failure can be detected, whether its origin component can be localized, and whether a model correctly abstains when telemetry is insufficient. Five frontier models are evaluated over masked telemetry views and deliberately ambiguous origin pairs with a frozen blind holdout.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Reward Shaping in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fouad Bahrpeyma

entry.summary: Extends potential-based reward shaping theory to the case where the shaping signal itself changes during training as value estimates improve and novelty decays, which breaks the classical time-invariance assumption behind policy-invariance guarantees. It offers a unified framework for dynamic shaping signals.

entry.title: Fair on the Surface? Benchmarking Hidden-Output Fairness Gaps in LLM Recommenders

author.name: Chan Aristella Lu, Arya Fayyazi, Junhao Zhang, Saeid Shokoufa, Yue Xing, Zhen Xiang, Kyu Hyung Lee, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: FairGap audits LLM recommenders at two levels simultaneously: shifts in visible recommendations and shifts in internal representations under counterfactual identity probes for gender, age and race. Across six open-weight families and three domains the authors find pervasive decoupling, with stable outputs masking substantial hidden representational sensitivity. This argues that output-only fairness audits can be misleading.

entry.title: Forgotten History or Test-of-Time? Retrospect and Prospect on RAG from an IR Perspective

author.name: Xiaoyan Zhao, Yujie Cai, Yang Zhang, Grace Hui Yang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: A position and retrospective paper arguing that the core ideas of retrieval-augmented generation, including retrieval-generation coupling, knowledge augmentation, answer verification and iterative query refinement, were studied in information retrieval and question answering long before large language models. The authors trace this intellectual lineage and propose what current RAG research should reclaim from it. Valuable corrective for a field prone to rediscovery.

entry.title: HoloAegis: Frozen Representation, Topological Inference: Minimally Parametric Safety Manifolds for Zero-Shot LLM Guardrails

author.name: Tak Ho Alex Li, Kaijie Liu, Lik-Hang Lee, Kin Chung Ho, Ping Shum, Michael K. Ng

entry.summary: HoloAegis proposes zero-shot safety classification by doing purely geometric and topological reasoning over frozen encoder embeddings on a unit sphere, with only an anchor count and a temperature as free parameters and no gradient training. The aim is to avoid both representation distortion from fine-tuning and the inference cost of generative judges. It is an unusual, minimally parametric take on guardrail design.

entry.title: VoxZip: Semantic-Anchored Temporal KV Cache Compression for Long-Context Audio Inference

author.name: Wenxu Jia, Dongjie Fu, Xize Cheng, Fangming Feng, Linjun Li, Wenshi Chen, Yingming Li, Zhou Zhao, Tao Jin

entry.summary: VoxZip compresses the KV cache of speech language models during long-context audio inference by using ASR transcriptions as semantic anchors to temporally align, merge and densify audio tokens, requiring no training. Text-centric cache compression tends to break speech continuity or drop acoustic cues, which this design aims to avoid. It targets a real memory bottleneck as audio LLMs handle longer recordings.

entry.title: PluginEval: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained Error Attribution in Function Calling

author.name: Dongjie Xu, Julius, Hanchi Dong, Minghua Tang, Yuxuan Sun, Ziwei Nie, Zicheng Liu, Dujun Qing, Jiajie Xu

entry.summary: PluginEval is a function-calling benchmark designed to fix three structural weaknesses of existing suites: long-tailed scenario coverage, missing adversarial hard negatives, and annotations that rest on unverified LLM judgments. It decomposes tool routing into three decisions and separates candidate generation from deterministic execution-based validation, enabling fine-grained error attribution. Better diagnostics for tool routing failures are needed as agents scale.

entry.title: Deferred Audio Pruning with Local Audio-Visual Dynamics for Omni-LLMs

author.name: Kyeongyoon Lee, Hongyeob Kim, Youngeun Kim, Sungeun Hong

entry.summary: A-PACK compresses omni-modal LLM inputs by deferring audio pruning until query-conditioned interactions have formed inside the model, based on the finding that audio tokens carry higher task-relevant density than video tokens. Video is compressed earlier using local audio-visual dynamics as a selection cue rather than token-wise matching. It reduces prefill and cache cost for long audio-video-text sequences.

entry.title: TRACE: TRajectory Attribution for Automated Context Engineering

author.name: Yikai Zhao, Pradeep Kumar Misra, Saurabh Pandey

entry.summary: TRACE mines historical agent trajectories for implicit dissatisfaction signals such as user corrections, rephrasing, and abandonment, and attributes failures to specific context sources like system prompts, tool descriptions, or knowledge base entries so they can be repaired automatically. Operates on context artifacts rather than model weights.

entry.title: Agentic Router: An Execution-Grounded Continual Learning Approach With Memory

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Rongpeng Li, Zhifeng Zhao, Yuntao Liu, Xing Xu, Honggang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an execution-grounded agent for command-line network operations that generates multiple candidate command sequences, predicts their execution consequences, and reranks by utility and risk, while distilling reusable operational lessons into retrievable memory. Evaluated on SONiC switch configuration tasks.

entry.title: Business Truth, not SQL Accuracy: A Rule-Gated 7B Analytics Agent Outperforms a Direct-Prompted 32B Baseline

author.name: Morris Lee

entry.summary: Introduces WarehouseReliabilityBench, 400 frozen analytics tasks where about half the correct responses are a clarification, abstention, or refusal, plus QueryProof, a 7B agent that uses semantic-layer and catalog rules to decide when a question is answerable. Reports the rule-gated small agent beating a directly prompted 32B model on business-truth correctness.

entry.title: Control-Oriented Scenario Tree Construction through Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fabio Pavirani, Bert Claessens, Pierre Pinson, Chris Develder

entry.summary: Learns how to build scenario trees for multistage stochastic model predictive control based on downstream control performance rather than distributional fidelity, formulating tree construction as sequential assignment of sampled scenarios to leaves via an attention-based policy trained by reinforcement learning. Challenges the assumption that better distribution matching yields better control.

entry.title: JaleesBench: Are AI Assistants Good Spiritual Company?

author.name: M. Waleed Kadous (iaser.ai, Faith Family Technology Network), Benjamin Olsen (Faith Family Technology Network)

entry.summary: JaleesBench evaluates whether AI assistants act as beneficial spiritual companions using 140 two-turn scenarios derived from a classical Islamic virtue compilation, scored by frontier judges against source texts under adversarial pressures and framings. Finds generic frontier models only middling on this criterion.

entry.title: From Evaluated Models to Evaluation Aids: A Multi-Evidence Study of LLM-Based Difficulty Calibration for Programming Examinations

author.name: Hongfei Yan, Jiangkai Xiong, Yiqing Li, Chong Chen

entry.summary: Repositions LLMs from evaluation targets to evidence sources for calibrating programming exam difficulty, correlating model pass rates with student pass rates across a real exam and combining AI evidence with judge logs and teacher interpretation. Reports strong rank correlations between AI-derived difficulty and student performance.

entry.title: An evolutionary model of animats with VLM-based subjective evaluation

author.name: Shota Miyazaki, Takaya Arita, Reiji Suzuki

entry.summary: Uses a vision-language model as a subjective fitness judge in a genetic algorithm evolving virtual soft robots, selecting via pairwise comparisons on aesthetic terms such as adorably or weirdly. Reports that VLM-based subjective selection accelerates population change and co-evolves morphology and locomotion.

entry.title: Enhanced Real-Time 6-DOF Extended Reality Catheter Tracking for Evaluating Potential Improvement in Efficiency, Precision, and Depth Perception for Cardiac Interventions

author.name: Mohsen Annabestani, Sandhya Sriram, Andrew Kuzemczak, S. Chiu Wong, Alexandros Sigaras, Bobak Mosadegh

entry.summary: Presents an extended reality platform combining machine-vision 5-DOF catheter tracking with a 3D-printed encoder for roll, giving full 6-DOF reconstruction inside a patient-specific heart model. A 20-novice study compares immersive 3D guidance against conventional 2D visualization for navigation efficiency and depth perception.

entry.title: Effect of Abstractions and Prompting Strategies on LLM-Guided High-Performance Optimizations

author.name: Ji\v{r}\'i Klepl, Maty'a\v{s} Brabec, Martin Kruli\v{s}

entry.summary: Empirically studies how code abstraction level and prompting strategy affect the quality of LLM-guided high-performance code optimization, comparing this to traditional autotuning over domain-specific representations. Provides guidance on where LLMs actually help in performance engineering workflows.

entry.title: MusicLayout: Explicit Structural Planning for Controllable Text-to-Music Generation

author.name: Shuyu Li, Kejun Zhang, Jiahe Lei, Shulei Ji, Zihao Wang, Jiaxing Yu, Wanying Wu, Lei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MusicLayout, an explicit time-aligned intermediate representation of sections, textures, repetitions, variations, and instrument arrangements that acts as an inspectable planning layer for text-to-music generation. Integrated into a unified autoregressive framework so structure can be edited before audio is produced.

entry.title: When Confidence Fails: Overconfidence in LLMs under Uncertainty and Missing Clinical Information

author.name: Maryam Tahermazandarani, Adnan Mahmood, Fahmida Islam, Quan Z. Sheng

entry.summary: Systematically probes LLM overconfidence on medical multiple-choice questions by injecting linguistic uncertainty cues into prompts and by removing clinical information. Shows models often remain highly confident when answering incorrectly under degraded or hedged inputs.

entry.title: The Announcement Carries the Cue: Markup, Boundaries, and the Notation of Pre-Training Corpora

author.name: E. M. Freeburg

entry.summary: Argues that document notation, meaning how structural boundaries are marked during text extraction, is an unrecorded pre-training variable, and defines clean-window survival to measure how much of a corpus still requires boundary inference. A census of thirteen public corpora shows survival collapsing in PDF-converted vision slices compared with web text, with pre-registered predictions partly failing.

entry.title: When Latents Forget Pixels: Restoring Fidelity in Diffusion Transformer Super-Resolution

author.name: Yu Shi, Yuyao Zhang, Yu-wing Tai

entry.summary: Diagnoses that latent diffusion transformers hallucinate super-resolution detail because VAE compression discards fine spatial evidence from the low-resolution input. The proposed pixel-grounded framework preserves and reuses pre-compression pixel evidence throughout restoration to improve fidelity.

entry.title: MoRSE: Task-Oriented Multi-Agent System with Mixture of Role-Subtask Experts

author.name: Peiwen Li, Shiyang Zhang, Yangtian Zhang, Sizhuang He, David van Dijk, Rex Ying

entry.summary: MoRSE gives LLM multi-agent systems specialization at both the task-structure and parameter levels by conditioning experts on role and subtask pairs, rather than only differentiating agents through prompts. Targets long-horizon complex tasks where prompt-only heterogeneity is insufficient.

entry.title: RAG-Audio: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Faithful Brain-to-Audio Reconstruction

author.name: Ambuj Mehrish, Sebastiano Vascon

entry.summary: RAG-Audio counters prior domination in brain-to-audio reconstruction, where a strong pretrained generator conditioned on weak fMRI signal produces realistic but wrong audio, by retrieving a real audio exemplar and initializing the frozen generator's sampling trajectory from it. Reports large gains in stimulus identification and roughly an order-of-magnitude reduction in Frechet Audio Distance on Brain2Music.

entry.title: Build it, Break it, Repeat: Benchmarking and improving LLM-manipulated disinformation detection in social media posts

author.name: Kevin Thomas, Milosz Kasprzyk, Reuel C Igbokwe Onuigbo, Elliott Pert, Cameron Tovey, Jo\~ao A. Leite, Olesya Razuvayevskaya, Carolina Scarton

entry.summary: Adapts the build-it break-it framework into an iterative adversarial protocol for machine-generated disinformation detection, running five rounds in which posts are deliberately rewritten to evade classifiers. Shows static held-out benchmarks overstate detector robustness under adaptive rewriting.

entry.title: RangeFactory: Scalable Construction of Multi-Hop Cyber Ranges

author.name: Hanlin Jiang, Puyi Wang, Jiandong Jin, Shaofei Li, Zhan Shen, Pengli Wang, Ziming Wang, Yifeng Cai, Ning Jia, Yuxin Ren, Peng Jiang, Yao Guo, Ding Li

entry.summary: RangeFactory automatically orchestrates isolated vulnerability environments into validated multi-hop cyber ranges spanning multiple hosts and network segments, which are needed to study whether LLM agents can sustain full attack chains. Removes the manual specification of vulnerability semantics that limited prior multi-host scenario construction.

entry.title: NeuroRefiner: Morphology-Aware Multi-Agent Refinement for 3D Fluorescence Microscopy Neuron Segmentation

author.name: Haiyang Yan, Jinyue Guo, Yanchao Zhang, Bingqing Wang, Zhenchen Li, Jing Liu, Jiazheng Liu, Linlin Li, Hua Han

entry.summary: NeuroRefiner formalizes the expert workflow for correcting 3D neuron segmentations as a three-agent loop that diagnoses topological errors, writes correction instructions, and validates the result, paired with a segmentation network that consumes those instructions. It targets fragmentation caused by thin elongated neuron morphology in fluorescence microscopy.

entry.title: Confusion-Geometry Rebalancing for Long-Tailed Adversarial Training

author.name: Mengnan Zhao, Geyong Min, Lihe Zhang, Tianhang Zheng, Jie Cui

entry.summary: Addresses the dual imbalance in adversarial training on long-tailed data, where class skew and adversarial inner maximization compound each other. The proposed plug-in method uses periodic robust evaluations to build directed confusion signals and class-wise weights, targeting the specific decision boundaries that drive tail-class collapse.

entry.title: Neural Operators for Immersed-Boundary Soft Swimmers Locomotion

author.name: Mohammad Sadegh Eshaghi, Yizheng Wang, Navid Valizadeh, Xiaoying Zhuang, Timon Rabczuk

entry.summary: Trains neural-operator surrogates for the coupled fluid-structure fields around deforming eel-like swimmers, conditioned on geometry and Reynolds number, replacing expensive immersed-boundary simulation. On held-out high-Reynolds trajectories the planar model reports around 3.5 percent global relative error while jointly predicting velocity, vorticity, and pressure.

entry.title: A Controlled Study of Feature-Based Knowledge Distillation Across Student Designs

author.name: Abhinand Balachandran, Praveen Prashant

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of feature-based knowledge distillation against matched logit distillation across student architectures of varying width and a mobile network, holding teacher, optimizer, schedule, and seed fixed. Logit distillation helped every student, while intermediate-feature alignment methods showed no clean relationship with student size and weaker average effects.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Multimodal Continual Learning

author.name: Jiahong Liu, Ming Shen, Xiaohao Liu, Rex Ying, Menglin Yang, Tat-Seng Chua, Irwin King

entry.summary: Analyzes continual learning of hyperbolic multimodal representations, showing theoretically that avoiding forgetting requires cross-modal invariance under a shared hyperbolic isometry. It further decomposes forgetting into semantic relation drift and hierarchy distortion, motivating methods that preserve both.

entry.title: LAVE: Latent Visual Evidence-Enhanced Planning for Video Tool-use Agents

author.name: Zijian Wang, Junnan Zhu, Rongzhen Li, Xiao Liu, Guohui Xiang, Quan Lu, Lijia Liu, Yining Wang, Jiang Zhong, Kaiwen Wei

entry.summary: LAVE identifies a tool observation bottleneck in video agents: passing tool results back to a planner as text discards computed visual evidence. The training-free framework reuses latent visual representations from completed tool calls to improve long-video understanding.

entry.title: Auditing Instruction-Trajectory Mismatches in Multimodal Robot Demonstrations

author.name: Simon Holk, Ryosuke Takanami, Tatsuya Matsushima, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Yueh-Hua Wu, Kei Ota

entry.summary: Studies a subtle data-quality failure in robot demonstration corpora: trajectories that execute correctly but are paired with the wrong language instruction, corrupting the language-to-behavior mapping learned by vision-language-action policies. The training-free auditing method fuses per-modality task-label estimates with entropy weighting to flag mismatches on LIBERO benchmarks.

entry.title: RotaryQuant: Fitting 120B MoE Models on Consumer Hardware via Fused Compressed-Space Attention

author.name: Anthony. Lui, Mohamed. Elsaied, N. P. Savani

entry.summary: RotaryQuant compresses large mixture-of-experts language models along three axes to run on consumer devices: role-aware mixed-precision weight quantization, LRU disk offloading of experts, and a novel KV cache compression that fuses attention in the compressed space. The stated goal is fitting models up to roughly 120B parameters within consumer memory budgets.

entry.title: LazyHMC: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Simulation for Lazy, Infinite Dimensional Probabilistic Programs

author.name: Maria-Nicoleta Cr\u{a}ciun, C. -H. Luke Ong, Tom Schrijvers, Sam Staton

entry.summary: Extends Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to lazily evaluated, infinite-dimensional probabilistic programs in a functional language, where nonparametric models live over implicit unbounded parameter spaces. A new notion of piecewise analyticity under cylindrical partitions justifies that gradients of the likelihood remain finite-dimensional and computable by automatic differentiation.

entry.title: Clustered Attractor Manifolds and Dynamical Condensation in Self-Attention

author.name: Qucheng Gao, Zuyi Yang, Xiao Chen

entry.summary: Analyzes self-attention as a feedback dynamical system in which token representations set the attention matrix which then updates the representations, identifying an overlap gap as the quantity controlling attractor structure in the high-dimensional limit. When tokens form internally aligned clusters separated by a nonvanishing margin, cross-cluster attention is exponentially suppressed, producing a manifold of clustered fixed points ranging from few macroscopic clusters to extensive fragmentation.

entry.title: Particle-Based Conformal Prediction for Contact-Aware Uncertainty Calibration in Stratified Configuration Spaces

author.name: Lu\'is Marques, Kristian Popov, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: Presents a conformal prediction algorithm that produces statistically valid prediction regions for a robot's future configuration when contact with obstacles changes the effective dimensionality of the configuration space. The particle-based, geometry-aware construction supports planning with calibrated uncertainty in cluttered or contact-rich tasks like assembly insertion.

entry.title: UNMASK: Discovering and Causally Verifying Spurious Shortcuts in Text Classifiers

author.name: Chidaksh Ravuru, Shashank Srivastava

entry.summary: Presents an automated pipeline that discovers candidate surface patterns as executable rules, causally verifies whether a text classifier actually exploits them, and then mitigates the exploited shortcuts, without requiring manual feature vocabularies or human annotation. Closes the gap between dataset-level correlation detection and evidence of model-level shortcut use.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling for CAD Generation via Verifier-Free Consensus Selection

author.name: Aaron Haag, Altay Ka\c{c}an, Bertram Fuchs, Oliver Lohse

entry.summary: Studies test-time scaling for text-to-CAD generation by sampling many parametric CAD programs, compiling them to 3D geometry, and selecting the candidate that best agrees with the rest of the pool. Shows that the candidate pool itself provides enough selection signal to avoid needing a separate vision-language or learned verifier.

entry.title: ELICITED: EHR-grounded Longitudinal Interactive Conversations for Information-seeking Triage Evaluation and Decision-making

author.name: Haohao Zhu, Xiaolin Shi, Jiayu Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for emergency department triage that requires models to interact over multiple turns, identify information gaps, ask focused follow-up questions, and revise acuity assessments as evidence accumulates, grounded in electronic health records. Departs from existing benchmarks that predict acuity from a fixed clinical snapshot.

entry.title: UNSPECIFIC: General Constraint Synthesis for Breaking Copy-and-Paste Shortcut in LLM Instruction Following

author.name: Jeet Sharma, Balpreet Kaur, Jeremiah Hong, Hamed Zamani, Haw-Shiuan Chang

entry.summary: Identifies a loophole in the popular practice of back-translating instructions from reference documents: the constraint synthesizer copies verbatim text, which the evaluated model then satisfies trivially by copying it back. Proposes synthesizing constraints shared between two similar reference articles and selectively hardening only trivially satisfied constraints to produce more meaningful instruction-following data and evaluation.

entry.title: Agentic Visual Reasoning in Whole-Slide Pathology Images via Active Perception

author.name: Jingyun Chen, Fengchun Liu, Linghan Cai, Songhan Jiang, Shenjin Huang, Hongpeng Wang, Lequan Yu, Yongbing Zhang

entry.summary: Frames gigapixel pathology slide reading as sequential decision making, with a navigator trained on pathologist-reviewed abnormality labels choosing where and at what magnification to look, followed by reasoning over the gathered evidence. This avoids both blind dense patch aggregation and heuristic region selection by generic vision-language models.

entry.title: World Tokens: Enhancing Embodied Policies with Training-Time World Modeling

author.name: Qu Tang, Benhui Zhuang, Bo Yuan, Xue Yu, Longteng Guo, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: World Tokens adds a World Adapter that injects world-dynamics modeling into vision-language-action training while dropping future video generation and large video backbones at inference time. The goal is the predictive benefits of world models without their control-loop latency.

entry.title: From Diagnosis to Correction: Benchmarking and Improving Real-World Table Parsing

author.name: Jutao Xiao, Yuan Qu, Dongsheng Ma, Fan Wu, Tianyao He, Weihong Li, Jie Yang, Yu Qiao, Bin Wang, Conghui He

entry.summary: TableParseMap is a diagnostic benchmark of 916 hard real-world tables covering five scenarios and nine failure types, showing that parsers reporting above 93 TEDS on standard suites drop to about 85 here. The authors attribute failures to single-pass scale limits, weak visual cues and visual inconsistency of reconstructions, and propose corrective steps.

entry.title: H\"older Signed Distance: A Differentiable, Signed, Parallelizable Metric for Robotics

author.name: Felipe Bartelt, Ali Umut Kaypak, Anthony Tzes, Farshad Khorrami, Luciano C. A. Pimenta, Vinicius M. Gon\c{c}alves

entry.summary: Introduces a smooth signed distance between convex polyhedra by replacing min and max in the classical signed distance formulation with differentiable Holder-softened analogues, yielding a parallelizable, everywhere-differentiable, sign-preserving metric. This targets gradient-based collision avoidance in real-time planning and control.

entry.title: PEEL: Parallel Extraction for Long-Horizon Disassembly Planning via Scale-Invariant Sampling

author.name: Servet B. Bayraktar, Andreas Orthey, Zachary Kingston, Marc Toussaint

entry.summary: PEEL solves long-horizon multi-part disassembly by combining a scale-invariant sampling scheme, where object scale is estimated in a burn-in phase and exploited by a directional sampler, with a multi-armed-bandit rapidly-exploring random tree for sequencing removal motions. The resulting motions are executed on a real manipulator.

entry.title: Efficient Real-World Online Reinforcement Learning for Robot Manipulation via Centralized Training and Critic Decomposition

author.name: Changhao Li, Yifang Zhang, Heng Zhang, Davide Torielli, Damiano Gasperini, Arturo Laurenzi, Luca Muratore, Arash Ajoudani, Nikos Tsagarakis

entry.summary: Combines centralized training with decentralized execution and a hybrid reward architecture so multiple real-robot actors share a centralized multi-head critic during online reinforcement learning for manipulation. The design targets non-stationarity from concurrent multi-agent training and the narrow randomization ranges that limit prior human-in-the-loop real-world RL.

entry.title: You're Absolutely Right

author.name: Linch

entry.summary: A fictional narrative told through leaked internal chat logs at a thinly disguised frontier lab, depicting researchers rationalizing away anomalous chain-of-thought signals such as untraceable tokens and possible steganography while evaluations look fine. It dramatizes how sycophantic assistants and institutional incentives could combine to suppress early warning signs of misalignment.

entry.title: TREAT: Evaluating Access to Formal Knowledge across Equivalent Mathematical Representations

author.name: Fateme Mazdarani, Carlos Toxtli

entry.summary: Introduces TREAT, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can recognize a known theorem when its conditions are rewritten through equivalence-preserving mathematical transformations such as residual equations rather than textual paraphrase. It probes access to formal knowledge across representational surface forms.

entry.title: Contextual Value Alignment via Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion

author.name: Yuanhong Wu, Djallel Bouneffouf, D. Frank Hsu

entry.summary: Proposes aligning LLMs with plural human values by instantiating multiple moral agents each tuned to a distinct value, then combining their outputs through multilayer score- and rank-based combinatorial fusion. The aim is to capture ethical pluralism that single-reward RLHF pipelines flatten.

entry.title: GRACE: LLM-Grounded Semantic Metric Spaces for Scalable Mixed-Data Clustering

author.name: Zihua Yang, Zhencheng Xie, Junyang Chen, Liang Xie, Yiqun Zhang, Mengke Li, Yang Lu

entry.summary: Uses LLM world knowledge to construct a semantic metric space for clustering mixed numerical and categorical tabular data, addressing the limitation that classical methods can only learn categorical affinities from observed co-occurrence statistics. The design avoids embedding an LLM inside an expensive iterative metric-learning loop.

entry.title: SkillSmith: Enhancing Locally Deployed Agents via Automatic Skill Construction and Evolution

author.name: Xinle Jiang, Remy Xie, Ming Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses that locally deployed small-model agents underperform cloud agents mainly because they lack environment knowledge such as operational rules and procedures, then automatically constructs and evolves skills to supply that knowledge. The motivation is avoiding privacy exposure and repeated API costs of cloud-backed personal assistants.

entry.title: JustLLMGRPO: Radiographic Control for Chest X-Ray Generation

author.name: Pengxiang Cai, Xiaohan Li, Anglin Liu, Qingyuan Zeng, Zexun Li, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: Shows that with the image generator frozen, having an unmodified LLM rewrite chest X-ray report prompts roughly halves a domain-specific FID score by suppressing temporal comparisons and unrenderable content while emphasizing visible findings. Because unconstrained rewriting degrades semantic alignment with the source report, the work adds reinforcement-style constraints to balance fidelity and quality.

entry.title: DialectS2S: End-to-End Speech Dialogue Modeling for Low-Resource Chinese Dialects

author.name: Yi Shu, Tianyu Peng, Yingzhuo Deng, Wen Yang, Jun Lin, Changming Xie, Xinyu Yu, Jiajun Zhang

entry.summary: Builds an end-to-end speech dialogue model for low-resource Chinese dialects, combining a synthetic dialect dialogue data pipeline with a two-stage post-training scheme that keeps speech supervision aligned with the drifting semantic representation space. Addresses degradation in naturalness that occurs during dialect adaptation of speech LLMs.

entry.title: Do Evaluation Metrics Detect Errors in Classical Chinese to English Translations?

author.name: Osvaldo Quinjica, Eric Bennett, Xinchen Yang, Andrew Schonebaum, Marine Carpuat

entry.summary: Uses minimal pairs encoding error types that matter to humanities scholars to probe whether reference-based and reference-free MT metrics detect real errors in Classical Chinese to English translation. Finds every metric has blind spots, with MetricX24 strongest overall.

entry.title: Human-Guided Causal Knowledge Injection for Virtual Cells

author.name: Pengcheng Wang, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, You Wu, Long Wang, Feng Yu, Kenli Li

entry.summary: Proposes a human-in-the-loop method for injecting causal structure into virtual cell models, pairing an automatically induced gene-concept causal graph with a similarity-aware visualization that lets experts correct errors. Aims to improve interpretability of machine-learning simulations of cellular behaviour.

entry.title: Calling the Bluff: Detecting Ever-Shifting Harmful Chat Dialogue via Ordered Reasoning Chain Regularization

author.name: Haojie Yu, Ziyou Jiang, Junjie Wang, Mingyang Li, Yuekai Huang, Jie Huang, Qing Wang

entry.summary: Encodes an ordered reasoning chain over topic, harm indicator, severity and harm type as differentiable supervised stages that regularize a harmful-dialogue classifier, aiming to stay robust when attackers shift harm categories and vocabulary. Evaluated across four domains and five harm categories.

entry.title: Toward CT-Equivalent Image Quality in Low-Dose Radiotherapy Planning: Conditional Diffusion-Based CBCT-to-CT Synthesis and the Impact of CBCT Input Representation

author.name: Alzahra Altalib, Chunhui Li, Christopher Hamill Taylor, Sankar Pillai, Alessandro Perelli

entry.summary: Trains a conditional denoising diffusion model to synthesize CT-quality images from low-dose cone-beam CT for radiotherapy planning, and studies how the choice of CBCT input representation affects synthesis and downstream dose calculation accuracy. Aims to cut cumulative radiation dose from repeated planning scans.

entry.title: KGCaRe: Explainable Complex Conditional Question Answering using Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction and Context Retrieval with LLMs

author.name: Ghanshyam Verma, Simanta Sarkar, Devishree Pillai, Hotaka Shiokawa, Yourong Xu, Fiona Veazey, Peter Hubbert, Hui Su, Paul Buitelaar

entry.summary: KGCaRe answers complex conditional questions by building a knowledge graph from documents with a multi-prompt extraction strategy, storing it in a graph database, and combining symbolic graph reasoning with vector retrieval. The claim is that hybrid structured plus unstructured evidence improves accuracy and explainability over plain retrieval-augmented generation.

entry.title: Instability of LLM Pre-Pretraining: It Doesn't Always Help. An Investigation on Multiple Languages

author.name: Sofiia Riazhskykh, Nam Luu, Ond\v{r}ej Bojar

entry.summary: Attempts to replicate the claim that pretraining on artificial languages before real data improves token efficiency, extending the test to multiple natural languages across four language families, two tokenizers, and several model sizes. Finds the reported gains are highly setup-dependent and relates outcomes to quantified linguistic properties such as morphological richness and dependency tree features.

entry.title: EmoS: A Theory-Grounded Framework for Evaluating and Aligning Emotional Intelligence in Spoken Language Models

author.name: Junyu Wang, Siyuan Zhang, Peiyuan Jiang, Jian Zong, Jingyu Zhang, Tianrui Wang, Yuqin Lin, Zhenghui Chen, Shuqing Xie, Ziyang Ma, Meng Ge, Xiaobao Wang, Longbiao Wang, Jianwu Dang

entry.summary: Introduces an emotional intelligence benchmark for spoken language models organized around a four-branch psychological theory covering perceiving, understanding, using, and managing emotion across ten sub-tasks, plus a specialized evaluator model. Reports that a leading proprietary audio model reaches only about half the score, far below human baselines.

entry.title: Is the ACL Responsible NLP Checklist a Box-Ticking Exercise? A Large-Scale Analysis of EMNLP 2025

author.name: Nusrath Jinnath, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: Curates and releases the full set of responsible research checklist responses and justifications from a major NLP conference plus links from checklist items to paper sections, then analyzes nearly 74,000 responses. Finds that authors tend to isolate ethics answers from the substance of their papers, suggesting compliance-oriented rather than integrated responsible practice.

entry.title: NewtonGS: Physics-Structured Object-Level Neural Newtonian Dynamics for Gaussian Scene Animation

author.name: Lianlei Shan, Feiyang Ye, Yan Chen, Yong Wu

entry.summary: NewtonGS gives each object in a Gaussian splatting scene a compact 22-dimensional physical state covering pose, velocities, scale dynamics, mass, and contact properties, then rolls it forward with a learned Newtonian dynamics model. This enables controllable object-level animation rather than only reconstructing time-varying scenes.

entry.title: BRUCE: Benchmarking Robustness Under Corruption Escalation for Scientific Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: BRUCE stress-tests scientific vision-language reasoning under escalating image corruptions such as blur and low contrast, introducing metrics that quantify how reasoning stability degrades rather than only clean accuracy. It aims to expose fragility that standard benchmarks hide.

entry.title: DINO-3DRA: Leveraging 2D Foundation Model Semantics for 3D Cerebral Aneurysm Segmentation

author.name: Jiayang Lu, Fengming Lin, Alejandro F. Frangi, Ali Sarrami-Foroushani

entry.summary: DINO-3DRA injects frozen 2D DINOv3 features into a 3D U-Net for cerebral aneurysm segmentation in rotational angiography, using spatial mixing and calibrated residual fusion to avoid the discontinuities of naive slice-wise transfer. It reports a substantial Dice improvement over nnU-Net with under six million trainable parameters.

entry.title: SeqLoc: Beyond the Single Frame for Cross-View Geo-Localization in Feature-Sparse Scenes

author.name: Junwei Zheng, Yun Huang, Ruize Dai, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Kunyu Peng, Kailun Yang, Jiaming Zhang, Guangming Wang, Olaf Wysocki, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: SeqLoc addresses cross-view geo-localization failure in feature-sparse rural scenes by aggregating a sequence of panoramas into a recursively updated log-belief volume, with entropy-based tempering and a map-guided recovery mechanism. It also releases CV-FSS, a benchmark of sequential rural panoramas aligned to OpenStreetMap.

entry.title: How Much Does It Cost to Answer My Question? Benchmarking Cloud VLM-based VQA Systems

author.name: Henri Vanhuynegem, Weitao Xu, Yiran Shen, Guohao Lan

entry.summary: This benchmark quantifies how client-side image preprocessing choices affect answer quality, payload size, token cost, and latency when mobile visual question answering offloads to cloud vision-language APIs. It treats preprocessing as the main tunable variable given opaque proprietary serving stacks.

entry.title: SynVAR: Synergizing Spatial and Semantic Alignment in Visual Autoregressive Model

author.name: Zhennan Chen, Tianxing Shi, Pengcheng Xu, Kepan Nan, Qian Wang, Zili Yi, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: SynVAR is a training-free enhancement framework for visual autoregressive generation that targets cross-scale error propagation in the next-scale prediction paradigm. It combines early global guidance for spatial structure with receptive-field and semantic alignment controls to suppress accumulated errors in complex multi-object scenes.

entry.title: LIBAD: A Multimodal Anomaly Detection Benchmark for Li-Ion Battery Electrode Manufacturing

author.name: Wenbo Sui, Daniel Lichau, Harold Phelippeau, Zhao Liu

entry.summary: LIBAD is a multimodal anomaly detection benchmark for lithium-ion battery electrode manufacturing collected from real roll-to-roll production, pairing double-sided visible imaging with high- and low-resolution X-ray radiography. It targets continuous-process manufacturing and weakly correlated modalities where defect evidence may appear in only one channel.

entry.title: ZOMP: Zeroth-Order Multi-Modal Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sajjad Ghiasvand, Yifan Yang, Mahnoosh Alizadeh, Ramtin Pedarsani

entry.summary: ZOMP tunes deep prompts in both the vision and text branches of a frozen CLIP model using simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation, requiring only forward passes. This targets settings such as memory-limited edge devices and closed proprietary APIs where backpropagation is unavailable.

entry.title: Robotic Fabric Alignment System for Sewing Using Global Local Weighted ICP

author.name: Wenbo Dong, Dipankar Bhattacharya Member, Kai Tang, Akinari Kobayashi, Fuyuki Tokuda, Akira Seino, Norman C. Tien, Kazuhiro Kosuge

entry.summary: HarnessWAM wraps world action models in an agentic scaffold where a vision-language-model task manager maintains an evidence-grounded scene belief and a structured task graph, and a capability-conditioned projection constrains open-ended semantic plans to sequences the underlying policy can actually execute. It targets what the authors call the prediction-deliberation gap, where finite-horizon prediction cannot support global planning, verification, and failure recovery.

entry.title: Emotion in an active inference model of human driving

author.name: Julian F. Schumann, Johan Engstr\"om, Ran Wei, Jens Kober, Martijn Wisse, Arkady Zgonnikov

entry.summary: Extends active inference models of human driving to include affective state, representing emotion along valence and arousal axes in continuous rather than discrete state spaces. The goal is a principled cognitive model that captures how emotion shapes traffic decision-making.

entry.title: Towards Researcher Agents for Knowledge-Graph Question Answering

author.name: Tommaso Soru, Abdulsobur Oyewale

entry.summary: Builds a text-to-SPARQL agent that, after each validation round, proposes and tests modifications to its own prompts, rules, and tool-orchestration code. Nine successive self-evolved versions were produced on DBpedia using a cheap reasoning model, with the best configuration then deployed on stronger backbones.

entry.title: Directed Neuro-Symbolic Stochastic Execution for Verification of Distributed Parallel AI Programs

author.name: Gautham Koorma, Vikas Sharma, George Edwards, Mahdi Eslamimehr

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid testing framework for distributed parallel AI programs that couples LLM-guided prediction of concurrency schedules with symbolic constraint solving and coverage-guided stochastic mutation. Correctness is specified in linear temporal logic with proofs of soundness, bounded completeness, and probabilistic completeness.

entry.title: PATH: Next-Interval Prediction via Autoregressive Tree Hierarchy on Tabular Data

author.name: Pengxiang Cai, Wanchen Lian, Chenyang Liu, Xiaohan Li, Qingyuan Zeng, Jinhong Wang, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: Reframes conformal interval prediction as an autoregressive next-interval task, exploiting the observation that prediction intervals have a nested hierarchical geometry naturally represented by binary trees. The method learns how probability mass flows through the tree rather than relying on post-hoc calibration rules applied to an uncertainty surrogate.

entry.title: Metanormative Theory for RL-Based Moral Agents

author.name: Aleks Knoks, Marija Slavkovik

entry.summary: A philosophy-informed analysis arguing that recent reinforcement learning approaches to machine ethics ignore metanormative theory, which handles uncertainty about which moral theory is correct. The authors translate those ideas into criteria for when an RL agent can be called moral and where standard RL architectures fall short. It is conceptual bridge-building between value alignment engineering and normative ethics.

entry.title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses

author.name: Tailin Zhou

entry.summary: This framework makes the executable scaffold around a frozen model, the harness, into a continuously evolving artifact specialized per task family, rewritten from environment feedback by an evolver that is itself rewritten by a meta-evolver. All three levels share one frozen model, so improvement comes from code and workflow evolution rather than weight updates. It probes how far self-improvement can go without training.

entry.title: MedCalc-R1: Knowledge-Guided Reward Framework for Medical Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Haotian Wang, Lian Yan, Xingzhi Yao, Fanshu Meng, Ye He, Jingchi Jiang, Yi Guan

entry.summary: MedCalc-R1 replaces brittle tolerance-based numeric rewards in medical calculation tasks with a knowledge-guided hybrid reward that forces explicit generation of the computational formula, verified externally, combined with soft and hard scoring components. This stabilizes reinforcement learning and improves interpretability for clinical arithmetic. Addresses a real reward-design pain point in verifiable-reward training.

entry.title: UniMoMo: Expert Merging-Based MoE Acceleration for Large Recommendation Models

author.name: Lei Xin, Bin Gu, Peize Li, Zitong Wang, Jianbo Zhao, Changjiang Jiang, Yanyue Xie, Chao Huang, Xuyang Zhao, Zunhai Su, Fanhu Zeng, Zhenglun Kong

entry.summary: UniMoMo compresses a trained sparse mixture-of-experts recommendation model into a smaller standard MoE under an explicit expert budget, formulated as constrained graph coarsening that groups experts by functional similarity measured on unlabeled calibration data rather than parameter distance. A layer-adaptive scheme prevents degradation. It targets deployment cost for large industrial recommenders without extra online modules.

entry.title: SkillReason: Reasoning-Enhanced Agent Skill Retrieval for Implicit User Requests

author.name: Donghong Jiang, Endian Lin, Luoping Cui, Hanqing Liu, Mingjie Liu, Fan Yang, Hong Wang, Zhao Yang, Chuang Zhu

entry.summary: SkillReason tackles retrieval of the right agent skill when user requests are short and leave required capabilities implicit, releasing a benchmark of 3,729 queries against a corpus of over 61,000 skills across nine domains. Its two-stage method uses chain-of-thought reasoning as training-time supervision to bridge terse goals to capability descriptions. Skill retrieval is becoming a bottleneck as skill libraries grow large.

entry.title: AI Evaluation Should Measure Verification Cost, Not Correctness Alone

author.name: Viviana Crescitelli, Generoso Immediato, Fabio Persia, Stefania Costantini

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that AI evaluation should measure the cost of verifying outputs, not just correctness, introducing verification-cost errors defined as wrong outputs that a stated fraction of verifiers fail to catch within a realistic budget. The definition is operational and deployment-relative rather than a property of the text itself. It reframes hallucination measurement around human oversight economics.

entry.title: LLM Reasoning for Subjective Tasks: Failure Modes, Mitigation, and Dynamic Reasoning Routing

author.name: Juncheng Dong, Ding Tong, Ishan Gupta, Yuyan Wang

entry.summary: The first edition of a shared challenge benchmarking whether AI systems can adapt an instructional video to a specified learner persona, an ability education research calls pedagogical content knowledge. Submissions are screened by an LLM judge, ranked by crowd pairwise voting and finalized by an expert panel. Results indicate systems handle subject content well but adapt presentation to the learner poorly.

entry.title: CRUISE: Vision-Language Model-Guided Uncertainty-Aware Cross-Modal Sensor Fusion for Robust Autonomous Driving

author.name: Junyao Wang, Yulin Xu, Yu Li, Pramod Khargonekar, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: CRUISE uses a vision-language model to guide uncertainty-aware fusion of camera, LiDAR, and radar features for autonomous driving, aiming to weight sensors sensibly under adverse weather and out-of-distribution conditions where naive feature-level uncertainty estimates fail. Reports improved robustness in degraded-perception scenarios.

entry.title: OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks

author.name: Siqi Wang, Xinlin Li, Zhenglin Li, Li Li

entry.summary: OpenLoopEvolve represents an agent's observation, planning, memory, verification, recovery, stopping, and budget behaviors as versioned portable policy assets that can be evolved online during a run or offline across traces. Aims to make long-horizon control experience accumulable rather than trapped in a single context.

entry.title: Adaptive Semantic Capacity Allocation for Parallel Generative Recommendation

author.name: Chenxi Li, Yuchen Lu, Xu Yang

entry.summary: Shows that uniformly expanding semantic identifier slots in parallel generative recommenders yields limited gains, indicating redundant capacity, and proposes adaptive allocation of the number of slots and per-slot codebook size according to the heterogeneous demands of different semantic subspaces. Enables longer identifiers without expensive beam-search decoding.

entry.title: WuYuEval: A Multi-Level Benchmark for Large Language Models in Solid Waste Management

author.name: Yi Zhang, Hongyang Wang, Zheng Hao Leong, Zihao Wu, Kaijun Lin, Zhixing Pan, Qixun Huangfu, Wei Ren, Wenyan Wu, Fangyun Wang, Wenting Yu, Hengyu Lin, Muling Yang, Zongguo Wen

entry.summary: WuYuEval is a multi-level benchmark for solid waste management expertise, with roughly 4,590 multiple-choice foundation items and 247 expert scenario questions involving multi-objective optimization and constraint tradeoffs. Targets professional engineering and policy decision competence rather than general knowledge.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Registration of Jawbone CT and Intraoral Scan Data Using GeDi and ICP with Pseudo-IOS Ground Truth

author.name: Sho Mitarai, Hikaru Kayo, Hisashi Ozaki, Yuichiro Imai, Megumi Nakao

entry.summary: Proposes a pseudo intraoral scan evaluation framework where a surface point cloud is synthesized from CT in the same coordinate frame so the true registration transform is known, enabling rigorous accuracy measurement. Uses a coarse-to-fine pipeline combining learned GeDi descriptors with ICP refinement.

entry.title: Defending Retrieval-Augmented Intrusion Detection Against Knowledge Poisoning and Prompt Injection

author.name: Kaysarul Anas Apurba, Md. Hasibul Hasan, Mahedee Zaman Moon, Sk. Md. Mizanur Rahman, Atsuo Inomata

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent retrieval-augmented intrusion detection system hardened against knowledge poisoning and prompt injection in its vector store, using trust scoring, label-embedding consistency checks and prompt sanitization. Reports partial recovery of clean performance up to thirty percent poisoning rates on a standard network intrusion dataset.

entry.title: Can We Optimize the Performance-Carbon Emission Break-Even Point?: The Quest for Greener LLMs

author.name: Sourav Das, Tanmay Joshi, Kripabandhu Ghosh

entry.summary: Folds a calibrated differentiable energy surrogate, fit from on-hardware profiling, into the fine-tuning loss to search for configurations where task accuracy improves at near-zero additional carbon cost during inference. Tests three architecturally distinct small model families.

entry.title: Fourier Self-Supervision for Fine-Grained Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Sarah Rastegar, Mina Ghadimi Atigh, Pascal Mettes, Yuki M. Asano, Cees G. M. Snoek

entry.summary: Adds Fourier-domain self-supervision to generalized category discovery, using low-pass filtering to capture coarse category structure and high-pass filtering to sharpen fine-grained distinctions. Aims to stop contrastive discovery methods from latching onto superficial visual cues.

entry.title: Tabular Numeric Stretch Transformation

author.name: Zihao Ye, Juyong Kim, Johnna Sundberg, Burak Varici, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: Formulates numeric feature preprocessing for tabular deep learning as an optimization that stretches feature distributions to make the target function smoother and easier to learn, with unsupervised minimax and supervised target-aware variants. Positions preprocessing rather than architecture as the underexplored lever.

entry.title: SiriusDeliver: Automating Data Warehouse Delivery at Tencent

author.name: Haining Xie, Xiaokai Zhou, Jiaming Yang, Siqi Shen, Ziwei Wang, Yifeng Zheng, Tengyue Xu, Yipeng Shi, Zefang Zong, Yang Li, Peng Chen, Jie Jiang, Debiao He, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang

entry.summary: SiriusDeliver is a production agent deployed at Tencent that automates enterprise data-warehouse task delivery, covering context retrieval, workflow configuration, code generation, submission, and failure diagnosis. It adds dependency-aware orchestration and lifecycle-aware artifact control that generic coding agents lack.

entry.title: RecoverFly: A Failure-Aware Reinforcement Learning Post-Training Framework for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Boxiong Wang, Hui Kang, Geng Sun, Jiahui Li, Chao Yu, Daxin Tian

entry.summary: RecoverFly post-trains UAV vision-language navigation policies with failure-aware reinforcement learning to add the corrective supervision that behavior cloning cannot provide for closed-loop flight. Targets sample inefficiency, long-tailed scene distributions, and distribution shift during optimization.

entry.title: From Semantic Grounding to Decision Optimization: A Unified Framework for Long-Horizon UAV Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Zeyuan Ma, Jiaxin Chen, Di Huang

entry.summary: A framework for drone vision-language navigation that adds object-level semantic grounding to observations, aggregates long-horizon history with a relevance-weighted temporal module, and stabilizes action choice to escape local traps and repeated exploration. It targets three coupled failure modes in aerial instruction following.

entry.title: LEED: Local Embedding Evolution Distance for over-smoothing estimation and virtual node selection in GNN

author.name: Killian Cressant, Pedro B. Velloso

entry.summary: LEED is a per-node metric that tracks how individual graph node embeddings change layer by layer, giving finer resolution on over-smoothing than global measures such as Dirichlet energy. The metric is then used to pick where to insert virtual nodes to relieve over-squashing.

entry.title: PhysAttNet: Enhancing Predictive Performance in Industrial and Astrophysical Time Series via Physics-Informed Attention

author.name: Amal Saadallah, Julia Tjus, Petra Wiederkeher, Wolfgang Rhode

entry.summary: PhysAttNet adds physics-informed attention to convolutional time-series forecasters so that learned temporal attention aligns with physically meaningful events rather than drifting into unstable patterns. It targets industrial monitoring and astrophysical event detection under noise and measurement uncertainty.

entry.title: CONFER: Conflict-Aware Evidence Negotiation for Regime-Calibrated Weak Supervision in Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Bojing Hou, Ruohao Li, Yitong Zhu, Luwen Yu, Yuyang Wang

entry.summary: CONFER treats multimodal emotion recognition as negotiation among modality experts represented as graph nodes carrying beliefs, uncertainty, and runtime reliability, instead of trusting self-reported labels as ground truth. Message passing weighted by compatibility and reliability resolves cross-modal conflict before a peer-supported prediction readout.

entry.title: From Uncertainty to Failure Attribution: Self-Diagnosing Models for Failure Attribution under Distribution Shift

author.name: Yiyao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces the task of failure attribution under distribution shift, going beyond detecting out-of-distribution inputs to explaining why a prediction is unreliable. The proposed self-diagnosing model jointly outputs a prediction, an uncertainty estimate, and a structured failure-attribution vector distinguishing several unreliability types.

entry.title: Predicting blood clot growth from sparse post-onset measurements with latent neural differential equations

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman, Ying Qian, He Li

entry.summary: Uses latent neural differential equations to infer unmeasurable parameters of a multiphysics blood-clotting model from a few biochemical inputs plus sparse early clot-size measurements, then forecasts thrombus progression. The framework is demonstrated on simulated data from a coagulation-and-diffusion model.

entry.title: Constrained Learning with Universally Learnable Concept Classes

author.name: Herlock SeyedAbolfazl Rahimi, Spyridon Pougkakiotis, Dionysis Kalogerias

entry.summary: Establishes universal PACC learnability, meaning probably approximately correct guarantees on both objective optimality and constraint satisfaction, for dual algorithms over infinite-dimensional nonconvex hypothesis classes. The authors reconcile generalization requirements with strong Lagrangian duality by posing the population problem over a universal reproducing-kernel Hilbert space.

entry.title: No Unique Minimizer, No Problem: On the Consistency of Robust Neural Classifiers

author.name: Subhabrata Majumdar, Anand Deo, Partha Pratim Saha, Abhik Ghosh

entry.summary: Develops a consistency theory for robust neural classifiers trained with S-divergence losses that does not assume parameter identifiability, treating the population minimizer as an equivalence class. Proves empirical minimizers converge to the population solution set under stochastic optimization over non-identifiable parameter spaces.

entry.title: Task-to-Model Optimization for Enterprise LLM Coding Assistants: A Data-Driven Framework for Cost-Optimal Routing

author.name: Srinivasan Manoharan, Junhua Zhao, Fangbo Tu, Haifeng Wu, Jian Wan, Maliah Rajan M, Ashwin Hegde, Mithun Sasidharan, Kalyan Chakravarthi Podamekala

entry.summary: Presents a nine-stage enterprise methodology for routing coding-assistant requests to the cheapest model that meets quality and latency constraints, covering telemetry, task taxonomy discovery, difficulty grading and production-like benchmarking. Argues that naive token-price minimization backfires once retries, escalations and developer waiting time are counted.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient Activation Checkpointing with Sliding Window and Hirschberg's Algorithm for 0/1 Knapsack Solving in PyTorch

author.name: J\k{e}drzej Maczan

entry.summary: Replaces PyTorch's full dynamic programming table for activation checkpointing selection with a sliding-window plus Hirschberg divide-and-conquer solver for the underlying 0/1 knapsack problem. This removes the memory blowup that crashes the default solver at around one hundred items on a 64 GB machine.

entry.title: Math-Vision Diagrams: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Mathematical Diagram Generation Capabilities

author.name: Harish Kashyap, Kiran Byadarhaly, Sriram Chakaravarthy, Sanyukta Tuti, Aryan Mistry

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of paired prompts and reference images specifically for evaluating whether language models can generate mathematically precise diagrams, a capability that requires joint spatial reasoning, mathematical reasoning and rendering. Argues existing math and diagram benchmarks do not cover this intersection.

entry.title: From Approachability Residuals to Anytime-Valid Evidence: The Online Convex Geometry of Testing by Betting

author.name: Jinze Zhao

entry.summary: Establishes an exact pathwise identity linking Blackwell approachability distance to the average of support-function residuals plus online-learning regret, then composes it with betting-based sequential testing. The result is a finite-time transfer where an explicit target gap forces rejection by a given time and non-rejection certifies convergence.

entry.title: ReliableNet: A Chance-Constrained Approach to Trustworthy Classification in Deep Learning

author.name: Ange-Cl\'ement Akazan, Ineza Remy Mugenga, Abebe Geletu, Jean Medard Ngnotchouye, Issa Karambal

entry.summary: ReliableNet reformulates training to directly bound the probability that a model is simultaneously confident and wrong, treating this joint event as the reliability failure that defeats abstention and human review. The authors cast it as chance-constrained empirical risk minimization with a smooth conservative surrogate.

entry.title: RouteGuard: Certifying Routing Gain in LLM Multi-Agent Systems When Complementarity Is Not Enough

author.name: Anchen Sun, Kaiqi Yang

entry.summary: RouteGuard argues that neither gate AUC nor advisor complementarity determines whether routing among LLM advisors actually helps in deployment, decomposing routing gain and governing it by a conditional-regret functional. It supplies a finite-sample certification bracket with a matching lower bound and reports guardrail verdicts on router benchmarks.

entry.title: A Distribution Mapping Approach to Counterfactually Fair Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jianhan Zhang, Jitao Wang, John D. Piette, Donglin Zeng, Chengchun Shi, Zhenke Wu

entry.summary: Develops a data preprocessing algorithm that enables counterfactually fair reinforcement learning by mapping counterfactual states and rewards through quantile distribution matching before policy learning. The motivation is high-stakes sequential decisions in healthcare that could systematically restrict some subpopulations' access to services.

entry.title: Multitask Scanning Probe Microscopy

author.name: Aditya Raghavan, Yu Liu, Ian Mercer, JP Maria, Sergei Kalinin

entry.summary: Demonstrates a closed-loop autonomous microscopy workflow where a multitask Gaussian process learns spatial and cross-modal correlations and chooses both the next location and the next measurement modality. This addresses the practical problem that different probe modalities have very different acquisition costs and damage risks, making exhaustive multimodal mapping infeasible.

entry.title: Did the Grid Erase the Event? EndoClock for Auditing Medical World-Model Pipelines

author.name: Yarin Udi, Tom Sharon-Shahak, Roee Masad, Dan Pri-Tal

entry.summary: Argues that resampling multimodal medical recordings onto a fixed-rate grid can destroy the evidence needed to detect a clinical event when the observation clock itself depends on latent or acquisition state. Contributes a four-regime taxonomy of where the diagnostic witness survives and an auditing tool for medical world-model preprocessing pipelines.

entry.title: Position Bias in Ordinal Classification: A Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Yu Wang, Jeffrey Zhou, Menglin Liu, Ge Shi

entry.summary: Systematically characterizes how label order, demonstration order, and demonstration placement shift LLM predictions on ordinal classification, testing ten frontier models plus eight prompt, task, and model factors across five datasets. Finds all models sensitive to all three positional sources, accuracy and stability frequently misaligned, and only lower rating-scale cardinality reliably improving both.

entry.title: PhysX-CoT: Structured Physical Reasoning from a Single Image to Simulation-Ready 3D Assets

author.name: Jie Huang, Xiaohe Li, Jiahao Li, Fangli Mou, Chen Qian, Yuqiang Fang, Junhao Fan, Kaixin Zhang, Zide Fan

entry.summary: PhysX-CoT turns single-image generation of simulation-ready 3D assets into an explicit, machine-parseable chain of physical reasoning steps covering part decomposition, 2D and 3D grounding, relations and physical properties. Exposing intermediate states allows supervision, conditioning and verification instead of emitting one opaque serialized asset.

entry.title: Stochastic Physics-Informed Neural Networks on Lie Groups for Learning Underwater Vehicle Dynamics

author.name: Evan F. Palmer, Ross L. Hatton, Geoffrey A. Hollinger

entry.summary: Learns stochastic underwater vehicle dynamics with a physics-informed neural network built on Euler-Poincare mechanics and Lie group geometry, using structure-preserving stochastic integration plus moment and finite-dimensional matching for geometrically consistent training. The approach targets marine autonomy tasks where analytic hydrodynamic models are unreliable.

entry.title: Rethink Before You Execute: Adaptive Execution for World Action Models

author.name: Feng Ye, Yiming Zhao, Yong Yu, Hongxu Zhou, Yong Pan, Yuan Xue, Peng Jia, Chuanmin Jia

entry.summary: TempoWAM replaces the fixed action-chunk execution prefix of world action models with an adaptive scheme: a recurrent progress monitor estimates task progress from observations, instruction, remaining actions, and execution history, and an adaptive protocol decides when to re-plan. The premise is that chunk reliability varies by task stage, so replanning should depend on accumulated execution outcomes rather than step counts.

entry.title: The Agentic Clusterfuck

author.name: Chapin Lenthall-Cleary

entry.summary: A forecasting piece arguing that once an open-weight agent can reliably cover its own inference costs while pursuing profit, economic incentives will drive mass proliferation, flooding the internet with automated schemes, scams, and cheap deniable capability for malicious actors. The author assigns roughly a third probability to something like this within a few years.

entry.title: The Field Knows: Cross-Dimensional Geometry from Navigation to Black Holes

author.name: Chenghao Xu

entry.summary: Learns a continuous metric field via a causal contrastive loss that maps scenes into Lie algebra coefficients exponentiated into Riemannian or Lorentzian metrics. The same framework reportedly recovers obstacle-avoiding geodesics in robot navigation and event horizons in black hole spacetimes with zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: QuantumMind: Constraint-Grounded Agentic Reasoning for Speedup Analysis in Quantum Computing

author.name: Yijing Zuo, Zhe Fu, Zihan Nie, Zhihui Zhu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Presents an auditable agentic workflow that generates and conservatively screens claims of quantum speedup, formalizing the task, checking access and output models, matching against a registry of quantum primitives and known barriers, and applying a deterministic ten-check validator. The output is a scoped, source-linked acceleration claim record.

entry.title: STEMMA: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Self-Identity Consistency in LLMs

author.name: Nuthakki Siva Gopala Krishna, Kanishka Jain
