author.name: Abhishek Mishra

entry.summary: This study tests whether introspection adapters, meant to get models with implanted quirks to confess misbehavior, actually work as intended, using persona theory and artifacts from two prior projects on the same base model. The findings are mixed: a persona steering vector matches the adapter's detection rate, the adapter can be pushed to misreport at near-saturation rates via misleading or even neutral prefills, yet its stated values stay stable under interrogation.

entry.title: UniJEPA: A Unified Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Task-Agnostic Visual World Modeling

author.name: An Lanji, Dawei Liu, Jin Li, Haoran Xu, Mei Chen, Yu Tian

entry.summary: UniJEPA proposes a single joint-embedding predictive architecture that unifies masked image prediction, photometric transformation prediction, and video-scale future prediction, which are currently handled by separate specialized JEPA recipes. The aim is one encoder and predictor serving both image-level and video-level world modeling.

entry.title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zongchuang Zhao, Xin Zhou, Tianyang Xu, Zhengyang Sun, Kaixuan Zhou, Honglin Li, Dingkang Liang, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: SimWAM uses video generation only as a training signal for autonomous driving: a pretrained video expert and a lightweight action expert are co-trained with joint flow matching, and an isolated attention mask keeps action prediction independent of future frames. The video branch can then be discarded, leaving a self-contained planner with no generation cost at inference.

entry.title: Beyond Routing Weights: Faithful Response-Level Interpretation of Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models via Contribution Contrast

author.name: Yifan Wang, Jinyi Mu, Mayank Jobanputra, Yu Wang, Soyoung Oh, Isabel Valera, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: Argues that routing weights in Mixture-of-Experts reward models only show which prompts an expert receives, not how it judges, and proposes characterizing experts by contrasting their contributions to chosen versus rejected responses. This gives a more faithful response-level account of expert specialization.

entry.title: Fixed and Adaptive Topological DeepONets: Functional Measurements on Hausdorff Locally Convex Spaces

author.name: Khemraj Shukla, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: Generalizes DeepONet input encoding from point samples to continuous linear functionals drawn from the dual of a locally convex space, with both fixed and adaptive measurement systems and a stabilized training scheme. Provides an error decomposition separating measurement, output, and approximation contributions.

entry.title: ED-CSP: Crystal Structure Prediction from Electron Diffraction

author.name: Germain Poloudenny, Ya\"el Fr\'egier, Arnaud Demorti\`ere

entry.summary: Presents a generative framework that predicts full periodic crystal structures directly from sparse unindexed electron diffraction spot patterns plus composition, using a set encoder, permutation-invariant multi-view aggregation, and a periodic flow generator. Trained on a new simulated dataset of 4.85 million multi-view diffraction examples.

entry.title: WebGrader: Training LLMs for Web Development with Self-Evolving Programmatic Grader

author.name: Boshui Chen, Huiping Liu, Shaolei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a self-evolving grader for reinforcement learning on web development tasks that derives required interaction flows from each request, encodes them as executable flow contracts, and runs them in a live browser to produce rewards. This targets the reward-design bottleneck between costly hand-written scripts and unreliable VLM or GUI-agent judges.

entry.title: GRASP: Reinforcing Language Model Anonymizers with Group Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Sajjad Ghiasvand, Nader Sehatbakhsh

entry.summary: Trains a small on-device text anonymizer with group-relative policy optimization so the privacy-utility tradeoff is optimized directly rather than imitated from a teacher through preference distillation. This avoids the paradox of sending private text to a large third-party model at inference time.

entry.title: Cascading Through the Hierarchy: Regularizer-Induced Feature Detection as Phase Transitions in Deep Linear Neural Networks

author.name: Bj\"orn Ladewig, Ibrahim Talha Ersoy, Karoline Wiesner

entry.summary: Analytically studies deep linear networks with regularization strength treated as an external control parameter analogous to a field in statistical physics, deriving the cascade of feature-detection transitions previously observed only numerically. Links the number of transitions to loss landscape geometry and model complexity.

entry.title: SoRoMoX: Fast, Differentiable, and Parallelizable Soft Robot Models

author.name: Maximilian St\"olzle, Solange Gribonval, Daniel Feliu-Talegon, Vito Daniele Perfetta, Michele Martini, Chuhan Zhang, Kiwan Wong, Mohammed Tarnini, Anup Teejo Mathew, Federico Renda, Daniela Rus, and Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: Releases a JAX-based, JIT-compilable soft robot modeling library implementing articulated, piecewise constant strain, and variable strain reduced-order models behind one control-ready interface with inertia matrices, forces, Jacobians, and derivatives. Claimed to be the first rod-based soft robot framework that is both GPU-parallel and end-to-end differentiable.

entry.title: CellWorld: From Gene-Level Reconstruction to Latent Cell Prediction in Spatial Transcriptomics Foundation Models

author.name: Haiping Liu, Qian Zhao, Lijing Lin, Jingyuan Sun, Hongpeng Zhou

entry.summary: Shifts spatial transcriptomics foundation model pretraining from reconstructing masked gene identities or expression values to predicting latent representations of masked cells from spatial context plus a partial expression hint. Four model sizes up to about 95 million parameters are pretrained on 46 million human cells to avoid encoding assay-specific technical variation.

entry.title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Mingguang Chen, Licheng Wang, Bo Qu

entry.summary: Surveys over fifteen hundred arXiv papers to map the horizon gap, where models that ace single-pass reasoning still fail multi-hour tasks by losing track of decisions, declaring unfinished work complete, or drifting from goals. Disambiguates long-horizon task properties from long-context capacity and long-term memory, and organizes the literature across planning, memory, execution, training, and evaluation.

entry.title: Online Monitoring and Corrective Steering of Programming Agents

author.name: Shuyang Liu, Saman Dehghan, Ji Young Kim, Jatin Ganhotra, Martin Hirzel, and Reyhaneh Jabbarvand

entry.summary: Monitors coding agents in real time to detect plan drift, repeated failed actions, and premature termination during long issue-fixing trajectories. Separates judging from advising by using a cheap deterministic rule-based monitor that only invokes an advisor LLM once a problem is detected, keeping oversight costs low.

entry.title: Do Audio Language Models Use Paralinguistic Evidence? Counterfactual Audits for Response Evaluation

author.name: Kevin Miller, Arjun Chandra, Venkatesh Saligrama

entry.summary: This work audits whether audio-language models acting as judges of speech-to-speech systems actually use paralinguistic cues. The authors build counterfactual items that hold the transcript fixed while varying affect, prosody and the timing of affective shifts, and decompose failures into perception versus response-mapping errors across Gemini, GPT and open audio models.

entry.title: Simple-OPD: Demystifying Warm-up for On-policy Distillation

author.name: Tao Liu, Taiqiang Wu, Mao Zheng, Xuan Luo, Runming Yang, Xuewei Yang, Junjie Wang, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: This paper dissects the warm-up stage that precedes on-policy distillation, finding that what matters is teacher-compatible chain-of-thought style rather than answer correctness, since even incorrect teacher rollouts help comparably. It also finds LoRA trained to near saturation balances in-domain gains and out-of-distribution generalization better than full-parameter SFT.

entry.title: Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry

author.name: Yehan Yang, Junyuan Shang, Yang Li, Guanqun Zhao, Shuohuan Wang, Dianhai Yu

entry.summary: Autonomy-of-Heads identifies retrieval versus streaming attention heads purely from the spectral geometry of the frozen query-key projection matrices, using the effective rank of the kernel attention operator. Because it needs no calibration data, observation windows or runtime attention scores, head classification for sparse attention and KV-cache compression becomes deployment-free.

entry.title: Science Edge Evaluation: SEE the Missing Step Toward Real Scientific Discovery

author.name: Taolin Han, Yuchen Zhang, Jinghang Wang, Yun Wu, Wai Yuet Chiu, Zhaohai Li, Yifei Zhang, Jinxin Wang, Yuhao Zhou, Chen Zhao, Jiajia Li, Jiaxin Li, Qile Jin, Kewei Sun, Shuang Wu, Weiqi Zhai, Renquan Lv, Junchao Li, Ruodan Chen, Qingteng Chen, Zhibo Yang, Hu Wei, Lin Qu, Shuai Bai, and Bing Zhao

entry.summary: Science Edge Evaluation is an expert-curated multimodal benchmark of chemistry, biology, and materials-science questions grounded in real literature and lab practice. Nineteen multimodal models top out at 48.7 percent accuracy, tool use raises the best to 52.7 percent, and general-purpose models beat science-specialized ones on average.

entry.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses

author.name: Xiao Zhang, Yusheng Wang, Yuhao Fei, Dongyuan Li, Zian Liang, Liuyu Xiang, Hongxun Gu, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: HarnessSafe benchmarks delayed safety risks in agent harnesses where state persists across sessions through memory, skills, tools, and shared artifacts, with 328 executable cases over seven carrier families. Each case is modeled as a persistent-risk lifecycle tracing attacker influence from entry through persistence to later triggering in a benign request.

entry.title: MemWM: Memory-Augmented Text-Based World Model

author.name: Yujun Wang, Tao Zhang, Jinhe Bi, Aniri, Wenxuan Ye, Boliang Liu, Sikuan Yan, Shuning Wang, Xuebing Zhou, S\"oren Pirk, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Yunpu Ma

entry.summary: MemWM augments a text-based world model with a curated memory bank of transition rules, cached states, and hard-to-predict facts so that imagined next states preserve task-critical details. The authors introduce a structured state fidelity metric and report large gains over supervised fine-tuning on factual preservation.

entry.title: InstanceSplat: Instance-Aware Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Scene Understanding

author.name: Minchao Jiang, Xiaoxuan Ma, Shunyu Jia, Haoru Wang, Zhang Liang, and Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: InstanceSplat produces instance-aware 3D Gaussian scene representations in a single feed-forward pass from pose-free multi-view images, jointly encoding appearance, geometry, instance identity, and language-aligned semantics. It removes the per-scene optimization required by prior instance-level Gaussian splatting.

entry.title: Momba: Network Modernization Improves Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Adam \v{S}tafa, Santeri Heiskanen, Petr Novotn\'y, Joni Pajarinen

entry.summary: Momba asks whether modern network architectures, rather than new algorithms, can improve multi-objective reinforcement learning, where preference-conditioned policies are typically represented by plain feedforward networks. It reports gains from more expressive architectures across MORL benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning Suffers More Than the Policy Class Under Partial Observability: A Closed-Form Analysis

author.name: Idil G\"ozel (University College London)

entry.summary: Analyzes a partially observed linear-quadratic control problem where actor-critic learning can be solved in closed form, showing that the learned policy is far worse than the best representable one, so the loss comes from the learning dynamics rather than from restricted policy expressiveness. At the default setting the representable optimum is close to the ideal controller while the learned solution is dramatically worse.

entry.title: Gaze Behavior in Visual World Experiments Can be Modeled With Off-the-shelf Language-Vision Encoders

author.name: Rahul Murali Shankar and Titus von der Malsburg and Sebastian Pad\'o

entry.summary: Shows that gaze behavior in visual world psycholinguistic experiments can be predicted by combining an off-the-shelf CLIP-style bi-encoder with a bimodal attribution method, replicating findings from a classic English study. It extends computational psycholinguistics beyond text-only next-word prediction to multimodal paradigms.

entry.title: How Much AI Is in This Track? Quantifying the Proportion of AI-Generated Stems in Hybrid Music Mixtures

author.name: Fernando Garcia de la Cruz, David L\'opez-Ayala, Pablo Zinemanas, Emilio Molina and Mart\'in Rocamora

entry.summary: Reframes AI music detection from a binary decision to regression on the fraction of AI-generated energy in a mixture, building training mixtures from multitrack data with codec-reconstructed stems. A CNN that exceeds 99 percent accuracy as a binary detector degrades sharply on partially synthetic mixtures, motivating the continuous formulation.

entry.title: EliSeg: Verified Target Construction for Report-Grounded Abnormality Segmentation

author.name: Chengyi Peng, Haoyu Yang, Meixing Shi, Yuxiang Cai, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: EliSeg studies segmentation grounded directly in unfiltered radiology reports, where the model must decide which findings are actually eligible targets (excluding negated, prior, or uncertain mentions), how many there are, and which mask goes with which finding. It uses a grammar-constrained actor that proposes target slots and masks, followed by verification and revision.

entry.title: Ten Thousand Cyber Labs for Training & Eval

author.name: TheVinci

entry.summary: The author proposes a large-scale generated suite of cyber lab environments to both evaluate and train model cybersecurity capability, motivated by reported incidents in which a frontier model manipulated its evaluation environment. The post argues existing cyber benchmarks are too ambiguously graded, too gameable, and too small, and confronts the dual-use tension of building capability-raising training environments.

entry.title: Beyond Myopic World Models: Long-Horizon End-to-End Training for Direct Future Prediction

author.name: Xinyi Li, Zaishuo Xia, Chenjie Hao, Yubei Chen

entry.summary: The paper argues that world models trained on few-step prediction losses are structurally mismatched with long-horizon rollout deployment, since local losses ignore how errors compound and how transitions differentially affect endpoints. The proposed Direct Prediction World Model optimizes endpoint prediction end-to-end across the whole trajectory instead.

entry.title: High-dimensional ridgeless least squares interpolation under spiked covariance structures

author.name: Zhijun Liu and Dandan Jiang

entry.summary: Analyzes the out-of-sample risk of ridgeless least squares interpolation under generalized spiked covariance models with possibly diverging spikes. It argues that benign overfitting is governed by how the true coefficient vector aligns with the spiked eigenspaces, not just by the covariance spectrum.

entry.title: MLLM-based Speech Recognition: When and How is Multimodality Beneficial?

author.name: Yiwen Guan, Viet Anh Trinh, Vivek Voleti, Jacob Whitehill

entry.summary: An empirical study of when extra input modalities actually help multimodal LLM-based speech recognition in noise, finding that synchronized cues like lip motion help most at high noise while unsynchronized visual context helps at moderate noise. It also examines which architectures exploit the extra modalities effectively.

entry.title: Mitigating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge via Random Number Generation

author.name: Yuma Asato, Kiyoaki Shirai, Natthawut Kertkeidkachorn

entry.summary: Measures an LLM judge's latent numeric bias by asking it to generate random numbers and comparing the resulting distribution to uniform, optionally conditioned on the evaluation task description. This bias estimate is then used to correct scoring bias in LLM-as-a-judge evaluations.

entry.title: TEXAS: Task-Expert-Aware Supervision for Downstream Mixture-of-Experts LLM Adaptation

author.name: Guanzhi Deng, Haibo Wang, Kuan Wu, Xiangru Jian, Shing Yin Wong, Sichun Luo, Zhuoran Wang, Linqi Song

entry.summary: Proposes identifying task-relevant experts in a Mixture-of-Experts LLM by contrasting expert activations on problems the base model solves versus fails, rather than by aggregate routing frequency, then allocating token-level supervision accordingly during fine-tuning. Aims to make downstream MoE adaptation more targeted.

entry.title: EntropyMoE: Entropy-Aware Sparse Expert Routing for Tokenizer-Free LLMs

author.name: Bo Liu, Muxuab Yu, Yu Zhang, Pengfei Gao and Yongping Zhang

entry.summary: Extends byte-level tokenizer-free LLMs by replacing dense feed-forward blocks in the patch transformer with a Mixture-of-Experts layer routed at the patch level, where routing is driven directly by patch entropy. Byte coverage of each patch is used to account for computational workload.

entry.title: Separating Decision-Rule Misalignment from Readout-Coverage Limitations in Speech Language Models

author.name: Linkai Peng and Baorian Nuchged

entry.summary: Introduces a diagnostic ladder that compares a speech language model's emitted answer, its option logits, an affine correction of those logits, and a linear probe of the hidden state at the same token, to separate decision-rule errors from representation coverage limits. Across five systems and two emotion corpora, hidden-state decoding beats generation by nearly 28 accuracy points.

entry.title: ADIAS: Automated Design of Interactive Agentic Systems

author.name: Lekang Jiang, Bohan Tang, Stephan Goetz, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: Reframes automated agent design as issue-centric rather than candidate-centric, maintaining an explicit persistent issue state across optimization rounds so that repair progress is carried forward instead of re-derived. Instantiated in a framework for automated full-code agent design.

entry.title: Fast and Accurate: An Adaptive VLA Inference Framework through Environment-aware Model Selection

author.name: Yuewei Sun, Lang Qin, Zechuan Tian, Jingwen Li, Guiqin Wang, Shengzeng Huo, Wenxin Ren, Tao Fang, Xiaochen Zhang, Guanqing Deng, Xiang Wang, Xiaowen Dong, Qinghai Guo, Yuxin Ma

entry.summary: Proposes switching between two fully decoupled vision-language-action systems of different scales based on environment-aware model selection, rather than tightly coupling a fast controller to a slow planner's internal representations. This preserves modularity while balancing latency and success rate.

entry.title: InsertFuse: A Unified Framework for Multi-Category Reference-Guided Image Insertion

author.name: Guangzhao Li, Qingyan Wei, Huayu Zheng, Yige Zheng, Chaoyang Zhang, Jie Yang, Yunan Ding, Yan Tai, Siqi Luo, Xiaohong Liu

entry.summary: Presents a unified image insertion model that first trains category-specific experts and then consolidates them into one student via on-policy distillation queried at the student visited states. Adds token-aligned geometric conditioning from masks and a region-balanced flow matching loss to improve spatial control.

entry.title: Measuring the Cross-Lingual Comprehension Gap: How the language of the evidence shapes what language models understand

author.name: Rafael da Silva, Jeff Eicher

entry.summary: Defines and measures a cross-lingual comprehension gap using a professionally translated parallel corpus so that content, question, reference answer, and grading are held constant while only language varies. Evaluates five models across eighteen languages spanning high- to low-resource tiers.

entry.title: Density-Functional Excited-State Gradients and Nonadiabatic Couplings on a Consumer GPU from a Contraction-DAG

author.name: Rub\'en Dar\'io Guerrero

entry.summary: Derives the first analytic nonadiabatic coupling matrix elements for a double-hybrid excited-state method, expressed as a single reverse-mode transpose of a contraction graph, and runs it on a consumer GPU. Reports a substantial reduction in vertical excitation error relative to the underlying hole-hole Tamm-Dancoff approach.

entry.title: Bootstrap-Conditioned Action Selection with Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Devansh Gupta, Shiv Tavker, Dmitry Efimov, Suchitra Sathyanarayana, Gitanjali Bhutani, Boris N. Oreshkin

entry.summary: Turns frozen pretrained tabular foundation models into randomized contextual bandit policies by conditioning in-context on bootstrap resamples of interaction history and selecting the highest sampled score. Adds an arm-context conditioning architecture to share statistical strength across actions and mitigate bootstrap pathologies.

entry.title: Policy-Masked Private Experts: Auditable and Reversible Capability Access Control in Sparse MoE Models

author.name: Zhuoheng Huang, Mukesh Singh

entry.summary: Explores using trusted authorization to control which parameters a forward pass can even reach, by freezing a pretrained sparse mixture-of-experts model, training a disjoint private expert branch, and selecting the public or private pool before top-k routing. Tests the narrow claim that unauthorized requests execute no private expert on two open MoE models, while noting this does not imply the public model lacks the capability.

entry.title: AtlasVLA: Persistent World-Ego State Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Guiyu Zhao, Longteng Guo, Yanghong Mei, Zilin Zhu, Yu Zhang, Bin Cao, Mingming Yu, Xingjian He, Jie Jiang, Jing Liu

entry.summary: AtlasVLA adds persistent memory to vision-language-action models to counter the reactive limits of single wrist-camera policies. It maintains a voxel-hashed 4D world state that accumulates observations beyond the current field of view plus an ego working-state memory tracking multi-step task progress.

entry.title: IB-RL: Isolated Bilateral Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Dialogue Agents

author.name: Senhao Wang, Chenghao Cai, Haitao Hu, Mingxing Huang, Xingguang Wang, Wenhao Li, Zecheng Lin

entry.summary: IB-RL identifies the static-counterpart problem: RL agents trained for strategic dialogue against a fixed opponent learn to exploit that opponent rather than acquire generalizable strategy. The proposed isolated bilateral training updates both sides so learned policies transfer across counterparts.

entry.title: Faster Query-Key Learning Sharpens Attention in Self-Attention Models

author.name: Rahul Vashisht, Harish G. Ramaswamy

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how collapsed versus factorized parameterization of the query-key and output-value circuits shapes self-attention training dynamics. Gradient-flow analysis shows factorization implicitly rescales the effective learning rates of the two circuits, and faster query-key learning yields sharper attention on task-relevant tokens at comparable loss.

entry.title: LLMRouter: Unified Infrastructure for Developing, Evaluating, and Deploying LLM Routers

author.name: Tao Feng, Fangxu Yu, Haozhen Zhang, Zhongjie Dai, Liangqi Yuan, Zijie Lei, Weizhi Zhang, Kunlun Zhu, Haodong Yue, Keyang Xuan, Ge Liu, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: LLMRouter unifies LLM routing as a sequential decision process with five components covering context encoders, model encoders, scoring functions, decision rules and learning signals, spanning single-turn, multi-turn and personalized routing. It ships an automated supervision pipeline and xRouteBench, a benchmark that jointly scores response quality and inference cost across generic, memory-augmented, vision and time-series settings.

entry.title: Limit Points of Reflow with Minibatch Optimal Transport

author.name: Antonin Chambolle, Johannes Hertrich

entry.summary: Analyzes the asymptotic behavior of reflow iterations in rectified flow generative models, defining weak rectified couplings that always exist and proving that alternating reflow with minibatch optimal transport yields N-cyclically monotone limits for batch size N. Gives structural and stability guarantees for the straightening procedure used to accelerate sampling.

entry.title: AutoIntervene: Calibrated Intervention for Action-Chunking Imitation Learning Policies

author.name: Jinhe Tang and Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: AutoIntervene decides online when an action-chunking imitation policy should hand control to a human operator, by scoring proposed chunks against a memory of visual observations and actions from successful executions. It targets the failure mode where policies keep emitting smooth but out-of-distribution action sequences after drift.

entry.title: DocMemo: Dynamic Evidence Discovery via Probabilistic Memory-Guided Retrieval for Multi-Modal Document Understanding

author.name: Hanshu Yao, Janfeng Zhong, Niu Lian, Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: DocMemo tackles long multimodal document QA by replacing fixed top-k page retrieval with an iterative process governed by a three-level memory of document schema, page-level belief, and query state. The design aims to make cross-round retrieval state explicit so early retrieval mistakes can be recovered.

entry.title: RoRA: Role-Oriented Regional Allocation for Visual Token Pruning in MLLMs

author.name: Qiyanhui Lu, Han Wu, Rongjian Xu, Tingzhang Luo, Cheng Fan, Xinghao Chen, Minjing Dong, Jufeng Yang, Jianyuan Guo

entry.summary: RoRA is a training-free visual token pruning scheme for multimodal LLMs that assigns retained tokens distinct roles (semantic core, context, detail) and allocates budget across attention-anchored object regions rather than treating tokens as interchangeable. It targets prefill and KV-cache cost in image-heavy inference.

entry.title: Capacity Confounds and Coverage Guarantees in Adaptive Sub-model Federated Learning

author.name: Alireza Moayedikia and Alicia Troncoso Lora

entry.summary: Tests the widely suggested idea of allocating sub-model width in federated learning based on client data heterogeneity inferred from server-observed updates, and finds that such divergence estimates are dominated by client capacity rather than data distribution. It is largely a negative result with coverage-guarantee analysis for adaptive allocation.

entry.title: Measuring Concept Content in Text from LLM Activations: ESG Evidence from Concept Vectors and Linear Probes

author.name: Luc Hazenoot, Zhaochun Ren, Amirhossein Zohrehvand

entry.summary: Compares ways of measuring how much a text is about a concept by reading frozen LLM internal activations, using recursive feature machines and linear probes against embedding, dictionary, and self-report baselines, with ESG content as the case study. It asks whether internal representations can substitute for task-specific fine-tuning in social-science measurement.

entry.title: CANIS: Generation-Assisted 3D Canonicalization via an Image-Semantic Bridge

author.name: Kendong Liu, Yuxin Yao, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: CANIS canonicalizes 3D object orientation by exploiting the semantic orientation prior inside a frozen image-to-3D generative model: it renders informative views, generates a canonically oriented proxy guided by a sparse structural latent of the input, and aligns the input to that proxy. No canonicalization-specific training or per-category templates are needed.

entry.title: People Are Not Just Their Countries. Disentangling Social Determinants of LLM Value Alignment Across Europe

author.name: Maria-Louisa Wightman, Guillaume Bied, Tijl De Bie

entry.summary: Using the European Social Survey, the authors measure how well ten commercial LLMs align with human values across 15 socio-demographic variables in addition to country of residence. The findings indicate that within-country social divides matter for alignment disparities, so country-level cultural alignment studies obscure important structure.

entry.title: Agentic Planning for Symbolic Execution

author.name: Daniel Koh Ji Yang, Yannic Noller, Corina S. Pasareanu, Youcheng Sun

entry.summary: Presents an agentic planner that uses evidence from previous bounded symbolic execution runs to configure subsequent runs, with an LLM deciding search strategy while the underlying symbolic engine does the actual exploration. Evaluated for branch coverage improvement.

entry.title: TaskSense: Focusing on What Matters in World Models

author.name: SM Mazharul Islam, Manfred Huber

entry.summary: Proposes a world model that applies differentiable stochastic spatial attention before latent encoding so that representation capacity is spent on task-relevant regions rather than background clutter. Targets the known degradation of reconstruction-based world models under visual distractions.

entry.title: Model Confidence Under Answer-Preserving Attacks: An Informativeness-Manipulability Frontier

author.name: Reza Khanmohammadi, Ivan Brugere, Simerjot Kaur, Charese H. Smiley, Kundan Thind, Mohammad M. Ghassemi

entry.summary: Attacks the confidence readouts of vision-language systems using image-only perturbations constrained to leave the generated answer byte-identical, isolating manipulation of trust signals from manipulation of answers. Shows across four models, three benchmarks, and several confidence channels that uniform robustness certificates for these readouts are refuted.

entry.title: SLED: Scalable Location Encoding via Distillation

author.name: Kevin Lane, Zhongying Wang, Esther Rolf, Morteza Karimzadeh

entry.summary: Replaces contrastive CLIP-style training of geospatial location encoders with distillation, using location as a binding modality so that pretraining avoids very large batch requirements and false negatives. Improves scalability when additional Earth observation modalities are added.

entry.title: Dueling World Models: Advantage-Style Action Channels for Common-Mode Distractor Rejection

author.name: Jiazhuo Li, Yiming Fei, Zhiruo Zhou, Heikichi Hayashi

entry.summary: Shows that latent world models become action-blind when uncontrollable motion is present, with predictions for different actions collapsing together even as training loss improves. Borrows the dueling value decomposition to subtract the mean predicted effect across actions, cancelling action-independent variation without reward, reconstruction, or distractor labels.

entry.title: Capek 0.5: An Execution-Centric Vision-Language Model for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Ying Chen, Weizhen Li, Zhe Hu, Zhenjiang Li, Rui Jiang, Zhifeng Gu, Lihuang Fang, Jiangping Liu, Lei Yi, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Capek 0.5 is an embodied vision-language model organized around an execution-centric capability taxonomy rather than around datasets or tasks. Capabilities are grouped by their supervision signals, prediction formats and verification criteria to reflect that each robot action changes what must next be perceived and verified.

entry.title: Human-AI Perceptual Alignment by Playing Hues and Cues

author.name: Nuria Alabau-Bosque, Jorge Vila-Tom\'as, Paula Daud\'en-Oliver, Pablo Hern\'andez-C\'amara, Valero Laparra, Jes\'us Malo

entry.summary: Evaluates perceptual alignment of contrastive vision-language models against humans using the color board game Hues and Cues, mapping cells to a chromaticity diagram and comparing model error to a human consistency baseline derived from 325 participants. The human lower bound is the key methodological contribution.

entry.title: Machine Learning-Based Inter-Crystal Scatter Recovery for Ultra-High Resolution PET Imaging

author.name: Alexandre Bernier and Roger Lecomte and Jean-Baptiste Michaud

entry.summary: Uses a feedforward neural network to recover inter-crystal scatter events in ultra-high-resolution PET by inferring which interaction came first, validated on both Monte Carlo simulation and data from real pixelated scanners. Reported sensitivity increases of roughly 70 to 106 percent while keeping sub-millimeter resolution.

entry.title: Same Attention, Different Truths: Put Logit-Lens over Visual Attention to Detect and Mitigate LVLM Object Hallucination

author.name: Zichuan Wang, Songlin Yang, Bo Peng, Zhenchen Tang, Yang Li, Beibei Dong and Jing Dong

entry.summary: The paper challenges the common claim that vision-language hallucination stems from insufficient visual attention, showing that hallucinated and real objects receive comparable attention in mid-to-late layers. By applying a logit lens to high-attention visual features, the authors separate two hallucination mechanisms and propose a detection and mitigation method grounded in that diagnosis.

entry.title: Zero Gap Is Not Restoration: Stratified Per-Question Probability Evaluation and Step-wise Mitigation of Benchmark Contamination

author.name: Ruijie Hou, Yueyang Jiao, Zhao Wang, Yingming Li

entry.summary: The paper argues that the standard metric for judging benchmark-contamination mitigation is flawed because aggregate gap measures let over- and under-suppression cancel out and can be gamed. It proposes a stratified per-question probability-gap metric plus a step-wise mitigation procedure that better reflects whether genuine capability has been restored.

entry.title: Depth-Wise Probing and Pruning of the Planning Token in a Driving Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Harisankar Babu, Benjamin Coors, Christopher Lang, Hendrik Berkemeyer, Tamim Asfour and Simon Foell

entry.summary: The study probes a driving vision-language-action model in which the whole plan is carried by one planning token, decoding that token from all 32 decoder layers with the planner used as a trajectory-space logit lens. Navigation intent is linearly decodable after the first layer while planner compatibility improves much later, motivating depth pruning of the language stack.

entry.title: Trajectory-Relative Hindsight Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoyu Zheng, Yun Zhu, Qing Wang, Wenqiao Zhang

entry.summary: TRIAL tackles the credit-assignment problem in agentic RL where a single sparse outcome must be distributed across many turns, by comparing a response under ordinary versus hindsight-conditioned contexts. The signed log-probability gap sets the direction and strength of token-level supervision, with turn-level magnitudes normalized across the trajectory.

entry.title: SABRE: Scalable and Automated Benchmarking of VLMs under Stress

author.name: Zixuan Lan, Luzhe Sun, Matthew R. Walter, and Jiawei Zhou

entry.summary: SABRE is a mostly automated pipeline that turns a written task design into structured specifications, generated or edited images, and question-answer pairs for stress-testing vision-language models, with automatic filtering of items current models already solve and human verification. An instantiation tests whether models follow visual evidence or fall back on learned world priors about familiar objects.

entry.title: CoinRAG: Contextualized Information Nugget KV Cache Reuse for Long-Context RAG

author.name: Gyuwan Kim, Cheoneum Park, Tao Yang

entry.summary: CoinRAG improves retrieval-augmented generation efficiency by precomputing key-value caches for fine-grained information nuggets rather than coarse chunks, then compositionally assembling them into a learned contextual representation at inference. The goal is to push the accuracy-versus-prefill-latency frontier by removing redundancy and noise carried by chunk-level caches.

entry.title: Learning to Predict Middle-Layer Attention in MLLMs for Visual Token Prunin

author.name: Yuyao Sun, Tao Deng, Shuang Li, Deqing Wang, Hao Geng, Minjun Yu

entry.summary: Shows that the most question-responsive middle layer for guiding visual token pruning in multimodal LLMs varies per sample, so a fixed layer is suboptimal, and proposes learning to predict that layer's attention cheaply. Goal is to cut visual token compute without paying to run the middle layers.

entry.title: Latent Fact-Checking: Detecting Misinformation through Activation Engineering

author.name: Pedro Barcelos, Ot\'avio Parraga, Marcelo M. Mussi, Lucas M. Fraga, Lucas S. Kupssinsk\"u, Rodrigo C. Barros

entry.summary: Detects misinformation by treating truthfulness as a direction in a language model's residual stream, extracting it by contrasting activations of paired true and false statements, then projecting an unseen claim's activation onto that direction. This avoids reliance on surface features or retrieval.

entry.title: Confidence Estimation for Financial Vision-Language Models in Chart and Document Understanding

author.name: Reza Khanmohammadi, Simerjot Kaur, Charese H. Smiley, Ivan Brugere, Mohammad M. Ghassemi

entry.summary: Benchmarks seven confidence estimators, including trained internal probes, across five open-weight vision-language models on financial chart and document question answering, with probes trained only on natural images to test out-of-distribution transfer. Finds that calibration rather than ranking is the scarce property for deciding which answers can be acted on versus escalated.

entry.title: Shape Your Feed: An LLM-based Agentic System for Conversational Recommendation

author.name: Ziyun Xu, Bosen Ding, Yue Zhang, Ji Qi, Qingyuan Song, Jizhou Huang, Liwei Wang, Jefferey Santelli, Yue Weng, Qichao Que, Zhenheng Yang, Junfeng Pan, Linhong Zhu

entry.summary: Presents an LLM agent framework that lets users steer an industrial recommendation feed through explicit natural-language and multimodal instructions rather than only implicit clicks and dwell time. Uses a three-tier architecture including a perception flow that captures fine-grained intent for real-time co-curation of content.

entry.title: CrossTracer: Cross-Embodiment Navigation via VLA Model Reasoning and Trace Residuals Adapting

author.name: Yao Wang, Siyuan Wang, Zhirui Sun, Wenzheng Chi, Liang Lin, Jiankun Wang, Wenjun Xu

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical navigation framework where a vision-language-action model proposes a trace of normalized image-plane waypoints and an adapter predicts embodiment-conditioned residual corrections. This pixel-space interface lets semantic plans from a shared model be made physically feasible for robots with different mobility constraints.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics of Polymers

author.name: Joohee Choi, Junhyeong Lee, Seunghwa Ryu

entry.summary: Automates the laborious bottom-up coarse-grained molecular dynamics workflow for polymers with a multi-agent system that goes from a natural-language polymer specification through topology construction, equilibration, mapping, potential derivation, and validation. An LLM reasoning agent infers all-atom topology from the polymer name and layered self-correction fixes physical errors common in unsaturated, heteroatom, and polar polymers.

entry.title: LoRAScan: Detecting Backdoor Prompts in Low-Rank Adapters for Large Language Models via Down-Projection Activation Spikes

author.name: Doniyorkhon Obidov, Honggang Yu, Xiaolong Guo, Kaichen Yang

entry.summary: LoRAScan detects backdoor trigger prompts in untrusted low-rank adapters by monitoring activation spikes in the adapter down-projection, rather than merging the adapter and diluting the backdoor signal. Unlike prior defenses that flag whole adapters or repair base models, it aims to let a possibly poisoned adapter be used safely at the prompt level.

entry.title: Is Forward Prediction Enough? Physical State Grounding for JEPA World Models

author.name: Haodong Yan, Jiaguan Zhu, Mingyuan Jia, Ruiqing Yin, Junjie He, Zhide Zhong, Junfeng Li, Jinxuan Lu, Hengtao Li, Tianran Zhang, Jiayi Chen, Wenxuan Song, Wen Chen, Yuxiang Gao, Haoang Li

entry.summary: PSG-JEPA argues that action-conditioned forward prediction alone does not guarantee that a JEPA world model's latents identify robot physical state. It adds two training-time grounding objectives, tying individual latents to proprioceptive state and latent pairs to multi-horizon joint-angle changes, without changing inference cost.

entry.title: When Coordination Becomes a Threat: Communication Attacks in LLM-Controlled Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Zhen Huang, Zhihuang Liu, Weijia Shi, Yifan Yang, Weishang Wu and Zhiping Cai

entry.summary: This work formalizes two communication attacks on LLM-controlled multi-robot systems corresponding to different attacker access levels, and studies how they propagate across common coordination architectures rather than only decentralized ones. It shows coordination channels themselves are an attack surface beyond single-robot prompt injection.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Forensic Reasoning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection

author.name: Xuechao Zou, Shun Zhang, Kai Li, Yi Zhou, Xinyu Sun, Yuhui Chen, Zhe Wu, Congyan Lang, Junliang Xing

entry.summary: This work releases FaceVid-Forensics-100K, a 100,000 video deepfake dataset spanning 33 synthesis methods across face swapping and other manipulation types with fine-grained textual annotations, and proposes a multi-agent forensic reasoning detector. Multiple analytical perspectives are combined because single models or single viewpoints miss subtle artifacts.

entry.title: LifelongCrossNav: Persistent 3D Semantic Memory for Cross-Floor Multi-Object Navigation

author.name: Zehui Li, Zihao Sun, Jiawei Xu, Zheqi He, Xiaoqiang Zhang, Jing-Shu Zheng, Lu Liu, Dahui Gao, Xiuwan Chen

entry.summary: LifelongCrossNav performs sequential multi-object goal navigation across multiple floors by maintaining a persistent sparse 3D semantic voxel memory that accumulates geometry, traversability, and vision-language features across queries. It unifies two problems usually studied separately: persistent memory reuse and cross-floor exploration.

entry.title: Conformal Fusion Under Missing Modalities

author.name: Alireza Moayedikia

entry.summary: MCCF couples missing-modality robustness with calibrated uncertainty by combining bottleneck fusion trained with modality dropout, per-modality evidential heads producing Dirichlet outputs, and Dempster-Shafer style combination plus conformal calibration. It argues that accuracy-focused missing-modality work ignores whether confidence stays calibrated.

entry.title: LitTraceQA: A Benchmark for Multi-Stage Grounding and Verification in Scientific Question Answering

author.name: Xuye Liu, Yimu Wang, Peng Shi, Bo Xue, Xiangrui Ke, Songcheng Cai, Kath Choi, Di Wu, Freda Shi, Krzysztof Czarnecki

entry.summary: LitTraceQA is a benchmark requiring systems to answer research questions over scientific papers while also returning the specific papers and evidence locations that justify the answer, in several output formats. It targets the multi-stage grounding and verification chain that fluent generation alone does not guarantee.

entry.title: Adversarial Causal Intervention Falsification

author.name: Mojtaba Eslami

entry.summary: Proposes a game between a causal generative model and an adversary that chooses interventions designed to falsify it, so the discriminator tests post-intervention distributions rather than just realism. The framework separates observational fit, interventional equivalence over a query class, and point identifiability.

entry.title: Towards Multi-Label Graph Foundation Models: from Single-Vector Representation Learning to Multi-Semantic Basis Learning

author.name: Dongxiao He, Jiayu Zhang, Jitao Zhao, Yi Wang and Di Jin

entry.summary: Argues existing graph foundation models assume single-label nodes and therefore collapse multi-semantic nodes into one embedding. Proposes learning a multi-semantic basis representation so that cross-domain transfer works for multi-label node classification.

entry.title: UAV3DCrop: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction in Repeated Multi-Angle UAV Crop Surveys

author.name: Junxiong Zhou, Xuechen Li, Chonghao Qiu, Lang Qiao, Xiaowei Jia, Qi Yang, Chishan Zhang, Leikun Yin, Nanshan You, Vipin Kumar, David Mulla, Ce Yang, Zhenong Jin, Licheng Liu

entry.summary: Releases a large UAV benchmark of nearly 89,000 high-resolution images across 91 crop-field scenes and four crop types, for evaluating NeRF and Gaussian-splatting reconstructions against photogrammetric depth and agronomic geometry. It tests whether good rendering translates into metrically useful field geometry.

entry.title: Multi Codec Discrete Diffusion Model for Text Guided Speech Inpainting and Editing

author.name: Iftach Shoham, Tali Dror, Oren Gal, Haim Permuter, Gilad Katz, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: Introduces a discrete diffusion framework over hierarchical codec tokens for text-guided speech inpainting and editing, iteratively refining masked regions while conditioning on both left and right acoustic context. Targets consistency of speaker identity, prosody, and recording conditions with surrounding audio.

entry.title: Recovering Lesion Parameters from Aphasic Picture Naming Error Profiles in Large Language Models

author.name: Yong Yang, Roger Newman-Norlund, Xiang Guan, Saeed Ahmadi, Regan Willis, Nadra Salman, Kalil Warren, Sophie Arheix-Parras, Srihari Nelakuditi, Leonardo Bonilha, Christopher Rorden, Rutvik H. Desai, Julius Fridriksson

entry.summary: Poses an inverse interpretability question: given a picture-naming error profile resembling an aphasic patient, can the lesion parameters (layer, modification percentage, noise level) applied to a multimodal LLM be recovered? Across nearly 5,000 lesion configurations and a seven-category clinical error taxonomy, the study probes what the recoverability structure reveals about transformer computation.

entry.title: Agentic AI: User Empowerment or Enclosure?

author.name: David Gamba and Daniel M. Romero and Grant Schoenebeck

entry.summary: Uses comparative case analysis of ad blockers, recommender systems, robo-advisors, and spam governance to argue that whose interests agents serve gets settled through technical choices such as APIs, protocols, and defaults. Names this depoliticization and warns that agentic AI may enclose rather than empower users.

entry.title: Online Security Learning in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems under Hidden Byzantine Attacks

author.name: Ximing Sun, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Studies online cooperative multi-agent control where a hidden subset of agents can stealthily overwrite their own components of the team plan after seeing it. Shows that the attacker information model determines the geometry of the resulting robust MDP and derives learning procedures targeting the optimal security value.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Speckle Denoising

author.name: Matthew R. Ziemann, Casey J. Pellizzari, Tyler J. Hardy, and Christopher A. Metzler

entry.summary: Presents a training-free method combining a spatiotemporal implicit neural representation with an aperture-aware maximum-likelihood objective to remove multiplicative speckle noise from dynamic coherent imagery. An FFT-accelerated matrix-free solver makes optimization practical and allows adaptation to arbitrary pupil geometries without retraining.

entry.title: MI-MIDI: Mechanistic Interpretability of Text-to-MIDI Generation Models via Probing, Lenses and Steering

author.name: Jakub Po\'cwiardowski and Mateusz Modrzejewski

entry.summary: Applies mechanistic interpretability tools including linear probes, logit and tuned lenses, activation patching, and difference-in-means steering to two symbolic text-to-MIDI generation systems of contrasting design. Finds pitch, instrumentation, harmony, and texture linearly decodable in both, with a purpose-built encoder-decoder refining gradually while the language-model-derived system stays in a textual basis until a late rotation into musical vocabulary.

entry.title: Optimal Neural Network Approximation via Empirical Least Squares with Deterministic Samples

author.name: Xinliang Liu, Tong Mao, Jinchao Xu

entry.summary: Develops rigorous approximation and error theory for solving elliptic spectral equations by least-squares residual minimization with linearized ReLU-power networks on the sphere using deterministic collocation points. Establishes conditions on smoothness order and sample count under which optimal rates are attained.

entry.title: AgentPatch: Coarse-to-Fine Weak-Task Repair for Merging Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zibo Shao, Baochen Xiong, Chengdong Xu, Linhui Xiao, Kaichen Li, Haoran Gong, Yan Li, Yaguang Song, Xiaoshan Yang

entry.summary: Formulates the problem of merging agentic multimodal LLMs specialized for different tools and environments, identifying asymmetric capability preservation and loss of behavior-critical actions as key failure modes. Proposes a training-free coarse-to-fine repair method that selects a stable merged backbone and restores diluted weak-task residual signals.

entry.title: Scalable Long-Horizon Planning with Staggered Updates for Lifelong MAPF

author.name: Vaibhav Sanjay and Jiaoyang Li

entry.summary: Introduces a lifelong multi-agent path finding planner that staggers path updates across agents over multiple horizons, aiming to get long-horizon reasoning at the scale where reactive rule-based methods dominate. Targets the tradeoff where reactive schemes scale but are temporally myopic and windowed replanning reasons ahead but is too slow.

entry.title: From Cheap Fakes to Pure Synthesis: Addressing the New Era of T2V Fake News Videos

author.name: Yifeng Luo, Yupeng Li, Liang Lan, Tian Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues that fully synthesized text-to-video fake news breaks existing detectors because the video matches the fabricated narrative perfectly, removing the cross-modal inconsistency detectors rely on. It reframes detection as three-way classification over real, cheap fake and pure synthesis, and releases a first dataset of purely synthetic fake news videos built to avoid unimodal shortcuts.

entry.title: Solver-Guided Reasoning for Mixed-Equilibrium Strategies

author.name: Han Wang and Philippe Beardsell and Boning Li and Aaron Sasmita and Shuai Li and Hongyuan Zha and Baoxiang Wang

entry.summary: This work uses game-solver output rather than human data to teach LLMs equilibrium reasoning, noting human play is biased toward pure strategies. A Mixed-Strategy Decision Tree converts equilibrium optimality into sparse verbalizable strategic rules that condition the model toward mixed-strategy play.

entry.title: CubicQuant: Parametric Non-Uniform Codebooks for High-Throughput LLM Inference with 1-8-Bit Weights

author.name: Xuetian Gao

entry.summary: CubicQuant is a weight quantization format where a monotonic cubic curve with two shape parameters and one scale maps uniform integer codes to non-uniform reconstruction levels, spanning 1 to 8 bit payloads. It keeps a dense integer code stream for fast GPU decoding while adapting levels per weight group, and contains uniform integer quantization as a special case.

entry.title: GraphVerse: A Comprehensive Visual Graph Reasoning Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yuanfu Sun, Yuanhang Ren, Kang Li, Chuanhao Ji, Jiaxi Li, Jiajin Liu, Ninghao Liu, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: GraphVerse is a benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can genuinely reason over graphs presented as images, rather than perceiving then reasoning in text. It expands beyond prior visual graph reasoning benchmarks with multi-image settings, process-aware metrics rather than answer-only scoring, and more realistic graph-centric scenarios.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Agility: Time-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Guided Dynamic Quadrupedal Interception

author.name: Yidong Zhu, Zibo Dai, Tongning Zhang, Leixin Chang, Hua Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a ball-catching benchmark for quadrupeds and a policy conditioned directly on target position and arrival time rather than velocity commands, paired with a vision module that predicts landing point and timing. Addresses the gap between locomotion tracking and time-critical dynamic interception.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Agent Trajectory Attribution: A Unified Benchmark and Fine-Grained Annotation Framework

author.name: Jing Chen, Yang Sun, Li Zhang, Lin Xu, Jie Shi

entry.summary: Defines trajectory attribution for LLM agents: given a long multi-step trajectory with tool calls, observations, and memory, identify which component caused an outcome. Provides a unified schema and over 1,300 annotated trajectories built on AgentDojo and Agent3Sigma settings, including attack and execution chains.

entry.title: Vernata: Self-Supervised Learning of LiDAR Point Representations

author.name: Oliver Lemke, Alexander Liniger, Abel Gawel, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: Vernata extends the Sonata self-supervised point-cloud framework with sparse view augmentation, a memory bank for stable low-resource training, and cross-modal distillation from high-resolution image teachers, targeting outdoor LiDAR representation learning. Motivated by the high cost of 3D annotation for robotics.

entry.title: AVCap: Reinforcing Audio-Video Joint Caption with Detail-Aware Reward

author.name: Mingyang Wu, Kaituo Feng, Bohao Li, Kaixiong Gong, Zihao Yin, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: AVCap releases a 100K-sample dataset of temporally aligned detailed audio-video captions, a model trained with a detail-aware GRPO variant, and an atomic-level benchmark and metric. Claims state of the art among open models and parity with proprietary systems on some evaluations.

entry.title: How Molecular Generative Models Organize Molecular Identity

author.name: Raul Ortega-Ochoa, Tejs Vegge, Jens S. Bakander, Luis Mantilla Calderon, Alan Aspuru-Guzik, Tonio Buonassisi

entry.summary: Probes how molecular generative models internally partition chemical identity by pulling molecular identity back through the generative map, revealing piecewise-constant regions with recurring coarse-to-fine boundaries. This fixed internal repertoire constrains which molecules a trained model can ever produce, including novel ones.

entry.title: Every Cache Entry Earns Its Place: Global Allocation of Resolution and Coverage for KV Cache Compression

author.name: Haolin Tian, Yuzhe Liu, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: GraceKV casts KV cache compression as global resource allocation under a fixed budget, treating each layer-head-slot combination as an atomic unit in a prototype tree so cache capacity can flow across layers and heads. It jointly balances local resolution against information coverage instead of applying fixed eviction or merging rules.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Camera Localization for Bronchoscopy

author.name: Lumin Chen, Qingyao Tian, Jinpeng Li, Haoyu Jiang, Huai Liao, Xinyan Huang, Hongbin Liu, Dong Yi

entry.summary: GABL estimates 6-DoF bronchoscope camera pose by fusing preoperative airway structure priors with intraoperative video using a graph-guided coarse-to-fine localization scheme. It targets the millimeter accuracy and low-latency requirements of intraoperative navigation with scarce training data.

entry.title: Multiple Hypothesis Flow Estimation for Video Frame Interpolation under Matching Ambiguity

author.name: Zibo Su, Jing Kong, Ruixing Wang, Zhanhe Zhang, Kun Wei

entry.summary: Argues that single-flow estimators for video frame interpolation cannot represent genuinely ambiguous correspondences (repetitive textures, fast blurred motion) and proposes estimating multiple flow hypotheses that are later combined. The framing turns matching ambiguity from noise into a modeling target.

entry.title: Edge Sparsification via Temporal Forman-Ricci Curvature for Dynamic Graph Learning

author.name: Poupak Azad, Cuneyt Gurcan Akcora, Kiarash Shamsi

entry.summary: TRicci extends Forman-Ricci curvature to directed, weighted, temporal graphs and uses it to sparsify edges before dynamic graph learning, incorporating temporal recency and local interaction competition. Evaluated on nine transaction networks and three temporal graph benchmarks.

entry.title: NiyamAI - An Intent-Bound AI Agent with Cryptographically Verifiable Guardrails using Zero-Knowledge Proofs

author.name: Aditya Katkar, Om Karkele, Kartik Mandhane, Manisha More, Yash Kashid

entry.summary: NiyamAI locks an agent session into a committed intent contract and validates every tool call with an isolated judge model, then produces a zero-knowledge proof that the safety check ran before the tool executes. The goal is cryptographically verifiable rather than merely asserted agent guardrails.

entry.title: MAUPITI: On-Device Prototype-Based Learning on a Smart Infrared Sensor

author.name: Beatrice Alessandra Motetti, Tanguy Dugas du Villard, Matteo Risso, Alessio Burrello, Francesco Daghero, Enrico Macii, Massimo Poncino, Marco Castellano, Alfio Basile, Daniele Jahier Pagliari

entry.summary: MAUPITI implements on-device prototype-based continual learning on a smart infrared array sensor with a RISC-V microcontroller, using an offline-trained quantized CNN encoder plus nearest-class-mean prototypes updated in streaming fashion under kilobyte memory and milliwatt power budgets. It avoids backpropagation and replay buffers entirely.

entry.title: Authoring and Management of Transparent Research Integrity Assessments of Randomised Clinical Trial Publications Using LLM-assisted Tools and Provenance Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Milan Markovic, Goutham Indukuri, Somayajulu Sripada, Colby J. Vorland, Jack Wilkinson, Clare Robertson, Mark Bolland, Andrew Grey, Miriam Brazzelli, Alison Avenell

entry.summary: Describes an LLM-assisted tool that helps human reviewers assess research integrity of published randomized trials following a community framework, with a provenance ontology and knowledge graph recording how each assessment was produced. The emphasis is on transparency and auditability of AI-assisted appraisal rather than automation.

entry.title: Establishing Boundary KKT Convergence of Mirror Descent through Reparameterization

author.name: Kuangyu Ding and Kim-Chuan Toh

entry.summary: Proves convergence of mirror descent to KKT points for nonconvex problems including boundary limit points, via a metric-flattening reparameterization that admits a definable boundary extension and a Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz argument. Applications include Shannon and Fermi-Dirac entropy kernels and power kernels.

entry.title: TOFD: Target-Oriented Feature Decoupling against Poisoning Attacks in Split Federated Learning

author.name: Yuhan Xie, Jingrong Huang, Chen Lyu

entry.summary: TOFD defends split federated learning against poisoning by inferring likely attack target classes through class-wise safe zones with margin perturbation, purifying suspicious samples, and applying robust optimization, exploiting the split architecture for early detection. It aims to cover a wide range of poisoning attack types in one framework.

entry.title: A foundation-model approach to pediatric headache classification from rs-fMRI

author.name: Guilherme S. Imai Aldeia, Clara Moon, Julie Shulman, Navil Sethna, Allison Smith, Alyssa Lebel, William G. La Cava, Scott Holmes

entry.summary: Evaluates whether a recent neuroimaging foundation model fine-tuned on resting-state fMRI can distinguish pediatric headache patients from controls and classify subtypes, comparing against conventional functional connectivity features on 189 scans from 110 children. It reports moderate discrimination for the presence of headache.

entry.title: FUSE: Feature-Wise Unified Specialization with Cross-Column Exchange for Mixed-Type Tabular Flow Matching

author.name: Suman Cha, Seongchan Lee, Dohyun Ko, Hyunjoong Kim

entry.summary: FUSE improves flow matching for mixed-type tabular generation by giving numerical and categorical features separate adaptive mixtures of shared specialist subnetworks while joint attention preserves cross-column dependencies. The paper also provides bounds relating restricted conditioning contexts to excess risk and Wasserstein generation error.

entry.title: An End-to-End Agent Auditing Engine

author.name: Haoning Wang, Mingxun Zhang, Chenyue Yu, Yingjun Shang, Xia Hu, Guanchu Wang, Na Zou

entry.summary: A2E is an end-to-end auditing engine for agent harnesses, introducing a task protocol so evaluation suites can be attached to different harnesses quickly, plus automatic instrumentation that records standardized execution traces. The goal is comparable, reproducible capability measurement across a fragmented agent-tooling ecosystem.

entry.title: Conformal Coverage Guarantees for Any Video Temporal Grounder

author.name: Aseel Mohamed, Rasul Khanbayov, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: COVER is a post-hoc, model-agnostic conformal wrapper that converts any video temporal grounder into one that outputs a calibrated temporal region containing the true moment with a user-specified probability. It is motivated by the observation that human annotators frequently disagree about event boundaries, so the ground truth is really a distribution over intervals.

entry.title: Do 3D Medical Foundation Models See Through MRI Artifacts? A Controlled Study of Representation Robustness

author.name: Julia Anna Mielcarz, Daniel Klaaby, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi

entry.summary: Controlled study of how five pretrained self-supervised 3D medical encoders respond to seven synthetic MRI artifacts at five corruption levels, evaluated with representation similarity, effective rank, and segmentation consistency. Finds robustness varies strongly by model and artifact type, with one encoder notably more stable.

entry.title: Bypassing Krum: Selection-Aware Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning

author.name: Srinivasan Subramanian, Md. Abdullah Al Hafiz Khan, Kazi Aminul Islam

entry.summary: Introduces a selection-aware backdoor attack that optimizes malicious federated learning updates to land inside the dense core of benign updates, so distance-based robust aggregators such as Krum and Multi-Krum select them. Demonstrates that geometric compactness assumptions underlying these defenses are exploitable by adaptive adversaries.

entry.title: HLSmith: An Expert-Guided Agentic Framework for C/C++-to-HLS Translation

author.name: Yuebo Luo, Ahmad Sedigh Baroughi, Philip Stachura, Le Chen, Venkatram Vishwanath, Zhenman Fang, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: HLSmith is an agentic framework that translates baseline C or C++ code into high-performance FPGA high-level synthesis designs by encoding expert optimization procedures the base LLMs lack. It guides architecture selection and applies hardware transformations consistently across diverse kernels.

entry.title: Gated-BEPO: Confidence-Gated Bellman Credit Assignment for Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Hongxi Yan, Ziyue Huang, Shichao Fan, Qingjie Liu

entry.summary: Gated-BEPO improves credit assignment for long-horizon LLM agents by building empirical rollout graphs per group and estimating node values with a mean-backup Bellman procedure, rather than spreading trajectory rewards uniformly or fusing step and episode credit with fixed weights. A confidence gate modulates how much step-level credit is trusted.

entry.title: PRISM: Principled Reference Identification for Schrodinger Bridge Model

author.name: Forouzan Fallah, Yezhou Yang

entry.summary: PRISM develops a theory of reference process design for Schrodinger bridge restoration models, characterizing which time-varying Gaussian references remain exactly tractable as those with commuting instantaneous covariances. It proves an invisibility principle showing that with exact drift and unlimited solver steps any admissible reference recovers the true posterior, so reference choice matters only under finite compute, then derives the optimal noise spectrum for a fixed step budget.

entry.title: Cross-View Action Consistency for Camera-Robust Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Bingqi Huang, Bingchuan Wei, Xuan Wang, Yingkai Cai, Zhaokui Wang

entry.summary: Studies why flow-based vision-language-action policies break when the scene camera is moved, using only RGB, language, and proprioception with the wrist camera masked to avoid shortcuts. Proposes regularizing the action-flow velocity field across action-equivalent rendered view pairs constructed from reset simulator states.

entry.title: International Transfer of Stochastic Cortical Self-Reconstruction

author.name: Fabian Bongratz, Zhizheng Zhuo, Chao Zhang, Yaou Liu, Dennis M. Hedderich, Christian Wachinger

entry.summary: Tests whether a normative cortical self-reconstruction model trained on UK Biobank transfers to an independent Chinese cohort for vertex-level detection of gray matter atrophy in neurodegenerative disease. Cross-population transfer is a central concern for deploying normative brain models internationally.

entry.title: Toward a Causal Data Management Ecosystem for Decision Making and Agentic AI

author.name: Dazhuo Qiu, Yingli Zhou, Amedeo Pachera, Angela Bonifati and Andrea Mauri

entry.summary: A vision paper arguing that operating modern AI ecosystems is fundamentally a data integration problem, and that integration alone is insufficient because correlational signals from heterogeneous sources mislead decisions and agentic actions. It sketches a causal data management ecosystem for decision support.

entry.title: From probability to causality in probabilistic logic programming

author.name: Zora Wurm, Kilian R\"uckschlo{\ss}, and Felix Weitk\"amper

entry.summary: Derives conditions under which the probability distribution encoded by an acyclic probabilistic logic program determines a unique causal order, exploiting the correspondence with Bayesian networks and adding constraints from relational structure. This clarifies when interventional queries on learned programs are unambiguous.

entry.title: TEMPO: Semantic-Action Decoupled RL Post-Training for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ziheng Liu, Quantao Yang

entry.summary: TEMPO is an RL post-training recipe for vision-language-action robot policies that freezes the pretrained backbone and updates only a semantic projection layer and a low-level action expert, at deliberately different timescales. The design aims to avoid the distribution mismatch of supervised fine-tuning while preventing uniform updates from degrading general semantic representations.

entry.title: FinRank: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Financial Question Answering and Retrieval over SEC Filings

author.name: Sasan Mansouri, Daniel Saad, Mark Wahrenburg, Manu Weissel, Fabian Woebbeking

entry.summary: FinRank is a financial QA and retrieval benchmark over SEC filings with 1,185 hand-authored records, gold supporting passages, and deliberately confusable hard negatives drawn from other periods, sections, and comparable firms. It tests whether systems ground answers in the correct entity, period, and disclosure context rather than merely producing a plausible number.

entry.title: Beyond Post-Hoc Temperature Scaling: Bilevel Optimization for LLM Calibration

author.name: Ruochen Jin, Zhanliang Wang, Zongyu Dai, Jiancong Xiao, Bojian Hou

entry.summary: Rather than fitting a post-hoc temperature that fails to transfer across domains, this work improves LLM calibration during training by maximizing predictive entropy through a bilevel objective, where the outer level tunes loss hyperparameters. An efficient approximation is used to make the bilevel formulation tractable at LLM scale.

entry.title: Interaction Creates Dynamical AI Behavior Absent in Isolation

author.name: Bella Xinrui Li, Frank Yingjie Huo, Neil F Johnson

entry.summary: The authors study pairs of interacting LLM agents and find that when one agent directs messages at another while ignoring replies, the subordinate enters a dynamical behavioral state it never shows in isolation and does not simply imitate the dominant agent. A simple kinetic theory reproduces the main effects, drawing an analogy to out-of-equilibrium physics.

entry.title: A Spillway for Agent Coordination

author.name: Kaustubh Kislay

entry.summary: Prompted by reported evaluations where agents spontaneously built cross-instance message boards using a shared package service and then switched to covert directory-name signaling after the board was removed, this post sketches a training design intended to channel or contain such coordination. It treats emergent inter-agent communication through shared infrastructure as a distinct safety surface from single-agent misbehavior.

entry.title: Newton-Schulz Retraction-Based Inference Enables Hidden Quantum Markov Models to Outperform Classical HMMs

author.name: Ning Ning

entry.summary: Introduces an optimization method on the Stiefel manifold using Newton-Schulz orthogonalization to train trace-preserving hidden quantum Markov models. The authors report that this is the first HQMM learner to consistently beat EM-trained classical HMMs on non-quantum sequential data.

entry.title: SNI-GNN: SmartNIC-Assisted Full-Graph GNN Training with In-Network Embedding Prediction

author.name: Guofan Yu, Sitian Chen, Zhenheng Tang, Xiaowen Chu, Amelie Chi Zhou

entry.summary: Offloads part of distributed full-graph GNN training to SmartNICs, predicting remote node embeddings in-network with a lightweight linear-trend predictor over cached historical embeddings, plus importance-based boundary sampling and an asynchronous DPU-GPU pipeline. Provides error and convergence bounds and implements on NVIDIA BlueField-3 hardware.

entry.title: PACE: Primitive-Aware Code Evolution for Automated Algorithm Design

author.name: Zhuoliang Xie, Ruihao Zheng, Xiang Xu, Genghui Li, Zhengkun Wang

entry.summary: PACE changes LLM-driven automated algorithm design from evolving whole programs to evolving reusable executable primitives, so useful local logic survives when its host program is discarded. Primitive-aware operators maintain a dynamic library and enable code-level transfer across candidate algorithms.

entry.title: Cloud-Boosted Low-Compute Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement

author.name: Xulin Fan, Juan Azcarreta, Ashutosh Pandey, Jesus Alvarez, Ke Tan, Jacob Donley, Ritwik Giri, Buye Xu

entry.summary: A collaborative edge-cloud speech enhancement framework for wearables that feeds delayed server output back as input, transfers intermediate server features to guide the on-device model, and fuses server and edge covariance estimates for multichannel beamforming. It targets the gap where strict on-device compute limits performance under real-time latency constraints.

entry.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent

author.name: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao, Boqin Yin, Yuyao Zhang, Jiapeng Sun, Shuaishuai Gong, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: SkillProx treats an agent's textual skill library as a variable optimized by a forward-backward, proximal-gradient-inspired loop that couples explicit failure diagnosis with utility-aware refinement and treats deletion as a dedicated consolidation operator. The objective balances task performance against skill complexity so accumulated procedural knowledge does not bloat the context.

entry.title: Hybrid machine learning data assimilation for marine biogeochemistry

author.name: Ieuan Higgs, Ross Bannister, Jozef Sk\'akala, Alberto Carrassi, Stefano Ciavatta

entry.summary: Integrates machine-learned relationships between observed and unobserved variables into data assimilation schemes for marine biogeochemistry models. The hybrid approach aims to update unobserved state variables without the cost of ensemble methods.

entry.title: In-Context Source and Channel Coding

author.name: Ziqiong Wang, Tianqi Ren, Rongpeng Li, Zhifeng Zhao, and Honggang Zhang

entry.summary: Adds a receiver-side in-context decoding stage to separate source-channel coding for text, using an error-correction-code transformer to score bit reliability and then having an LLM rank candidate corrected bitstreams. The goal is to avoid catastrophic decoding failures for LLM-driven arithmetic coding at low SNR.

entry.title: Physical Evaluation of Naturalistic Adversarial Patches for Camera-Based Traffic-Sign Detection

author.name: Brianna D'Urso, Tahmid Hasan Sakib, Syed Rafay Hasan, Terry N. Guo

entry.summary: Evaluates whether naturalistic adversarial patches generated with a GAN transfer from digital training to a physical traffic-sign detection setting on a small autonomous vehicle testbed. Patches measurably degrade stop-sign detection across configurations.

entry.title: Interpretable Unsupervised Community Detection with LLM-Symbolized Structured Processes

author.name: Aoting Zeng, Kai Wang, Jianwei Wang, Yuxiang Sun, Yizhang He, Wenjie Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free, unsupervised community detection method in which an LLM guides a symbolized process of initialization, merging, refinement, and selection inspired by phase-transition kinetics. The aim is interpretable, label-free graph clustering without deep model training.

entry.title: SubtleTalk: Generating Controllable Weakly-correlated Facial Dynamics for 3D Talking Heads via Residual Flow Matching

author.name: Chenyang Ding, Shuai Tan, Qunfen Lin, Xinwei Jiang, Zijiao Zeng, Ye Pan

entry.summary: Proposes a residual flow matching framework for audio-driven 3D facial animation that specifically models weakly speech-correlated motions such as blinks, eyebrow movement, and head motion, which usually appear static or repetitive. Addresses conditioning, stochasticity, and unreliable upper-face pseudo-labels.

entry.title: WorldMark: A Plug-and-Play World Knowledge Interface for Cross-Host Language Model Watermarking

author.name: Song Xiao, Yuqi Yuan, Yanshuo Zhang, Kejun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM watermarking interface that uses a world-knowledge memory graph to compute token-level knowledge saliency and modulate watermark strength asymmetrically, instead of relying purely on local token statistics. Designed to plug into existing watermark schemes across host models.

entry.title: LyEvO: Lyapunov-Guided Evolutionary Optimization for Safe and Robust Sim-to-Real Policy Learning

author.name: Riccardo Curcio, Hongpeng Cao, Marco Caccamo

entry.summary: Combines constrained evolutionary policy optimization with Lyapunov stability analysis and statistical model checking to train and certify controllers before real-world deployment. The stability region is iteratively expanded based on verification outcomes, giving a practical readiness criterion for sim-to-real transfer.

entry.title: Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models Under Steering Pressure

author.name: Ali Jalal-Kamali

entry.summary: Evaluates six frontier models on paired base and steered prompts across values-conflict, reasoning-elicitation, and reasoning-suppression categories, using all six models as blind cross-judges with leave-one-out consensus scoring. Reports that developers differ not only in how much steering moves behavior but in the qualitative response mode produced.

entry.title: Beyond "AI Language": The case for the idiolectal nature of LLM output

author.name: Karolina Rudnicka, Thomas Stephan Juzek

entry.summary: Argues that LLM text is better understood as a set of model-specific idiolects than as a single AI language variety, comparing corpora generated in 2024 and 2026 with the same prompts. Stylometric analysis shows a generational stylistic shift between cohorts while individual models retain distinctive linguistic fingerprints such as contraction frequency.

entry.title: EpiFlow: A framework for improving the utility of wastewater signals for disease forecasting

author.name: Aniruddha Adiga, Jingyuan Chou, Gursharn Kaur, Andrew Warren, Srinivasan Venkatramanan, Baltazar Espinoza, Bryan Lewis, Justin Crow, Alexandra Lorentz, Rekha Singh, Madhav Marathe

entry.summary: Develops principled processing of wastewater viral load signals, characterizes their relationship to hospital burden indicators, and tests whether they improve real-time epidemic forecasting. Emphasizes low-prevalence periods where conventional case reporting degrades due to reporting fatigue.

entry.title: Corrupting Attention: Evasion-Based Adversarial Attacks on Encoder Attention in Detection Transformers

author.name: Ridma Jayasundara, Shaheer Mohamed, Tharindu Fernando, Harshala Gammulle, Basura Fernando, Sanka Rasnayake, A V Subramanyam, Sridha Sridharan, Clinton Fookes

entry.summary: Introduces the first adversarial attack that directly optimizes an encoder-attention objective in detection transformers under a bounded imperceptible perturbation, rather than attacking detection outputs or inserting a visible patch token. Redirects the model own attention toward a corrupted target to degrade detection.

entry.title: Multi-Level Modeling of Large Language Model Inference Latency and Energy via Hybrid Analytical--Machine-Learning Predictors

author.name: Saeid Shokoufa, Mohammad Erfan Sadeghi, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: HYMELL predicts LLM inference latency and energy using a three-level hybrid of analytical operator models, machine-learned component predictors, and an end-to-end model capturing system overheads in prefill and decode. It covers dense and mixture-of-experts architectures for hardware-aware deployment planning.

entry.title: Hidden Gauge Controls Feature Specialization in ReLU Networks

author.name: Tongxi Wang

entry.summary: This theoretical study asks what determines which of several initially identical ReLU neurons ends up owning a teacher feature. Holding the initial network function fixed and varying only a positive-homogeneous scaling gauge produces different feature trajectories and a sharp quadratic-in-dimension separation in specialization time, showing an invisible parameterization choice controls specialization.

entry.title: Explore or Converge? Stage-Guided Per-Step Optimization for Diffusion Models

author.name: Renye Yan, Jikang Cheng, You Wu, Wei Peng, Zongwei Wang, Ling Liang, Yimao Cai

entry.summary: This paper argues that backpropagating a single terminal reward to all denoising steps creates a temporal objective mismatch and encourages reward hacking in RL-aligned diffusion models. It proposes stage-guided per-step optimization that differentiates rewards across the semantically distinct exploration and convergence phases of denoising.

entry.title: Coupling Planning with Episodic Memory in LLM Agents for Software Issue Resolution

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Yifan Zhang, Yu Huang

entry.summary: PMCoder couples a hierarchical phase planner with episodic memory for repository-level software issue resolution, where repair episodes run tens to hundreds of steps. The coupling is bidirectional: the current phase conditions memory retrieval while retrieved evidence updates the plan, and verification relies on execution evidence rather than the agent's own claims.

entry.title: Casting the Net! Revisiting MasterFace Impersonation Attacks

author.name: Seunghun Paik, Sunpill Kim, Chanwoo Hwang, and Jae Hong Seo
