entry.summary: Revisits MasterFace attacks on face recognition under realistic constraints of decision-only queries and no internal system knowledge, contesting follow-up work that concluded such attacks cannot beat the false-match-rate baseline in modern systems. Reports impersonation above the standard baseline.

entry.title: Generative Embedding Benchmark: How Much Information Survives in a Dense Embedding?

author.name: Yun Li, Biao Yang, Peixi Wu, Yunhao Zhou, Mingzhou Jiang, Wei Yuan, Fan Yang, Wenwu Ou

entry.summary: The Generative Embedding Benchmark measures how much answer-relevant content survives in a dense embedding by having a decoder answer questions using only the frozen embedding and the question text. This shifts embedding evaluation from separability and retrieval toward generative information recoverability.

entry.title: HRDiT: Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation with Off-the-Shelf Diffusion Transformer Models

author.name: Yu Xue, Haoxuan Qu, Zhuoling Li, Hongbin Xu, Jianxiong Yin, Simon See, Hossein Rahmani, Jun Liu

entry.summary: HRDiT enables training-free high-resolution generation from off-the-shelf diffusion transformers by diagnosing and addressing two failure modes: spatial disorder in the generated layout and long generation time. Most prior training-free high-resolution work targets U-Net diffusion models instead.

entry.title: Does More Retrieved Evidence Help Visual Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Diffusion Language Models?

author.name: Jiankun Wang, Yisen Gao, Ziwei Zhang, Xingcheng Fu, Jiaxin Bai, Chen Gao

entry.summary: Shows that for diffusion language models in visual retrieval-augmented generation, retrieving more pages improves recall but passing all of them to the generator often reduces accuracy due to semantic conflict between sources. Traces this to source-coherence loss in parallel denoising and shows the interference is detectable in the first-step answer-block distribution, enabling early filtering.

entry.title: Scenix: Sparse-View 3D Scene Reconstruction via Executable Scene Programs

author.name: Kai Li, Lutao Jiang, Zhenyang Li, Jiayu Dong, Jierui Zhang, Yingda Yin, Runze Zhang, Kai Yan, Xiaoyang Huang, Keyang Luo, Xin Wang, Xiangyu Zhao, Weikai Chen

entry.summary: Scenix reconstructs structured, editable indoor 3D scenes from a few uncalibrated RGB images by predicting executable scene programs that specify room structure and object placement. It avoids reliance on human masks, dense video, or ground-truth layouts required by prior methods.

entry.title: Stable Curves, Unstable Items: Item-Level Scaling Heterogeneity in Video LLMs

author.name: Wenzhang Sun, Chunfeng Wang, Xiangchen Yin, Yujia Chen, Hao Li, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: Shows that smooth aggregate scaling curves for video LLMs under increasing visual token budgets hide large opposing item-level effects: 12.5 to 25.5 percent of items are correct at a lower budget and wrong at a higher one, with oracle headroom of 9 to 19 accuracy points. Concludes no single visual budget is right for all items.

entry.title: ReQuant: Fixed-Grid Discrete Refinement for Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Yongge Ma, Guoan Wang, Feiyu Wang, Yaoming Li, Qian Zhang, Zihan Yan, Yinjun Han and Tong Yang

entry.summary: ReQuant adds a backpropagation-free refinement stage after post-training quantization that revisits discrete integer weight assignments on the fixed grid, improving models that other PTQ methods treat as final. It is agnostic to the initializing PTQ method and preserves the deployable quantized format.

entry.title: C2Dex: Contact-Consistent Reconstruction and Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Monocular Video

author.name: Jie Ren, Zhehao Jiang, Yinhong Yang, Haorui Jia, Han Jiang, Ben Li, Yao Yao, Cheng Lin, Qiu Shen, Zhenshan Bing, Xiao-Xiao Long, Xun Cao

entry.summary: C2Dex transfers dexterous manipulation from monocular human video by recovering stable object-side contacts in canonical object space, aggregating noisy per-frame hand-object reconstructions into a shared interaction representation. This contact-consistent representation is then retargeted across different robot hand embodiments while preserving task-relevant geometry.

entry.title: Unsupervised Adaptation of PDE Foundation Models

author.name: Ziye Song, Zhao Wei, Xin Yu, Ivor Tsang, Yueming Lyu

entry.summary: Adapts pretrained PDE foundation models to unseen equations without any ground-truth solutions, by pretraining a neighborhood-attention transformer on diverse time-dependent PDEs and then finetuning with LoRA against a physics residual and boundary-condition objective. Also addresses uneven learning across physical quantities.

entry.title: M2-SMap: Memory-Efficient Semantic Mapping with Hierarchical Multi-Model Representation

author.name: QiYing Deng, ZhongLai Wang, Yuan Gao, Wei Dong

entry.summary: M2-SMap builds memory-efficient semantic maps for robots by hierarchically decomposing RGB-D point clouds and fitting a mix of compact geometric primitives instead of storing dense point clouds. It aims to avoid the object-adhesion and overfitting failures of prior multi-model map fitting driven by local geometry.

entry.title: Interpretable reinforcement learning with decision-tree pruning

author.name: Mark Leon Ringer, Michel Tokic

entry.summary: Presents a pruning procedure that converts trained RL policies into compact decision-tree rules using structural and usage-aware edit operators, with each candidate edit validated by re-executing the policy for return and interpretability proxies. Tested on classic control and MuJoCo tasks.

entry.title: HNR-DAC: Hard-Negative Reranking and Distribution-Aligned Classification for Scientific Claim Verification

author.name: Zhenchao Wang, Xin Chen, Luoxi Zhang, Min Yang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: HNR-DAC improves scientific claim verification by training a reranker against the most confusable non-gold paragraphs and then training the label classifier on the retrieved top-1 paragraph it will actually see at inference, rather than on gold evidence. It closes a common train-test mismatch in evidence-based classification pipelines.

entry.title: Recipes for Creativity: Iterative Generation and Evaluation in Large Language Models

author.name: Rens Anderson, Tessa Verhoef, Amirhossein Zohrehvand

entry.summary: A pilot study adapting an evolutionary program-search loop to recipe generation, comparing outputs against human bake-off entries using LLM-based creativity scoring while varying iteration count, temperature, and the size of the in-loop selection model. The main finding is that more iterations do not help while the choice of in-loop evaluator dominates results, with a smaller scorer yielding higher scores.

entry.title: SCALE: Scientific Concept Aggregation via LLMs and Embeddings for Fine-Grained Taxonomy Extension

author.name: Daniele Raimondi, Feichi Lu, Oliver Grun, Mariia Eremina, Andrea Perlato

entry.summary: SCALE uses LLMs plus embeddings to aggregate fragmented author keywords into coherent conceptual units and inserts them as a new fine-grained level below topics in a large open scholarly taxonomy. It aims to make keyword-level specificity usable as stable knowledge organization.

entry.title: A Finite E-Group of Nilpotency Class Three

author.name: Xinan Dai, Wenhao Deng, Yidong Shi, Tailin Wu, Yuchen Yang

entry.summary: Resolves a group theory question by proving that a specific 3-group of very large order is an E-group of nilpotency class three, using a linear map induced by power relations on the Frattini quotient and showing it admits no nonzero proper invariant subspace. This answers an open question posed by Caranti.

entry.title: Foundation Models Adaptation for Multi-View Multi-modal Cardiac MRI Segmentation and Direct Ejection Fraction Estimation

author.name: Sina Amirrajab, Cian M Scannell, Volker Vehof, Michael Bietenbeck, Ali Yilmaz

entry.summary: A challenge-participation report on fine-tuning and combining cardiac MRI foundation models for multi-view, multi-sequence segmentation, plus direct ejection fraction regression from frozen model embeddings via attention-based multiple instance learning. It probes how well cardiac foundation models transfer across heterogeneous acquisition protocols.

entry.title: From Optimal Actions to World Models: Identifiability of Transition Kernels in Discounted MDPs

author.name: Neal Batra

entry.summary: A theoretical study of how much of an MDP transition kernel can be identified purely from knowing which actions are optimal across a whole class of reward functions, rather than from observed Q-values. The author characterizes the exact equivalence class of kernels that induce identical optimal policies, sharpening earlier inverse-RL identifiability results.

entry.title: Is SwiGLU's Open Positive Tail Necessary? Evidence from Closed-Tail Gating with MemGLU

author.name: Yuting Ge, Pengju Yang, Mingkai Nie

entry.summary: The paper tests whether the unbounded positive tail of SwiGLU gating is actually needed in decoder-only transformer feed-forward layers by introducing a closed-tail alternative, MemGLU. In paired small-scale pretraining runs the two match within roughly 0.1 percent validation loss, though diagnostics show the models use their gates differently, suggesting networks adapt to whatever gate geometry is available.

entry.title: When GNNs Fail: Quantifying and Overcoming Temporal Correlation Volatility in Time Series

author.name: Chen Shao, Yue Wang, Zhenyi Zhu, Zhanbo Huang, Tobias K\"afer, Zonghan Wu and Danai Koutra

entry.summary: The authors show that graph neural network forecasters degrade when pairwise correlations between time series change over time, and introduce Temporal Correlation Volatility as a model-agnostic metric to quantify that drift. They then analyze representational limits of static-topology GNNs and propose remedies for dynamic-correlation regimes.

entry.title: TEPA: Revoking Stale Memories for Conflict-Robust Language Agents

author.name: Yan Zhou, Yue Ouyang, Kaiyang Zheng, Suncheng Xiang

entry.summary: TEPA gives language-agent long-term memory an explicit validity state, storing observations as keyed precedents and revoking them when newer evidence contradicts an existing key, while retaining revoked entries for audit. The paper frames stale-but-retrievable memory as memory pollution and tests the mechanism under hidden-regime drift, executable file drift, and preference change.

entry.title: MirrorWorld: Taming Video Diffusion Models for Mirror Reflection Generation

author.name: Youjun Zhao, Alex Warren, Gary K.L. Tam, Rynson W.H. Lau

entry.summary: MirrorWorld adapts video diffusion models to generate physically consistent mirror reflections by explicitly modeling what scene content should appear in a mirror and how it should be spatially arranged. It is framed as reflection-aware video inpainting, addressing a specific physical-consistency weakness of current generators.

entry.title: Wasserstein Mahalanobis Distances for Recovering Latent Geometry

author.name: Chuxiangbo Wang, Shiying Li, Caroline Moosm\"uller

entry.summary: Generalizes the Mahalanobis distance to probability measures by replacing displacement vectors with optimal-transport displacement fields and covariances with Wasserstein tangent-space operators. It shows the resulting metric recovers latent geometry under smooth nonlinear pushforwards, connecting to nonlinear ICA.

entry.title: Optimized Certainty Equivalent Risk Minimization Using Samples: Algorithms, Convergence Rates, and Applications

author.name: Sumedh Gupte, Prashanth L. A., Sanjay P. Bhat

entry.summary: Studies sample-based optimization of Optimized Certainty Equivalent risk measures, covering entropic risk, mean-variance and smoothed CVaR, with a link to utility-based shortfall risk that enables a sample-average estimator. Provides mean-squared-error bounds and convergence rates for the optimization procedure.

entry.title: Beyond Visibility: Real-Time Surface Accessibility Fields from Sparse LiDAR

author.name: Bradley Scott, Sam Schofield, Richard Green

entry.summary: Defines an accessibility field that labels each surface point by whether a given tool can physically reach it, computed in real time on GPU from streaming sparse LiDAR without requiring complete noise-free meshes. It goes beyond visibility estimation by accounting for tool geometry and approach clearance.

entry.title: Fairis: Fairness-Aware Aggregation with Provable Influence Containment against Fairness Poisoning Attacks in Collaborative Machine Learning

author.name: Devharsh Trivedi, Nesrine Kaaniche, Nikos Triandopoulos, Maryline Laurent, Jackson Walters

entry.summary: Introduces a server-side reweighting rule for federated learning that bounds the influence any single client can exert while accounting for local fairness gaps, defending against adversaries that maximize group disparity while keeping accuracy intact. Shows that a prior fairness-aware aggregation scheme can be gamed by an adversary observing the global fairness score.

entry.title: I Seek You in Videos: Identity-Conditioned Queries for Person-Centric Video Reasoning

author.name: Shibo Gao, Chongxiao Wang, Chenglong Huang, Jie Ma, Haolin Shi, Fei Ding, Jing Li, Qiang Lyu, Yangyang Liu, Yang Liu, Jun Liu, Linlin Huang, Peipei Yang

entry.summary: The ICQ task requires models to jointly reason over a video and a reference image of a specific person, combining identity grounding with behavior and temporal understanding. The authors release a benchmark of nearly 1,400 real complex videos with question-answer pairs organized by difficulty, plus a system addressing the task.

entry.title: Target-Weighted Neyman Allocation: Experimental Design for Heterogeneous Treatment Effects under Population Shift

author.name: Hoang Dang, Luan Pham, Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage stratified experimental design that allocates sample sizes and treatment probabilities using pilot variance estimates, targeting precision of group-level treatment effects weighted by the deployment population rather than the experimental one. Includes an oracle closed-form rule and extensions to uncertain deployment composition.

entry.title: A proximal subgradient method for nonconvex stochastic optimization under the Kurdyka-{\L}ojasiewicz condition

author.name: Felipe Atenas, Alejandro Jofr\'e, Pedro P\'erez-Aros, David Torregrosa-Bel\'en

entry.summary: Develops a proximal stochastic subgradient method for nonsmooth nonconvex composite problems, using progressively refined sample averages and an Armijo-type line search tolerant to stochastic error. Convergence is established under a Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz condition.

entry.title: Deep Evidential Regression for Sparse Forest Height Estimation from Multimodal Satellite Imagery

author.name: Laura Bader, Muhammad Ammar Ahmed, Xiao Xiang Zhu, G\"oran Kauermann

entry.summary: Applies deep evidential regression to estimate forest canopy height from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery with quantified predictive uncertainty, on a benchmark with sparse tree-inventory labels over Bavaria. Focus is uncertainty under label sparsity and geographic distribution shift.

entry.title: NTDH: Complex Reasoning for Comprehensive Affective Analysis

author.name: Tianlei Zhu, Zhiwei Liu, Yuyan Wang, Xiao-Yang Liu, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: Recasts sentiment and emotion analysis across continuous, ordinal, and multi-label outputs as a single reasoning problem with verifiable rewards, and synthesizes targeted affective reasoning traces to train it. Claims to be the first unified reasoning treatment covering both sentiment and emotion tasks.

entry.title: MiGHT-EHR: A Multi-task Graph Transformer for Heterogeneous Temporal Electronic Health Records

author.name: Anirudh Rayas, Yuan Wang, Pavan Turaga

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-task graph transformer that jointly models heterogeneous clinical entities, longitudinal visit trajectories, and shared dependencies across clinical prediction tasks in electronic health records. Argues existing EHR models capture only a subset of these three properties.

entry.title: Do AI Personas Grow? Analyzing and Benchmarking Personality Evolution in LLM Agents After Life Events

author.name: Ming Wang, Peidong Wang, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Shi Feng, Fiona Fui-Hoon Nah, Ee-Peng Lim

entry.summary: Studies whether persona-conditioned LLM agents change personality plausibly after simulated life events, using Big Five traits as a psychometric anchor and comparing trajectories against human longitudinal findings. Provides a benchmark over eleven life events across traits, personas, and models.

entry.title: Can MLLMs Decode the Creative Leap? Introducing C4 for Cross-Concept Understanding

author.name: Ming Wang, Yuqing Zhang, Tingna Xie, Xiangju Li, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Shi Feng, Yifei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a cognition-inspired framework for evaluating whether multimodal LLMs can recover intended meaning from non-obvious conceptual substitutions, instantiated on Chinese idiom puzzles. Frames item construction as cross-concept encoding and model inference as decoding, with an annotated bridge-path concept graph.

entry.title: TradeVerse: A Longitudinal Benchmark of Political Negotiation in International Trade

author.name: Debodeep Banerjee and Amitangshu Dasgupta

entry.summary: Builds a longitudinal benchmark from reconstructed World Trade Organization meeting minutes where member states argue over specific trade concerns across many rounds and years. Defines tasks that require tracking argument state over long multi-turn institutional histories rather than reading isolated documents.

entry.title: SyncSBC: Decentralized Swarm Behavior Prediction for Synchronized Autonomous Control

author.name: Varun Raveendra, Connor Mattson, Daniel S. Brown

entry.summary: Enables individual swarm robots to classify the collective behavior of the whole swarm from purely local sensing, then reach synchronized decisions through distributed consensus without any central coordinator. Demonstrates high classification accuracy, low synchronization delay, and two applications on physical robots.

entry.title: Automated item evaluation: Predicting item acceptance and rejection using LLM-generated critiques

author.name: Hotaka Maeda, Yikai Lu

entry.summary: Predicts whether standardized test items would be accepted or rejected from a large operational item bank of over fifty thousand English and math items, using fine-tuned encoders on raw item text, on LLM-generated critiques, and a fusion of both. Aims to replace costly expert review and field testing for item quality screening.

entry.title: NxN E-valuation: Hypothesis Certification via a Conformal CRT Null

author.name: Bin Wang, Yan Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes an e-value based certification procedure that can validate an LLM-generated hypothesis without hand-building a case-specific null, using a conformal conditional randomization null over a large dataset. Targets the problem that LLMs propose plausible hypotheses prolifically but hallucinate, while self-verification and held-out testing both leak spurious findings.

entry.title: Discovering Conceptual Metaphors Across Topics and Media Types

author.name: Alexandria Leto and Rohan Das and Juan V\'asquez and Abram Handler and Maria Leonor Pacheco

entry.summary: Presents an unsupervised method to extract linguistic metaphors from text and group them into evidence for underlying conceptual metaphors, then compares which framings dominate across topics and media types. Motivated by the way alternative framings of the same abstract issue lead to different reasoning and policy attitudes.

entry.title: Suppress and Diversify: Refining Robust Pathways for Corruption Robustness

author.name: Jiangang Yang, Wenhui Shi, Xiaoran Xu, Wenyue Chong, Luqing Luo, Jing Xing, Jian Liu

entry.summary: Analyzes internal computational pathways to explain corruption robustness, reporting a progressive decay of robust features across network layers and linking their prevalence to performance. Proposes a parameter-free, architecture-agnostic refinement that dynamically selects robust pathways and diversifies them with symmetry-preserving transformations at zero test-time overhead.

entry.title: MolBioKG: Grounding Out-of-Graph Molecules in Biomedical Knowledge Graphs via Multi-Resolution Structural Anchoring

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Hikaru Shindo, Shuan Chen, Kaushalya Madhawa, Jun Jin Choong, Yuna Oikawa, Takashi Fujiwara, Keisuke Ozawa

entry.summary: MolBioKG tackles the cold-start problem of querying biomedical knowledge graphs with molecules that are not registered as graph nodes. It indexes 2.74 million molecules by scaffolds, fragments, functional groups and fingerprints, then anchors an unseen SMILES string to structurally similar in-graph entities and traverses their biomedical neighborhoods without task-specific training.

entry.title: Sub-Quadratic Bisimulation Metrics via Approximate Nearest Neighbors: Coverage-Augmented Guarantees and Computable Two-Sided Certificates

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Joyanta Jyoti Mondal

entry.summary: This paper makes bisimulation metric computation sub-quadratic by using approximate nearest neighbor indexing to choose which state pairs get exact Wasserstein updates, with monotone lower and upper sweeps bracketing the true metric. The central theoretical result is a coverage-augmented anytime bound showing index quality alone cannot control global error because uncovered pairs keep their initialization gap.

entry.title: Surg-UniWorld: A Unified Surgical World Model with Multimodal Control Experts

author.name: Rulin Zhou, Wanhao Liu, Guoheng Ma, Liangjin Shao, Qiujie Song, Yidu Wang, Guankun Wang, Tong Chen, Long Bai, Luping Zhou, and Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Surg-UniWorld is a controllable surgical world model that synthesizes instrument-tissue interaction video under multiple conditioning modalities. A hierarchical surgical anchor from the first frame and semantic masks preserves scene identity, while modality-specific experts interpret edge, depth and other conditions to avoid anatomical distortion and instrument drift.

entry.title: AnyTrack: Unifying Visual Object Tracking with Any Modalities

author.name: Hao Li and Yunzhi Zhuge and Wenning Hao and Pingping Zhang and Xiaoxiong Zhang and Dong Wang and Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: AnyTrack is a single tracker that handles arbitrary combinations of input modalities instead of requiring a separate model per modality pair. A modality-aware interaction module bridges modality gaps and aggregates temporal cues to keep tracking stable when modalities are missing or degraded.

entry.title: Retrieval-Constrained Policy Optimization for Attack Technique Extraction from Cyber Threat Intelligence

author.name: Jiayun Zhang, Junshen Xu, Zejun Xie, Yi Fan

entry.summary: TTP-R1 maps cyber threat intelligence text to MITRE ATT&CK techniques using retrieval-constrained policy optimization, treating the task as set prediction rather than token-level sequence generation. This gives direct supervision on whether the predicted technique set is complete and correct across a label space of several hundred techniques.

entry.title: PAST: Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination for Efficient Diffusion Model

author.name: Renye Yan, Jikang Cheng, You Wu, Wei Peng, Zongwei Wang, Ling Liang, Yimao Cai

entry.summary: PAST speeds up RL fine-tuning of text-to-image diffusion by adaptively terminating sampling based on denoising progress and prompt difficulty, and by adding an intrinsic reward to compensate for sparse external reward. The authors give theoretical justification for the intrinsic reward and dynamically shorten training episodes.

entry.title: FutureBridge: Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding

author.name: Quanquan Li, Hongbo Zhang, Yihe Chi, Jingyu Li, Xidong Xi, Liuyang Song, Hongzhen Zhang, Yuxiang Huang, Jing Ke, Siyuan Ma, Junyi Lin, Guitao Cao

entry.summary: FutureBridge improves large-small model collaborative decoding by ranking candidate tokens according to how well the small model can continue from them, rather than by the large model's local preference. Counterfactual scores computed under a fixed verified future trajectory train a lightweight reranker that needs only the current state at inference.

entry.title: Control-Anchored Residual Flow Matching Conditioned on Gene Geometry for Virtual Cell Perturbation Modeling

author.name: Quanquan Li, Yihe Chi, Liuyang Song, Hongbo Zhang, Jingyu Li, Xidong Xi, Conghua Wei, Yijie Sun, Yu Chen, Xin Liu, Qi Hu, Jing Ke, Guitao Cao

entry.summary: GeneGeoFlow predicts single-cell transcriptional responses to unseen perturbations using a control-anchored residual flow conditioned on gene-wise geometry derived from biological networks. The key argument is that ontology and coexpression networks encode stable associations, so they should shape representation geometry rather than be treated as intervention-response pathways.

entry.title: Unordered Landmark Visual Navigation

author.name: Hao Ren, Junzhe Zhu, Yihan Li, Zetong Bi, Le Zheng, Zhi Li, Yiqing Yuan, Zhaoliang Wan, Dizhe Zhang, Lu Qi, Hui Cheng

entry.summary: This paper defines unordered landmark visual navigation, where an agent must reach an image goal using only an unordered RGB image collection with no temporal ordering, depth, LiDAR or odometry. The proposed framework mitigates perceptual aliasing and noisy associations that break existing methods when temporal priors are removed.

entry.title: ControlRef: Efficient Layout-Guided Multi-Instance Generation via Anchored 4D-RoPE

author.name: Yunkai Yang, Yudong Zhang, Xinying Chen, Haoyuan Liang, Yizhuo Niu, Jinshuai Cheng, Kunquan Zhang, Liziyue Fang, Weitao Wan, Runmin Dong

entry.summary: ControlRef makes layout-guided multi-instance image generation efficient in multimodal diffusion transformers by replacing redundant full-resolution canvas padding and shifted rotary position embeddings with an anchored 4D-RoPE scheme and an instance-layout control attention mask. This preserves low-frequency positional structure while cutting overhead on sparse layouts.

entry.title: From Points to Edges: Edge-Conditioned Spectral Operators for Physics-Sensitive PDE Learning

author.name: Zhentao Tan, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: The Edge-Conditioned Spectral Operator modulates global spectral mixing in neural PDE solvers using local edge-wise variations, rather than adapting modal mixing only from center-point features. This makes the operator responsive to physics-sensitive local structures such as sharp permeability interfaces in Darcy flow.

entry.title: Prune Once: Retraining-Free Task-Agnostic Pruning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Minseok Kang, Hyunwoo Kim, Chanyoung Kim, Minwoo Kim, Jaekoo Lee, Dahuin Jung

entry.summary: PORTA prunes vision-language models without retraining or task-specific data, using an activation-variation criterion estimated from generic calibration samples. The claim is that the pruned model stays broadly usable across multimodal tasks, which matters for edge deployment of VLMs.

entry.title: MaskFlow: Precise, Consistent and Seamless Regional Image Editing

author.name: Rui Xu, Yang Yong, Shunzi Yang, Ruihao Gong, Chengtao Lv

entry.summary: MaskFlow trains regional image editors by folding the edit mask into the flow-matching probability path so generation inside the region and preservation outside are jointly optimized, with a Soft-Poisson module to remove visible seams. Targets precise localization plus natural blending in mask-based editing.

entry.title: Finding Usable Weight Mechanisms with Tiled SVD

author.name: Ash Manvi and Samreena Tajreen

entry.summary: Proposes reading interpretable mechanisms directly from weight matrices via column-tiled SVD, where each triple of input direction, output direction, and singular value acts as a trigger-write-strength unit, evaluated on Gemma-2-2B with a pre-registered protocol. Positions this as an alternative to sparse-autoencoder dictionaries whose feature identity lives outside the weights.

entry.title: GPTKB 2.0: Browsing, Querying, and Auditing a Disambiguated LLM-Derived Knowledge Base

author.name: Yujia Hu, Tuan-Phong Nguyen, Simon Razniewski

entry.summary: GPTKB 2.0 is a browsable knowledge base materialized from an LLM containing 38.4M triples over 1.6M canonical entities, with context-guided entity disambiguation performed during recursive construction rather than string matching. The demo exposes provenance and disambiguation decisions and supports SPARQL queries, making LLM-extracted knowledge auditable.

entry.title: Decoupling Intention from Trajectory: A Representational Deduction Framework for World Action Models

author.name: Xiangkai Ma, Yue Ma, Junjie Wang, Sheng Xu, Mingyang Li, Han Zhang, Yuzheng Zhuang, Wenzhong Li, Zhihao Yuan

entry.summary: PILOT argues that world action models entangle high-level physical state evolution with low-level trajectory generation because their visual branches only predict static observations. Its representational deduction module models transition information about how world states evolve under interaction, and uses that to condition motion planning.

entry.title: Not All Problems Are Best Modeled as MILP: A DSL-Centric Framework for Flexible and Accurate Optimization Modeling

author.name: Shaofeng Zhang, Hongyuan Su, Qingwen Peng, Zefang Zong, Shengcai Liu, Ke Tang, and Yong Li

entry.summary: OptiDSL argues that LLM-based optimization modeling should not default to mixed-integer linear programming, since forcing complex domains into linear constraints inflates modeling complexity and restricts solver choice. It has LLMs map natural language onto domain-specific language representations, decoupling formulation from execution.

entry.title: BONSAI: Evolvability-Guided Tree Search over Skills

author.name: Yash Priya Shastri, Anand Eswaran, Adnan Qidwai, Pankaj Thorat, Sachin Joshi

entry.summary: BONSAI optimizes natural-language skill documents for frozen agents by steering Monte Carlo tree search with evolvability, the capacity of a region of document space to keep producing viable variants, rather than held-out score alone. The motivation is that score-greedy editing cannot distinguish a narrow overfit peak from a broad improvable plateau.

entry.title: Grammar Engineering Meets LLMs: Development of Cantonese and Irish ParGram Treebanks

author.name: Chit-Fung Lam and Elaine U\'i Dhonnchadha

entry.summary: Reports the construction of Cantonese and Irish treebanks within a parallel grammar framework and evaluates whether a multilingual open-weight model can assist grammar engineering, finding translation quality generally unsatisfactory and prompt language irrelevant. Formal syntactic structure generation showed mixed usefulness.

entry.title: Learning Fault-Tolerant Locomotion with Adaptive Gait Timing

author.name: Giovanbattista Gravina, Luca Rossini, Carlo Rizzardo, Arturo Laurenzi and Nikos Tsagarakis

entry.summary: A deep RL controller for quadruped locomotion under actuator power loss, using an asymmetric actor-critic where the critic sees privileged fault information and the actor learns to infer a matching latent from proprioception via an alignment loss. The focus on heavier quadrupeds addresses cases where aggressive high-frequency compensation is infeasible.

entry.title: Assessing AI-generated music detection in real-world broadcast monitoring

author.name: David L\'opez-Ayala, Fernando Garc\'ia de la Cruz, Pablo Zinemanas, Emilio Molina and Mart\'in Rocamora

entry.summary: BAMM is a 40-hour dataset of real television recordings containing both AI-generated and human-made music, created to test whether AI-music detectors survive genuine broadcast conditions. Detectors that are near-perfect on clean audio degrade substantially on synthetic broadcast simulation and further on real broadcast, showing prior synthetic evaluations were overoptimistic.

entry.title: CoBa: Cost-Effective Test-Time Scaling via Compute-Balanced Routing

author.name: Yan Zhou, Yue Ouyang, Kaiyang Zheng, Suncheng Xiang

entry.summary: CoBa treats test-time scaling as a compute-allocation problem, deciding at each step whether to spend the next unit of compute on generating more candidates, verifying existing ones, or stopping. Cheap verification is applied broadly and only uncertain or high-value candidates are routed to a stronger verifier, reporting competitive accuracy on math contest benchmarks at lower cost.

entry.title: Wasserstein Policy Gradient for Entropy-Regularized Linear-Quadratic Control

author.name: Zhaoyu Zhu, Rui Gao, Shuang Li

entry.summary: A theoretical analysis of Wasserstein policy gradient for entropy-regularized discounted linear-quadratic control, showing the optimal policy remains linear-Gaussian and that the transport gradient stays tangent to that class. The infinite-dimensional flow therefore reduces exactly to a finite ODE for gain and covariance, with proven global well-posedness and exponential convergence.

entry.title: Certified Feedforward Tracking for Unknown Nonlinear Systems via Invertible Neural Networks

author.name: Berk Altiner, Rajasree Sarkar, Arunava Banerjee, Zongxuan Sun, and Kenneth Kim

entry.summary: Uses an invertible neural network as a surrogate for an unknown nonlinear system so that feedforward control inversion is exact by construction, then applies conformal prediction to obtain finite-sample probabilistic bounds on tracking error. Demonstrated on a DC-motor load with nonlinear friction.

entry.title: Mixture of Geodesic Factor Analyzers on Riemannian Homogeneous Spaces

author.name: Hengchao Chen, Yuanyao Tan, Chao Huang, Hongtu Zhu, Qiang Sun

entry.summary: Introduces mixtures of geodesic factor analyzers for clustering manifold-valued data on Riemannian homogeneous spaces, with proven root-n consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator. Algorithms are implemented for spheres, shape spaces, and hyperbolic spaces.

entry.title: Omni-modal decomposition autoencoders learn full-stack wearable disentangled representations

author.name: Ioannis Ziogas, Ensieh Khazaei, Bilal Taha, Aamna Al Shehhi, Ahsan H. Khandoker, Leontios J. Hadjileontiadis, Dimitrios Hatzinakos

entry.summary: Presents omni-modal variational decomposition autoencoders that learn modality-conditioned time-frequency latent subspaces across many heterogeneous wearable sensor streams. The framework targets classification, disentanglement, fusion, and generation in one model.

entry.title: Decision Predicate Graphs: Enhancing Interpretability in Tree Ensembles

author.name: Leonardo Arrighi, Luca Pennella, Gabriel Marques Tavares, Sylvio Barbon Junior

entry.summary: Introduces Decision Predicate Graphs, a model-agnostic graph representation that captures the decision predicates and their relationships across a tree ensemble to give a global interpretation. It aims to avoid the visual clutter or fidelity loss of prior tree-ensemble visualization methods.

entry.title: Identity-Preserving Aging and De-Aging of Faces in the StyleGAN Latent Space

author.name: Luis S. Luevano and Pavel Korshunov and Sebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Proposes a StyleGAN latent-space method for face aging and de-aging that avoids conditional GAN or diffusion training and explicitly optimizes for identity preservation verified by face recognition systems. Aimed at forensic and security use cases.

entry.title: The Word and the Way: Strategies for Domain-Specific BERT Pre-Training in German Medical NLP

author.name: Henry He, Johann Frei, Raphael Schmitt

entry.summary: Presents a family of German biomedical and clinical RoBERTa models trained on a 13.5GB mixed corpus, comparing continued pretraining, training from scratch, and domain vocabulary adaptation. Evaluated on German medical NER and classification tasks.

entry.title: Evaluating XAI Support From A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Policy in Human-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Mateus Levi Sim\~oes Fernandes, Alberto Sardinha

entry.summary: Runs the first systematic user study of explanations generated from an intrinsically explainable hierarchical RL policy in the Overcooked-AI human-agent benchmark, delivering subtask explanations as text or audio. Found no significant team performance effects but a notable reduction in some subjective measures for audio explanations.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation with Online Personalized Energy-Based Cache for Fine-Grained Video Expression Recognition

author.name: Masoumeh Sharafi, Muhammad Osama Zeeshan, Soufiane Belharbi, Alessandro Lameiras Koerich, Marco Pedersoli, Eric Granger

entry.summary: Proposes a cache-based, parameter-free test-time adaptation method for video facial expression recognition that personalizes to individual subjects using an energy-based cache instead of updating model weights. Targets the cold-start problem where too few target samples exist to build reliable class prototypes.

entry.title: Improving Low-Resolution Face Recognition under Limited Data: How Synthetic Data Generation Can Close the Domain Gap

author.name: Luis S. Luevano, \"Unsal \"Ozt\"urk, Hatef Otroshi Shahreza, Anjith George and S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Systematically compares synthetic data strategies for low-resolution face recognition on edge devices, spanning interpolation degradation, knowledge distillation, domain transformers, realistic degradation pipelines, and identity-aware super-resolution front ends. Quantifies how much synthesis effort actually translates into recognition accuracy when paired low- and high-resolution data is scarce.

entry.title: Flowing Through States: Neural ODE Regularization for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mohamed Ghanem, Bernd Finkbeiner

entry.summary: Draws an analogy between Markov decision process trajectories and ordinary differential equation flows to regularize latent representations so they follow consistent continuous dynamics. The aim is to align representation learning with true environment dynamics rather than leaving latent transitions implicit.

entry.title: Pre-Inference Routing for Cost-Efficient Document Field Extraction

author.name: Sreerekha Rajendran

entry.summary: Predicts document difficulty before extraction from cheap signals such as image quality and layout, then routes each document to a cheaper or stronger extractor. Identifies two necessary conditions for routing to pay off and reports large cost reductions on receipts and degraded forms at nearly unchanged accuracy.

entry.title: Factorized Hypothesis Search for Evidence-to-Taxonomy Retrieval

author.name: Linhai Ma, Ethan F. Wei, Xueqing Peng, Yan Wang, Lingfei Qian, V\'ictor Guti\'errez-Basulto

entry.summary: Tackles retrieval when the query is indirect evidence, such as a table cell whose meaning depends on its row, column, and datatype, rather than an explicit statement of the target concept. Maintains multiple partial interpretations along named semantic dimensions to render structured queries and verify candidates dimension by dimension.

entry.title: Plan-and-Avoid: Real-Time Aircraft Trajectory Coordination in a Multi-Agent Environment

author.name: Huseyin Emre Tekaslan and Ella M. Atkins and Natasha Neogi

entry.summary: Presents a real-time framework that protects a declared priority aircraft trajectory, such as a contingency landing plan, by predicting uncertainty-aware separation violations and issuing vehicle-constrained advisories to nearby traffic. Advisories modify other aircraft trajectories so that well-clear separation holds for all agents.

entry.title: TRACE: A Multi-Layer Benchmark for Human AI Controller Coordination Under Drift and Failure

author.name: Joshua Zuniga, Srinivasan Subramanian, Ramya Madhuri Narapureddy, Md Abdullah Al Hafiz Khan

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark of nearly two thousand traces where controlled drift is injected into household task trajectories so that deviations can be localized to a specific layer of the human, AI decision module, and controller stack, with known onset times. Aims to enable diagnosis of where and when coordination breaks down in coupled cyber-physical loops.

entry.title: bioMoR: Biology-Guided Mixture-of-Recursions for Effective Genomic Learning

author.name: Koushik Howlader, Tirtho Roy, Md Tauhidul Islam, Wei Le

entry.summary: bioMoR applies Mixture-of-Recursions adaptive-depth computation to gene and pathway level omics transformers, so only biologically important tokens receive deep processing. Biological priors enter at three points: graph-based embedding sharing, a structural attention bias, and a graph-aware router that sets per-token recursion depth.

entry.title: Stockmark-Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-JapanDocReader: Structured Document Parsing via Capability Injection and Forgetting Control

author.name: Shi Chen, Hayato Aida, Makoto Morinaga, Shohei Tanaka, Kosuke Arima

entry.summary: This work injects Japanese structured document parsing into an existing Nemotron-3 Nano Omni reasoning multimodal model while trying to preserve its document VQA ability. It compares parsing-only SFT, mixed SFT and parsing-focused RL, finding parsing-only SFT causes measurable VQA forgetting.

entry.title: ArchEGraph: A Large-Scale Graph Dataset for Geometry-Topology-Physics Aligned Building Energy Modeling

author.name: Yihui Li, Yihui Chen, Kaidi Zha, Xiaoyue Yan, Zhexuan Yu, Shiqi Dai, Jun Xiao, Jun Yin, Ramon Elias Weber, Borong Lin

entry.summary: ArchEGraph is a large benchmark linking building geometry and topology to simulated zone-level thermal loads, with 5,481 buildings and about 49,000 validated building-weather simulation cases represented as heterogeneous graphs. It supports training fast surrogate models that give architects rapid energy feedback during design.

entry.title: Multiscale Reward Hedging from Correct Demonstrations

author.name: Pahan Dewasurendra

entry.summary: This theory paper studies learning from correct demonstrations when many answers are valid and the learner never sees whether its own answer was acceptable. It gives the first horizon-free reward-hedging guarantee for continuous reward classes by hedging in a shared vote over tolerant optimality tests at every accuracy scale.

entry.title: Graph Machine: Exploring Edge Mechanisms as an Inductive Bias

author.name: Lintai Hou

entry.summary: Graph Machine adds two explicit edge mechanisms to a transformer-like architecture: edges modulating attention between nodes, and nodes exchanging addresses to update edges, allowing differentiable construction and revision of relational graphs across layers. On controlled Sudoku experiments it beats transformer baselines, with ablations attributing gains to the edge mechanisms.

entry.title: Are Visual Place Recognition Models Recognizing Places or Conditions? Distractor-Augmented Evaluation and Condition Suppression

author.name: Beomsu Kim, Minwoo Jung, Giseop Kim

entry.summary: This paper shows that visual place recognition descriptors encode illumination, weather and seasonal appearance, so with condition-similar distractors in mixed-condition databases models can retrieve by condition rather than by place. It introduces distractor-augmented recall to quantify the effect and a condition suppression technique evaluated across eleven methods.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Hyperdimensional Computing and Kernel Methods via the Nystr\"om Method

author.name: Quanling Zhao, Anthony Hitchcock Thomas, Ari Brin, Xiaofan Yu, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: NysHD connects hyperdimensional computing to kernel methods by using the Nystrom approximation to turn any user-defined positive semidefinite similarity function into a corresponding high-dimensional vector encoding. This gives a principled recipe for the encoding step that largely determines HDC accuracy, importing decades of kernel design knowledge.

entry.title: Rigid-Covert GNSS Spoofing of UAV Swarms: A Structural Blind Spot, Its Detection Limit, and Absolute-Anchor Defenses

author.name: Minseok Park, Joon Soo Yoo

entry.summary: This paper shows that UAV swarm defenses that cross-check GNSS against measured inter-drone geometry have a structural blind spot: a slowly varying common translation preserves all pairwise distances and is therefore invisible to any relative-only detector. The authors derive a drift-dependent detection floor for anchor-residual detectors and propose absolute-anchor defenses.

entry.title: SkillEval: Decomposing Agent Skill Quality into Interpretable Signals

author.name: Jiahui Han, Qinuo Li, Ziheng Peng, Haotian Wu, Haoze Liu, Danfeng Shan, Guanchu Wang, Huiqi Deng, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: SkillEval evaluates agent skill documents directly rather than only through downstream task performance, arguing that downstream tests conflate skill quality with task compatibility and give no actionable improvement signal. It decomposes document-level quality into interpretable properties of the skill markdown file.

entry.title: Deal Me Maybe: The Role of Emotions in Multi-Agent Negotiation

author.name: Massimiliano Luca, Apoorva Singh, Bruno Lepri

entry.summary: Studies how prompt-assigned emotional states change LLM price-negotiation outcomes across 36 emotion pairings, five models, and 350 products. Finds large, role-dependent effects, for example angry buyers almost never closing deals while happy buyers close often but at worse prices.

entry.title: Debias in Text, Believe Your Eyes: Text-Anchored Cross-Modal Transfer for Visual Counter-Commonsense Reasoning

author.name: Chen Ling, Hanqian Li, Dongnan Liu, Keyu Qian, Jungang Li, Xinglong liu, Shiyi Wang, Xin Dong, Pengcheng Zhu, Wei Zhou, Linjian Mo, Nai Ding

entry.summary: Analyzes why multimodal models fail at counter-commonsense visual questions and finds the bottleneck is not perception: the correct answer is already in the decoding space, but the shared language decoder resolves conflicts in favor of dominant language priors. Proposes text-anchored debiasing transferred across modalities as a fix.

entry.title: Blind to the Pivotal Vote: Aggregate Independence Metrics Miss Where Verification Actually Helps

author.name: Yang Shu

entry.summary: Argues that aggregate measures of LLM judge-panel independence hide where extra evidence actually helps: adding an execution-based signal shows no effect on effective vote count, yet the entire accuracy gain concentrates in decisions with one-vote margins. Recommends targeting verification at pivotal ballots.

entry.title: Real-time Whole-Body Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators Carrying Arbitrarily Shaped Payloads via Kinematically-Coupled SVSDF

author.name: Yisheng Li, Longji Yin, Tingrui Zhang, Ruize Xue, Haoda Zhu, Nan Chen, Siqi Liang, Yuxi Liu, Fu Zhang

entry.summary: A real-time whole-body motion planner for mobile manipulators carrying arbitrarily shaped, non-convex payloads, using chain-decomposed kernel collision checks that preserve true geometry plus a staged pipeline that skips optimization when a trajectory is already collision-free. Addresses payload oversimplification and kinematic coupling that stall existing planners.

entry.title: Beyond Text Matching: Towards Reference-Free Evaluation for Human-Oriented Binary Reverse Engineering

author.name: Xiuwei Shang, Li Hu, Xiao Jiang, Jieke Shi, Junda He, Zhou Yang, Shaoyin Cheng, Guoqiang Chen, Weiming Zhang, David Lo

entry.summary: Studies reference-free evaluation of human-oriented binary reverse engineering outputs, where test execution and source references are usually unavailable, and assesses how well an LLM-as-judge setup substitutes for costly human review. Motivated by the failure of text-matching metrics to credit semantically equivalent but lexically different outputs.

entry.title: Human-Centered Explainable AI for TinyML Edge Devices: A Pareto-Based Selection Framework with LLM-Guided Design

author.name: Zeinab Dehghani, Dhavalkumar Thakker, Koorosh Aslansefat, Kuniko Paxton, Bhupesh Kumar Mishra, Baseer Ahmad and Rameez Raja Kureshi

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-objective, Pareto-based procedure for selecting explainability methods for TinyML deployments in clinical settings, using an LLM to help generate candidate designs and combining stakeholder preferences with explanation quality and deployment cost proxies. It frames XAI choice as a human-centered design optimization problem.

entry.title: A MARL Centered Reference Architecture for Large Language Model Augmentation in Smart Manufacturing

author.name: Fouad Bahrpeyma and Dirk Reichelt

entry.summary: A position and taxonomy paper mapping where large language models can augment or replace cooperative multi-agent RL coordination in smart manufacturing, organized around four attachment points: policy, reward design, inter-agent communication, and hierarchical planning. It also proposes a reference architecture.

entry.title: Representation Handoffs for OpenArm-Based Laboratory Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Yang Shen, Chonghao Cheng, Ziyi Zhao, Jialuo Zhu, Zhenyi Yi, Qi Zhao, Jian Yang, Yuhui Shi, Chin-Teng Lin

entry.summary: A field report on a laboratory mobile manipulator combining dual open-source arms, a mobile base, RGB-D and lidar sensing, and ROS2 execution, organized around structured handoffs from natural language to registered skill calls to grounded object poses and executable motion. It emphasizes constraining language into validated skills for safety.

entry.title: Beyond the Black Box: Interpretable Models of Human Randomisation Failures

author.name: Ngoc Linh Dao

entry.summary: Uses 84,060 decisions from a zero-sum card game to ask whether interpretable models can match black-box sequence models at predicting humans failing to randomize, and finds that transparent specifications with frequency-tracking extensions recover much of the predictive power while exposing the behavioral structure. It links behavioral game theory to interpretable machine learning.

entry.title: Geo-Spatial Concept Probing of Large Language Models: Abstraction, Compositionality, and Grounding

author.name: Karim Radouane and Jose G Moreno and Lynda Tamine

entry.summary: The authors build a controlled benchmark of spatial concepts such as direction, distance, and topology to probe whether LLMs possess abstraction, compositionality, and grounding rather than surface pattern matching. Question-answering tasks serve as the probe, isolating individual conceptual properties instead of conflating skills as natural-language benchmarks do.

entry.title: AI-amplified democratic backsliding: an exploration

author.name: casimirwypyski

entry.summary: A pilot index scoring countries by vulnerability to AI-amplified democratic backsliding along five pathways including labor displacement, information-environment pollution, elite defection, and concentration of coercive capacity. The authors present it explicitly as an early exploratory instrument and invite criticism of its construction.

entry.title: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Tokens: How Vision Language Models Cut AI Energy Costs While Improving Accuracy

author.name: Bhavika Jalli, Nikhil Korati Prasanna, Jayanta Choudhury

entry.summary: The paper argues that rendering multivariate telecom KPI time series as 2D plots and feeding them to vision-language models cuts input tokens by roughly 3.6 to 10.4 times versus raw numeric tokenization, with measured inference energy reductions of 1.8 to 2.5 times. A fine-tuned vision model reportedly matches or exceeds text-token accuracy while saving energy at edge deployments.

entry.title: Recovering Explanations from Transformed Rule-Based Ontologies

author.name: Alex Ivliev, Markus Kr\"otzsch, Maximilian Marx

entry.summary: Studies how to translate a proof of a derived fact under optimized, rewritten Datalog rules back into an explanation in terms of the original ontology rules. Establishes computational complexity of this proof-transformation problem and identifies two practical specification languages.

entry.title: TransSLR: A Lightweight Transformer for Sign Language Recognition

author.name: Lucia Yen Wanchi, Samuel Johnny, Victor Tolulope Olufemi, Emmanuel Aaron, Moise Busogi

entry.summary: Trains a small temporal transformer encoder from scratch on 64-frame normalized pose sequences for Central African Sign Language recognition, after showing that fine-tuning high-resource sign language models fails due to lexical and visual domain gaps. Targets a benchmark whose prior best accuracy was roughly 70 percent.

entry.title: CoDAT: Collaborative Dual-Attention Transformer with Low-Cost Temporal Modeling for Efficient Edge Action Recognition

author.name: Novendra Setyawan, Chi-Chia Sun, Mao-Hsiu Hsu, Wen-Kai Kuo, Jing-Ming Guo, Jun-Wei Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes an efficient video action recognition transformer for edge devices that replaces multi-head attention with a dual branch combining spatial convolutional attention for local aggregation and strided single-head attention for global context. Compresses query, key, and value tensors along both spatial and channel dimensions to fit latency, memory, and power budgets.

entry.title: UniCycleFlow: Bidirectional Unpaired Image Translation with a Shared Rectified Flow

author.name: Xianhao Zhou, Jianghao Wu, Shaoting Zhang, Guotai Wang

entry.summary: UniCycleFlow represents bidirectional unpaired image translation as forward and reverse integration of one shared time-conditioned velocity field, instead of two direction-specific generators linked by cycle consistency. This forces both directions to obey a common local transformation rule rather than only matching round-trip endpoints.

entry.title: Understanding Differentiable Embeddings Through Differential and Integral Geometry

author.name: Xinyu Zhang and Klaus Mueller

entry.summary: This paper shows that several seemingly unrelated diagnostics for judging trustworthiness of nonlinear dimensionality reduction, including projection glyphs, map-continuity scores and transport-based path inconsistencies, all derive from one geometric object induced by any differentiable embedding. It offers differential and integral views that unify local sensitivity and path-dependent behavior.

entry.title: Bend the Basics: Degradation-Aware Deformable Tokenization for All-in-One Image Restoration

author.name: Zihao He and Yunfeng Wu and Xinchao Wang and Songhua Liu

entry.summary: The Flexible Image Transformer makes all-in-one image restoration degradation-aware across the entire pipeline, from patch sampling to pixel reconstruction, instead of only injecting degradation conditioning into backbone blocks. A lightweight encoder predicts a global degradation vector and a spatial severity map that steer deformable tokenization.

entry.title: CEDAR: Agent-Orchestrated Tree Search for Goal-Directed Optimization of Complex Systems

author.name: Yingtao Tian

entry.summary: CEDAR uses LLM agents plus tree search to automatically design and tune complex feedback-driven system dynamics models toward a specified goal, replacing labor-intensive workflows in specialized modeling languages. It targets the artificial life challenge of predicting how feedback structure produces emergent behavior.

entry.title: How Should I Pick a Foundation Model for My Robot? In Favor of a Community Evaluation Framework for Social Robots

author.name: Eric Nichols, Alva Markelius, Hatice Gunes

entry.summary: This position paper argues that public leaderboards do not help researchers choose foundation models for social robots, since embodied real-time interaction demands fall outside their scope while direct human studies are too costly to run at scale. It proposes five evaluation dimensions including conversational competence, user safety, embodied character, scene effectiveness and audience appropriateness, arranged in a three-tier funnel from cheap general metrics to simulation to human studies.

entry.title: Does Splitting a Triage Decision Across Agents Hide Bias or Help Catch It? A Multi-Agent Simulation Study of LLM-Based Resource Allocation Under Audit Capacity Constraints

author.name: Paul-Peter Arslan

entry.summary: Simulates disaster triage with paired cases differing only in one demographic attribute and compares a single LLM decision-maker against a nine-agent pipeline with assessment, allocation, and independent audit roles under audit-capacity limits. Asks whether role decomposition surfaces or conceals demographic bias.

entry.title: Same physical state, different collective dynamics: state encodings select synchronization outcomes in language-model agents

author.name: Takahiro Ezaki, Naoto Imura and Katsuhiro Nishinari

entry.summary: Holds a physical synchronization task fixed while changing only how the environment state is encoded for LLM agents, comparing circular-moment summaries against histograms. Encoding choice flips collective outcomes entirely, synchronizing in all seeds under one encoding and none under the other, with the direction reversing between model families.

entry.title: Confirming Our Biases? Evaluating the Capabilities, Risks, and Societal Impact of Large Language Models

author.name: Mudar Adas, Polina Tsvilodub, Michael Franke, and Martin V. Butz

entry.summary: Evaluates six LLMs on 160 prompts across ten opinion and factual topics, varying whether prompts direct the model to support or challenge a position and what beliefs the user expresses. Maps the boundary between implicit framing effects and explicit prompt-driven agreement, i.e. sycophancy.

entry.title: FedDOSE: Federated Learning Framework Decomposing Site Effects for Modeling Brain Dynamic Functional Connectivity

author.name: Deepank Girish, Yi Hao Chan, Yubin Zheng, Sukrit Gupta, Jagath C. Rajapakse

entry.summary: FedDOSE is a federated learning framework for multi-site fMRI that explicitly decomposes scanner-site effects while modeling dynamic rather than static functional connectivity. A modularity-guided tensor decomposition block encodes high-dimensional dynamic connectivity under privacy constraints.

entry.title: Bootstrap validity in Bayesian semi-parametric models

author.name: Magid Sabbagh and David A. Stephens

entry.summary: Develops conditions under which Bayesian bootstrap and Dirichlet-process posteriors for a low-dimensional target parameter in semiparametric models are asymptotically normal and concentrate correctly. The work relaxes standard stochastic equicontinuity assumptions and traces which conclusions fail when assumptions are dropped.

entry.title: Unmasking Removal-Budget Confounding: A Matched Operating-Point Evaluation Framework for Adaptive Data Cleaning

author.name: Wei-Hsiang Chen, Pin-Hsuan Yu, Chen-Hsuan Fang, Jung-Hua Wang

entry.summary: Identifies removal-budget confounding in adaptive data cleaning, where changing partition granularity silently changes how many samples get discarded, so reported precision gains may reflect a smaller budget rather than better corruption detection. Proposes matched-budget and matched-recall controls plus threshold-independent metrics.

entry.title: Beyond Co-Movement: Locality by Exposures Enables a Joint Factor-Graph Framework for Portfolio Diversification

author.name: Sara Chehab, Giorgos Iacovides, Parisa Yazdanparast and Danilo Mandic

entry.summary: Proposes a portfolio construction framework that redefines graph locality in terms of shared systematic factor exposures instead of observed return co-movement, jointly regularizing factor and graph representations. Formalized as an alternating optimization that lets allocations act on underlying market structure rather than sample correlation artifacts.

entry.title: TA-RAG: Tone Awareness as a Design Imperative for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yong-Bin Kang and Anthony McCosker

entry.summary: Shows that retrieved documents impose their own communicative style on retrieval-augmented generation systems, often overriding explicit user tone instructions, a phenomenon the authors call contextual decoupling. Proposes a design approach that treats tone alignment as a first-class requirement alongside factual grounding, motivated by peer-support health communication.

entry.title: KReF: Training-Free Retrieval for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting and Predictive Uncertainty

author.name: Yang Zhang, Rui Su

entry.summary: KReF is a training-free probabilistic forecaster that retrieves historical lookback-future pairs and treats their similarity weights as an empirical predictive distribution, yielding quantiles, CRPS and point forecasts directly. It avoids the delayed-feedback problems of sequential conformal methods at long horizons.

entry.title: Progressive Alignment of Recommender Foundation Model through Multi-Phase Post-Training

author.name: Oseong Choi, Hoeinn Kim, Jihoon Lee, Byungsoo Kang, Taeyeong Jang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a three-phase post-training recipe for recommendation foundation models that separates downstream adaptation from business-metric alignment, using linear probing to stabilize new heads, then full fine-tuning, then alignment. It argues that optimizing click or like objectives does not align serving policies with actual business quality metrics.

entry.title: AdvTiles: Physical Adversarial Camouflage Clothing against Person Detectors via Learnable Tiles

author.name: Jinlei Wang, Jiahuan Long, Mingkai Sun, Yafei Guo, Yuanhao Huang, Ming Wang, Junqi Wu, Jiacheng Hou, Hongbo Chen, Xingxing Wei, Tingsong Jiang, Wen Yao

entry.summary: AdvTiles builds physical adversarial camouflage clothing from learnable tiles, using a straight-through Gumbel-Softmax estimator to jointly optimize which tile patterns are used and how they are laid out. This gives finer local control than optimizing a whole-body texture while keeping a natural camouflage appearance.

entry.title: Evolving Parallel Algorithm Portfolios via Potential-Aware Instance Generation with LLMs

author.name: Shaofeng Zhang, Shengcai Liu, Zhiyuan Wang, and Ke Tang

entry.summary: PIAC improves LLM-driven construction of parallel algorithm portfolios by co-evolving instances and algorithms without needing high-quality reference solutions. It introduces a potential-gain measure of instance hardness and diversifies generation beyond a single mode to improve few-shot generalization on combinatorial optimization.

entry.title: R2S-EGO: Dual-Proxy Refinement for Sparse-Capture Real-to-Sim

author.name: Shuai Fang, Xin Deng, Yuchen Kang, Zhenjiang Li, Jie Chen

entry.summary: R2S-EGO builds real-to-sim scene representations from sparse human capture by pairing a simulator-derived robot proxy that defines which viewpoints the robot will actually need with a capture-anchored geometry proxy that supplies structural conditioning for synthesized views. Fixed-budget view selection targets support deficits where geometry evidence exists.

entry.title: MiCoPro: End-to-End Mixed Precision HW/SW Co-design with HW-aware Proxy Model

author.name: Zijun Jiang and Yangdi Lyu

entry.summary: MiCoPro is an end-to-end framework for layer-wise mixed-precision quantization that uses a hardware-aware proxy model to predict the accuracy and speed effects of candidate bit-width assignments, plus a deployment path for edge devices. Aims to close the gap between MPQ search algorithms and actual hardware execution.

entry.title: A Rate Separation for Agnostic Direct Sums

author.name: Mihir More, Aritra Das, Debayan Gupta

entry.summary: Answers an open question about agnostic PAC learning of direct sums by exhibiting two classes with identical single-instance learning rates whose r-fold direct sums have different rates. Shows the single-instance curve does not determine the direct-sum curve.

entry.title: Explicit, Not Longer: What Makes Epistemic Stance Survive Memory Compression

author.name: Alex Kwon

entry.summary: Tests what makes a claim's epistemic hedging survive compression into agent memory, using matched notes that differ only in whether the stance is a labelled field or a parenthetical aside. Explicit labelled fields raise retention by roughly fifteen points across models, with a pre-registered replication.

entry.title: PHASE-Tree: Modeling Character-State Evolution in Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue

author.name: Bo Tang, Jianan Yang, Junyi Zhu, Yiquan Wu, Rui Zhao, Zhengyu Yang, Yang Zhang, Feiyu Xiong, Zhiyu Li, Jiajun Shen

entry.summary: PHASE-Tree represents role-play characters as a multi-timescale tree with an immutable identity root and mutable persona, session, and moment layers so traits can be updated locally without destabilizing the rest. Adds a benchmark that tests whether a model speaks from a character's currently evolved state rather than just preserving a static persona.

entry.title: Exact Thrust-Reversal Limits of Bidirectional Propellers under Bounded Motor Inputs

author.name: Ahmed Ali, Chiara Gabellieri, Antonio Franchi

entry.summary: Formalizes why bidirectional propellers cannot exactly track thrust trajectories that cross zero, since thrust is signed-quadratic in rotor speed and input authority vanishes at zero speed. Derives necessary and sufficient reproducibility conditions based on the order of the zero crossing, giving concrete design rules for shaping thrust reversals.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Reasoning Distillation of Large Language Models for Feedback Controller Design in Complex Dynamical Systems

author.name: Zhongchao Zhou, Yixuan Xie, Wenwei Yu, Yuxi Lu, Yaonan Zhu, Qian Niu, Yutaka Matsuo and Yusuke Iwasawa

entry.summary: CoDyControlBench evaluates LLMs on feedback controller design across 132 configurations spanning degrees of freedom, coupling, damping regime, and controller type, extending beyond the linear single-degree-of-freedom cases prior benchmarks used. It compares commercial and open models and distills reasoning into smaller models for edge deployment.

entry.title: Understand Before Detect: Vision--Language Learning for Omni-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Haoyang Yuan, Boyang Li, Yingqian Wang, Yimian Dai, Nuo Chen, Xinfei Huang, Shuqi Yi, Zaiping Lin, Weidong Sheng, and Wei An

entry.summary: Reframes cross-domain infrared small-target detection as an understanding task first, using vision-language learning to retain scene semantics that sparse target-only supervision discards. Aims to fix the sharp performance drop existing detectors suffer under domain shift.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Graph Embedders for Link Prediction and Topology Reconstruction

author.name: Robert Jankowski, Maksim Kitsak, Dorota Celi\'nska-Kopczy\'nska

entry.summary: Benchmarks 13 unsupervised hyperbolic graph embedding methods drawn from machine learning, network science, and algorithmics under one protocol for link prediction and topology reconstruction. Finds performance tracks embedding paradigm rather than disciplinary origin, with no method dominating everywhere.

entry.title: PHOENIX: Fine-Tuned SLM-Powered Autonomous Satellite Lifetime Extension via Predictive Self-Healing and Multi-Agent AI Recovery

author.name: Sumaiya Islam, Harsha Kumara Moraliyage

entry.summary: PHOENIX proposes running a fine-tuned small language model onboard a CubeSat so that faults occurring during the long out-of-contact stretch of each orbit can be diagnosed and acted on autonomously, with a multi-agent recovery workflow. The motivation is the high early-failure rate of small satellites.

entry.title: Reading Copom's Tone: A Weighted LLM Framework for Hawkish-Dovish Sentiment, Forward Guidance, and Uncertainty

author.name: Gabriel de Macedo Santos

entry.summary: Builds an LLM pipeline that scores Brazilian central bank statements for hawkish versus dovish tone, weighting sentence-level expressions by intensity and adding a document-level layer for forward guidance explicitness and uncertainty. It extends an existing bank sentiment classifier concept with intensity weighting and bounded indices.

entry.title: GeoDistill-Refine: Silhouette-First Geometry Distillation for Annotation-Free Spacecraft Segmentation

author.name: Yonglong Zhang, Zongwu Xie, Yang Liu

entry.summary: GeoDistill-Refine distills segmentation masks produced by a promptable foundation model into a compact spacecraft segmentation network without any human annotation, stabilizing the teacher by voting across six fixed prompts. A second stage refines the student with signed-distance, skeleton, and area objectives, and a reliability gate down-weights untrustworthy pseudo-masks.

entry.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools

author.name: Afreen Alam, Evgenija Popchanovska, Ana Gjorgjevikj, Maryan Rizinski, Lubomir T. Chitkushev, Irena Vodenska, Dimitar Trajanov

entry.summary: The paper maps the fragmented landscape of open-source LLM evaluation, red-teaming, guardrail, and observability tools onto risk taxonomies and governance frameworks, which currently use incompatible vocabularies. It proposes a structured protocol so organizations can determine which tools cover which risks and where gaps remain.

entry.title: Probabilistic Block Term Decomposition for the Modelling of Higher-Order Arrays

author.name: Jesper L{\o}ve Hinrich, Morten M{\o}rup

entry.summary: Proposes a variational Bayesian formulation of the Block Term Decomposition for tensors, using a von Mises-Fisher matrix prior to enforce orthogonality in the Tucker-like blocks. Demonstrated on synthetic and two real higher-order datasets.

entry.title: Mobile Interaction for Assessing Fatigue, Sleep, and Activity in Neurodegenerative and Chronic Diseases

author.name: Julian Fierrez, Alejandro Pe\~na, Aythami Morales, Ruben Tolosana, Ruben Vera-Rodriguez, Meenakshi Chatterjee, Ahmaniemi Teemu, Wan-Fai Ng, Walter Maetzler, Nikolay V. Manyakov, Jennifer Kudelka, Ralf Reilmann, C. Janneke van der Woude, Kristen Davies, Victoria Macrae, and IDEA-FAST Consortium

entry.summary: Explores using passively collected smartphone interaction data as an objective proxy for fatigue, sleep disturbance, and activity in patients with neurodegenerative and inflammatory diseases, as an alternative to infrequent self-report questionnaires. Part of a large multi-site clinical consortium effort.

entry.title: DREAMS: Diverse Reactions of Engagement and Attention Mind States Dataset

author.name: Monisha Singh, Gulshan Sharma, Ximi Hoque, Abhinav Dhall

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset of facial video from 32 participants watching emotion-eliciting stimuli, annotated for both engagement and attention states, to study how the two constructs relate. Intended for affective computing and learning-analytics research.

entry.title: When Semantics Saturate or Emerge: Adaptation-Conditional Semantic Utility in Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Wei Liu, Xing Deng, Haijian Shao

entry.summary: Asks whether text descriptions chosen for source-free cross-domain few-shot learning based on zero-shot accuracy remain useful after target-domain visual adaptation. Finds two regimes across four datasets, semantic saturation where large initial gains from detailed descriptions nearly vanish after low-rank adaptation, and cases where semantic benefit only emerges later.

entry.title: Ising Acceleration for Multi-Robot Multi-Target Planning

author.name: Ahmet Efe, Recep B. Uludag, Chris H. Kim, Ulya R. Karpuzcu

entry.summary: This study evaluates where real CMOS Ising machine chips fit in a multi-robot multi-target planning stack, examining target sharing, tour construction and pathfinding on 45-spin all-to-all devices. It proposes Ising-based planning formulations and a multi-mapping pipeline that reuses limited spin resources.

entry.title: ECAD: Expanding Class-Agnostic Detection Beyond Thing-Centric Objectness

author.name: Liang Wan, Zixin Ren, Yupeng Zhang, Yuhan Wang, Fangzhuo Gao

entry.summary: ECAD extends class-agnostic detection beyond countable objects to semantically meaningful regions such as sky, road, water and sports courts that current detectors absorb into background. The authors build a benchmark to support this expanded notion of objectness for scene understanding and spatial reasoning.

entry.title: RegionDet: A Benchmark for Region Detection Beyond Object Instances

author.name: Liang Wan, Yuhan Wang, Yupeng Zhang, Zhen Xu, Han Wang, Fangjie Fu, Sirui Zhu

entry.summary: RegionDet defines and benchmarks region detection, where targets are defined by visual state, context, relations or human activity, such as construction areas, damaged road segments, queues and group conversations, rather than by discrete object instances. It provides annotated data for systematically evaluating such localization.

entry.title: ZIPBrain: Can EEG Foundation Models Be Faster, Locally Deployable, but Accurate?

author.name: Lingwei Li, Yirong Kan, Peng Chen, Xu Cao, Zheng Chen, Yasuhiko Nakashima

entry.summary: ZIPBrain reduces the token count of EEG foundation models by partitioning tokens into redundant and unique groups and merging redundant ones, exploiting the low signal-to-noise character of EEG. Targets locally deployable, real-time clinical monitoring where quadratic attention cost is prohibitive.

entry.title: Towards Assurance Closure in AI-Native Large-Scale Agile Software Development

author.name: Ricardo Britto

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that agent-driven large-scale software engineering requires assurance closure: machine-operable reasoning about what must be true, what evidence supports it, and how uncertainty should bound agent authority. It surveys existing mechanisms across formal methods, testing, and runtime assurance and identifies six residual gaps.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Modeling Competitive Human Driving: A Cut-in Prediction Study

author.name: Yu Song

entry.summary: Compares game-theoretic inverse reinforcement learning models against a physics-based game-theoretic baseline for predicting aggressive cut-in lane changes, using the highD naturalistic driving dataset. Reports overall prediction accuracy above 75 percent with moderate cut-in precision.

entry.title: A Disturbance in the Force: Force Actuation on the RAVEN II Surgical Robot with Parallel Motor-Cable Units

author.name: Haonan Peng, Dun-Tin Chiang, Jordan Hendricks, Andrew Lewis, Jared Shing, Haokun Feng, Yun-Hsuan Su, and Blake Hannaford

entry.summary: Describes a parallel motor-cable rig with six units around a surgical robot workspace that applies controlled external forces to the end effector without obstructing motion. The system is intended to generate representative training data for learning-based force estimation, addressing the long-standing haptic feedback gap in surgical robotics.

entry.title: CertBind from Multimodal Connectivity to Certifiable Retrieval Decisions

author.name: Shuheng Cao, Zhenhao Zhang, Ruiqi Chen, Renjie Cao, Weijia Zhang, Siyu Zhang, Jiaxin Liu, Xiangyu Zeng, Haotian Geng, Fan Gu

entry.summary: Proposes a multiscale theory for composing frozen multimodal encoders through lightweight connectors while certifying that added cross-modal reach does not silently degrade native retrieval. Combines conformal rank control, overlap-aware calibration budgets, and finite-sample recovery radii to yield covered top-k candidate sets.

entry.title: KNOWPLAN: Knowledge-Driven AI Agents for Smart Degree Pathway Planning

author.name: Shuheng Cao, Weijia Zhang, Jiaqi Wu, Xiyun Hu, Yat Yang, Juqy Chen, Zhaoxiang Feng

entry.summary: Builds an agent system for university degree planning that strictly separates catalog extraction from student-specific path optimization, so a planner cannot mask extraction failures by only crawling what its current plan needs. Includes a confidence-scored exploration policy over atomic catalog actions and measures the interface between stages.

entry.title: Beyond Starry Night: Shortcut-Aware Control-State Planning for Artist-Grounded Text to Image Generation

author.name: Kuan Xing, Ye Wang, Changyi Gan, Yuheng Li, Thao Nguyen, Yi Chang, and Yilin Wang

entry.summary: Atelier addresses the tendency of image models to answer artist-name prompts with canonical shortcuts such as recurring motifs and stock palettes instead of honoring the user scene. It compiles artistic intent into an explicit control state separating scene anchors, preserve or transform decisions, style hypotheses and shortcut-avoidance constraints, then iteratively refines candidates.

entry.title: LiFTER: A Grounded Neuro-Symbolic Microscope for Continuous-Time Dynamic Graph Forecasting

author.name: Minwoo Yu, Young-guk Ha

entry.summary: LiFTER predicts links in continuous-time dynamic graphs using executable temporal rules applied to preserved grounded facts, so each score is a signed sum of rule executions with inspectable entity bindings and temporal ordering. Interpretability is built into the predictor rather than added afterward.

entry.title: Calibrating WEAT Against Anisotropy: ZCA Whitening as a Geometric Pre-Processing Step for Embedding Association Tests

author.name: Seitaro Ono, Senna Ross, Jun Saiki

entry.summary: Proposes ZCA whitening as a preprocessing step before running the Word Embedding Association Test, arguing that anisotropic embedding geometry undermines cosine-based bias measurement. Evaluated across ten standard models and bias tests.

entry.title: Summarize First, Download Later: Onboard VLMs for Bandwidth-Efficient Earth Observation

author.name: Junghwan Park, Sangcheol Sim, Woojin Cho, Darongsae Kwon

entry.summary: Proposes downlinking quantized onboard VLM summaries of satellite imagery first, letting ground operators ask visual questions to verify relevance, and only then requesting full raw scenes. Targets the bandwidth and contact-window bottleneck in Earth observation.

entry.title: When One Modality Is Not Enough: Multimodal Sex and Life-Stage Classification of Red Deer from Aerial RGB-Thermal Video

author.name: Hugo Markoff, Christoph Praschl, Ivan Ludo\v{s}ki, Sara Beery, Michael {\O}rsted, David C. Schedl

entry.summary: Classifies sex and life stage of red deer from high-altitude drone video by fusing RGB and thermal streams, motivated by the fact that the two modalities fail under opposite conditions such as canopy cover versus loss of fine detail. Goes beyond counting toward herd composition estimates managers actually need.

entry.title: Local Epistemic Uncertainty Guided Active Sampling for Plug-and-play Diffusive Image Restoration

author.name: Jiaqi Zhang, Zheng Pang, Rongrong Gao, Qiyuan Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: LEADer uses pixel-wise epistemic uncertainty to guide both spatial data constraints and adaptive step sizes in plug-and-play diffusion image restoration, replacing fixed constraints and uniform sampling schedules. Aims to handle spatially non-uniform degradation while cutting redundant sampling steps.

entry.title: Identifying the Key Biomechanical Features of Movement Adaptation during Exoskeleton-Assisted Locomotion

author.name: Peter Seungjune Lee and Katja Mombaur

entry.summary: Analyzes how nine participants biomechanically adapt over time to ankle exoskeleton assistance versus zero-torque and no-exoskeleton walking, tracking kinematics, inter-joint coordination, and metabolic cost. The finding is that adaptation is gradual and strongly individualized.
