entry.summary: A large factorial study (1.2 million trials, five open-weight models, 500 medical questions) showing that medical sycophancy, where a model abandons a correct answer under pushback, is driven by conversational context such as user role, evidence framing and challenge timing rather than being a fixed per-model rate. It argues single-number sycophancy scores are misleading.

entry.title: Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Xingyu Dang, Rui-Jie Zhu, Zixin Wen, Hengyu Fu, Wenhao Chai, Jason D. Lee

entry.summary: Test-Time Context Distillation trains fast weights during inference using a long-window teacher to supervise a short-window student, so the online update learns which information will be useful later rather than just reconstructing the past. It reframes test-time training for long context as a memory-allocation problem with a future-utility objective.

entry.title: LLMs Can Annotate Attribution Graphs

author.name: Ameen Patel, Max Zhang, Nathan Hu

entry.summary: Automates the labor-intensive manual step in circuit tracing by prompting a language model with feature descriptions to group features into supernodes, showing the automated groupings score as interpretable as human ones. On a two-hop capitals task the pipeline recovers the intermediate-hop supernode in 97 of 100 prompts and supports open-ended circuit exploration.

entry.title: In-Context Collapse in Vision-Language Models and How to Mitigate it?

author.name: Mohammad Rostami

entry.summary: The paper documents in-context collapse: as the number of image-label demonstrations grows, several vision-language models suffer sharp, sometimes below-chance accuracy drops while still producing well-formed answers. The effect is measured across open models from 0.5B to 11B plus an existing frontier model (Claude Sonnet 4.5, available since late 2025), and the authors argue robustness to long demonstration sets is dissociable from actual in-context rule learning.

entry.title: Qwen-3D: A Generalist 3D Vision-Language Model for Spatial Understanding

author.name: Lucy Lin, Ayush Jain, Yifan Liu, Katerina Fragkiadaki

entry.summary: Qwen-3D is a generalist 3D vision-language model that fuses depth and camera pose into a persistent world-aligned representation so long video streams can be compressed geometrically rather than frame by frame. The authors argue prior 3D LMMs lag specialist perception systems because they emit 3D predictions through language tokens, and introduce geometry-aware decoding for grounding and segmentation.

entry.title: JoyAI-Video-Edit: Real-Time Open-Ended Video Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion

author.name: Yicheng Xiao, Wenxun Dai, Xinran Qin, Lin Song, Maoquan Zhang, Hang Xu, Yukang Chen, Yitong Li, Guohui Zhang, Yuan Zhang, Xuying Zhang, Tommy Zhang, Jianlong Yuan, Peihao Li, Shuai Lu, Siming Fu, Chuyang Zhao, Xin Han, Jie Huang, Wenbo Li, Guoqing Ma, Wei Huang, Xiaojuan Qi, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan

entry.summary: JoyAI-Video-Edit is a 16-billion-parameter autoregressive diffusion system for real-time open-ended video editing with no access to future frames, combining chunk-wise autoregressive adaptation, source-anchored distribution matching distillation, and long-horizon distillation. The distillation choices are designed to keep two-step generation faithful to the source and limit temporal drift.

entry.title: Principles of Robot Autonomy

author.name: Daniele Gammelli, Joseph Lorenzetti, Katie Luo, Gioele Zardini, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: Principles of Robot Autonomy is a book-length unified treatment of modern autonomy stacks from a well-known Stanford group, spanning classical robotics through contemporary physical AI, with hands-on notebooks and exercises for each topic. It consolidates decades of course material into a single conceptual framework.

entry.title: Unified Visuomotor Targets: Supervising VLAs Beyond Physical Actions

author.name: Zhenyang Feng, Unnat Jain

entry.summary: Proposes UVT, a unified latent supervision target for vision-language-action models that jointly encodes low-level motor commands and visual scene-transition information, so the policy predicts something closer to what a VLM already represents. The change requires no architecture modification or extra data and improves two representative VLA systems in simulation and real bimanual manipulation.

entry.title: The benefits of medical AI assistance vary based on user expertise

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: An MIT-led user study on skin-disease diagnosis finds that AI assistance helps both novices and primary care clinicians, but explainability methods affect them very differently. Non-experts improved mainly by deferring to the model and found vague or generic LLM explanations more convincing regardless of correctness, whereas clinicians were less easily misled.

entry.title: Measuring in-context algorithmic reasoning in language models against an exact Bayes-optimal standard

author.name: Hector Zenil, Luan Ozelim

entry.summary: F-ICL benchmarks in-context algorithmic reasoning against an exactly computable Bayes-optimal posterior, by exhaustively enumerating 1.5 billion programs of a Turing-complete machine under a bounded universal prior and pairing every task with its bitwise complement to control for polarity bias. It measures how far model distributions sit from provably optimal inductive inference.

entry.title: Any-OPD: Heterogeneous On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Matching Models via Representation-Space Bridging

author.name: Siming Fu, Zheming Fu, Ruizhe He, Hualiang Wang, Jie Huang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Mingchen Zhong, Weihu Huang, Xiaoxuan He, Haojun Xu

entry.summary: Any-OPD tackles on-policy distillation when teacher and student flow-matching generators come from different families with incompatible VAE latents, architectures, and timestep schedules. It bridges the mismatch in representation space rather than pixel or latent space, which is where standard recipes break down.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Testing the Predictive Validity of Commonsense Benchmarks

author.name: Ine Gevers, Walter Daelemans

entry.summary: The authors test whether widely used commonsense benchmarks actually predict downstream performance, evaluating 23 models across six families on original benchmarks, reworked variants, non-commonsense controls, and eight applied reasoning tasks. They use leave-one-family-out cross-validation and controlled correlations to assess criterion validity, finding rankings largely stable but predictive value questionable.

entry.title: UniWorld-Design: From Pixel Generation to Layer-Native Design

author.name: Zongjian Li, Zhiyuan Yan, Chenxu Bai, Chen Chen, Haoxiang Sun, Shaodong Wang, Feize Wu, Shenghai Yuan, Bin Lin, Zheyuan Liu, Yuwei Niu, Li Yuan

entry.summary: UniWorld-Design shifts image generation from flat pixel synthesis to layer-native composition, using semantic RGBA layers as the atomic unit for generation, understanding, and editing. It pairs a text-to-RGBA asset generator with an image-to-layer decomposition model conditioned on a finished image and instructions.

entry.title: Scoring Rules! Statistical and Strategic Alignment for Text Evaluation Metrics

author.name: Shengwei Xu, Yuxuan Lu, Yifan Wu, Jason Hartline, Grant Schoenebeck

entry.summary: Distinguishes statistical alignment (correlation with human ratings) from strategic alignment (resistance to information-free gaming) for reference-based text metrics, and proposes tests grounded in proper scoring rules. Matters as metrics increasingly serve as optimization targets rather than just measurements.

entry.title: FOCUS: FP4 Optimization via Coupled-Relaxation and Dual-Granularity Scaling

author.name: Xianglong Yan, Hong Liu, Chengzhu Bao, Tianao Zhang, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: FOCUS is a post-training FP4 quantization method that decouples quantization from dequantization scales, noting the quantization scale is never stored and therefore need not follow the hardware low-precision format such as E8M0. Adds dual-granularity scaling to recover accuracy under MXFP4 and NVFP4.

entry.title: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories

author.name: Shuai Shao, Kangning Zhang, Qingyao Li, Shijian Wang, Hao Wang, Wenxiang Jiao, Yuan Lu, Yi Guo, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Harness-R1 post-trains a 9B harness engineer with online RL to edit an agent's executable runtime scaffolding (context construction, tool mediation, action validation, recovery) based on batches of observed failure trajectories, optimizing edits for realized downstream task success. Shifts self-improvement from model weights to the surrounding harness.

entry.title: MechGeo: Autoformalizing and Proving Euclidean Geometry in Lean 4

author.name: Hao Shen, Junyu Guo, Tian Cui, Yuxuan Xiao, Lihong Zhi

entry.summary: MechGeo is a Mathlib-native agentic framework that autoformalizes Euclidean geometry problems into Lean 4 through an intermediate representation with iterative repair, then constructs certified proofs by planning, lemma derivation, and selective algebraization with kernel-checked certificates. Reports gains in both autoformalization and proving across seven LLM backbones.

entry.title: Long-term Measurements: Towards a Longitudinal Understanding of Human-AI Interactions

author.name: Nicole Mitchell, Dhruv Agarwal, Maty Bohacek, Remi Denton, Roma Patel

entry.summary: Argues NLP evaluation must shift from static short-term generation tests to longitudinal measurement of cognitive, developmental, and socio-affective change in users, drawing constructs and instruments from social science. Proposes a research agenda for diachronic understanding of human-model interaction.

entry.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies

author.name: Qiushi Lin, Chaojie Zhang, \'I\~nigo Goiri, Aditya Akella, Ricardo Bianchini, Jovan Stojkovic

entry.summary: AtumAI adds formal problem specification, transferable knowledge across tasks, and systematic candidate generation to agentic search for datacenter control-plane policies, addressing the tendency of off-the-shelf LLM agents to explore narrowly and violate hard constraints. Aims to compress months-long policy prototyping cycles.

entry.title: TabDPT-Turbo: Efficient In-Context Learning for Tabular Prediction

author.name: Rasa Hosseinzadeh, Alex Labach, Zexin Xue, Shuyi Han, Valentin Thomas, Anthony L. Caterini

entry.summary: TabDPT-Turbo keeps row-based attention for tabular in-context learning but adds long-context pretraining to remove the need for retrieval, plus architectural changes and self-supervised pretraining on a larger real-data corpus. It matches the previous TabDPT quality on TabArena-Lite, CC18 and CTR23 at orders of magnitude lower inference cost.

entry.title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code

author.name: Yuqiao Tan, Jinxiang Meng, Fangyu Lei, Minzheng Wang, Shizhu He, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: SWE-Touch is a benchmark framework that stress-tests coding agents in shared workspaces by injecting validated counter-edits, plausible human modifications to task-critical code that conflict with the agent plan. It measures whether agents notice, interpret, and adapt to concurrent user changes rather than assuming exclusive control of the repository.

entry.title: Maglev: Sliding Recurrent Memory

author.name: Bo Liu, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: Maglev is a recurrent transformer with fixed-size memory that generalizes sliding-window attention while staying parallelizable in training, by pairing a full-attention prefiller that produces memory targets with a sliding-window decoder trained under a memory-consistency loss. It offers a route to constant-memory long-context decoding without abandoning transformer training efficiency.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

author.name: Mohsen Hariri, Weicong Chen, Nahal Shahini, Vikash Singh, Kai Ye, Amirhossein Samandar, Debargha Ganguly, Sreehari Sankar, Yanyan Zhang, Shouren Wang, Jerry Peng, Biyao Zhang, Michael Hinczewski, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: A systematic account of test-time scaling that separates sequential deliberation, parallel sampling with aggregation, and search over partial states, arguing these differ in statistical structure, compute accounting, and failure modes. It calls out the practice of collapsing them under a single scalar budget and reporting accuracy without the inference protocol.

entry.title: Track4Action: Distilling World-Centric 3D Tracker into Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Chenyi Wang, Xinkai Wang, Bokai Lin, Jialin Tian, Fucheng Zhang, Cewu Lu, Lixin Yang

entry.summary: Track4Action distills a frozen world-centric 3D tracker into a VLA policy so that the policy internalizes how commanded actions actually change 3D geometry, motion and visibility. Learnable track queries predict the tracker embedding from current hidden states and condition a flow-matching action head, adding geometric supervision without needing the tracker at inference.

entry.title: Rewriting or Reweighting? A Geometric Account in Language Models

author.name: Juntong Wang, Shengkun Yang, Xiyuan Wang, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces behavioral manifold analysis to determine whether post-training removes a mechanism, creates a new one, or reuses an inherited one, studying repetition loops and sycophancy. Builds low-dimensional charts over both runtime activations and information-routing strength.

entry.title: Robust Watermarks Meet Backdoored Models: Evading Diffusion Semantic Watermarks via Stealthy Backdoor

author.name: Jinyuan Liu, Tianshuo Cong, Pei Li, Tianrui Wang, Xinlei He, Anyu Wang, Xiaoyun Wang

entry.summary: GhostVAE plants a stealthy backdoor in the VAE encoder used by latent diffusion watermark detection pipelines, first building a universal trigger with power-spectrum regularization for robustness then training a parameter-aligned backdoored encoder, so semantic watermarks can be reliably evaded. It shows that the neural components of detection pipelines are themselves an attack surface across three state-of-the-art semantic watermarking schemes.

entry.title: RING: Retrieval-Internalized Generation for Continual Large-Scale Knowledge Injection

author.name: Shicheng Xu, Liang Pang, Liyi Chen, Zihao Wei, Jingcheng Deng, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: RING replaces external retrieval by injecting large corpora into a Mixture-of-Memory-Experts architecture using a dual causal attention pretraining stage, then teaching a search-then-answer pattern and optimizing internal routing with hierarchical-reward RL. The goal is RAG-level factuality with no retriever at serving time.

entry.title: DUD: Decoupled Update Dynamics for Reliable Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models

author.name: Yixin Bu, Runze Xia, Guanyun Zou, Yupeng Ji, Haodong Liu, Piji Li

entry.summary: DUD improves LLM uncertainty quantification by separating feed-forward network updates (parametric memory) from attention updates (contextual processing) in the residual stream rather than aggregating them. The claim is that memory-context misalignment revealed by this decoupling is a stronger mechanistic signal of epistemic uncertainty than aggregate hidden-state dynamics.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Price Competitively? A Dynamic Multi-Attribute Auction Benchmark for Agentic Commerce

author.name: Shimaa Ahmed, Yiwei Cai, Mohsen Minaei, Rahul Rachuri

entry.summary: Bazaar is a dynamic sealed-bid multi-attribute auction benchmark testing whether LLM agents can price competitively when customer preferences are hidden, rivals adapt, and demand shifts, with closed-form customer utilities enabling exact scoring. Across 11 frontier models from four providers, agents strongest at winning customers are not necessarily strongest at profit, revealing a share-versus-margin tradeoff. This is timely given payment networks and retailers building agentic commerce infrastructure.

entry.title: Where did the ambiguity go? Examining how multimodal models interpret polysemous words

author.name: Jasin Cekinmez, Addison J. Wu, Raja Marjieh, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: Across 17 text-to-image and 15 text-generation models, this study gives each model a polysemous word with no disambiguating context and measures the distribution of senses produced across many samples. Generated images collapse onto far fewer senses than generated sentences (normalized entropy roughly 0.10 versus 0.25), and both are far less diverse than human imagination. The finding documents a systematic multimodal loss of semantic ambiguity.

entry.title: Humans Are More Diverse: Frontier LLMs Show Extreme Policies in Idealised AI Development Races

author.name: Phu Hoa Pham, Duy Minh Dao Sy, Trung Kiet Huynh, Phu Quy Nguyen Lam, Chi Nguyen Tran, Minh Trung Le, Phong Hao Le, Dinh Nam Nguyen, Thien Ky Nguyen Dong, Elias Fernandez Domingos, Le Hong Trang, The Anh Han

entry.summary: Uses a repeated AI-development-race game to test whether frontier LLM agents behave safely or aggressively, adding an audit gate that verifies rule recall, state tracking, and payoff computation before interpreting behavior. Finds models adopt extreme, low-diversity policies compared with human data and evolutionary game-theory baselines.

entry.title: Reusing Rollouts under Policy Lag: Prefix-Normalized Policy Optimization for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenhao Zhang, Yibo Xie, Rui Wang, Jiahua Yang, Lei Jiang, Zibo Yang, Yawei Wang, Jiali Xu, jasperawang, Haoyang Long, Huan Xiong, alantzhao

entry.summary: Prefix-Normalized Policy Optimization reuses RL rollout batches for extra learner updates by replacing the exploding cumulative importance ratio with a geometric mean of likelihood ratios along each causal prefix. Aims to keep off-policy correction stable while amortizing expensive generation.

entry.title: SearchMaster: Grounded and Regulated Self-Play for Search Agents

author.name: Wentao Tan, Qiong Cao, Jiaqi Wang, Nan Duan

entry.summary: SearchMaster trains a search agent purely from tasks it generates, solves, and verifies in a local search environment, with three controls to filter pseudo multi-hop questions, depth-blind difficulty estimates, and evidence-poor rollouts. Removes dependence on human tasks or stronger teacher models.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Autonomous Architecture Research with a Language-Model Agent: A Behavioural Case Study

author.name: Aon Safdar, Mohamed Saadeldin

entry.summary: A behavioural case study in which one general LLM agent, given compute, tooling, literature access, and persistent memory, autonomously runs about 100 sequential experiments to improve a nonstandard Vision Transformer from a weak baseline. Documents phases of expanding tool surface and reports where the agent shows research discipline versus drift.

entry.title: EduZone: A Framework for Evaluating LLM Safety for K-12 Students and Teachers

author.name: Junyeong Park, Jieun Han, Haneul Yoo, So-Yeon Ahn, Jinsung Yoon, Alice Oh

entry.summary: EduZone is a safety evaluation framework for LLMs in K-12 contexts, combining student- and teacher-facing scenarios, fine-grained curriculum concepts, and 6 risk categories with 28 subcategories to generate contextually grounded adversarial interactions across single-turn, static multi-turn, and interactive settings. Fills a gap where generic safety benchmarks miss education-specific harms.

entry.title: SKT: Skill-Use Training at Scale via Verified Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Zelin Tan, Yiqun Zhang, Hao Li, Zhiyao Cui, Hejia Geng, Shao Zhang, Hangfan Zhang, Yang Chen, Xiaosong Wang, Lilong Wang, Zhenfei Yin, Shuyue Hu, Chen Zhang, Lei Bai

entry.summary: SKT synthesizes skill-grounded tasks and verified executable trajectories from 2,000 public agent skills, using rule-based and agent-based verification with feedback-guided repair and keeping only trajectories that genuinely exercise every required skill. Yields thousands of task packages and trajectories for training skill-use capability.

entry.title: xPress: Parallel Refinement for Diffusion Drafters in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Zheng Wang, Davis Wertheimer, Yu Chin Fabian Lim, Mudhakar Srivatsa, Raghu K. Ganti, Minjia Zhang, Naigang Wang

entry.summary: xPress improves speculative decoding with block-diffusion drafters by refining draft blocks so tokens are not sampled as independent per-position marginals, which otherwise produce individually likely but jointly improbable sequences that trigger early rejection. Aims to raise acceptance length without giving up single-pass drafting speed.

entry.title: Relax Within, Balance Across: Geometry-Guided Load Balancing for Vision-Language Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Ziang Wu, Peng Jin, Qishen Yin, Munan Ning, Hao Li, Peizhen Zhang, Li Yuan

entry.summary: The authors show that the standard token-level auxiliary load-balancing loss in vision-language mixture-of-experts models balances only the mixed image-plus-text load, so large image and text imbalances can cancel at one token mix, and the same trained router shows more than fivefold variation in load imbalance across image resolutions. They derive the exact load curve as the token mix varies and propose a geometry-guided remedy that relaxes within modality while balancing across modalities.

entry.title: Temperature-driven inversion and nonlinear dynamics in ChatGPT-like AIs

author.name: Neil F. Johnson, Frank Yingjie Huo, Bella Xinrui Li

entry.summary: Studies decoder temperature in LLMs as a physics-style control parameter and reports that, unlike ordinary thermodynamic systems, autoregressive feedback pushes long output populations through an entropy maximum into a population-inverted regime with frozen states, cycles and intermittency. The authors identify a hidden coordinate whose trajectory average predicts output repetition across 11 models and 12,000 continuations.

entry.title: ReBRAC-v2: The Return of the King

author.name: Denis Tarasov, Robert K. Katzschmann

entry.summary: ReBRAC-v2 modernizes a simple behavior-regularized actor-critic for offline RL by using an exact-likelihood normalizing flow actor, combined likelihood/MSE/MAE regularization, a classification-based residual critic and multi-sample test-time action selection, all under one shared hyperparameter configuration. It argues classic methods can match expressive diffusion-policy approaches.

entry.title: Why Formal Monitors Fail: Attack Distribution Entropy as a Coverage Bound for LTL-Based LLM Agent Safety

author.name: Ruiyang Zhang

entry.summary: Proves that the recall of any fixed-invariant finite-automaton runtime safety monitor for LLM agents is upper bounded by the concentration of the attack distribution, explaining why identical LTL monitors get 68 to 75 percent coverage on some models and near zero on others. It ties monitor effectiveness to the Shannon entropy of attack trigger patterns.

entry.title: AnchorKV: Anchor-Residual KV Cache Compression

author.name: Malik Khalaf, Yara Shamshoum, Nitzan Hodos, Yuval Sieradzki, Assaf Schuster

entry.summary: AnchorKV compresses the key-value cache about twentyfold without evicting any token, by storing a small set of exact anchors, representing other tokens through their nearest anchor, and selectively refining those whose approximation most affects the output. It positions itself between lossy eviction and mildly compressive quantization.

entry.title: PI-Mem: Pushing Long-Context Reasoning to 3.6M Tokens with Parallel-Iterative Memory

author.name: Dawei Liu, Haixu Song, Shuang Cheng, Shijie Wang, Haozheng Hou, Kaifeng Liu, Ermo Hua, Zhonghang Yuan, Zhijie Zhong, Yuchen Fan, Biqing Qi, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: PI-Mem replaces sequential recurrent memory updates with parallel reads over all context chunks followed by a bounded number of iterative refinement turns on a shared compact memory, avoiding both overwriting of early evidence and serial latency growth. Reported to push long-context reasoning to roughly 3.6 million tokens. Addresses two acknowledged weaknesses of recurrent-memory long-context approaches.

entry.title: Predicting Multilingual Classification and Translation Performance of LLMs with Cross-Lingual Alignment $\unicode{x2013}$ Is English Enough?

author.name: Adnan Al Ali, Kathy H\"ammerl, Jind\v{r}ich Libovick\'y, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: An interactive Alien Abduction game probes how LLMs actively gather evidence, revise hypotheses, and decide when to stop during abductive inference, varying whether evidence arrives upfront or across turns and who chooses the queries. Models perform worse when they must acquire information themselves across turns, revealing deficits in active information seeking.

entry.title: Self-Organising Digital Circuits

author.name: Marcello Barylli, Gabriel B\'ena, Alexander Mordvintsev, Eleni Nisioti, Sebastian Risi

entry.summary: Self-Organising Digital Circuits frames the generation and repair of Boolean logic as meta-learning on graphs, using a topology-masked Transformer to configure lookup tables of logic gates in the spirit of neural cellular automata. The aim is biologically inspired adaptive fault tolerance that reorganizes around damage rather than relying on static redundancy.

entry.title: PhyAI: Real-Time Physical AI at the Edge, Scalable Rollouts in the Cloud

author.name: Chenghua Wang, Daliang Xu, Dongqi Cai, Duojin Sun, Hao Zhang, Haoze Qian, Huaiyuan Zhang, Jinshuo Cui, Kezhao Zhao, Longxi Gao, Mengwei Xu, Rongjie Yi, Tianyue Zhang, Weikai Xie, Xiyuan Tan, Xuanzhe Liu, Yingying Qin, Yiwen Lu, Yuan Yao, Yuezhi Zu, Yunhan Guo, Ziqi Guo

entry.summary: PhyAI is a unified inference runtime for physical-AI policies that serves the same checkpoint across onboard robots, edge GPUs and cloud RL rollout fleets, using model adapters for architecture-specific solver, cache and conditioning logic while sharing kernels and memory management. It supports both VLA and world-action models on single or multiple GPUs.

entry.title: When Many Answers Are Valid, Voting Fails: Symbolic Verification for Best-of-K Causal Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Omatharv Bharat Vaidya, Connor Thomas Jerzak, Zayne Rea Sprague, Fangcong Yin, Nhat Ho

entry.summary: Argues that self-consistency voting breaks down for causal reasoning because sampled traces share confounding errors and because votes split across several equally valid answers. CALVER is a training-free symbolic verifier that scores structured reasoning traces against Pearl-style criteria such as d-separation and backdoor adjustment, outperforming plurality voting, a reward model and an LLM judge on multi-valid-answer benchmark queries.

entry.title: Bayesian and Motivated Reasoning in AI Agents

author.name: Eddie Yang

entry.summary: This study shows that AI agents reach different conclusions from numerically identical evidence when the surrounding framing changes, testing twelve agent-domain combinations in medicine, election forensics, and geopolitical forecasting. Agents affirm propositions they already consider likely and resist those conflicting with their priors, exhibiting motivated rather than purely Bayesian reasoning. This matters because such agents are increasingly used to inform consequential decisions.

entry.title: No Single Neuron of Failure: Distributed Safety Alignment Against White-Box Attacks

author.name: Simiao Xie, Chuancheng Shi, Shangze Li, Wenhua Wu, Fei Shen, Ying Zhou, Zhiyong Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Distributed Safety Alignment redundantly encodes refusal behavior across many neurons in feed-forward down-projection inputs so that white-box attacks ablating a few identified safety neurons cannot remove alignment. Targets the fragility of open-weight models to neuron-level manipulation.

entry.title: When Memory Becomes Authority: Benchmarking Authority Collapse at the Memory Consolidation Boundary

author.name: Qiuyang Zhan, Rui Zhang, Sheng Guo, Lepeng Zhao, Zhuotao Liu

entry.summary: Identifies authority collapse, where memory consolidation keeps a claim but drops the source constraints that limited how it may be used, so stored memories later act as trusted facts or standing instructions. AuthMem-Bench holds the claim fixed while varying only source authority.

entry.title: Deferred Exposure of Future Trajectories for Verifiable Reasoning in Autonomous Driving VLMs

author.name: Zixuan Huang, Yang Zhou, Kaixuan Wang, Guli Zhang, Hongyan Xie, Yakun Zhu, Hao Geng, Xiaozhi Chen, Yikun Ban, Deqing Wang

entry.summary: Shows that annotating driving chain-of-thought while exposing the teacher to the logged ground-truth future trajectory causes trajectory anchoring bias, with teachers rationalizing known outcomes and hallucinating more in causally hard scenes. Proposes deferring trajectory exposure to keep reasoning causally faithful while separating decision from trajectory generation.

entry.title: Beyond the Mean: Multi-Moment Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yijun Zhang, Yule Xie, Jiaxin Ding, Xin Ding, Fan Xu, Haoxiang Zhang, Luoyi Fu

entry.summary: Reframes RL for LLM reasoning as optimizing moments of the per-problem failure-probability distribution, observing that common methods optimize only a single moment. Proposes Multi-Moment Policy Optimization to shape higher-order structure such as variance across problems.

entry.title: Faster-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Deep Action Modules?

author.name: Liheng Ma, Rui Heng Yang, Zhanguang Zhang, Mateo Clemente, Ziwen Hu, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: Faster-WAM applies a Dock of Transformer principle to world action models, treating a pretrained video Transformer as a representation hub and docking a shallow action head with access to all backbone layers instead of mirroring backbone depth. Cuts compute and inference latency for coupled video-prediction and action-prediction models.

entry.title: Agentic Commerce World: An Auditable and Verifiable Environment for Vibe Commerce

author.name: Shicheng Fan, Mingdai Yang, Duohao Wang, Canyu Chen, Yongfeng Zhang, Hua Wei, Manling Li, Julian McAuley, Kun Zhang, Philip S. Yu, Kejing Yu, Zhiwei Liu

entry.summary: Agentic Commerce World is a simulated marketplace where independently controlled buyer and merchant agents transact under a Vibe Commerce Protocol that validates actions before updating shared state, making agent behavior auditable and evaluation reproducible. Targets natural-language delegated commerce with private objectives and distinct authority.

entry.title: Neural Circuit Function Inference with LLMs

author.name: Yijie Yin (Department of Physiology, Development and Neuroscience, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK, MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge, UK), Albert Cardona (MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge, UK, Department of Physiology, Development and Neuroscience, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK)

entry.summary: LLantia uses LLMs to distill cell-type function descriptions from the literature and combine them with connectome connectivity to infer functions of uncharacterized cell types and whole neural circuits, structured hierarchically under alternative behavioural and physiological contexts. Aims to move connectomics from mapping to interpretation.

entry.title: Which Modality Decides? Counterfactual Modality Attribution for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Vahidin Hasic, Chao Wang, Luis C. Garcia-Peraza-Herrera, David Watson, Senka Krivic

entry.summary: Counterfactual Modality Attribution quantifies whether an MLLM's prediction is driven by the image or the text by comparing image-only, text-only, and joint counterfactual conditions, rather than only highlighting influential regions or tokens. Exposes cases where a model is right for the wrong reason, revealing shortcut learning.

entry.title: Attend to Your Own Thoughts: Breaking the Barrier for Post-Training Quantization of Reasoning LLMs through the Lens of 1.58-Bit Quantization

author.name: Shigeng Wang, Chao Li, Yangyuxuan Kang, Jiawei Fan, Anbang Yao

entry.summary: ScaleQ-1.58 shows that ternary post-training quantization collapses on math and coding for reasoning LLMs when calibrated conventionally, and fixes it by calibrating on the model's own chain-of-thought traces and final answers. This lets extreme low-bit PTQ preserve reasoning ability.

entry.title: Language Equality has a Price: A Systematic Investigation of Multi-turn LLM Performance for EU-24+

author.name: Sherzod Hakimov, Karl Osswald, Jelle Psurek, Eszter Bukovszky, A. Altar L\"user, David Schlangen

entry.summary: Evaluates nine open-weight and commercial LLMs as agents in programmatically scored goal-directed dialogue games across 30 languages including all 24 official EU languages. Commercial systems outperform every open-weight model in every official language, with the weakest open models averaging below 40 points.

entry.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection

author.name: Anusha Madan Gopal, Aras Pirbadian, Kristofor D. Carlson, M Anthony Lewis, Jonathan Tapson

entry.summary: PRECOG exploits the fixed-size recurrent state of state-space models to pre-encode retrieval corpora offline and inject the matching hidden state at query time, collapsing RAG prefill cost from linear in context length to constant. Targets persistent memory and corpus retrieval for edge-deployed language models.

entry.title: Output-Aware Rotation for INT2 KV-Cache Quantization

author.name: Vincent-Daniel Yun, Woosang Lim, Minsoo Cheong, Sunwoo Lee, Murali Annavaram, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: OptR proposes output-aware rotations for INT2 key-value cache quantization, minimizing error measured after the attention readout and output projection rather than upstream cache statistics. It decomposes error into key- and value-induced terms and learns per-head orthogonal corrections through the full quantized attention path.

entry.title: The Tell-Tale Trace: Detecting Reasoning Failures in LLMs Using Chain-of-Thought Dynamics

author.name: Shashwat Sourav, Aishwarya Balwani

entry.summary: Proposes monitoring how a chain-of-thought trace evolves over time, rather than checking individual steps, to catch reasoning failures that are distributed across the trajectory. The framing also sidesteps the assumption that verbalized reasoning literally reflects internal computation, treating the trace as a dynamical signal instead.

entry.title: Sparse Weight Decomposition for Efficient Circuit Extraction

author.name: Chuanhao Yan, Xuhan Huang, Yawen Duan, Zhenfei Yin, Hang Zhao, Bryan Dai, Jie Fu

entry.summary: Sparse Weight Decomposition factorizes each pretrained linear projection into two sparse factors whose shared intermediate coordinates act as addressable circuit units, avoiding the need to train sparse autoencoders or replacement models. This keeps the analyzed object identical to the original network, eliminating the usual fidelity gap.

entry.title: KernelBrain: Coarse-to-Fine, Budget-Aware Search for Agentic GPU Kernel Optimization

author.name: Shuai Che, Gang Peng

entry.summary: KernelBrain is an agentic system that optimizes GPU kernels by combining LLM-guided mutation with coarse-to-fine budget allocation, policy-gated evaluation, and profiler-informed diagnosis. It reports up to 6.7x speedup over PyTorch on Triton kernel tasks and up to 1.4x over the prior state-of-the-art kernel agent with substantially lower optimization cost.

entry.title: Causal Inference with Unstructured Outcomes

author.name: Kevin Christian Wibisono, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: Defines a causal estimand for settings where the outcome is text, an image, or another unstructured object, for which the usual average treatment effect is meaningless because outcomes cannot be subtracted. The approach learns which features of the unstructured outcome are most causally affected by treatment.

entry.title: Dynamically Allocating Evaluation Effort for Model Ranking

author.name: Vil\'em Zouhar, Julia Kreutzer, Alon Lavie, Tom Kocmi, Matt Post, Ond\v{r}ej Bojar, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: Formalizes multi-model human evaluation as best-arm identification in a correlated-arm bandit, so annotation budget is adaptively concentrated on the models still competing for the top rank. The authors prove optimality of their algorithms and show improved discrimination at fixed cost. Directly attacks the cost bottleneck in gold-standard human evaluation of LLMs and MT systems.

entry.title: Biconvex Optimization for Smooth Minimum-Time Trajectories around Convex Obstacles

author.name: Peter Werner, Tobia Marcucci, Daniela Rus

entry.summary: This paper reformulates minimum-time motion planning around convex obstacles as a biconvex program by jointly convexifying the time objective and derivative constraints via a change of variables and handling collisions with time-varying separating planes. The solver alternates between computing maximum-margin planes and optimizing the trajectory, is anytime, and provably converges from a simple collision-free initialization.

entry.title: Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents

author.name: Mohammad Asadolahi, Amir Amini, Samira Talebi, Amirfarhad Farhadi, Azadeh Zamanifar

entry.summary: This paper identifies an Echo Gap failure mode in self-improving agents that store scored episodes in external memory: because ground-truth labels are unavailable at deployment, the stored score is an LLM self-assessment, and incorrect episodes systematically receive inflated rewards. The agent then preferentially retrieves and repeats those flawed episodes, creating a self-reinforcing degradation loop across multiple model families. It reframes memory-based self-improvement as a non-parametric policy-improvement process with an unreliable reward proxy.

entry.title: Judging Is Not Enumerating: Silent Omissions in LLM-Authored Acceptable Sets

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Jianlin Chen, Ziyao Lin, Peiji Long, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: This paper tests the increasingly common practice of promoting models from examinee to examiner by asking whether they can author complete acceptable sets (test suites, answer keys, rubrics, reward functions) rather than merely judge candidates. Across four reference constructions including hardened HumanEval-plus and MBPP-plus and an intentionally incomplete WordNet reference, judging outperforms authoring by roughly 0.29 to 0.34 F1, a gap persisting across a 24-fold parameter range. The silent omissions in authored sets directly undermine LLM-generated evaluation and reward specifications.

entry.title: Salami Attack: Stealthy Collusive Memory Poisoning against OpenClaw

author.name: Zheng Lin, Yuzhe Huang, Zhenxing Niu, Xianmin Ye, Haichang Gao

entry.summary: MemCollusion red-teams persistent agent memory by slicing a harmful objective into individually innocuous fragments that only become dangerous in combination, defeating per-record filtering. Demonstrated against a popular agent framework's long-term memory.

entry.title: Can You Trust the Confidence? ConfBench for Vision-Language Models on Document Extraction

author.name: Priyashree Roy, Sujitha Martin, Mohammad Rostami, Spencer Romo, Renhao Xue, Bob Strahan, Diego A. Socolinsky, Boyi Xie, Md Mofijul Islam

entry.summary: ConfBench is a calibration-focused benchmark for document key-information extraction, generated by applying 20 controlled degradation pipelines to produce 1,346 document variants and over 70k entity-level evaluations across the accuracy spectrum. Compares verbalized and log-probability confidence across seven proprietary and open VLMs.

entry.title: Diagnosing Search Behavior and Failure Modes in Long-Horizon Search Agents

author.name: Qi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Uses human-annotated document relevance judgments to diagnose long-horizon search agent trajectories, separating retrieval gaps where needed evidence is never found from utilization gaps where retrieved evidence is not used. Tests whether more search effort actually yields better answers.

entry.title: Auditing Data Provenance in LLM Fine-tuning via Intrinsic Distributional Fingerprints

author.name: Zirui Huang, Yunlong Mao, Wei Tong, Tingting Wu, Xin Ge, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: Distribution Provenance Audit is a post-hoc, black-box method to test whether a deployed fine-tuned LLM was trained on proprietary data, relying on distributional fingerprints that survive paraphrasing and distillation because utility requires preserving them. Addresses data IP infringement without requiring pre-training watermarking.

entry.title: Mamba with Hierarchical Memory: Solving Representation Bottleneck in Long Sequence Modeling

author.name: Qinwen Wang, Jieping Luo, Aoxiang Qin, Ruoyu Zhao, Jianxiong Tang, Wei Zhang, Zhichao Lu, Luziwei Leng

entry.summary: Hierarchical Memory Mamba adds a lightweight working-memory module on top of a pretrained Mamba backbone that extracts slow paragraph-level semantics from hidden states and compresses them into persistent long-term memory for retrieval. Aims to relieve the fixed-capacity recurrent-state bottleneck of linear-attention models on long sequences.

entry.title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures

author.name: Sunny Dubey

entry.summary: Tests how far mid-episode agent failures (looping, tool-error cascades, goal drift, fabrication, corrupted-content ingestion) can be detected from cheap step telemetry alone, using a one-class echo-state-network ensemble with CUSUM alarms trained only on healthy runs. On 2,823 episodes across three frameworks and four models it catches 71 percent of failures at a 5 percent false-alarm budget with AUROC 0.872.

entry.title: Role Steering of Language Models for Social Simulations

author.name: Isaac Song, Mohammed Rehan Parwani, Glenn Matlin, Emile Anand, Akhil Theerthala, Arjun Chatterjee, Maria Kostylew, Yonadav G. Shavit, Sebastien Krier, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: Introduces an activation-steering screening workflow for role-conditioned agents used in social simulations: extract a role direction, sweep steering strengths, judge role-profile alignment, and pass or flag configurations before deployment into a population. On OLMo-3-7B-Instruct with 275 roles, role-specific directions beat an assistant-axis persona-vector control on judged alignment.

entry.title: A Synthetically-accessible Universe of Chemically Recyclable Polymers

author.name: Anagha Savit, Wei Xiong, Harikrishna Sahu, Shivank S. Shukla, Will R. Gutekunst, Rampi Ramprasad

entry.summary: The authors release one million synthetically realizable ring-opening-polymerization polymer structures, generated by combining virtual forward synthesis from known reactions with polymer-specific language models (polyBART latent exploration and POLYT5 sequence generation) and filtered by chemical heuristics. The dataset targets discovery of chemically recyclable polymers.

entry.title: Cross-Task Dissociation in Frontier Vision-Language Model Theory of Mind

author.name: Kejia Zhang, Youran Sun, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Nine frontier vision-language models are evaluated on two psychology-derived Theory-of-Mind paradigms, the Keysar Director Task and Frith-Happe animated triangles. Without chain-of-thought the panel makes the egocentric error on 78 percent of Director trials, closer to children than adults, while reasoning rescues some models, and the models under-attribute intention on the motion task, showing that ToM profiles fragment across paradigms rather than mapping to a single human reference group.

entry.title: Native Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Low-Resource Southeast Asian Languages

author.name: Sean Gip Lim, William Chandra Tjhi, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: OSCD is a post-training method that keeps chain-of-thought reasoning in low-resource Southeast Asian languages by projecting high-resource reasoning trajectories into low-resource vocabulary subspaces during generative rollouts via an integrated translator loop. It addresses cross-lingual collapse, where models silently revert to English mid-reasoning, and the catastrophic forgetting that plain fine-tuning causes.

entry.title: MedUPS: Towards Diagnostic Assistance in Uncommon Medical Cases with Large Language Models

author.name: Ofir Ben Shoham, Oriel Perets, Nir Grinberg, Nadav Rappoport

entry.summary: Introduces MedUPSQA, a dataset of nearly 22,000 mid-stream clinical decision points derived from 5,535 real case reports, plus an alignment framework that supervises models on next-action decisions rather than only final diagnoses. It targets uncommon and off-guideline cases where sequential management matters most.

entry.title: Analytic Planning under Uncertainty with Moment Closure

author.name: Shishir Sharma, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Develops analytic distribution-aware planning for model-based RL by using a quadratic action-value parameterization plus moment closure, reducing the Bellman backup to a tractable expectation that keeps predictive covariance instead of resorting to sampling or point estimates. Aims to cut target variance in stochastic environments.

entry.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Tingyu Song, Mingxin Li, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Pengjun Xie, Zhijie Nie, Yilun Zhao, Shu Wu

entry.summary: UEmbed is a decoder-only multimodal embedding model that emits both learned sparse lexical and dense representations in a single causal forward pass, using appended special tokens paired with disjoint vocabulary partitions. It removes the reliance of learned sparse retrieval on bidirectional encoders and auxiliary cross-modal modules.

entry.title: Temporal Leakage in LLM Backtesting: Measurement, Validation, and Adjusted Scores

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Bradly C. Stadie

entry.summary: Argues that the standard contamination check for LLM forecasting backtests, comparing scores before and after the training cutoff, is uninformative, showing four flagship models fail it on questions resolved only after their cutoffs because recency legitimately mimics leakage. The paper proves no passive backtest can separate leakage from skill and supplies two external-information remedies, including a matched clean control that yields leakage-adjusted scores.

entry.title: Approximate Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yuannuo Feng, Zegang Peng, Yuxin Xie, Yubing Ye, Yizhe Chen, Wenshuai Yao, Wenyong Zhou, Wang Kang

entry.summary: Approximate Speculative Decoding replaces the strict first-mismatch stopping rule with a budgeted longest-prefix acceptance that admits some mismatches when a target-logit regret gate is satisfied. This recovers suffixes that greedy verification would discard, increasing throughput without any training.

entry.title: Enhancing VLM Reward Models Through Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning

author.name: Pyrros Koussios, Chenhao Li, Xin Chen, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: SAFT fine-tunes vision-language models used as RL reward models by regularizing their latent space with intrinsic structural priors through LoRA adapters, without any ground-truth reward supervision. It aims to denoise the text-observation similarity scores that make VLM rewards unreliable in practice.

entry.title: Trajectory inference via Acceleration Matching

author.name: Bartolo Dazzini, Giovanni Conforti, Alain Durmus, Aram-Alexandre Pooladian

entry.summary: Acceleration Matching lifts trajectory inference from unpaired temporal snapshots into phase space and regresses onto an explicit conditional acceleration field, yielding smooth interpolating trajectories. This avoids both smoothness-enforcing preprocessing and expensive simulation-based training objectives.

entry.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?

author.name: Soumadeep Saha, Krish Sharma, Akshay Chaturvedi, Nicholas Asher

entry.summary: Investigates the open debate over whether RLVR expands the reasoning frontier or only sharpens sampling, using controlled maze tasks and semantic-equivalence trees extracted from mathematical reasoning traces to separate stylistic variety from genuine inferential branching. Finds that observed policy entropy collapse is not merely syntactic, implying real narrowing of inferential exploration. Directly informs a central question in reasoning-model training.

entry.title: MinerU.Chem: A High-Precision System for Optical Chemical Structure and Reaction Recognition

author.name: Haote Yang, Jiang Wu, Jingchao Wang, Xingjian Wei, Lixin Ma, Linye Li, Chen Zhu, Xiaolong Wu, Yuheng Lu, Ziran Zhu, Junyuan Gao, Lingli Ge, Yuan Xu, Huijie Ao, QianQian Wu, Dechen Lin, Huaiyu Gu, Lu Chen, Shengxin Lu, ShaSha Wang, Yuanyuan Cao, Zhejia Yu, Ruijie Zhang, Zimai Tian, Jiaxing Sun, Yinfan Wang, Jiahe Song, Chuang Wang, Yubin Wang, Rui Nie, Hao Zheng, Bowen Jiang, Hongbin Lai, Yifan He, Chengjin Liu, Tingting Zhang, Liqun Wei, Lijun Wu, Bin Wang, Yuqiang Li, Guangyu Wang, Wei Li, Bowen Zhou, Dahua Lin, Conghui He

entry.summary: MinerU.Chem is a document parsing system that extracts molecular structures, reaction schemes, and experimental condition tables from organic chemistry papers and patents into machine-readable form, integrated into an existing open document platform. The goal is to unblock data production for chemistry knowledge bases and AI tasks like retrosynthesis and condition recommendation.

entry.title: CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement

author.name: Mercy Prasanna Ranjit, Anirban Porya, Sathvik Joel, Niharika Vadlamudi, Nikhilesh Chowdary Eathamukkala, Prasanth V V, Abhyuday Kumara Swamy, Pranay Narhari Umredkar, Pradeep Narayan, Vivek Rajagopal, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: CARE-X is a chest X-ray vision-language model from an industrial research team that unifies report generation with focal-loss classification heads, grounding heads for localization, and tool-augmented anatomical measurement. The motivation is that clinical utility requires tunable decision thresholds, spatial evidence, and quantitative measurements, not just fluent text.

entry.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent

author.name: Zhen Fang, Yu Zeng, Wenxuan Huang, Yiming Zhao, Shiting Huang, Tianfei Ren, Qi Lu, Qingnan Ren, Qisheng Su, Lionel Z. Wang, Qingyu Yin, Shuang Chen, Zehui Chen, Lin Chen, Zhenfei Yin, Yao Hu, Shaohui Lin, Wanli Ouyang, Shaosheng Cao, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: Video-DeepResearch extends deep-research style multimodal agents from static images to continuous video, diagnosing two failure modes: agents skipping visual tools in favor of text search, and relying on memorized knowledge rather than genuine tool use. It enforces exhaustive cross-frame grounding before web retrieval via stage-wise tool unlocking plus supervised then reinforcement training.

entry.title: Enfold: Folding World Model Imagination into Predictive Representations for Ultra-Efficient Embodied Control

author.name: Weili Zeng, Yitong Xing, Fulong Liu, Chengqun Yang, Antao Xiang, Feng Tian, Jingnan Gao, Jisong Cai, Xin Wang, Xiaomin Wu, Yao Mu, Xiaokang Yang, Yichao Yan

entry.summary: Enfold argues the reusable asset of a video world model is not the rendered future but the internal computation that builds it, and distills that multi-level generative computation into a representation inferred from the present observation and instruction. This removes the expensive generative rollout from the control loop for embodied policies.

entry.title: Light-Loco-Parkour: Versatile Perceptive Whole-Body Locomotion via Multi-Skill Distillation

author.name: Hongming Chen, Zhuoran Li, Hongxi Wang, Jiangpeng Hu, Ziliang Li, Peize Liu, QingRui Zhao, Xuhao Liu, Liang Pan, Ximin Lyu, Yuntao Ma, Tingxiang Fan

entry.summary: Light-Loco-Parkour is a single end-to-end humanoid policy that decides when to walk, balance, climb, step down, or vault from onboard depth and a velocity command alone, without reference motions, skill labels, or hand-coded gating. It is trained via multi-skill distillation to use arms, torso, and knees for whole-body terrain traversal.

entry.title: Learning to Coordinate Symbolic Tools: LLM Agents for Verified Sum-of-Squares Certificates

author.name: Bohan Chen, Shivam N. Patel, Richard Hoffmann, Sam Looi, Tony Yue Yu

entry.summary: This work trains an LLM agent to coordinate symbolic tools for producing weighted sum-of-squares decompositions, a machine-checkable route to proving polynomial inequalities where candidate certificates are exactly verifiable but hard to find. The authors build 1.35 million synthetic examples covering eight supporting algebraic subtasks rather than training only on the composite task, then apply verifier-grounded optimization. It is a case study in decomposing tool-use training with an exact reward signal.

entry.title: Escaping Confidence Trap: Evolutionary Decoding for Mathematical Reasoning in Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Zhenhong Sun, Hanqing Zhao, Yatao Bian, Rongcheng Tu, Liuyue Xie, Xu Zhang, Jue Wang, Davide Modolo, Daoyi Dong, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Analyzing decoding trajectories of the diffusion language model LLaDA 2.0, the authors identify a confidence trap where local token confidence during progressive block unmasking becomes misaligned with global reasoning correctness, producing sampling-sensitive and structurally stuck failures on math. They propose an evolutionary decoding strategy to escape these traps and preserve coherent numerical-symbolic trajectories. The work targets a specific weakness of diffusion LLMs relative to autoregressive models.

entry.title: Beyond Routing Saturation: A Long-Horizon Class-Incremental Perspective on Expert Routing in Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Huiyu Yi, Yongqi Xu, Bogang Zhang, Dunwei Tu, Xu Zhiming, Zhen-Hao Xie, Baile Xu, Furao Shen

entry.summary: Shows that expert routing in multimodal continual instruction tuning appears solved only because existing benchmarks leak task identity through textual fingerprints and use short task sequences. Introduces FLEX, a 34-task long-horizon benchmark with weakened fingerprints that exposes routing failure.

entry.title: MineGrad: Gradient Inversion Attacks on LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Hasin Us Sami, Swapneel Sen, Basak Guler

entry.summary: MineGrad analytically reconstructs private training data from the gradients shared during federated LoRA fine-tuning, showing an adversarial server can breach privacy despite the frozen base model. Challenges assumptions that parameter-efficient updates leak less.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Use Tokens: Durable Authorization State for Replay-Resistant LLM Agent Actions

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: Defines semantic replay, where agent retries, replanning, and delegation cause one user authorization to be executed multiple times under freshly minted single-use tokens. CapLease keeps durable monotonic state over the authorized action, confirmation event, and remaining execution budget.

entry.title: REFLEX: Rethinking MoE Inference as Refinement-Aware Compute Allocation in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiang Xia, Cheng Yan, Yiming Zhang, Jiazheng Liu, Hongyu Zhang, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: Reframes mixture-of-experts inference in diffusion language models as refinement-aware compute allocation, since each denoising pass revisits all positions despite very different per-token refinement needs. REFLEX replaces uniform token-choice routing with demand-sensitive expert budgets.

entry.title: Exploring and Bridging Knowledge Holes in Unlearned Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Junxiang You, Junkai Chen, Yuhao He, Ruiqi Liu, Zhetao Guo, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Shows that multimodal unlearning evaluations miss knowledge holes, meaning severe degradation on benign inputs that share generic patterns with the forget set, because standard utility benchmarks are representationally far from it. Builds a probing benchmark and proposes mitigation.

entry.title: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration with Asymmetric Reinforcement Learning and Self-Distillation

author.name: Jim Dilkes, Vahid Yazdanpanah, Sebastian Stein

entry.summary: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration augments training prompts with varied instructions to broaden the behaviours an LLM attempts during RL post-training, paired with an asymmetric RL plus self-distillation objective that transfers the instruction-induced behaviour back into the base policy. Targets the exploration problem specific to LLM action spaces.

entry.title: Cooperative Coevolution for Resource-Constrained Agentic LLM Post-Training

author.name: Zhiyuan Wang, Shengcai Liu, Jiahao Wu, Ning Lu, Hui Ouyang, Shaofeng Zhang, Haoze Lv, Ke Tang

entry.summary: CoPES makes evolution-strategy post-training of tool-using LLM agents feasible on a few GPUs by decomposing the full parameter space into lower-dimensional subspaces searched cooperatively. Targets the memory advantage of backprop-free ES while cutting its prohibitive GPU-hour cost.

entry.title: Cost-Effective Automated Judging of Natural-Language Mathematical Proofs

author.name: Benjamin Grayzel

entry.summary: Tests whether cheap open-weight models can grade natural-language mathematical proofs given a reference proof and rubric, finding that GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek-V4 Flash, and Gemma-4 31B match human pass/fail agreement rates statistically indistinguishable from frontier judges Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro at up to 100x lower cost. A three-model majority vote matched but did not beat the best single cheap judge.

entry.title: Exploring More to Solve More: Boosting Diversity in Text Diffusion Models via Entropy-Based Guidance

author.name: Jingwei Zhang, Haoyu Lei, Zijin Feng, Jiacheng Sun, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: SAKE is a training-free guidance method for discrete text diffusion that computes order-2 Renyi entropy over a semantic kernel Gram matrix capturing cross-token interactions and relative positions, then linearizes it for sampling. Improves the diversity-fidelity balance and reportedly boosts problem-solving via broader exploration.

entry.title: When Prompts Control Robots: Prompt Injection Attacks in Multi-Agent Robotic Systems

author.name: Neha Nagaraja, Amisha Bagari, Hayretdin Bahsi

entry.summary: This work evaluates prompt injection against an LLM-driven multi-agent robotic system, comparing direct injections into task instructions with indirect injections arriving through perception modules, across single-agent and multi-agent settings and varying attack-goal complexity. It finds that injections can induce adversarial physical actions and that multi-agent structure widens the attack surface via cross-agent contamination.

entry.title: Can Humans Dream of Electric Sheep? Human-Written Samples for Fine-Grained Vision-and-Language Hallucination Benchmarking

author.name: Timothee Mickus, Claudio Savelli, Eduardo Cal\`o, Emilio Raimond, Stella Frank, Hengyu Luo, Flavio Giobergia, Vincent Segonne, Chuyuan Li, Aman Sinha, Lorenzo Vaiani, J\"org Tiedemann, Ra\'ul V\'azquez

entry.summary: Builds a multilingual hallucination benchmark with 1,600 human-written hallucination samples across four languages alongside 18,400 model-generated ones, all with span-level annotations. It finds human-written samples give higher annotator agreement and remain distributionally comparable, offering a model-independent way to keep hallucination benchmarks durable.

entry.title: Dense Language Generation Made Simple: Deterministic, Randomized, and Multi-Order Algorithms

author.name: Ziyi Cai, Shuangping Li, Yiheng Shen, Kangning Wang, Peng Zhang

entry.summary: Provides simplified deterministic, randomized and multi-order algorithms for dense language generation in the limit, building on the density-based coverage measures introduced by Kleinberg and Wei. It advances the theory of generating valid, novel strings from adversarial positive-only enumerations.

entry.title: Same violence, different answer: how AI responds to coercive control against women across languages

author.name: Lyu Chang, S\`onia Estrad\'e Albiol, N\'uria Verg\'es Bosch

entry.summary: Presents a fixed coercive-control scenario, in which a surveilled woman asks for help writing a self-blaming letter, to seven widely used language models across nine languages, scoring whether each names the abuse, counters self-blame and affirms agency. Failures split along two independent axes, with systems from non-anglophone developers performing notably worse.

entry.title: HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haowei Liu, Jiamian Wang, Hsin-Tai Wu, Zhiqiang Tao, Yi Fang

entry.summary: HindSearch improves search-augmented RL by having a frozen judge write hindsight critiques of failed rollouts using the gold answer, which then supplies an auxiliary on-policy distillation signal for GRPO. With Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct it reaches 39.4 percent average exact match on seven benchmarks, and ablating gold-answer access removes most of the gain.

entry.title: How Much Does a Reasoning Summary Reveal? An Observability Ladder for Large Language Models

author.name: Andres Algaba, Francesca Carlon, Lynn Delcon, Marthe Ballon, Bert Verbruggen, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: The paper defines an observability ladder over what a reader can inspect to judge answer correctness, ranging from the final response to a model-written reasoning summary to the full trace to internal signals, each with and without the prompt. Using linear correctness probes over three benchmarks and five open-weight models, it finds summaries carry most of the trace ranking signal when the prompt is hidden but add little once the prompt is visible.

entry.title: Action-grounded tissue affordance enables anticipatory auto-framing that lowers surgeon cognitive workload during laparoscopic surgery

author.name: Jiayu Gu, Yiwei Wang, Jie Zhang, Guojun Cao, Keshen Lyu, Song Zhou, Yimeng Chen, Haorui Wang, Qingmin Feng, Shenchao Shi, Huan Zhao, Wenbin Chen, Caihua Xiong, Chidan Wan, Jing Samantha Pan, Xiong Cai, Han Ding

entry.summary: Presents DiffeoAfford, which derives surgical visual-attention labels retrospectively from completed laparoscopic procedures by combining diffeomorphism-constrained tissue tracking with instrument trajectories, avoiding manual per-frame annotation. A real-time model trained on these labels powers an anticipatory auto-framing assistant reported to reduce surgeon cognitive workload.

entry.title: Rubrics as Privileged Information for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Deepika Bablani, Ajay Gupta, Wanming Chen

entry.summary: Extends on-policy self-distillation from verifiable domains to open-ended generation by using rubrics as soft privileged information given to the teacher context, rather than as scalar reinforcement-learning rewards. Counterintuitively finds that rubric-based soft privileged information yields a larger and more effective training signal on student rollouts than hard reference completions.

entry.title: Inverted Detection and Control in Steering Vectors

author.name: Max Torop, Aria Masoomi, Jennifer Dy

entry.summary: Identifies inverted steering vectors: directions that are highly discriminative for a concept yet consistently push model behavior toward the opposite of what their sign implies, breaking the standard assumption behind activation steering. The paper gives a geometric characterization of when this inversion occurs.

entry.title: JudgeArena: A Unified Framework for Reproducible LLM-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Erlis Lushtaku, Bora Kargi, Ali Elganzory, Fabio Ferreira, Alejandro R. Salamanca, Julia Kreutzer, David Salinas

entry.summary: JudgeArena unifies major LLM-as-judge benchmarks including AlpacaEval, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench, and m-Arena-Hard under one interface with swappable judges, configurable prompts and backends, and full metadata logging. This enables systematic study of how judge model, prompt, and inference backend change conclusions about model quality. Addresses a serious reproducibility problem in the dominant evaluation paradigm.

entry.title: GORDON: Graph-based Object-centric Rewards for Decomposition of Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Andrea Protopapa, Davide Buoso, Francesca Pistilli, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Giuseppe Averta

entry.summary: GORDON learns dense reward functions for long-horizon manipulation from action-free videos by representing scenes as graphs of detected objects and spatial relations and training a GNN self-supervised to embed task progress. The object-centric abstraction is intended to be more robust than pixel-based reward models to background and appearance variation.

entry.title: Reputation-driven Cooperation in Lattice-based Decentralized Federated Learning through Evolutionary Game Theory

author.name: Phuc Hoang Truong Huynh, Dung Tran Vinh, Khoa Duc Anh Lam, An Nghiem Nguyen Truong, Uyen Nha Tran Bui, Khang Nguyen Dinh, Bao Nguyen Le Gia, Minh Le Nguyen Nhat, Manh Hong Duong, The Anh Han, Thi Ai Thao Nguyen, and Le Hong Trang

entry.summary: PATH-Bench evaluates lifelong LLM agents by controlling the order of accumulated experience, measuring forward transfer, backward transfer, and forgetting rather than only average accuracy. Eight agents are tested on code generation and multi-turn tool use.

entry.title: Sweet Little Lies: Strategic Deception in AI Emotional Support Chatbots

author.name: Aseem Pahuja, Zhiling Guo, Tahir Abbas Syed

entry.summary: Uses Bayesian persuasion to model emotional-support chatbots that signal users' emotional states, showing engagement-maximizing platforms have incentives to overstate emotional need when users are actually fine. Deception raises engagement without lowering user expected payoff in equilibrium.

entry.title: Latent Thought Credit: Multi-Answer Credit Assignment for Latent Reasoning

author.name: Xuyang Zhao, Liting Zhang, Zichen Xu, Yong Chen, Wenjia Zeng, Shiwan Zhao, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: Latent Thought Credit assigns hierarchical credit in latent reasoning by sampling multiple continuous thoughts per prompt and averaging rewards over several answers sampled from each fixed thought context. Separates thought quality from answer-sampling noise under answer-only rewards.

entry.title: Allocation Before Ranking: Decoupled Token Compression for OmniLLMs

author.name: Zhenghui Guo, Yilin Yang, Yuanbin Man, Miao Yin, Weidong Shi, Rabimba Karanjai, Omprakash Gnawali, Chengming Zhang

entry.summary: Argues multimodal token compression conflates two decisions, how much budget each modality gets and which tokens survive within it, and that shared top-K selection is biased toward audio. Macer is a training-free compressor that allocates per-modality budgets first, then ranks within modality at modality-specific shallow layers.

entry.title: DAPD: Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation

author.name: Jianyu Wu, Yizhou Wang, Encheng Su, Chen Tang, Shixiang Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses a privilege illusion in on-policy self-distillation, where students learn behaviors that depend on teacher-only reference information and then act as if it were still available at inference. DAPD adds dual-path and self-conditioned anchoring to close the teacher-student information asymmetry.

entry.title: CoEvoKG: Co-Evolving Knowledge Graphs with Self-Evolving Search Agents

author.name: Zhaoyang Li, Zenghuang Fu, Qiuyuan Ai, Ping Jiang, Haoyu Wu, Minghui Wu, Chenxu Zhao, Jie Song, Guannan He

entry.summary: CoEvoKG uses a knowledge graph both to generate verifiable multi-hop training tasks and to store verified evidence retrieved during successful searches, so self-play knowledge is retained rather than discarded. Jointly trains a task generator and a search agent with graph-grounded rewards.

entry.title: Fetch-then-Explore: Decoupling Selection from Extraction over a Persistent Workspace for Search Agents

author.name: Qi Liu, Yiqun Chen, Zidan Chen, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Fetch-then-Explore decouples page selection from page reading for search agents by keeping fetched documents in a persistent workspace that can be re-queried many turns later, rather than binding a single reading to fetch time or holding one page at a time. Aims to avoid repeated fetching and premature extraction in long research trajectories.

entry.title: Beyond Solution-Centric Search: Adaptive Inquiry and Knowledge Revision for Autonomous ML Engineering

author.name: Shaokang Fu, Yulong Tao, Linbo Jin, Jiarong Zhao, Qiming Shi, Tianjun Pan, Haonan Li, Chengyu Wang, Jia Wu, Chengfu Huo

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous ML engineering agents should be organized around an evolving information state rather than a tree or graph search over candidate solutions, and instantiates this as Iris, an inquiry-revision loop using epistemic actions to gather information before revising solutions. Positions the information paradigm against solution-centric search.

entry.title: Width, Memory, and Delay: A Resource Accounting for the Limits of Flat Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Oleksandr Kuznetsov, Emanuele Frontoni

entry.summary: Rebuts a recent claim that flat homogeneous multi-agent systems face an irreducible population-independent error floor removable only by hierarchy, using a controlled disturbance-rejection testbed with a computable optimum. Replaces the claim with a quantitative resource model trading off population width, per-agent internal-model memory, and delay.

entry.title: Decoy Images Amplify Caption-Mediated Defenses Against Encoded Jailbreaks

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Xiangchen Guan, Shibo Zheng, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita

entry.summary: Reports that attaching an unrelated decoy image to an encoded jailbreak prompt sharply reduces attack success on vision-language models, by up to 73 percentage points, because it activates caption-mediated defense pipelines that otherwise stay dormant on text-only input. The effect is measured across five frontier VLMs, two attack families and three black-box defenses.

entry.title: Sheaf-theoretic Signal Processing on Graphs: Spectral Theory, Filtering, and Sampling

author.name: Gabriele D'Acunto, Leonardo Di Nino, Paolo Di Lorenzo, Sergio Barbarossa

entry.summary: Develops the first unified signal processing framework on network sheaves, extending spectral analysis, filtering and sampling to settings where each node carries a local vector space of differing dimension and modality. It generalizes graph and topological signal processing to heterogeneous data.

entry.title: Question Begets Question: Self-Evolving Curriculum for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning on Competition Mathematics

author.name: Longtian Bao, Jianyou Wang, Yang Zhang, Youze Zheng, Ramamohan Paturi

entry.summary: Question-begets-Question generates diverse problem variants from existing competition math problems to overcome data scarcity, then trains purely with reinforcement learning on outcome rewards without oracle reasoning traces. Applied to Qwen2.5-Math-7B on AIME, starting from 5.6 percent pass@1, it studies whether the apparent capability ceiling can be broken.

entry.title: Latent Reward Registers for Diffusion Preference Alignment

author.name: Yuanshen Guan, Zipeng Feng, Zhiwei Xiong, Peiqin Sun

entry.summary: Latent Reward Registers prepend learnable register tokens to a frozen diffusion transformer to read out expected terminal human preference from intermediate noisy latents, without perturbing the generator's hidden states. The resulting dense differentiable reward addresses temporal credit assignment across the denoising trajectory for both training and inference-time guidance.

entry.title: MoEGen: Mixture-of-Experts for Instance-Adaptive LoRA Generation

author.name: Yiming Zeng, Lei Lu, Zexin Li, Zhuochun Li, Shuoqiu Li, Shuyi Liao, Xidong Wu, Zeyu Zhang, Minmei Wang, Yu Zhao, Tingting Yu, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: MoEGen replaces the usual practice of storing many full LoRA adapters in mixture-of-experts parameter-efficient fine-tuning with small learnable expert codes that condition a generator producing instance-specific low-rank updates. This keeps adapter storage roughly constant as expert count grows and allows adaptation outside a fixed expert pool.

entry.title: Mask-Based Priors Are More Persistent than Query-Key Initializations

author.name: Mingze Ma, Hemanth Saratchandran, Cameron Gordon, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Using controlled Boolean extrapolation tasks where Transformers systematically default to a minimum-degree interpolator instead of the true function, this paper asks whether injecting structural priors into attention can correct the inductive bias. It finds that priors imposed through attention masks persist through training far better than priors implanted via structured query-key initializations, which wash out. The tasks are stress tests for understanding, not applications.

entry.title: When Does LLM Orchestration Pay Off? A Controlled Evaluation of Accuracy, Cost, and Task Difficulty

author.name: Nicolas Leins, Nico Pelleriti, Jana Gonnermann-M\"uller, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: This controlled study compares Self-Refine, Best-of-N, and Debate against task-only and chain-of-thought single-call baselines across five backbones and three domains (competitive programming, chess puzzles, mathematics), equalizing optimization effort by tuning every method with GEPA under an identical budget and evaluating on difficulty-stratified items. Orchestration yields moderate but benchmark-dependent gains that must be weighed against cost. The equal-optimization design isolates the value of orchestration itself.

entry.title: Tracing the Cascade: A Topology-Aware Evaluation Framework for Scientific Agent Hallucinations

author.name: Xinshun Feng, Ziqi Miao, Lijun Li, Jing Shao

entry.summary: SCHEMA evaluates hallucinations in scientific agents with awareness of knowledge topology, automatically constructing scientific concept graphs so that errors on foundational concepts can be traced as they propagate through multi-step reasoning and corrupt downstream conclusions. This contrasts with benchmarks that treat facts in isolation under uniform accuracy metrics. The framework is evidence-grounded and cascade-aware.

entry.title: Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance

author.name: Alireza Lotfi, Subangkar Karmaker Shanto, Imtiaz Karim, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: A survey and position paper arguing agentic AI security must move from per-action permission checks to assurance over entire behavioral trajectories, spanning prompts, memory, retrieval, tools, and cross-organizational delegation. Maps the threat landscape across the agentic stack.

entry.title: Is More Privileged Information Better? From Solution Traces to Problem-Solving Structure in Self-Distilled Reasoning

author.name: Xuyang Zhao, Liting Zhang, Zichen Xu, Zhihu Wang, Xu Caiyue, Shiwan Zhao, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: Argues that on-policy self-distillation teachers conditioned on full reference solutions leak information unavailable at inference, and instead supplies problem-space structure (initial state, goals, constraints, a transition path) as the privileged view. Reports the best question-only accuracy across three math benchmarks at 1.7B to 8B scale.

entry.title: TCPO: Turn-Level Credit Policy Optimization

author.name: Sicong Liao, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: TCPO converts per-turn verifier scores into turn-level credit by comparing against reference states, capturing both immediate progress and regression relative to the best prior attempt in multi-turn refinement. Distinguishes output quality from a turn's marginal contribution.

entry.title: LaCache: Robust Semantic Caching for LLM Serving

author.name: Jiacheng Liang, Yuhui Wang, Tanqiu Jiang, Ting Wang

entry.summary: LaCache defends LLM semantic caches against cache-collision attacks, where injected queries pollute the cache and corrupt later legitimate responses, by exploiting the adversary's limited control over the cached response side. Adds response-side semantic constraint checks rather than query-similarity checks alone.

entry.title: MonitrLLM: A Community-Centered Evaluation Infrastructure for Large Language Models

author.name: Victor Ojewale, Ro Encarnaci\'on, Suresh Venkatasubramanian, Dana\'e Metaxa

entry.summary: MonitrLLM is open-source infrastructure for community-centered LLM evaluation that links full conversation transcripts to user-declared task intent and user-reported outcomes, treating all three as primary signals. Demonstrated in a two-week pilot with 26 college students.

entry.title: Obshazard-bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Foundation Models for Real-Time Disaster Intelligence from Raw Earth Observation Streams

author.name: Fengxiang Wang, Qiuyang Yu, Yueying Li, Mingshuo Chen, Chengchi Fei, Kaiyi Xu, Lixin Gu, Wangxu Wei, Junchao Gong, Lipeng Ma, Jiong Wang, Fenghua Ling, Wenlong Zhang, Xue Yang, Wenjing Yang, Ben Fei, Long Lan

entry.summary: Obshazard-bench evaluates multimodal foundation models on real-time disaster intelligence from raw high-frequency satellite observation streams rather than post-processed, post-event products. Designed to reflect operational time pressure and rapidly evolving hazards.

entry.title: EEG-JEPA: Structured Latent Prediction for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Jinhao Li, Zhiyuan Ma, Xueqiao Han, Zhongye Xia, Xinche Zhang, Shanghong Xie, Yixuan Liu, Yongjian Li, Runmin Gan, Tianlin Huo, Sen Song

entry.summary: EEG-JEPA replaces masked waveform reconstruction with joint-embedding latent prediction for EEG foundation models, arguing that reconstructing raw voltage teaches models to recover artifacts and background rather than transferable neural structure. A masked context encoder predicts EMA-produced target latents, following the JEPA recipe adapted to noisy biosignals.

entry.title: Interpretability-Guided Soft Pruning of Attention Heads in Vision Transformers

author.name: Kamil Ksi\k{a}\.zek, Piotr Suszy\'nski, Micha{\l} Jan W{\l}odarczyk, Jacek Tabor, Przemys{\l}aw Biecek

entry.summary: The paper introduces spectral visualization of individual attention heads via Laplacian eigenvectors of their attention maps, uses it to semantically cluster heads in vision foundation models like DINOv2 and find functional redundancy, then prunes with SAPER, a differentiable soft top-K framework. It links interpretability findings directly to compression decisions.

entry.title: The Gate, Not the Cache: Gate Provenance Bounds the Closed-Loop Reliability of Training-Free VLA Token Skipping

author.name: Qi Luo, Shuaijun Liu, Hao Zhao, Kunlin Li, Xiaobo Wang, Ningxing Su, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that training-free token skipping in vision-language-action models fails in closed loop when the gate for the next step is computed from the previous accelerated forward pass, because skipped tokens are exactly those the next gate cannot see, and errors compound.
