entry.summary: Asks whether training-log statistics from the same runs can sharpen comparisons between stochastically trained models, using arm-specific covariate adjustment so the reported effect remains the raw mean difference. Across three architectures and three vision datasets, early-training log covariates often reduce uncertainty, with covariate selection identified as the main pitfall.

entry.title: Evaluation Blindness: How Silent Measurement Failures Corrupt AI Systems from Training to Deployment

author.name: Priyanka Bajaj (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: Introduces the notion of evaluation blindness, where a measurement function returns healthy-looking readings while the system is actually failing, and argues that training-time reward gaming, silent importance-sampling errors, and benchmark contamination are instances of the same phenomenon as production monitoring gaps. Frames these as a unified lifecycle measurement problem.

entry.title: NOMADD: Numerical Optimization of Models Adapting to Data Drift

author.name: Swapn Shah, Keith Burghardt

entry.summary: NOMADD is a post-hoc numerical adjustment method that mitigates concept drift for tabular models without retraining, applicable across trees, neural networks, and tabular foundation models. It targets deployment settings where labels are delayed and retraining is impractical.

entry.title: Paired Recipient-based Evaluation of Survival Prediction for Deceased Donor Kidney Transplants

author.name: Misaki Matsuura, Mohammadreza Nemati, Dulat Bekbolsynov, Stanislaw Stepkowski, Kevin S. Xu

entry.summary: Evaluates survival prediction models for deceased-donor kidney transplants using a novel paired-recipient framework that compares graft outcomes for two recipients receiving kidneys from the same donor, approximating counterfactual matching benefit. The design addresses whether predictions are actually useful for allocation decisions rather than just accurate on average.

entry.title: PLAN: Parallel Liquid-Inspired Approximation Network for Efficient Representation Learning in Flexible Job Shop Scheduling

author.name: Dhivya Dharshini Kannan, Wei Zhang, Jieyi Bi, Yingpeng Du, Tianjun Wei, Jie Zhang, Zuming Liu, Anupam Trivedi

entry.summary: PLAN reformulates continuous liquid neural network dynamics into a discretized, parallelizable form to give flexible job shop scheduling a lightweight alternative to heavy attention-based deep reinforcement learning policies. The goal is comparable scheduling quality with far fewer parameters and lower inference latency.

entry.title: SynEnergy: Anomaly Semantic-Guided Diffusion for Synthetic Energy Data Generation

author.name: Lin Jiang, Dahai Yu, Ravikumar Gelli, Guang Wang

entry.summary: SynEnergy generates synthetic fine-grained energy consumption data using an anomaly-semantics-guided diffusion model, explicitly preserving sparse anomalous events from extreme weather, outages, and behavior shifts that existing generators smooth away. It targets privacy-constrained sharing of data for forecasting, demand response, and grid reliability studies.

entry.title: Lightweight Chunk Selection for Mobile Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Sicong Chang, Yidan Shen, Wen Yu, Jiefu Chen, Xin Fu, Renjie Hu

entry.summary: Studies lightweight retrieval chunk selection for on-device RAG, framing selection as evidence alignment and combining three cheap complementary features rather than invoking an extra LLM or compressor. The motivation is that the top-ranked chunk by similarity is often not the most evidence-supporting one, while mobile budgets forbid heavy rerankers.

entry.title: AS-FedBridge: Pseudo-Spike Bridge Distillation for Heterogeneous ANN-SNN Federated Learning

author.name: Shengyang Li, Yiting Dong, Liuyang Song, Ximing Wang, Luyuan Xie, Cong Li, Qingni Shen, Zhaofei Yu

entry.summary: AS-FedBridge enables federated training that mixes conventional neural networks with spiking neural networks by bridging the semantic gap between continuous activations and discrete spikes using pseudo-spike distillation. It targets energy-constrained edge deployments where SNNs are attractive.

entry.title: ConformalShift: Targeted Event Reordering Against Adaptive ECG Monitoring

author.name: Arash Vashagh, Yasmin Vashagh

entry.summary: Shows that adaptive conformal prediction on streaming ECG events can be attacked purely by reordering authentic events, without touching waveforms, labels, or scores, suppressing detection of ventricular beats. Success rates far exceed random reordering on MIT-BIH records.

entry.title: Learning and Clustering on Temporal Graphs: Principles, Primitives, and Pooling

author.name: Nelson Aloysio Reis de Almeida Passos, Emanuele Carlini, Salvatore Trani

entry.summary: A survey-style synthesis of learning and clustering on temporal graphs, connecting graph neural pooling with classical community detection through shared spectral foundations. It questions whether GNN-based pooling actually beats established clustering algorithms once efficiency and recovery accuracy are considered.

entry.title: PRISM: Powerful Time Series to Image (TS2I) Representations for Multivariate Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mateusz Smendowski, Kamil Faber, Piotr Nawrocki, Nathalie Japkowicz, Roberto Corizzo

entry.summary: PRISM systematically studies how to convert multivariate time series into multi-channel images for anomaly detection and whether vision backbones can match time-domain baselines. Over 7000 experiments show well-designed image representations are competitive.

entry.title: Should the Boundary Term Be Learned in Reflected Diffusion? Conormal Trace and Reflection Masking

author.name: Ziyue Wang, Takafumi Kanamori

entry.summary: Analyzes score matching for reflected diffusion on bounded domains and shows the leftover boundary term reduces to a single scalar per boundary point, the diffusion-weighted normal component of the score. The paper proposes a parametrization that enforces the required boundary trace without extra trainable parameters or stochastic boundary losses. Improves the theoretical soundness of constrained-domain generative diffusion.

entry.title: FOUND-AF: Benchmarking ECG Foundation Models for Atrial Fibrillation Detection

author.name: Amirhossein Taleshinosrati, Yangyang Wang, Atitaya Phoemsuk, Vahid Abolghasemi, Naser Hossein Motlagh, Sadasivan Puthusserypady, Daniel Teichmann, Abdolrahman Peimankar

entry.summary: FOUND-AF benchmarks nine public ECG foundation models from five families for atrial fibrillation detection under a single leakage-controlled, deployment-oriented protocol with identical preprocessing and classifiers. Resolves the confound that prior comparisons used different datasets and validation setups. Provides a fair picture of which pretrained ECG representations actually transfer.

entry.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

author.name: Abdallah Khemais

entry.summary: Extends a companion theoretical result on when activation patching and weight-space ablation agree, decomposing interaction effects from ablating carriers across multiple layers and testing the closed-form attention Jacobian bound on a real pretrained model rather than toy transformers. Aims to put interpretability ablation practice on firmer footing. Contributes to the reliability of causal interpretability tooling.

entry.title: FLARE: Few-shot Learning-based Adaptive Reflective Engine

author.name: Dhanasekar Sundararaman, Bharat Gandhi, Aashna Garg, Minjie Li

entry.summary: Challenges the claim that reflective instruction evolution such as GEPA supersedes few-shot optimization, introducing FLARE which pairs reflective mechanisms with a small set of few-shot reference examples. Evaluated on retrieval-augmented reasoning, tool calling, and multi-label emotion classification benchmarks. Contributes to the fast-moving prompt-optimizer literature.

entry.title: On the Non-Specificity of Statistical Measures Used in Script Decipherment

author.name: Nikhil Raghavendra

entry.summary: Tests the specificity premise behind statistical arguments that undeciphered sign systems encode language, by constructing SIGIL, a 3,000-text generative emblem corpus with compositional meaning but no phonological values. A pre-registered registry of 54 published methods shows SIGIL is classified the same as the Indus corpus on every reproducible criterion. A constructive negative result for computational decipherment claims.

entry.title: What Language Does and What the Evidence Supports: A Functional Role Taxonomy and Evidence Audit of Language Grounding in Embodied Agents

author.name: Yifan Guo, Chenghao Li, Zhu Wang, Wei Xu, Yu Li, Yulong Zhu, Zhuo Sun, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: A survey that separates what language does inside embodied agents from what the evidence actually supports, defining five functional roles (specification, embodied representation, action orchestration, grounding regulation, execution coupling) and the observations or interventions needed to test each claim. Applying the framework reveals a recurring gap where interpretable linguistic intermediates may be wrong, unused, or causally inert. Useful epistemic hygiene for the language-conditioned robotics literature.

entry.title: Aligning Large Vision-Language Models at Test Time: A Trajectory-Guided Structured Sampling Approach

author.name: Tianbao Jiang, Weicong Ni, Gerard de Melo, Linlin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes test-time alignment for large vision-language models using trajectory-guided structured sampling, curating a reasoning memory bank that decomposes complex questions into ordered primitive steps and using it to refine inference dynamically. Motivated by the cost of post-training RL and the mismatch between training objectives and inference-time distributions. An inference-time alternative to RL alignment for visual reasoning.

entry.title: RIDGE: Re-Noising with Internal Dynamic Guidance for Image Editing

author.name: Ruiliang Gong, Zhen Wang, Yanghao Wang, Long Chen

entry.summary: RIDGE is a training-free, inversion-free image editing method that corrects the geometry of the target-side state used at each flow step, replacing the standard equal-displacement construction whose updates become too aggressive at high noise levels. It maintains the edited state as an evolving approximation of the unavailable clean target.

entry.title: Predictive Enhancement Calibration for Latent Breast MRI Virtual Contrast Enhancement

author.name: Qin Lei, Hao Wu

entry.summary: Predictive Enhancement Calibration addresses a mismatch between natural-image latent autoencoders and the non-canonical intensity scale of MRI when synthesizing contrast-enhanced breast MRI from pre-contrast scans. It uses a shared case-adaptive coordinate during training and predicts the missing upper intensity endpoint at inference, integrated with a pretrained latent flow transformer.

entry.title: A fully nonlinear structural vector autoregressive model identified via independent innovation analysis

author.name: Savi Virolainen

entry.summary: Introduces a structural VAR model in which the contemporaneous mapping from shocks to observables may be nonlinear and non-additive, identified by exploiting how an observed exogenous variable shifts the conditional distributions of independent shocks. A contrastive learning objective recovers the shocks, and added structure strengthens identification beyond the componentwise-transformation ambiguity of standard independent innovation analysis.

entry.title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale

author.name: Banruo Liu, Haoran Qiu, \'I\~nigo Goiri, Rodrigo Fonseca, Ricardo Bianchini, Esha Choukse

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Microsoft researchers present what they describe as the first production-scale characterization of agentic coding workloads, using sampled GitHub Copilot traces from June 2026 covering 3.2M users, 13M sessions, 761M model calls, and 95 trillion tokens. They show agentic sessions consist of sparse user turns that expand into autonomous loops of model calls plus tool execution, with KV cache hit rates around 90 percent within a turn but dropping to roughly 55 percent across turn boundaries. The findings have direct implications for scheduling, caching, and capacity planning in inference infrastructure.

entry.title: RAG-TESTER: Automated End-to-End Testing of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Ange Maiztegi, Jon Ayerdi, Miren Illarramendi, Aitor Arrieta

entry.summary: RagTester automatically generates retrieval documents, test inputs, and expected outputs for RAG pipelines, executes them, and grades results with an LLM judge, deliberately targeting complex passages, unanswerable queries, and document coverage. It is evaluated across 24 combinations of eight generator models and six embedding models. The contribution is a software-testing perspective on end-to-end RAG reliability.

entry.title: MRAFnd: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Zero-Shot Fake News Detection

author.name: Lehan Zhang, Yinlei Cheng, Shiqi Hu Yiheng Zhou, Shangxi Li, Naidong Zhao

entry.summary: MRAFnd detects multimodal fake news about unseen events by retrieving analogous past disinformation campaigns rather than judging items in isolation, then reasoning over cross-modal inconsistencies. Targets zero-shot generalization to novel events.

entry.title: An Embedded RISC-V Evaluation of Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks in Hard-Constrained Recurrent Physics-Informed Models

author.name: Enzo Nicolas Spotorno, Josafat Leal Filho

entry.summary: Using identical trained weights, this paper measures whether Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks retain their claimed parameter efficiency when deployed as residual branches of hard-constrained recurrent physics-informed models on embedded RISC-V hardware, given that learnable B-spline activations have a very different execution profile from MLPs. It is a deployment-cost reality check rather than an accuracy study.

entry.title: VGER: Voxel-Guided Global Event Ranking for Event Cloud Attribution

author.name: Youxin Jiang, Baoheng Fu, Hongwei Ren, Xiangqian Wu

entry.summary: VGER is a training-free attribution method for point-based event-camera networks that ranks individual events by importance using voxel-guided global structure rather than naively transplanting point-cloud saliency methods. It aims to make event-based model predictions interpretable at the event level.

entry.title: Stop Replacing Noise with Noise: Two-Source Reliability Assessment for Label Correction and Sample Reweighting in Label-Noise Learning

author.name: Wenxiao Fan, Kan Li

entry.summary: Argues that refurbishment-based noisy-label learning couples label trust and pseudo-target trust through a single score, so distrusting a noisy label automatically trusts a pseudo target that may reproduce the same noise. The proposed method decouples the two using separate reliability signals derived from shallow versus deep representation diagnostics.

entry.title: Design-Time Optimization of Deep Neural Networks for Intermittent Learning on Microcontrollers

author.name: Jakob Schubert, Maximilian Kasper, Maximilian Linke, Benedict Herzog, Mark Deutel, Axel Plinge, Dominik Seuss, Christopher Mutschler

entry.summary: Presents a design-time multi-objective optimization method for neural networks that must train on microcontrollers under intermittent power, using a per-layer energy predictor that includes checkpointing overhead. This avoids costly repeated on-device deployment during design.

entry.title: POEM: Phase-Aware $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ Feature Rotation for Time Series Forecasting Under Periodicity Drift

author.name: Jiawen Zhu, Shuhan Liu, Shengxuan Li, Qiming Shi, Di Weng

entry.summary: POEM handles periodicity drift in time series forecasting by learning a phase-correction coordinate and applying an invertible two-dimensional rotation to paired latent features. This lets the model accommodate shifting cycle timing instead of assuming a fixed time grid.

entry.title: Internalizing Academic Writing Workflows for Introduction Generation via Struct-Aware Policy Learning

author.name: Meicong Zhang, Tiancheng Su, Jiahao Cheng, Guoxiu He, Xinqi Tao, Dejia Song

entry.summary: StructPO internalizes a multi-stage academic writing workflow for generating paper introductions into a single-pass policy controlled by explicit stage tokens, avoiding the cost and cross-stage drift of prompt pipelines or agent workflows. It adds struct-aware credit assignment separating local stage quality from global coherence, plus refinement-guided optimization to fold revision behavior into the first pass. A general recipe for compressing agentic pipelines into one policy.

entry.title: On the Diversity of Analogy Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Yuanhao Shen, Daniel Xavier de Sousa, Caio C\'esar Sifuentes Barcelos, Hongyu Guo, Xiaodan Zhu

entry.summary: Evaluates the diversity, not just the quality, of analogies produced by ten open and closed LLMs and finds pronounced domain homogeneity, with models repeatedly drawing on a narrow set of target domains both across queries and within a model. Argues this limits cross-domain connection making and scientific ideation value. Adds to the growing evidence of creativity collapse in aligned models.

entry.title: Global Graph-Validated Optimization for VLM-based 3D Indoor Scene Generation

author.name: Jialu Huang, Yingxuan You, Fei Wang, Zheng Dang

entry.summary: This work generates open-vocabulary 3D indoor layouts by having a VLM produce a graph-based intermediate representation that separates semantic coherence from physical feasibility, then applying hybrid global optimization. It targets failures where pairwise or local constraints yield globally inconsistent or physically infeasible scenes.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Representation-Guided Generative Dataset Distillation

author.name: Mingzhuo Li, Guang Li, Linfeng Ye, Jiafeng Mao, Takahiro Ogawa, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: SRG performs generative dataset distillation guided by self-supervised representation geometry, building class prototypes from real-image SSL features and steering diffusion synthesis to preserve the discriminative structure of frozen pretrained encoders. This matches the modern practice of adapting frozen backbones rather than training from scratch.

entry.title: 3DGSI-Assessor: A Large-Scale Dataset and An LMM-based Method for 3D Gaussian Splatting Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Yuke Xing, Jiarui Wang, William Gordon, Zhu Li, Guangtao Zhai, Yiling Xu

entry.summary: The authors release a large image quality assessment dataset for compressed 3D Gaussian Splatting content and a multimodal-model-based metric that reports separate geometry and color distortion diagnoses. Conventional image metrics fail to capture splatting-specific artifacts such as floaters and surface scattering.

entry.title: Geospatial-Prior Guidance for 3D Semantic Scene Completion

author.name: Meng Wang, Shougao Zhang, Wenzhe He, Ruihui Li, Nan Hu, Zhuo Tang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: GeoScene improves 3D semantic scene completion from onboard camera images by adding satellite imagery and structured map data as soft priors, learning voxel-wise reliability weights that balance onboard observations against possibly stale or misaligned geospatial cues. This helps fill occluded and out-of-view regions.

entry.title: SEER: A Self-Grounded Evidence Interface for Controlled Spatial Relation Classification

author.name: Feixiang Liu, Likun Wang, Qiang Qiu, Hui Xu, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: SEER is a training-free inference-time interface that makes spatial relation reasoning explicit for frozen vision-language models: it first localizes the queried subject and object with candidate relations hidden, then constructs a role-labeled view alongside the full image and box geometry. It targets failures where a model recognizes both entities but answers from the wrong instance.

entry.title: UniEvo-RS: Omni-Prompt Unified Remote Sensing Segmentation with Representative Exemplar-Driven Prototype Evolution

author.name: Kunquan Zhang (Sun Yat-sen University), Peilang Li (Sun Yat-sen University), Xikun Hu (National University of Defense Technology), Yunkai Yang (Sun Yat-sen University), Yushan Zou (National University of Defense Technology), Zhiwei Zhang (Sun Yat-sen University), Runmin Dong (Sun Yat-sen University)

entry.summary: UniEvo-RS is a unified prompt-driven remote sensing segmentation framework where prototypes evolve from a small set of representative annotated exemplars, mirroring how human annotators refine samples before batch mapping. It supports multiple prompt intents and task routing for operational mapping workflows.

entry.title: GeoMAR: Unleashing Geometrically Aligned Features for Masked Autoregressive Blind Face Restoration

author.name: Lu Gan, Hanyu Yan, Chaofeng Chen, Junqi Hu, Dan Zeng

entry.summary: GeoMAR improves blind face restoration by extracting explicit component-level geometric descriptions as spatially faithful anchors and fusing them with degraded features through a key-value to query exchange, then replacing one-shot codebook prediction with masked autoregressive refinement. It targets fragile prediction under severe degradation.

entry.title: Multi-Task Multi-Frame Visual Piano Transcription

author.name: Yonghyun Kim, Hoyeol Sohn, Juhan Nam, Alexander Lerch

entry.summary: V2N is presented as the first complete visual piano transcription system, predicting note onset, offset, key hold, and velocity from video using a shared temporal backbone with per-frame supervision. Video helps because the sustain pedal makes audio-based systems report pedal-extended rather than physical key-release offsets.

entry.title: Lightweight 3D Object Detection via Mamba-Based Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Quoc Cuong Ninh, Huy Xuan Pham, Anh Tung Nguyen, Dinh Hoan Trinh

entry.summary: A knowledge distillation framework transfers object-level voxel representations from a strong LiDAR detector to lightweight students via selective voxel-space feature alignment, exploiting the linear-complexity properties of Mamba-style sequence modeling. The goal is embedded-device 3D detection for driving and navigation.

entry.title: Forbidden Region Dynamic Active Constraints in Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery

author.name: Zejian Cui, Ferdinando Rodriguez y Baena

entry.summary: This paper presents an energy-dissipative forbidden-region active constraint pipeline for robot-assisted surgery that accommodates respiration-induced tissue deformation using depth sensing and a very fine mesh representation. It targets the passivity, deformation handling, and speed obstacles blocking clinical adoption of haptic guidance constraints.

entry.title: Accelerating Human-Aware Robot Trajectory Generation via Diffusion and Consistency Distillation

author.name: Byeong-Il Ham, Hyun-Bin Kim, Kyung-Soo Kim

entry.summary: This work generates collision- and self-collision-aware manipulator trajectories with sampling-based planners, trains a diffusion model on the resulting dataset, and applies consistency distillation to accelerate inference for human-robot interaction settings. It targets non-redundant arms where extra constraints cannot be handled as null-space tasks.

entry.title: Training nGPT

author.name: Ilya Loshchilov, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Presents a practical training recipe for the normalized transformer (hyperspherical parameter and activation constraints) applied to modern hybrid Mamba-2 plus Transformer mixture-of-experts models, introducing logit gradient preconditioning, logarithmic learning-rate decay, GatedAdamW and angular update control. A 14B-total-parameter nGPT reaches the same validation loss as an AdamW-trained baseline with roughly half the training tokens.

entry.title: Similarity Weighted Aggregation with Global Differential Privacy for Federated Brain Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Muhammad Irfan Khan, Eero Lehtonen, Joni Obradovic, Elina Kontio, Esa Alhoniemi, Suleiman A. Khan, Mojtaba Jafaritadi

entry.summary: DP-SimAgg combines similarity-weighted aggregation to handle non-IID institutional data with server-side differential privacy, applying L2 clipping to bound collaborator updates and injecting calibrated Gaussian noise, applied to federated brain lesion segmentation. It aims to preserve segmentation quality under both statistical heterogeneity and formal privacy guarantees. The setting is multi-institution medical imaging where data cannot be pooled.

entry.title: CT-PrepAgent: Bounded Policy and Controlled Execution for Adaptive CT Data Preparation

author.name: Xiaolin Fan, Yue Pei, Yingying Zhang, Haogang Zhu

entry.summary: CT-PrepAgent is an LLM agent that adapts CT imaging data-preparation pipelines to heterogeneous acquisitions using a bounded action policy plus deterministic execution and inspection gates. Replaces hand-written, dataset-specific preprocessing rules.

entry.title: Trustworthy AI in Digital Health: A Comprehensive Review of Robustness and Explainability

author.name: Abdullah Mamun, Shovito Barua Soumma, Hassan Ghasemzadeh

entry.summary: A review synthesizing robustness and explainability research for AI in digital health, organized across the lifecycle from problem formulation to deployment and human interaction. Positions fairness, accountability, and privacy alongside the two focal dimensions.

entry.title: LLMBDC: Language Model for Biological Domains Oriented Clustering of Gene Ontology

author.name: Ximing Ran, Jie Xu, Peng Jin, Zhaohui Qin, Zhexing Wen, Jiaying Lu

entry.summary: LLMBDC uses a language model to cluster redundant Gene Ontology enrichment terms into interpretable higher-order biological domains, replacing fixed similarity metrics and static hierarchy maps with context-aware grouping. It aims to make routine genomics enrichment output readable without manual curation.

entry.title: Unleashing the Potential of Large Language Models: A Blueprint for Real-Time, Enterprise-Ready Deployments

author.name: Muhammad Faizan Raza (Luna), Shuo (Luna), Yang, Satish Mahadevan Srinivasan, Joanna F. DeFranco

entry.summary: This blueprint paper proposes a pattern-driven LLMOps architecture integrating real-time ingestion, continual learning with sparse temporal adapter routing and freshness-aware replay, SLO-aware adaptive retrieval that predicts a per-query passage budget, and automated human-in-the-loop feedback. It targets knowledge staleness, forgetting, hallucination, and weak feedback loops in regulated enterprise deployments.

entry.title: REIMU: Efficient Heterogeneous Hierarchical Reasoning for SSL-Based Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Kwok-Ho Ng, Tingting Song, Bingwen Feng, Peiya Li

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of recurrent hierarchical reasoning backbones (weight-shared recurrence, homogeneous and heterogeneous hierarchical reasoning modules) on top of self-supervised speech frontends for detecting synthetic speech. It reports which recurrence structures actually help deepfake detection versus conventional single-pass heads.

entry.title: DeVIT: Low-Power Vision Transformer Acceleration Using Delta Computation

author.name: Reyhaneh Hosseinzadeh, Parham Zilouchian Moghaddam, Mehdi Modarressi

entry.summary: DeVIT is a hardware accelerator design that exploits value locality in quantized vision transformers by computing on deltas between similar values, reducing power and memory bandwidth. It targets deployment on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: ProtoAct: Turning Wet-Lab Protocols into Embodied Robotic Actions

author.name: Zhe Liu, Jiaming Gu, Zhaohui Du, Zhe Wang, Huanbo Jin, Quan Lu, Qi Wang, Ting Xiao, Minting Pan, Dongzhan Zhou

entry.summary: ProtoAct converts free-text biology wet-lab protocols into state-aware, robot-executable action sequences using retrieval of annotated exemplars, a consistency checker for missing steps, and a constrained JSON action schema. It ships BioP2E, a manually annotated set of cell-culture protocols with hundreds of grounded steps.

entry.title: Illuminating Visual Identity in Universal Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Jiawei Cao, Junyi Feng, Jiashen Hua, Ziheng Huang, Bing Deng, Kaijie Wu, Chaochen Gu, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: The paper formalizes visual identity discrimination as a missing capability in universal multimodal embeddings and introduces MVEB, a large benchmark covering instance retrieval, re-identification, and identity preservation, along with methods to improve identity-aware embeddings. It argues current MLLM-based embedding models conflate semantic similarity with identity.

entry.title: Beyond Magnitude and Shape: A Direction-Aware Loss for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jaehoon Lee, Jun Seo, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: CosDir is a scale-invariant loss that aligns the difference vectors of forecasts and targets by cosine similarity, restoring gradient signal for small directional moves where mean-squared error training performs poorly. It targets decision-driven forecasting where the sign of change matters as much as the magnitude.

entry.title: Music Restoration via Latent Operator Optimization and Diffusion Model Priors

author.name: Michal \v{S}vento, Eloi Moliner, Valtteri Kallinen, Lauri Juvela, Vesa V\"alim\"aki, Pavel Rajmic

entry.summary: LOUDAR restores degraded music by treating the unknown distortion as a learnable operator in the latent space of a pretrained audio autoencoder, alternating between estimating the clean latent and updating operator parameters under an unconditional latent diffusion prior. This removes the need for paired data or knowledge of the specific degradation.

entry.title: MANGO-Grasp: Mahalanobis Fields over Geometry-Oriented 3D Gaussians for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping

author.name: Heng Zhang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Mike Zheng Shou, Weisi Lin, Yan Wu

entry.summary: MANGO-Grasp represents objects as anisotropic geometry-oriented 3D Gaussian primitives allocated by local surface complexity and encodes robot hands as morpho-kinematic keypoint descriptors, enabling dexterous grasp synthesis that transfers across different multi-fingered hands. It targets cross-embodiment generalization without per-hand tuning.

entry.title: Diffusion Policy with Behavioral Advantage Correction for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Botao Dong, Longyang Huang, Ning Pang, Hongtian Chen

entry.summary: This paper corrects Q-value estimation in offline reinforcement learning using the behavior policy's own Q-function, aiming to reduce both overly pessimistic conservatism and overestimation bias, with a convergence analysis and an error bound. Diffusion models are used to express the policy and limit distribution shift.

entry.title: Grounding Agentic VLMs with Dedicated Segmentation for Fine-Grained Vehicle Damage Assessment

author.name: Vishwajeet Shivaji Hogale, Anjali Pai, Nitya Ravi

entry.summary: Shows that a strong vision-language model classifies vehicle damage accurately (about 87 percent) yet is spatially ungrounded, hallucinating damage in reflections and missing thin scratches, and proposes pairing the agentic VLM with a dedicated segmentation module for fine-grained localization. Provides a concrete case study of the semantics-versus-grounding gap in deployed VLM pipelines.

entry.title: GeoID-PINN: Identifiability-Aware Regional Epidemic Inference with Geographic Coupling

author.name: Weixiong Hua, Fan Bu

entry.summary: GeoID-PINN is a physics-informed neural network for regional SIRD epidemic dynamics that models spatial coupling through a row-stochastic source-composition matrix regularized toward priors built from distance, adjacency, or commuting data. Simulations show identifiability improves markedly with a compatible prior and degrades badly under misspecification.

entry.title: CT-HEG: A Bidirectional, Timestamp-Attributed Event Graph for ICU In-Hospital Mortality Prediction - An Architectural Ablation Study

author.name: Mohammad Nasir Uddin, Rahnuma Tabassum Orpita, Asaduzzaman Anik, Eklachur Rahman Bhuiyan, Marjahan Risalat, SM Wali Ullah, Asif Ahamed

entry.summary: Introduces a continuous-time heterogeneous EHR graph schema that encodes ICU stays as typed timestamped graphs with visit, vital, and lab nodes plus timing and value edge attributes without imputation, instantiated as a heterogeneous graph attention network. An architectural ablation on MIMIC-IV isolates which design choices actually drive mortality prediction.

entry.title: Measuring Explainer Stability via Attribution Separability

author.name: Eddie Conti, \'Alvaro Parafita, Axel Brando

entry.summary: Proposes a distribution-based framework for quantifying the stability of feature-attribution explanations, identifying how far down a ranked attribution vector the ordering remains statistically reliable. Extends this to compare attribution methods by ranking robustness across a dataset.

entry.title: Adaptive Sampling for Automated Post-Disaster Rapid Damage Assessment via Level-Set Cost-Aware Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Boyang Xu, Mostafa Reisi Gahrooei, Mohammad Ilbeigi, Hao Yan

entry.summary: Combines cost-aware Bayesian optimization with level-set estimation to route autonomous data collectors such as UAVs toward the most informative regions during post-disaster damage assessment. The adaptive sampling policy reduces assessment uncertainty faster than static survey strategies.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Hybrid Neural Operator for Transient Magnetization Prediction in Power Magnetics

author.name: Yachao Zhu, Qiujie Huang, Sinan Li, Yang Li, Gang Lei, Jianguo Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a compact physics-informed hybrid neural operator that predicts transient magnetization and core loss in power magnetics from measured field history, with energy-consistency regularization on the B-H relationship. Targets regimes with non-sinusoidal waveforms, minor loops, dc bias, and temperature variation that steady-state loss formulas cannot capture.

entry.title: Revisiting TD Target Aggregation under Uncertainty in Q-Learning

author.name: Lipeng Zu, Xiaonan Zhang

entry.summary: SADQ modifies the temporal-difference target in deep Q-learning by using one-step rollout predictions from a learned dynamics model to regularize the greedy maximization, which otherwise trusts the largest but possibly noisiest value estimate. The aim is to dampen overestimation error amplified through bootstrapping.

entry.title: Operationally Feasible Synthetic Power-Grid Scenarios via Learning the AC-Operable Joint Distribution

author.name: Chenhan Xiao, Xinyu He, Haoran Li, Hanghang Tong, Yang Weng

entry.summary: Learns the joint distribution over grid topology, branch parameters, and time-varying loads such that generated synthetic power-grid scenarios are actually solvable under AC power flow. This replaces post-hoc feasibility filtering or optimization with feasibility-aware distribution learning.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimal Semiparametric Contextual Dynamic Pricing with Multimodal Revenue

author.name: Xueping Gong, Zhuoluo Zhang, Zhaowei Miao, Jiheng Zhang

entry.summary: A theoretical treatment of contextual dynamic pricing where demand follows a semiparametric surplus-index model and revenue need not be concave or unimodal. The authors propose a layered decision-partitioning policy with pilot correction and prove it attains minimax-optimal smoothness-dependent regret. Relevant to pricing and revenue-management practice where standard regularity assumptions fail.

entry.title: Dual-domain U-Nets with embedded back projection operators for motion-resolved 4D CBCT reconstruction

author.name: Ivo Herzig, Pascal Paysan, Daniel Barco, Marc Andr\'e Stadelmann, Frank-Peter Schilling, Igor Peterlik, Michal Walczak, Lijin Aryananda, Woo Sang Ahn, Rudolf Marcel F\"uchslin, Lukas Lichtensteiger

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-domain U-Net for motion-resolved 4D cone-beam CT reconstruction that takes free-breathing projections and predicts a static inhalation volume plus ten displacement vector fields, with non-trainable back-projection operators replacing skip connections. Removes the need for respiratory signals or projection binning. Could shorten scan times and reduce dose in image-guided radiotherapy.

entry.title: Less Traffic, Better Outcomes: Competition-Aware Request Dispatch in Real-Time Ad Exchanges

author.name: Jonaid Shianifar, Blaz Mramor, Fangda Zou, Matthieu C. Martin, Xingsheng Guo, Zhihua Zhu, Rong Zhou, Bichen Shi

entry.summary: Describes a competition-aware request dispatch system for a production ad exchange that uses distributional bid prediction and probabilistic forwarding to decide which demand-side platforms see each request, adapting thresholds online to non-stationary markets. Validated in four sequential online experiments on a live platform. Shows sending less traffic can improve auction outcomes.

entry.title: Knowing the Form, Not the Function: Automatically Auditing Answer--Authority Decoupling in Legal Benchmarks

author.name: Hsien-Jyh Liao

entry.summary: Tests whether answer correctness proxies for legal-authority grounding by auditing four LLMs on 238 Taiwan bar-exam items where each has a verified governing provision. The two dimensions dissociate in both directions: many answer-correct responses miss the gold authority, and a sizable fraction of answer-incorrect responses cite it. Undermines a common assumption in legal benchmark scoring.

entry.title: Standalone DINOv3 for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing

author.name: Changhao Zhao, Haoxiang Li, Yuke Li, Hai Liu, LingLin Zeng

entry.summary: DinoSplat-OV adapts a standalone DINOv3 backbone with text alignment to training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation of satellite imagery, using Laplacian propagation over patch predictions and multi-scale handling. It avoids the costly pixel-level annotation that limits remote sensing segmentation.

entry.title: CAPE-T2V: Captioner-Anchored Prompt Enhancement toward Two-Sided Conditioning Alignment in Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Yizhuo Jia, Jingyun Hua, Yuanxing Zhang

entry.summary: CAPE-T2V targets the mismatch between prompts rewritten at inference by a prompt enhancer and the detailed captions a text-to-video diffusion transformer was trained on. It anchors the enhancer to the training captioner so both sides of conditioning use the same detail selection, organization, and phrasing.

entry.title: XiDepth: a Lightweight and Efficient Network for Self-supervised Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Elena Izzo, Riccardo Toniolo, Lamberto Ballan

entry.summary: XiDepth is a compact self-supervised monocular depth network designed to avoid energy-expensive depth-wise convolutions and attention so it maps well onto constrained embedded hardware. It targets the accuracy versus deployability trade-off for robotics and edge vision.

entry.title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics

author.name: Rainier Natividad, Raye Chen-Hua Yeow

entry.summary: A position paper proposing Human-Centric Embodied Intelligence as an organizing framework for soft wearable robots, arguing that intelligence in exosuits and assistive garments emerges from the coupled human-device system rather than the controller alone. It surveys how morphology, multimodal sensing, adaptive cognition and compliant actuation should be co-designed with the wearer's physiological adaptation.

entry.title: Chess on Ice: Curling Tactical Decision-Making via Backward Induction and Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Patrick Oberlin, Matteo Cederle, Aren Karapetyan, Saverio Bolognani, Gian Antonio Susto, Florian D\"orfler

entry.summary: Applies DDPG with finite-horizon backward induction to curling tactics, handling continuous state and action spaces, stochastic shot outcomes reflecting player skill, and sensitivity of transitions to small action perturbations. Provides quantitative comparison of tactical options in an underexplored game.

entry.title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI

author.name: Taye Akinrele, Sindhuja Penchala, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: Survey organizing the cognitive shortcomings of generative and agentic AI into five dimensions: persistent state modeling, goal-directed autonomy, self-monitoring and control, environment interaction, and learning and adaptation. Intended as a taxonomy-driven map of what still blocks reliable long-horizon operation.

entry.title: AiFlow: Token-Native Reactive Orchestration with Bounded Backpressure for Streaming LLM Applications

author.name: Qunhui Zhang

entry.summary: AiFlow proposes a token-native reactive orchestration model that normalizes provider streaming deltas into typed events flowing through a directed graph, with per-node guardians enforcing queue bounds, worker concurrency, ordering, overflow policy, cancellation propagation, and retry discipline. It replaces ad hoc callback code for backpressure in streaming LLM applications.

entry.title: Loanword or Switch? The Annotation Boundary, Not the Model, Drives Kazakh-Russian Code-Switching Identification

author.name: Bogdan Savelyev

entry.summary: This paper shows that off-the-shelf language identification and letter heuristics over-report Kazakh-Russian code-switching because integrated Russian loanwords in shared Cyrillic script look like switches. The authors release a document-level gold LID set whose guidelines keep borrowings as Kazakh, plus a mixed-only sentiment pool, and show across six approaches that the bottleneck is the annotation boundary rather than model class.

entry.title: FedCARE: A Multi-Objective Personalised Federated Learning Framework for Smart Healthcare

author.name: Rojalini Tripathy, Padmalochan Bera, Shreya Ghosh, Rajkumar Buyya

entry.summary: FedCARE personalizes federated learning for hospitals that pursue different and sometimes conflicting clinical objectives while holding partially non-overlapping feature sets. It combines multi-objective optimization with personalization rather than assuming a single shared global objective.

entry.title: Amortized Interventional Forecasting for Multivariate CIR Processes

author.name: Andreas Sauter, Sumit Sourabh, Drona Kandhai, Erman Acar

entry.summary: Proposes an amortized model that predicts multi-horizon responses to external shocks in multivariate mean-reverting financial processes without per-scenario retraining, plus a causal generative process for benchmarking. The point is that standard correlated CIR models cannot answer interventional questions.

entry.title: CRS-Triage: Confidence- and Reliability-Aware Selective Triage under Incomplete Clinical Evidence

author.name: Guan Qiang, Yushen Chen, Tianlong Liu, David Rotenberg, Ethan H. Kim, Fang Fang

entry.summary: CRS-Triage predicts emergency department acuity from incomplete and unreliable EHR data while emitting a confidence score, deferring cases below a threshold to clinicians. It explicitly accounts for evidence reliability as well as predictive confidence.

entry.title: A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence via Asymptotic Equivalence with the Target

author.name: Patrick Forr\'e

entry.summary: Gives a self-contained proof of the Markov chain convergence theorem via a criterion the author calls asymptotic equivalence with the target, based on singular masses in Lebesgue decompositions vanishing in both directions. The criterion is shown necessary and sufficient on countably generated spaces and verified in several general cases. Foundational probability theory with implications for MCMC analysis.

entry.title: How Many Labels Are Enough? ALDA: Active Learning Deployment Advisor for Medical Image Classification

author.name: Julia Machnio, Mads Nielsen, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi

entry.summary: ALDA helps practitioners choose an active-learning strategy before committing an annotation budget, by fitting parametric learning curves during a short pilot phase and predicting whether and when each strategy reaches a clinical performance target. Framed around the real risk that a poorly chosen AL strategy raises rather than lowers labeling cost. Deployment-oriented contribution for medical imaging projects.

entry.title: ANCHOR-RE: An Agentic Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Grounded Biomedical Relation Extraction

author.name: Shufan Ming, Yikun Han, Gibong Hong, Rui Zhang, Halil Kilicoglu

entry.summary: ANCHOR-RE combines ontology-guided reasoning, external knowledge grounding, and data-driven verification rules with LLM inference for biomedical relation extraction, aiming to keep symbolic precision while gaining LLM contextual recall. Evaluated on SemRepGS, DDI, and ChemProt with both proprietary and open-weight models, plus generalization tests beyond the benchmarks. Relevant to automated biomedical knowledge base construction.

entry.title: NanoMorph-3D: An End-to-End Physics-Driven Unrolling Framework for Nanomaterial Reconstruction

author.name: Beiyuan Zhang, Hesong Li, Ziqi Wu, Ruiwen Shao, Ying Fu

entry.summary: NanoMorph-3D is an end-to-end unrolled physics-driven network for 3D nanomaterial reconstruction from electron tomography, tackling the missing-wedge problem and heavy noise. It trains on a large synthetic dataset that models nonlinear electron attenuation and organizes shapes by a nanomorphological taxonomy.

entry.title: When Oracle Conditioning Misleads Deployment: Conditioning-Availability Bias in Echocardiographic Segmentation

author.name: Dang P. M. Cao, Hieu D. Pham, Hieu Pham

entry.summary: This paper shows that phase-conditioned cardiac ultrasound segmentation models trained and evaluated with clean oracle auxiliary signals can fail badly when only estimated signals are available at deployment, a protocol-level form of shortcut learning. It proposes paired gap measurements plus deployment-aware checkpoint selection and phase perturbation testing.

entry.title: Towards Reliable and Reproducible Fetal Brain Biometry: A Deep Learning Approach Using MRI

author.name: Francesca Maccarone, Marina Di Stefano, Giorgio Longari, Giulia Frigerio, Gloria Rizzato, Rocco Prudentino, Nivedita Agarwal, Tommaso Ciceri, Denis Peruzzo, Simone Melzi

entry.summary: A fully automated four-stage deep learning pipeline extracts fetal brain biometric measurements from super-resolution reconstructed 3D MRI, jointly predicting distances and the anatomical landmarks that define them. Interpretable landmark output is intended to make automated measurements auditable against manual clinical practice.

entry.title: A Wearable Stiffness-Rendering Haptic Device with a Honeycomb Jamming Mechanism for Bilateral Teleoperation

author.name: Thomas M. Kwok, Bohan Zhang, Wai Tuck Chow

entry.summary: The HJ-Haptic is a 20 gram wearable device using a honeycomb jamming mechanism under vacuum to render object stiffness between roughly 1.15 and 2.64 newtons per millimeter for bilateral teleoperation. Flexural testing and teleoperated grasping trials show operators can modulate grip force based on the feedback.

entry.title: A False Average: Chain-of-Thought Monitors Collapse Where They Are the Only Defense

author.name: Shikhar Shiromani, Leo Richter

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, The authors show that chain-of-thought monitoring collapses exactly where it is the only defense: rewriting an agent's reasoning to read as good-faith engineering while leaving every command and output byte-identical drops a held-out monitor's catch rate on that subset from about 95 percent to under 11 percent in a single gradient-free attempt. Because aggregate monitor accuracy is dominated by hacks visible in the actions, it hides this near-total failure, and the attack transfers across monitor families and agent settings.

entry.title: CN101 - A Digital Thermodynamic Computer for Generative AI

author.name: Lars Holdijk, Denis Melanson, Zier Mensch, Brandon Birchall, Vincent Cheung, Nicholas Lehrter, Maxwell Aifer, Samuel Duffield, Jan Ole Ernst, Rajath Salegame, Antonio J. Martinez, Gavin Crooks, Miranda Cheng, Zach Belateche, Marc Bright, Patrick J. Coles, Faris Sbahi

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, CN101 is a digital thermodynamic computer for generative AI in which stochastic physical dynamics are the computational primitive, computing answers as time-averaged statistics of an equilibrating trajectory. Crucially it moves this equilibration-style computation off Langevin dynamics and analog substrates into a digital implementation, removing much of the engineering difficulty that has confined the paradigm to analog hardware.

entry.title: An AI Approach to Verified Production Cryptographic Libraries

author.name: Chuyue Sun, Su Fong, Zhiyi Kuang, Yizheng Jiao, Nina Narodytska, Haoze Wu, David L. Dill, Clark Barrett

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, CryptoProver synthesizes internal specifications and Verus-checked proofs for production Rust cryptography from high-level API contracts, producing an independent proof of curve25519-dalek and a first verification of RustCrypto's chacha20 against RFC 8439. It moves LLM-assisted formal verification from isolated proof obligations to real deployed libraries.

entry.title: Slides2MindMap: Reconstructing Cognitively Efficient Knowledge Hierarchies from Lecture Slides

author.name: Yuzhi Wang, Rongjun Ye, Shengyuan Chen, Huachi Zhou, Jiaqi Bai, Chuang Zhou, Zhicong Hong, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: The authors define the Slides2MindMap task of reconstructing cognitively efficient knowledge hierarchies from entire course slide decks and release S2M-Bench, comprising 12,774 slide pages with expert-annotated mind maps across 24 university courses. Evaluation is grounded in cognitive science criteria balancing global and local knowledge focus. The application area is intelligent education tooling.

entry.title: From AI Technical Debt to Agentic Technical Debt: A Systematic Mapping of Root Causes and Manifestations in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Muhammad Tukur, Hayatullahi B. Adeyemo, Tao Chen, Nour Ali, Anis Zarrad, Marco Agus, Rick Kazman, Rami Bahsoon

entry.summary: This systematic mapping study introduces Agentic Technical Debt as a category distinct from prior AI technical debt models, arguing that autonomous reasoning, multi-agent collaboration, tool orchestration, and persistent memory create debt that emerges, propagates, and amplifies dynamically rather than sitting in static components. It catalogs root causes and manifestations across agentic systems. The intended audience is software architecture and maintenance practitioners.

entry.title: Homebot: A Personal AI Agent for Conversational Home Assistance and Automation

author.name: Shengyuan Ye, Yixin Zhang, Han Liang, Liekang Zeng, Jiangsu Du, Mu Yuan

entry.summary: Homebot is a locally deployable household assistant that unifies voice and messaging channels over a shared runtime combining LLM responses with registered tools and skills, using wake-word activation, streaming ASR and TTS, and an explicit dialogue-state protocol. Emphasizes clear channel, tool, and skill contracts for customization.

entry.title: A Fortran General-Purpose Transpiler: Proof of Concept

author.name: Shivamshan Sivanesan, Kazem Ardaneh

entry.summary: FGPT is a proof-of-concept compiler pipeline that transpiles Fortran into GPU-adapted Fortran, automatically differentiable Fortran via Tapenade, or NumPy and JAX code. It targets the scientific-computing expertise gap where legacy Fortran codebases must reach modern differentiable and accelerator ecosystems.

entry.title: Symbolic Attack Chain Generation from Atomic Red Team Techniques: An Empirical Study of Predicate Representation Granularity

author.name: Ramya Varunsegar

entry.summary: This empirical study asks whether the nine-category predicate scheme used by state-of-the-art automated attack-chain planners is actually necessary, comparing predicate granularities in a pipeline where an LLM translates Atomic Red Team techniques into PDDL and a classical planner reasons deterministically. It measures the effect of representation choices on plan validity, cost, and fidelity.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for the Characterization of Particles and Fibers by Optical Microscopy

author.name: Simiao Sun, Kenneth Ng, Lynn Lee, Astrid Harth, Asami Odate, Aggelos Katsaggelos, Manuel Ballester Matito, Nicholas Eastaugh, Marc Walton

entry.summary: The authors distill a multimodal teacher that combines microscopy image embeddings with text embeddings for illumination modality, magnification, and specimen identity into a student model, producing block-structured embeddings whose components remain physically interpretable. The goal is reliable automated characterization of particles and fibers under varying optical conditions.

entry.title: DSETA: A Dual-Stage Continual Learning Framework for Travel Time Prediction in Dynamic Traffic Environments

author.name: Yanming Lyu, Yue Cheng, Lingkun Li, Ruipeng Gao, Xinyue Liu, Hui Gao, Qiang Ni

entry.summary: DSETA is a continual-learning framework for ride-hailing arrival-time prediction that splits incremental updates into inter-day and intra-day stages so long-term traffic trends are disentangled from short-term congestion shocks. It targets accuracy degradation under distribution shift in production ETA systems.

entry.title: UOT-IR: Structured Routing of High-Polyphony Symbolic Music into Fixed-Budget Representations

author.name: Ziyue Kang, Nan Nan, Chenhao Lin, Xiaohong Guan

entry.summary: UOT-IR treats compression of densely orchestrated symbolic music into fixed track or slot budgets as a structured routing problem solved with constrained unbalanced optimal transport, without training. The aim is to preserve structural roles, orchestration compatibility, and playability where heuristic simplification fails.

entry.title: FL-OA: A Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning Framework with Outsourced Auditing for Intelligent Devices

author.name: Hongliang Zhang, Zhongyuan Yu, Fenghua Xu, Teng Hu, Jian Meng, Jiguo Yu

entry.summary: FL-OA is a Byzantine-robust federated learning framework that outsources update auditing to collaborating parties, aiming to work without assuming a majority of honest clients or a clean server-side root dataset. It also addresses benign-update divergence and high-dimensional comparison difficulties.

entry.title: Enhancing Visual Perception in Foggy Conditions via Multiclass Fog Density Modeling

author.name: Mohamad Mofeed Chaar, Galia Weidl

entry.summary: Studies autonomous driving perception under five synthetic fog density levels derived from Waymo data with learned depth estimation, and finds that training separate density-specific models beats a single unified model, especially in severe fog. It quantifies the benefit of conditioning perception on weather severity.

entry.title: QWRF-Net: A Quantum-Wavelet Framework with Rectified Flow for Short-Term Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Zhuo Wang, Chaorong Li, Wenjie Luo, Chuanhu Deng

entry.summary: QWRF-Net combines quantum-inspired components, wavelet multi-scale decomposition and rectified flow generation for short-term radar precipitation nowcasting, aiming to preserve intense convective cores at longer lead times. It targets hydrometeorological early warning for flash flooding.

entry.title: SPECTRA: Band-Routed Embedding and Stage-Wise LoRA for Cross-Sensor Fine-Tuning of Geospatial Foundation Models

author.name: Xingyan Li, Jordan A. Caraballo-Vega, Jie Gong, Mark L. Carroll, Jianwu Wang

entry.summary: SPECTRA adapts Earth-observation foundation models to downstream sensors whose spectral bands differ from pretraining, using band-routed embeddings plus stage-wise LoRA to cut adaptation cost. It tackles spectral mismatch and fine-tuning efficiency jointly rather than separately.

entry.title: EntailLLM: Verifying LLM-Generated Vulnerability Discovery Paths with Domain Knowledge via Logic Programming

author.name: Kaustuv Mukherji, Jaikrishna Manojkumar Patil, Colton Payne, Paulo Shakarian, Dana Warmsley, Nigel Stepp, Evelyn Kim

entry.summary: EntailLLM checks whether LLM-proposed vulnerability discovery paths through a binary's call graph are logically entailed by an independent domain knowledge graph, using temporal annotated logic for verification. It evaluates across several CWE classes in safety-critical software such as medical devices.

entry.title: DeGS: A Scalable 3DGS Architecture via Decoupled Workload Parsing and Reorganization

author.name: Minnan Pei, Gang Li, Zeyu Zhu, Siting Wang, Junwen Si, Zhuoran Song, Yu Feng, Fangxin Liu, Xiaoyao Liang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: DeGS is a hardware architecture for 3D Gaussian splatting inference that decouples the tightly coupled checking-and-blending dataflow, reorganizing workloads to remove spatial redundancy from irregular Gaussian coverage and temporal redundancy from asynchronous pixel termination. This restores scalability as the number of processing elements grows.

entry.title: UniqueSplat: View-conditioned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Generalizable 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Haixu Song, Xiaoke Yang, Shengjun Zhang, Jiwen Lu, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: UniqueSplat makes feed-forward Gaussian splatting view-conditioned, predicting Gaussians tailored to each query viewpoint instead of one fixed set shared across all views as in pixelSplat and MVSplat. The view prior is baked into network parameters so Gaussians adapt dynamically at query time.

entry.title: HarMoE: Multi-Source Chest Radiograph Pretraining with Dataset-Disentangled Experts

author.name: Haozhe Luo, Ziyu Zhou, Shelley Zixin Shu, Mauricio Reyes

entry.summary: HarMoE pretrains chest radiograph models from many heterogeneous multi-label classification datasets rather than relying mainly on a single image-report corpus, using dataset-disentangled mixture-of-experts routing to keep clinical semantics from being entangled with dataset identity. This aims to improve transfer across sources with different label ontologies and acquisition pipelines.

entry.title: Topological Simplification in Predictive Coding Networks

author.name: Adam Shaw, Jiayu Li, Michael Sperling, Michael Kim, Alvin Jin

entry.summary: Uses layer-wise persistent homology to study how predictive coding networks reshape representation topology, finding that smaller networks collapse connected components earlier across layers and reporting correlations between topological simplification and model size or performance. Provides quantitative structural insight into a neuro-inspired bidirectional architecture.

entry.title: Forecasting Revenue with its Customer-Base Drivers: When and Why Coordination Helps

author.name: Kyeongbin Kim, Daniel McCarthy, Dokyun Lee

entry.summary: Introduces a customer-based multi-task transformer that forecasts revenue by jointly modeling acquisition, repeat purchase, order size, and their coordination across 966 firms of weekly transaction data. Reports large error reductions over established customer-base benchmarks and a small, statistically insignificant edge over direct total-sales forecasting.

entry.title: The Ignition Is Real, and It Lives at the Readout: Latent composition, difficulty-clocked ignition, and the interface-constituted commit in a recurrent-depth reasoner

author.name: Simon Lam-Muir

entry.summary: Attempts to determine whether the reported compositional ignition in latent-reasoning models is genuine computation, an instrument artifact, or inherited from verbal training data, by regrowing an independent 30M-parameter recurrent-depth reasoner from the same recipe and seed and tracking both vocabulary readout and hidden state. It reports that the ignition event appears at the readout, arrives later for deeper problems, and reproduces across two same-seed realizations with divergent training trajectories.

entry.title: TabletCraft: Bridging a 4,000-Year Cultural Gap with Bidirectional Akkadian NMT and Cuneiform Rendering

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: TabletCraft is an open-source system for bidirectional Akkadian translation plus rendering of composed text as cuneiform tablets, extending beyond prior scholar-oriented one-way translation. It lets non-specialists write in the world's oldest writing system rather than only read translations.

entry.title: Surrogate Substitution Preserves PHI Detectability: A Multi-Detector Equivalence Study

author.name: Qiming Bao, Sherry J. H. Feng, Kim Chester Eugenio, Meng Fon

entry.summary: Studies whether replacing protected health information with realistic same-type surrogates (instead of placeholder tags) degrades the ability of downstream PII detectors to find those spans. Using paired equivalence testing (TOST) on 57k spans across multiple detectors, the work provides a methodological protocol that scores utility only on masked spans. Matters for privacy-preserving clinical NLP pipelines.

entry.title: Conformal risk control for model-form uncertainty in parametric non-intrusive reduced-order models

author.name: Edgar Jaber (CB, ENS Paris Saclay), R\'emy Vallot (CB, Michelin), Thibault Dairay (CB, Michelin), Mathilde Mougeot (CB, ENSIIE, ENS Paris Saclay)

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for quantifying model-form uncertainty in non-intrusive reduced-order models of parametric PDEs by randomly perturbing reduced bases on the Stiefel manifold and wrapping the result in distribution-free conformal risk control. Aims to give reliability guarantees in extrapolation and small-data regimes. Relevant to industrial surrogate modeling and simulation.

entry.title: SRAP: SVD-Refined Adversarial Perturbations for Imperceptible Face-Swap Defense

author.name: Sungwon Cho, Kwanghyun Ko, Myungjoo Kang

entry.summary: Analyzes why PGD-based protective perturbations against face-swapping look visually bad, attributing it to spatially diffuse perturbations and salient high-frequency energy concentrated in later singular components. SRAP refines perturbations using identity-sensitivity estimates and SVD truncation to preserve protection while improving imperceptibility. Contributes to proactive deepfake defenses.

entry.title: Divide-and-Conquer: Towards Generalizable Amortized Bayesian Inference for the Drift Diffusion Model

author.name: Yufei Wu, Shanqing Gao, Andreas Voss, Francis Tuerlinckx

entry.summary: Proposes decomposing drift diffusion model datasets into pairwise shards so a single amortized Bayesian inference network can generalize across study designs, rather than requiring retraining per design. Inference is done on shards and recombined, exploiting the model's independence assumption. Practically useful for cognitive science workflows.

entry.title: Socially Grounded Agentic AI: Coordinating Plural Perspectives through Social Theory

author.name: Matt Ratto, Abhishek Moturu, Daniel Silver

entry.summary: Argues that pluralistic alignment lacks an account of how values are socially organized, contested, and coordinated, and imports concepts from sociology to structure how agentic systems represent and reconcile multiple legitimate perspectives. Offers conceptual and design resources rather than experiments. Contributes to the theory side of alignment beyond single-value optimization.

entry.title: Modeling Scientific Experiment Scenes: Dataset and Model

author.name: Minghao Zou, Qingtian Zeng, Shangkun Liu, Cong Liu, Paul L. Rosin, Guanghui Yue, Jun Liu, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: PhysScene is presented as the first scene graph generation dataset for physics laboratory experiment scenes, with dense annotations of instruments and fine-grained physical relations. The authors highlight long-tailed predicate distributions and a visual-textual semantic gap as core challenges.

entry.title: CrossScope: A Role-Asymmetric World Model for Joint Dual-Scope Surgical Video Prediction

author.name: Wanhao Liu, Jinsong Lin, Rulin Zhou, Chi Kit Ng, Wenbin Pan, Zhiqing Tang, Dongyue Li, Liwei Luo, Yanshen Wu, Panshuo Li, Zhiyong Xiong, Huxin Gao, Tamas Haidegger, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: CrossScope is a surgical world model that predicts future frames from two independently moving endoscopes in mother-child ERCP, transferring cross-view evidence asymmetrically according to each view's role rather than assuming symmetric fusion. It formalizes role-asymmetric dual-scope future prediction.

entry.title: Residual Flow Matching with Dynamic Cross-Interaction for 3D Multi-Person Motion Prediction

author.name: Wei Wei, Yinyuan Zhao, Ruixuan Yu

entry.summary: This method predicts 3D multi-person motion with flow matching over residuals from a deterministic coarse kinematic prior, rather than generating skeletal sequences from pure noise, and adds a dynamic cross-interaction mechanism between agents. The prior stabilizes structure during early noise-dominated steps.

entry.title: Morphology-Aware Implicit Super-Resolution Network for Pathological Images

author.name: Jiaming Liang, QiHui Han, Haolin Chen, Chengxin Ye, Jiawen Liu, Jiazhou Chen, Xiaoqi Sheng, Hongmin Cai

entry.summary: Morph-ISR treats super-resolution of whole-slide pathology images as continuous coordinate-based reconstruction with morphology-aware priors, aiming to preserve cellular texture and boundaries rather than oversmoothing. The goal is to let cheaper low-resolution scanners support diagnostic-quality digital pathology.

entry.title: PLS-Calib: A Partial Least Squares Framework for Event Camera and Odometry Calibration under Ground Motion Constraints

author.name: Guangyu Li, Xiao Li, Yujie Wu, Changshuo Wang, Prayag Tiwari, Jiang Cai, Fangwen Yu, Mingkun Xu

entry.summary: PLS-Calib performs extrinsic rotation calibration between an event camera and wheel odometry for ground robots that cannot excite all six degrees of freedom, using partial least squares regression to model latent motion relationships. It is proposed as a numerically stabler alternative to canonical correlation analysis approaches that suffer ill-conditioned covariance matrices.

entry.title: Contact-Driven Localization in a Freeform Robotic Self-Assembled Structure

author.name: Mohammadali Rashidioun, Michael Sosa, Petras Swissler

entry.summary: This paper localizes modular self-assembling robots using only binary contact information about which neighbors are docked, via a virtual-force scheme where robots are attracted to connected neighbors and repelled from unconnected ones. The aim is to eliminate dependence on external tracking or expensive sensors in swarm self-reconfiguration.

entry.title: Ekova: A Personality-Support Agent for Self-Discovery Dialogue

author.name: Yuyan Chen

entry.summary: Ekova proposes Personality Support as a paradigm distinct from emotional support, aiming to help users articulate and understand themselves rather than relieve distress. It contributes a Chinese dataset of 8,590 self-discovery dialogue samples across five interaction personas and a multi-persona system trained with a style-tailored fine-tuning framework. The authors are explicit that this is not clinical intervention.

entry.title: Neuro-Evolved Heuristics for Variable Gapped Common Subsequence Identification

author.name: Marko Djukanovi\'c, Christian Blum, Aleksandar Kartelj, Saso Dzeroski, Ziga Zebec

entry.summary: This work automates the design of beam-search heuristics for the multi-sequence variable gapped longest common subsequence problem, representing heuristics as a fixed-architecture neural network whose weights are optimized by a genetic algorithm in a neuro-evolutionary loop. It replaces hand-crafted guidance functions that generalize poorly. Applications include sequence alignment and time-series analysis.

entry.title: Logographic Character Visual Pretraining via Semantic-based Contrastive Learning

author.name: Daqian Shi, Wei Cao, Xiaoyu Zheng, Lida Shi, Xiaolei Diao, Cedric M John

entry.summary: The paper proposes contrastive visual pretraining for logographic characters (e.g., Chinese) that injects visual-semantic component information so recognition works despite heavily imbalanced, long-tailed character frequency distributions. It targets historical and low-frequency character resources where large balanced datasets do not exist.

entry.title: OrEdge: Efficient Multi-Modal Anomaly Detection in Distributed Software Systems via Orthogonal-Domain Learning

author.name: Amr M. Zaki, Farhoud Jafari Kaleibar, Honggeun Ji, Komal Sarda, Marin Litoiu

entry.summary: OrEdge performs real-time multi-modal anomaly detection over logs, metrics, and traces in distributed software systems using orthogonal-domain temporal reconstruction instead of attention or graph architectures, aiming for much smaller models and lower compute. It targets edge-deployable observability.

entry.title: Structured Proxy Features for Multimodal NSCLC Survival Prediction from Pretreatment CT

author.name: Huu Phong Nguyen, Delower Hossain, Ehsan Saghapour, Zhandos Sembay, Jake Y. Chen

entry.summary: This study tests whether adding six simulation-derived proxy features that encode interactions among tumor characteristics improves multimodal survival prediction for non-small-cell lung cancer from pretreatment CT, radiomics, and clinical variables. The premise is that standard radiomic and deep features treat imaging descriptors as independent quantities.

entry.title: PartMat: Material-Aware 3D Part Decomposition with a Single Global Latent

author.name: Guangming Fu, Jin Song, Yiyun Fei, Guoqiu Li, Ruigao Yang, Jianan Jiang

entry.summary: PartMat decomposes a single 3D object into material-consistent parts such as fabric, wood, or metal using one global latent, rather than functional-semantic parts generated independently per part. This avoids compute scaling linearly with part count and better matches editing needs in applications like interior design.

entry.title: PatTree: a novel approach for automated creation of multimodal, graph-based patient representations for medical classification tasks

author.name: Julia Gehrmann, Lars Quakulinski, Hamza Naseem, Oya Beyan

entry.summary: PatTree automatically constructs graph-based, multimodal patient representations from messy real-world clinical data, avoiding the resource-intensive harmonization normally needed before integration. The goal is scalable and reproducible multimodal clinical classification despite missing values, mixed modalities, and inconsistent semantics.

entry.title: Automatic Patient-Specific Microwave Ablation Planning Accelerated by a Physics-Guided Deep Learning Model

author.name: Seonaeng Cho, Minjee Seo, Minju Seol, Juil Park, Joon Ho Kwon, Kyungho Yoon

entry.summary: Builds a digital-twin planning framework for liver microwave ablation that replaces expensive multiphysics simulation with a physics-guided neural surrogate inside a genetic algorithm optimizing antenna trajectory, power, and duration. The surrogate is trained on simulations over patient-specific tumor and vessel anatomy.

entry.title: LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation

author.name: Eugene Lee, Oseong Choi, Byungsoo Kang, Taeyeong Jang

entry.summary: Uses LLMs to convert the text of user comments into informative Bayesian priors that warm-start Thompson sampling for comment recommendation, addressing cold start when arms have no interaction history. Segment-level hierarchies account for aggregate differences in response patterns. A practical bridge between semantic models and bandit exploration.

entry.title: Mapping the City Through the Lens of Language Models

author.name: Wanqi Liu, Rong Zhao, Zhizhou Sha, Qinyu Cui, Yecheng Zhang

entry.summary: Measures the implicit urban assumptions ten open-weight LLMs make when a city is underspecified, by having them rate anonymized morphological profiles of real urban centers on 40 audited indicators, with reliability screens, lineage-aware aggregation, and independent replication. Finds a shared preference for larger, faster-growing, infrastructure-dense, less sprawling profiles. Relevant to bias auditing in planning and policy uses of LLMs.

entry.title: A Unified 2D Framework for DeepLesion Detection, Segmentation and Short Report Generation

author.name: Ruida Cheng, Tejas S. Mathai, Benjamin Hou, Qingqing Zhu, Zhiyong Lu, Matthew McAuliffe, Ronald M. Summers

entry.summary: An NIH-affiliated group builds a single 2D pipeline over the DeepLesion CT dataset that detects lesion boxes, segments them, and generates short radiology findings text with LLM-based reasoning. It reports moderate detection (mAP50 about 70) and segmentation (Dice about 63) plus BLEU/ROUGE report metrics. It matters as an integrated clinical workflow prototype rather than a methodological advance.

entry.title: Open-Linguistic Concept Unified Learning for Cross-Site Interpretable Dermatology Image Diagnosis

author.name: Chengyu Wu, Junpeng Tan, Wanxiang Luo, Yaqi Wang, Yandong Wen, Yefeng Zheng

entry.summary: This paper builds concept-based interpretable dermatology diagnosis that generalizes across sites and modalities by unifying heterogeneous clinical concept taxonomies into an open-linguistic space, so a vision-language model does not need per-dataset label engineering. It also allows clinician interventions beyond a fixed predefined concept list.

entry.title: Energy Efficiency of Locally Deployed LLMs: A Preliminary Quantitative GPU Power Benchmark on Consumer Hardware

author.name: Philipp M. Z\"ahl, Anika Hennig

entry.summary: A hardware-level energy benchmark measures GPU power draw for nine open-source models from 1B to 7B parameters running locally on a single consumer RTX 4060Ti via Ollama, reporting joules per prompt, joules per output token, and throughput. Results indicate that architecture and quantization matter beyond raw parameter count for energy cost. It provides a reproducible protocol for on-premise sustainability accounting.

entry.title: Don't Offer What Can't Be Done: Deterministic Executability Gating for LLM Skill Selection at Scale

author.name: Ortal Ashkenazi, Vitalii Kloz, Mykhailo Ulianchenko

entry.summary: Describes a deployed three-stage skill-selection pipeline for a commercial customer-care assistant that adds a deterministic gate filtering out skills that cannot actually execute given account state. Argues semantic relevance alone is insufficient for production agent routing.

entry.title: Understanding Online Failure Prediction in Linux Through Complementary Multi-View Explainability

author.name: Diogo D\'oria, Jo\~ao R. Campos

entry.summary: This experience report builds an explainable online failure prediction pipeline for Linux, combining consensus-based feature selection with temporal onset analysis, subsystem-level causal analysis, and complementary diagnostics. The motivation is that accurate alerts are useless without diagnostic insight, and that high accuracy may reflect workload-specific telemetry correlations rather than real failure processes.

entry.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism

author.name: Donna M Bye, Levin Kuhlmann

entry.summary: A critical humanities-style argument that the dominant framing of AI anthropomorphism as user error reflects institutional authority rather than established evidence, and that it delegitimizes users' relational experiences with AI systems. It calls for re-examining who gets to define appropriate human-AI interaction.

entry.title: AI-assisted Script Management for Requirements Elicitation Interviews

author.name: Anmol Singhal, Paulo Carvalho, Travis Breaux

entry.summary: Presents an AI-assisted workflow for requirements elicitation interviews that generates theory-guided scripts from business goals and provides live topic-coverage tracking and probing support. It studies how integrated rather than isolated AI support changes the interview process and resulting requirements artifacts.

entry.title: FAST-GS: Frequency Aware Space-time Gaussian Splatting for Photorealistic Dynamic Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Zhengyang Zhang, Ziyu Lu, PengCheng Li, Hongbo Duan, Yi Liu, Pengting Luo, Peiyu Zhuang, Xinghui Li, Shaohua Ma

entry.summary: FAST-GS replaces single-polynomial motion models in 4D Gaussian splatting with a Fourier decomposition that separates low-frequency global trajectories from high-frequency local motion, aiming to reduce cumulative trajectory drift in long dynamic sequences. It preserves real-time rendering while improving quality on complex motion.

entry.title: RamanPFN: learning from Raman spectral structure with a tabular foundation model

author.name: Xingyu Pan, Huan Wang, Jinjia Guo, Zhenlin Zhao, Siming Dong, Jixi Lu

entry.summary: RamanPFN adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to Raman spectra by preserving spectral structure and joint visibility of related bands, instead of the feature-subsampled views that standard in-context tabular inference uses on very wide inputs. It targets small labelled spectral datasets where task-specific deep networks and latent-variable chemometrics both struggle.

entry.title: Open-Set Visual Text Forensics via Sparse-Constraint Rectified Flow

author.name: Jiangling Zhang, Shuxuan Gao, Zeyu Chen, Yichao Liu, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: This generative forensics method localizes manipulated text in images by estimating the local restoration cost needed to bring a query image back to authentic visual-text statistics, using a sparsity-constrained rectified flow rather than a discriminative forgery classifier. Self-supervised artifact injection mitigates training data scarcity for unseen open-set attacks.

entry.title: Syntax Meets Semantics: Understanding Scientific Formulae

author.name: Yuni Susanti, Moritz Schubotz

entry.summary: Empirically studies the correspondence between the syntactic form of scientific formulae and their semantic descriptions, finding that native representation spaces show very weak observable alignment despite latent correlation. The work matters for mathematical information retrieval and scholarly search systems.

entry.title: DyFrDet: Towards Accurate Small Object Detection via Dynamic Frequency Suppression with Label Disambiguation

author.name: Zihan Yang, Yang Guo, Hongxing Zhang, Dan Lu, Siyuan Yao

entry.summary: DyFrDet targets small-object detection by dynamically suppressing frequency-domain background noise via an adaptive feature pyramid and by disambiguating noisy assignment labels. Reports improved localization for objects with few discriminative pixels.

entry.title: UNVaMP: Neural Knowledge Tracing with Variational Regularization of Latent Knowledge Dynamics

author.name: Carson J. Cook, Ahmed J. Zerouali, Anthony Schmidt, Reginald Ziedzor, Paul Lin, Luke G. Eglington

entry.summary: UNVaMP is a knowledge-tracing architecture that combines observed student interactions with memory to produce latent knowledge trajectories, with explicit control over trajectory smoothness via variational regularization. It can run as a pure neural predictor or as a hybrid with an interpretable measurement layer.
