entry.summary: The authors show that VLA brittleness to paraphrased instructions is architectural rather than a semantic understanding failure: the models internally retain correct task identity, but joint encoding of dynamic visual input and text shifts features that the action head cannot tolerate. They propose re-binding grounded semantics to fix the failure without large-scale data collection.

entry.title: Learning What to Remember and What to Internalize in LLM Self-Evolution via Adaptive Memory-Parameter Coordination

author.name: Tianyun Ji, Zhenya Huang, Jiayu Liu, Zirui Liu, Yu Su, Hongbin Pei

entry.summary: COVE coordinates two self-evolution channels for deployed LLM agents: externalized editable memory or skills for fast adaptation, and parameter updates for deeper internalization, deciding per task which channel should absorb new experience. The framing addresses the flexibility-versus-capability trade-off when APIs and requirements change post-deployment.

entry.title: Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance

author.name: Alireza Lotfi, Subangkar Karmaker Shanto, Imtiaz Karim, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: A systematization of agentic AI security arguing that safety must be assessed over whole action trajectories against system rules and invariants, not just per-action permission checks. It maps the threat landscape across the agentic stack, from untrusted prompt, memory, and retrieval inputs at the single-agent level up to cross-organizational delegation.

entry.title: Latent Thought Credit: Multi-Answer Credit Assignment for Latent Reasoning

author.name: Xuyang Zhao, Liting Zhang, Zichen Xu, Yong Chen, Wenjia Zeng, Shiwan Zhao, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: Latent Thought Credit addresses credit assignment for continuous latent reasoning by sampling multiple latent thoughts per prompt, freezing the context after each, and averaging rewards over several sampled answers to estimate that thought's value. Hierarchical advantages then separately optimize the latent-thought phase and the answer phase.

entry.title: Allocation Before Ranking: Decoupled Token Compression for OmniLLMs

author.name: Zhenghui Guo, Yilin Yang, Yuanbin Man, Miao Yin, Weidong Shi, Rabimba Karanjai, Omprakash Gnawali, Chengming Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that top-K token compression in omni-modal LLMs conflates two decisions, how much retained budget each modality gets and which tokens within a modality survive, which biases retention toward audio at video's expense. Macer is a training-free compressor that first allocates explicit per-modality budgets then ranks within modality at modality-specific shallow layers.

entry.title: TCPO: Turn-Level Credit Policy Optimization

author.name: Sicong Liao, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: TCPO converts per-turn verifier scores into genuine credit for multi-turn reinforcement learning by comparing each turn against reference states, using retrospective credit for progress or regression relative to the best prior state. The insight is that a dense score measures current output quality while credit must measure the turn's contribution to the refinement trajectory.

entry.title: DAPD: Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation

author.name: Jianyu Wu, Yizhou Wang, Encheng Su, Chen Tang, Shixiang Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses a privilege illusion in on-policy self-distillation, where the student imitates behavior that depended on reference information it will never see at inference, and traces it to teacher-student information asymmetry. DAPD adds dual-path anchoring with a self-conditioned bridge to keep the student's learned behavior reproducible from its own context.

entry.title: SSTG-Nav: Metric-Grounded Spatial-Semantic Topological Graphs for Reusable Object Navigation

author.name: Daojie Peng, Bingtao Wang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: SSTG-Nav builds a reusable metric-semantic topological memory for object navigation so that long-lived service robots accumulate knowledge instead of exploring familiar spaces from scratch, explicitly separating recognizing an object from identifying a reachable stopping place and retaining recovery standoffs when map evidence is wrong. On 1,000 HM3D-v2 episodes across 36 scenes the goal-independent topology reaches a 99.4 percent geometric success ceiling.

entry.title: EduPluginBench: Executable Assurance for AI-Generated Educational Plugins

author.name: Nizam Kadir

entry.summary: EduPluginBench is an executable benchmark and staged admission pipeline for AI-generated educational plugins that checks properties compilation and functional tests miss, such as least privilege, telemetry consent, provenance, privileged-write authority, lifecycle constraints and bounded failure. Staged gates raised release-blocking-defect recall by about 75 percentage points across 1,440 activation-checked mutants with no false rejections observed among 120 clean references.

entry.title: Hybrid Lagrangian-Eulerian Model for Lagrangian Fluid Simulation

author.name: Ruoyan Li, Wei Wang, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: Combines Lagrangian particle dynamics with an auxiliary Eulerian grid representation for neural fluid simulation, using adaptive downsampling to avoid wasting capacity on uniform regions and a global anchor to reduce temporal drift. Mirrors classical hybrid numerical solvers in a learned simulator.

entry.title: Rapid Embodiment Adaptation for Quadrupedal Locomotion

author.name: Dichen Li, Bo Ai, Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters, Hao Su, Henrik I. Christensen

entry.summary: Presents online embodiment adaptation for quadruped locomotion, inferring hardware parameters from short interaction histories and conditioning a randomization-trained generalist policy on the inferred state within about half a second. Evaluated on joint-range constraints and trunk-mass changes representing kinematic degradation and dynamic variation.

entry.title: MedPRESS: A Multi-turn Benchmark for Patient-Pressure-Induced Medical Sycophancy in LLMs

author.name: Saman Sarker Joy, Niloy Farhan

entry.summary: MedPRESS is a benchmark of 600 five-turn medically grounded dialogues that escalate patient pressure through personal experience, social proof, evidence claims, and direct challenge, measuring whether models abandon correct medical advice. Twenty models spanning general, medical, open-weight, and proprietary families are evaluated.

entry.title: Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report

author.name: Haonan Chen, Chu Li, Zhicheng Wang, Yuanwei Liu, Yuanjiang Wang, Shaohua Jiang, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Technical report on a two-stage multimodal embedding model for a large short-video platform, aiming to combine the serving efficiency of contrastive encoders with the fine-grained discrimination usually requiring chain-of-thought generation. It targets billion-scale indexing plus hard-negative discrimination in industrial search and recommendation.

entry.title: Action Chunk Scheduling for Batched Robot Policy Serving

author.name: Rohan Bansal, David He, Nadun Ranawaka Arachchige, Zhenyang Chen, Soobum Kim, Kexin Rong, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: This paper introduces the problem of serving one robot foundation policy to many robots from a remote GPU and casts it as a scheduling problem, building a system called Armory validated on simulated and real robot fleets. It shows that naive batching heuristics break down when robots consume action chunks at different rates, exposing a mismatch between standard batching and closed-loop robot control.

entry.title: Learning Panorama-Aware VLA for Mobile Manipulation with Whole-Body Teleoperation

author.name: Donglin Yang, Haoran Chen, Xingyu Chen, Lixing Liu, Manyi Li, Changhe Tu, Ke Xu, Xiaojian Ma, Si Liu

entry.summary: This work pairs a whole-body teleoperation rig for a wheeled bimanual robot with a panorama-aware VLA policy that uses wide field-of-view observations instead of narrow local cameras. It targets the data and perception bottlenecks in mobile manipulation.

entry.title: Inter-Residue Geometry Attention for Antibody-Specific Epitope Prediction

author.name: Chuanliu Fan, Nan Yu, Junjie Wu, Guohong Fu

entry.summary: Proposes using folded 3D residue geometry as the positional signal inside attention itself, via local-frame 3D rotary position encoding, for predicting which antigen residues a specific antibody binds. This replaces the usual pattern of bolting graph or point-cloud encoders onto sequence-ordered protein language model embeddings.

entry.title: Cognitive Demand Steering for Adaptive Meta-Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: John Scoville, Shengzhuang Chen, Yejin Bang, Stefan Winzeck, Jonathan Richard Schwarz

entry.summary: Cognitive Demand Steering is a training-free meta-reasoning loop where an LLM evaluator estimates the residual reasoning still needed rather than scoring progress so far, and uses that forward-looking signal to steer strategy, backtracking, and termination. It avoids the controller training and coarse search actions of prior meta-reasoning frameworks.

entry.title: V-Mem: Modality-Routed Retrieval for Long-Term Multimodal Agentic Memory

author.name: Dingyi Kang, Dongming Jiang, Yi Li, Guanpeng Li, Bingzhe Li

entry.summary: V-Mem diagnoses why multimodal agent memories fail on image-related questions, identifying a modality gap where queries retrieve same-modality content and a similarity-relevance gap where the most similar item is not the evidence. It proposes modality-routed retrieval for long-term interleaved text and image conversation memory.

entry.title: Is More Privileged Information Better? From Solution Traces to Problem-Solving Structure in Self-Distilled Reasoning

author.name: Xuyang Zhao, Liting Zhang, Zichen Xu, Zhihu Wang, Xu Caiyue, Shiwan Zhao, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: Argues that on-policy self-distillation teachers conditioned on full reference solutions leak information unavailable at inference, and instead supplies problem-space guidance describing initial state, goals, constraints, and a chosen transition path. Across three math benchmarks and models from 1.7B to 8B this yields the best question-only accuracy among compared privileged views.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Use Tokens: Durable Authorization State for Replay-Resistant LLM Agent Actions

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: Shows that single-use authorization tokens cannot prevent agents from executing one user-approved action multiple times, because replanning, retries, delegation, and crash recovery cause fresh tokens to be reissued for the same intent, which the authors call semantic replay. CapLease adds an issuer-side durable, monotonic record of the authorized action, confirmation, and remaining execution budget.

entry.title: CoEvoKG: Co-Evolving Knowledge Graphs with Self-Evolving Search Agents

author.name: Zhaoyang Li, Zenghuang Fu, Qiuyuan Ai, Ping Jiang, Haoyu Wu, Minghui Wu, Chenxu Zhao, Jie Song, Guannan He

entry.summary: CoEvoKG uses a knowledge graph both as a generator of verifiable multi-hop training tasks and as a persistent evidence store, jointly training a task generator and a search agent whose rewards depend on answer correctness and graph-supported entity paths. Verified evidence from successful searches is deduplicated and written back, so the graph and agent improve together instead of discarding search knowledge.

entry.title: One-Sided Quantile Coupling for Flow Matching

author.name: Jin-Young Kim, So-Yoon Cho, Hyun-Gyoon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces a one-sided coupling for flow matching that avoids quadratic mini-batch optimal-transport assignment by mapping data ranks along a few random orthogonal projections to Gaussian quantiles to construct the paired source sample directly. Aims for structured couplings at near-zero extra cost.

entry.title: KING: Embodiment-Aware Kinematic Graph Neural Network for Unified Motion Representation of Legged and Wheeled Robots

author.name: Taku Okawara, Aoki Takanose, Kenji Koide, Shuji Oishi, Masashi Yokozuka

entry.summary: KING is a graph neural network kinematic model that encodes robot embodiment structure (joint counts, wheels versus feet) so a single learned model supports odometry across legged and wheeled platforms. Targets proprioceptive odometry where exteroceptive sensing degrades and IMU drifts.

entry.title: Caliber: Cross-Architecture Extraction-Cost Control for Score-Returning APIs

author.name: Chi Wang, Hanwen Wang, Yu Xia, Zihan Wang, Guangdong Bai

entry.summary: Caliber defends score-returning prediction APIs against model extraction by calibrating i.i.d. Gaussian noise on logits, with proofs that agreement with clean predictions degrades monotonically in noise scale and that recovering clean logits imposes a provable per-input query cost. Frames the defense as choosing an explicit utility-versus-extraction-cost operating point.

entry.title: UDT: Reconciling U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers with Data-Adaptive Token Reduction

author.name: Junno Yun, Ya\c{s}ar Utku Al\c{c}alar, Mehmet Ak\c{c}akaya

entry.summary: UDT reconciles U-Net and Diffusion Transformer design by introducing data-adaptive token reduction to build multi-scale encoder-decoder structure, addressing degraded late-layer representations and imbalanced encoder-decoder behavior in isotropic DiTs. Presented as an alternative to representation-alignment regularizers.

entry.title: RoMeRL: Balancing Feedback Coverage and the Memory-Reward Trap in Self-Evolving Agent Memory via Reduced-Order Utility States

author.name: Yi Yang, Zhennan Chen, Yihong Zhuang, Tiehan Fan, Yinan Chen, Jian Li, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: RoMeRL tackles two coupled failures of learned memory for self-evolving LLM agents: utilities indexed by ever-growing trajectories dilute sparse feedback, and trajectory-level rewards misattribute credit to co-retrieved irrelevant memories. It compresses the utility space into fixed-dimensional per-task memory states factorized by outcome polarity and memory dynamics.

entry.title: ScrambleToolBench: Agents Search Exhaustively Even When Their Own Map Points to the Next Step

author.name: Vernon Toh, Navonil Majumder, Zhengyuan Liu, Nancy F. Chen, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: ScrambleToolBench strips semantic cues from tool schemas in an interactive terminal environment so agents must discover hidden tool behavior purely by trial and error, with added twists like mapping drift. The headline finding is that agents search exhaustively even when information they have already gathered indicates the next step.

entry.title: InfiniSplat: Implicit Gaussian Decoding for Large-Baseline Monocular View Synthesis

author.name: Jiawei Wang, Hao Yu, Yongzhen Hu, Xinyi Yang, Tao Ni, Xin Zhan, Junbo Chen, Xiaowei Zhou, Ruizhen Hu, Sida Peng

entry.summary: InfiniSplat performs feed-forward single-image 3D Gaussian Splatting using a surface-aligned rather than pixel-aligned Gaussian representation, so that primitives attach to inferred scene geometry instead of fixed image-grid positions. This is aimed at holding up under large baseline viewpoint changes where pixel-aligned methods degrade.

entry.title: ChainVLA: Chaining Vision-Language-Action Queries through a Unified Execution State for Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Yuzhi Huang, Weijue Bu, Ziyi Xiong, Jie Wu, Fanding Huang, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: ChainVLA is a 1.2B-parameter policy that chains successive action-chunk queries through a shared, revisable execution state combining a recurrent working state, sparse event memory, and a motion continuation term. It targets long-horizon manipulation where each replan currently discards prior context.

entry.title: Learning to Coordinate Symbolic Tools: LLM Agents for Verified Sum-of-Squares Certificates

author.name: Bohan Chen, Shivam N. Patel, Richard Hoffmann, Sam Looi, Tony Yue Yu

entry.summary: Trains an LLM agent to coordinate symbolic tools for producing weighted sum-of-squares certificates that machine-verifiably prove polynomial inequalities, using 1.35 million synthetic examples across eight supporting algebraic subtasks plus verifier-grounded optimization. Decomposing the composite task into trainable subskills is the key design choice.

entry.title: Bayesian and Motivated Reasoning in AI Agents

author.name: Eddie Yang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that AI agents reach different conclusions from identical numerical evidence when the surrounding framing changes, across medicine, election forensics, and geopolitical forecasting. Agents behave like motivated reasoners, favoring conclusions congruent with their prior beliefs rather than updating in a Bayesian manner.

entry.title: Where did the ambiguity go? Examining how multimodal models interpret polysemous words

author.name: Jasin Cekinmez, Addison J. Wu, Raja Marjieh, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: Compares how 17 text-to-image and 15 text-generation models handle ambiguous words given with no disambiguating context, finding that image generations collapse onto far fewer senses than text generations, and both are far less diverse than human imagination. Reveals a systematic multimodal ambiguity gap.

entry.title: Control Under Compression: Reliability Frontiers for Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Yinghan Hou, Zongyou Yang

entry.summary: Presents CompressAgent, an environment-verified benchmark measuring what happens to tool-using agent reliability when the persistent system-side control context (tool specs, policies, recovery protocols) is compressed. Across nine control contexts and over 15,000 runs it finds a nonlinear, method-dependent reliability frontier where naive rewriting degrades operational control well before token savings pay off.

entry.title: Agentic Stage-One Stellarator Optimization: Autonomous Multi-Objective Search for Finite-Beta Equilibria

author.name: Tingjia Zhang, Hongke Lu, Zhuoran Meng, Runlai Xu

entry.summary: Presents an agentic system that autonomously coordinates stage-one stellarator design, searching high-dimensional plasma boundary shapes and finite-beta MHD equilibria under multiple physics objectives while managing Fourier resolution, objective priorities, and solver budgets. The motivation is that expert-driven iterative optimization limits both design throughput and consistent dataset production for fusion research.

entry.title: Where Reasoning Diverges: Localized Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Weijun Gao, Xiang Ding, Tiancheng Xing, Haoyang Liu

entry.summary: Localized Multi-Agent Debate represents each agent's reasoning trace as typed nodes, finds the earliest point of genuine disagreement, and confines debate to those local segments while committing agreed-upon earlier steps. Evaluated on four multi-hop QA benchmarks across ten backbones from four families, it reports the best macro-averaged judge accuracy.

entry.title: Does the Competitive Component of Adversarial Self-Play Improve Legal Reasoning? A Controlled Negative Result

author.name: Miseog Shawn Kim

entry.summary: Reports a controlled negative result: adding an adversary and a verifiable survival reward to legal-argument self-play training yields no benefit over an otherwise identical non-competitive run, across four independent comparisons. Citations on both sides were machine-verified so survival depended on verified authorities rather than rhetoric.

entry.title: When Memory Updates but Behavior Does Not: Repairing Implicit Stale Dependencies in Personalized Agent Responses

author.name: Haofei Sun, Lin He

entry.summary: Targets the gap where memory-augmented agents update stored user state yet still plan around stale values, because verification checks the drafted response rather than the memory. StateAuditor reverses the direction, proposing old-to-new transitions from timestamped evidence and using deterministic code to pin quotations, confirm recency, and gate repairs on verified provenance and chronology.

entry.title: CoEvo-Mem: Co-Evolving Retrieval Policy and Memory Bank for LLM Agents

author.name: Bowen Ye, Yongchao Xu, Zhijian Li, Xiang Yin, Junkai Ma, Wenzhao Li

entry.summary: CoEvo-Mem closes the loop between retrieval and memory maintenance for long-term agents, noting that retrieval determines which memories get usage signals while memory updates reshape future retrieval. It combines frozen-LLM route-specific query rewrites with a lightweight residual router that co-adapts alongside the evolving memory bank.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Autonomous Architecture Research with a Language-Model Agent: A Behavioural Case Study

author.name: Aon Safdar, Mohamed Saadeldin

entry.summary: A behavioural case study in which one general-purpose LLM acts as the sole researcher on a neural architecture design problem across roughly 100 sequential experiments with tooling for experiment tracking, literature access and persistent memory. Documents how the agent improves a weak Vision Transformer baseline and where its autonomous research process breaks down.

entry.title: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration with Asymmetric Reinforcement Learning and Self-Distillation

author.name: Jim Dilkes, Vahid Yazdanpanah, Sebastian Stein

entry.summary: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration augments training prompts with varied instructions to broaden the behaviours an LLM attempts during RL post-training, then uses a combined asymmetric RL and self-distillation objective to fold that diverse experience back into the base policy. Targets the exploration problem specific to LLM action spaces.

entry.title: Fetch-then-Explore: Decoupling Selection from Extraction over a Persistent Workspace for Search Agents

author.name: Qi Liu, Yiqun Chen, Zidan Chen, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Fetch-then-Explore decouples page selection from information extraction by holding fetched pages in a persistent workspace that the agent can revisit and re-read later, instead of fixing a reading at fetch time or discarding pages when a new one opens. Aims to fix context waste in long multi-search research tasks.

entry.title: Auditing Data Provenance in LLM Fine-tuning via Intrinsic Distributional Fingerprints

author.name: Zirui Huang, Yunlong Mao, Wei Tong, Tingting Wu, Xin Ge, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: Distribution Provenance Audit is a post-hoc, black-box method to test whether a fine-tuned LLM was trained on proprietary data, relying on the idea that models must preserve the distributional fingerprint of their fine-tuning data to stay useful. It is designed to survive evasions like paraphrasing and distillation.

entry.title: SKT: Skill-Use Training at Scale via Verified Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Zelin Tan, Yiqun Zhang, Hao Li, Zhiyao Cui, Hejia Geng, Shao Zhang, Hangfan Zhang, Yang Chen, Xiaosong Wang, Lilong Wang, Zhenfei Yin, Shuyue Hu, Chen Zhang, Lei Bai

entry.summary: SKT synthesizes verified skill-use training data from 2,000 public agent skills, generating single- and multi-skill task packages with rule-based and agent-based verification, feedback-guided repair, and retention of only trajectories that genuinely use each required skill. Yields roughly 4,000 task packages and tens of thousands of trajectories for post-training.

entry.title: Mamba with Hierarchical Memory: Solving Representation Bottleneck in Long Sequence Modeling

author.name: Qinwen Wang, Jieping Luo, Aoxiang Qin, Ruoyu Zhao, Jianxiong Tang, Wei Zhang, Zhichao Lu, Luziwei Leng

entry.summary: Hierarchical Memory Mamba adds a lightweight working-memory module on top of a pretrained Mamba backbone that extracts slow paragraph-level semantics and compresses them into a retrievable long-term memory. Aims to relieve the fixed-state capacity bottleneck of recurrent linear attention models on long sequences.

entry.title: Faster-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Deep Action Modules?

author.name: Liheng Ma, Rui Heng Yang, Zhanguang Zhang, Mateo Clemente, Ziwen Hu, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: Questions whether world action models need action modules as deep as their video backbones, and proposes docking lightweight output heads onto a frozen pretrained video Transformer that serves as a representation hub with access to all layers. Faster-WAM instantiates this to cut robot-action inference latency.

entry.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies

author.name: Qiushi Lin, Chaojie Zhang, \'I\~nigo Goiri, Aditya Akella, Ricardo Bianchini, Jovan Stojkovic

entry.summary: AtumAI adds formal problem specification, transferable learning across tasks, and systematic candidate generation beyond LLM proposals to agentic search over datacenter control-plane policies such as scheduling and resource management. Targets the months-long manual cycle of designing and prototyping such policies.

entry.title: Conservation laws determine what physical learning remembers

author.name: Bijaya Dangol

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that conserved quantities in physical learning rules for resistive networks (equilibrium propagation, coupled learning, adjoint coupled learning) determine their inductive bias, proving equilibrium and coupled learning are trajectory-equivalent for single outputs while adjoint coupled learning dissipates conserved mass at twice its loss. It clarifies what analog-hardware learning rules actually memorize and how to design experiments that distinguish them.

entry.title: SPARC-Rad: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset and Evaluation Pipeline for Spatial and Anatomical Reasoning in Radiology Vision-Language Models

author.name: Satvik Tripathi, Mustafa Ege Seker, Kristian Quevada, Ebubechukwu D Enwerem, Pratham Khandelwal, Emine Meltem, Bera Koca, Shahriar Faghani, Jacinta Arnold, Dania Daye, Tessa S. Cook

entry.summary: SPARC-Rad is a manually curated benchmark of 300 radiologist-authored image-question pairs from healthy control CT, MRI and radiography studies that specifically probes spatial and anatomical reasoning in vision-language models rather than disease classification or report generation. It targets a capability gap that existing medical VLM benchmarks largely ignore.

entry.title: Tensor Probabilistic Model Checking of Finite-Horizon Markov Chains (Extended Version)

author.name: Jianlin Li, Nick Guo, Peter Ye, Yizhou Zhang

entry.summary: This paper recasts step-bounded probabilistic model checking of Markov chains as dense tensor computation so that off-the-shelf compiler toolchains and hardware accelerators can be used, proves the mapping sound, and implements it in a tool. It targets the dense-transition regime where explicit and symbolic representations scale poorly.

entry.title: Pretrain on Small Synthetic Data, Scale Large for Free: Symmetry-Aware Foundation Model for Logic Rule Induction

author.name: Yin Jun Phua

entry.summary: The paper introduces a canonical export procedure that decodes discrete logic rules from literal scores in a way that is exactly equivariant to atom naming, example order, polarity flips and label swap, letting a rule inducer trained on small synthetic schemas generalize to much larger ones without retraining. It is instantiated on a disjunctive-normal-form neural rule inducer.

entry.title: Element-Aware Group Learning for E-Commerce Image Generation

author.name: Jingtong Chen, Jiahui Wang, Xue Zhao, ShaoGuo Liu, Minghao Li

entry.summary: This paper improves GRPO-style post-training of vision-language models that write image-editing prompts for e-commerce creatives by assigning credit at the level of design elements such as composition, background and selling-point presentation rather than only at the full-prompt level. It avoids the step-level supervision or learned critics that other fine-grained credit-assignment methods require.

entry.title: Beyond Gene Reconstruction: Learning Cell Representations through Complementary Transcriptomic Views

author.name: Jiaqi Xiong, Yuntao hu, Yu Zheng, Yifei Shi, Xinyue Guo, Jiaxin Qi

entry.summary: Argues that masked-expression reconstruction pretraining for single-cell foundation models optimizes gene dependencies rather than whole-cell embeddings, and proposes contrastive pretraining over complementary transcriptomic views. Adaptations include co-expression-guided gene partitioning, expression-aware negatives, and competence-gated contrastive weighting.

entry.title: What Could the Agent See at 19:05? Generating Temporal Enterprise Scenarios from Real Research and Replaying Them to Evaluate Agents

author.name: Tezan Sahu, Himani Arora

entry.summary: Proposes generating temporally consistent enterprise scenarios so agents can be evaluated at arbitrary earlier moments of an episode rather than only against a single final snapshot, with attention to per-user visibility and future-state leakage. Scenarios are replayed to grade time-relative correctness across multiple applications.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Proximal Causal Inference under Hidden Confounding and Interference

author.name: Omar Faruque, Pavan Raj Ravi, Jianwu Wang

entry.summary: Extends proximal causal inference to spatiotemporal data by constructing treatment- and outcome-inducing proxies that capture both local and neighborhood confounding, deriving a spatiotemporal outcome confounding bridge. Targets settings like climate and environmental policy where hidden confounders and interference both violate standard assumptions.

entry.title: PICTURE: Enhancing Theory-of-Mind in Large Language Models by Revealing, Not Hiding, Characters' Lack of Knowledge

author.name: Eojin Jeon, SangKeun Lee

entry.summary: Argues that the common theory-of-mind trick of hiding events unknown to a character hurts performance due to rigid output-format constraints, and instead generates free-form perspective explanations while training the model to inhibit responses to information the character lacks. Targets a longstanding weakness in LLM social reasoning.

entry.title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code

author.name: Yuqiao Tan, Jinxiang Meng, Fangyu Lei, Minzheng Wang, Shizhu He, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: SWE-Touch benchmarks coding agents in shared workspaces where a human concurrently edits task-relevant code, using validated counter-edits mined from repair trajectories that conflict with task completion. It measures whether agents notice, reconcile, or blindly overwrite user changes.

entry.title: HP-JEPA: Hierarchical Partitioning for Multi-Resolution Graph Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning

author.name: Ruichen Xu, Jingxiang Qu, Wenhan Gao, Jiaxing Zhang, Linsey Pang, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Yann LeCun, Yuefan Deng

entry.summary: HP-JEPA extends joint-embedding predictive learning to graphs by predicting masked targets across an ordered bank of coarse-to-fine partitions rather than one fixed partition. This multi-resolution supervision aims to capture complementary structure at different graph scales for transferable self-supervised representations.

entry.title: Sharp Root Anti-Concentration via Projective Incidence and Ordered Root Laws

author.name: Zijun Wang, Yuchen Miao, Yifan Hu, Huanmin Liu

entry.summary: Resolves open one-dimensional root anti-concentration questions relevant to online optimization of piecewise-Lipschitz functions, characterizing the worst-case interval-hitting constant via a projective incidence quantity. The result is dimension-free and removes a previous square-root-in-dimension loss.

entry.title: Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Wonseok Lee, Jimyeong Kim, Jungmin Ko, Wonjong Rhee

entry.summary: For reinforcement learning on diffusion language models, this work injects higher-reward rollouts from a stronger external policy alongside on-policy rollouts to escape the low-positive-reward regime. It handles the resulting length mismatch and mixed-reward instability with a length-aware integration scheme.

entry.title: From Digital to Physical Reservoir Computing: Co-Optimizing Soft Robotic Reservoirs via Dynamics Matching

author.name: Nicola Visentin, Maximilian St\"olzle, Mariano Ram\'irez Montero, Francesco Braghin, Daniela Rus, Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: Investigates whether soft robotic physical reservoirs can be pretrained to imitate high-performing digital reservoir dynamics, jointly optimizing physical design parameters, a diffeomorphic state map, and feedforward-feedback control through a differentiable physical model. This turns physical reservoir computing from an as-is exploitation of body dynamics into a co-design problem.

entry.title: Round-Trip Consistency: Bidirectional Diffusion Models Can Predict Their Own Rollout Errors

author.name: Alexander Scheinker

entry.summary: Trains a single latent diffusion model that can step a dynamical system forward or backward via a direction flag, so that rolling forward then backward provides a self-supervised measure of accumulated rollout error without ground truth. The round-trip discrepancy is validated as an error proxy on magnetohydrodynamics, astrophysical turbulence, and face video.

entry.title: Tevatron Meets Megatron: Expert-Parallel LLM Reranker Training on an Academic Budget

author.name: Zhichao Xu, Xueguang Ma, Shengyao Zhuang, Luyu Gao, Wenqian Ye, Yu Wang, Jamie Callan, Jimmy Lin

entry.summary: Integrates a Megatron-Core backend into the Tevatron retrieval toolkit so that academic groups can train billion-scale and mixture-of-experts rerankers with expert parallelism, while keeping the existing data pipeline and Hugging Face checkpoint compatibility. Benchmarks show parity with FSDP under comparable settings plus better support for large MoE training.

entry.title: LieStoNet: Learning Lie Symmetries from Spatiotemporal Data for Stochastic Dynamical Systems

author.name: Shida Liu, Abhishek Gupta, Sumit Sinha, L. Mahadevan

entry.summary: Introduces a template-free method for discovering Lie point symmetries of stochastic differential equations directly from observed trajectories, without prespecifying symmetry groups or canonical coordinates. It builds on established SDE Lie symmetry theory and extends symmetry discovery, previously studied for deterministic systems, to the stochastic setting.

entry.title: Thermalizing Stochastic Programs

author.name: Mirko Amico, Andra\v{z} Jelin\v{c}i\v{c}, Colin Oscar Nancarrow, Leo Tyrpak, David Roberts, Seth Morton, Dalton Sakthivadivel, Ashwin Gopal, Guillaume Verdon

entry.summary: Presents a toolchain for compiling general stochastic programs, expressed as directed factor graphs or parametrized stochastic circuits, onto thermodynamic sampling hardware by approximating each factor as a native energy-based model. It analyzes how per-factor compilation error accumulates and adds context matching and trajectory-level REINFORCE post-training to reduce residual error.

entry.title: The Condition-Number Barrier in Sparse Least Squares

author.name: Honghao Lin, Vahab Mirrokni, David P. Woodruff

entry.summary: Establishes a conditional hardness result showing that the linear dependence on the restricted condition number in sparse least squares cannot be improved by polynomial-time algorithms, assuming a small-set expansion style hypothesis. Confirms a prior conjecture about limits of sparse convex optimization.

entry.title: Deep Research Pretraining via Predictive Navigation

author.name: Jiang Zhou, Zhiyuan Fan, Xing Wu, Tinghao Yu, Feng Zhang, Lilin Wang

entry.summary: Introduces an offline pretraining recipe for deep research agents that converts citation graphs and hyperlinked passages into synthetic search-inspect-write trajectories, avoiding costly live retrieval rollouts. Teaches navigation and evidence synthesis behaviour before any environment-grounded RL.

entry.title: Prompt-Induced Waste in Large Reasoning Models: A Preregistered Two-Harness Benchmark of Coding Agents

author.name: Sarel Weinberger, Amir Hozez

entry.summary: A preregistered benchmark across six reasoning models, two agent harnesses, and 24 coding tasks measuring how prompt wording causally affects reasoning token spend, with over 4,600 runs including holdout and replication studies. Finds instructions to compare several approaches inflate reasoning tokens by two to seven times without improving correctness.

entry.title: From Chains to Trees: Parent-Conditioned Drafting for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding

author.name: Zixian Li, Tong Li, Chi Xie, Xiaohui Song, Haonan Lu

entry.summary: Extends semi-autoregressive speculative decoding from a single drafted chain to a tree of parent-consistent continuations, reusing the pretrained Markov head to score alternative children without retraining or extra backbone passes. This mitigates the failure where one early mismatch invalidates the whole drafted block.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Embodied Decision-Making via Multimodal Memory Compression

author.name: Bingxuan Li, Rui Yang, Cheng Qian, Jiateng Liu, Jeonghwan Kim, Zhenhailong Wang, Manling Li, Tong Zhang, Heng Ji

entry.summary: DunphyBench evaluates embodied agents that must gather evidence across multiple housing environments over long horizons, infer implicit multi-dimensional human preferences, and choose among candidates under partial observation. The accompanying method compresses multimodal memory to keep long trajectories tractable.

entry.title: DrawAI: Agentic Benchmark and Workflow for Making Raster Images Editable

author.name: Pu Cao, Qingye Kong, Xuedan Yin, Xuekun Zhao, Rupeng Yan, Qing Song, Yao Zhang, Lu Yang

entry.summary: DrawAI formalizes converting a flat raster image back into a structured, editable artifact, and provides both an agentic benchmark and a reconstruction workflow that balances visual fidelity against editability. It targets a practical gap where generative image outputs cannot be inspected or rearranged component by component.

entry.title: HiResNets: Native Full-HD Video Recognition with Foveal Residual Streams

author.name: Shivani Mall, Swarnim Jain, Joao F. Henriques

entry.summary: HiResNets process native full-HD video with residual networks whose blocks read and write to a high-resolution residual buffer through log-polar warps, giving log-squared rather than quadratic growth in compute with resolution. Layers learn to foveate on different regions and scales.

entry.title: CAPEval: A Decoupled Caption Evaluation across Understanding and Generation

author.name: Zhipeng Liu, Haochen Wang, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: CAPEval is a caption evaluation benchmark that splits caption quality into coverage of ground-truth visual content and precision of the claims made, using human-written references and human-verified atomic checklists. It argues that collapsing caption quality into one score hides the distinct needs of multimodal understanding versus text-to-image generation.

entry.title: Embodied Passive Aeroacoustic Perception Enables Relative Sensing and Pursuit Between Aerial Robots

author.name: Yanbaihui Liu, Ravi Prakash, Li-Yu Lo, Nils Roede, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: SonicFly proposes passive aeroacoustic perception, in which a drone estimates and follows another drone using only the leader intrinsic flight sound, despite the strong self-noise from its own rotors. The paper frames the flying robot as embedded in its own evolving acoustic field and demonstrates relative sensing and pursuit outdoors.

entry.title: DreamTrajectory: Trajectory-Guided Action Generation with World Model Alignment for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Zheng Yang, Wenjie Zhang, Xiangyu Chen, Wenxuan Song, Xianpeng Wang, Yihang Kang, Wen Chen, Lujia Wang, Renjing Xu, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: DreamTrajectory adds an explicit task-space motion plan and a world-model-based check on whether predicted action chunks actually realize the intended motion for mobile manipulation. It addresses the coordination of base and arm motion in large action spaces where open-loop chunk execution accumulates error.

entry.title: Multi-View Unified Camera Fields: Geometry-Shaped Action-Facing Representations for RGB-Only Multi-Camera VLA Policies

author.name: Jiarui Yang, Yehao Lu, Yuning Su, Yufeng Xie, Yu Zhong, Haiyu Lan, Tianjing Hao, Kaixiang Lu, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Enyu Li, Junwei Liang

entry.summary: MVUCF is a training-only auxiliary objective that shapes multi-camera VLA representations into a shared latent field with recoverable metric depth and cross-view token correspondence. It avoids adding inference cost while improving spatial grounding for RGB-only multi-camera policies.

entry.title: PolymerGPT: Multi-property Optimization with a Decoder-Based GPT Model for Generative Polymer Design

author.name: Charlie Pyle, Adarsh Gadari, C. Adrian Figg, Zhenquan Jia, Yaohang Li, Chunjiang Zhu

entry.summary: PolymerGPT is a decoder-only generative model for inverse polymer design that conditions generation on up to 37 physical properties simultaneously through learned conditioning tokens, rather than optimizing a single property. It aims at practical materials discovery where realistic macroscopic behavior requires multi-property control.

entry.title: GABench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on Graph Analysis Tasks

author.name: Jiarui Tan, Zhongjian Zhang, YaBo Guo, Jiawei Liu, Yujie Xing, Muhan Zhang, Cheng Yang, Chuan Shi

entry.summary: GABench evaluates LLM agents on end-to-end graph analysis, requiring them to access graph data and execute operations in an environment rather than answering text-serialized graph questions in a prompt. It broadens coverage across graph task types and graph varieties to test planning and tool use jointly.

entry.title: RL-Lock: Reinforcement Learning for Generating Interlocking Assemblies

author.name: Xuyang Ma, Chaewoon Kim, Haonan Zhang, Rulin Chen, Ziqi Wang, Peng Song

entry.summary: RL-Lock reframes generation of interlocking 3D assemblies, where parts hold together purely by geometry without glue or fasteners, as a sequential voxel-assignment decision problem solved with reinforcement learning. This replaces combinatorial shape-decomposition search for producing prescribed numbers of mutually locking pieces.

entry.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chunji Lv, Yangguang Wei, Junlin Liu, Yang Gao, Ming Liu, Xinming Wang, Jinyang Wu, Guoren Wang, Changsheng Li

entry.summary: PCSD improves self-distillation for agentic reinforcement learning by weighting token-level teacher supervision according to how persistently the teacher-favoring signal holds locally, rather than trusting isolated token discrepancies or applying one weight per step. This targets sparse-reward multi-turn trajectories where a privileged teacher is only sometimes reliable.

entry.title: RefactorAssist: Agentic Refinement for Reliable Code Refactoring

author.name: Jonathan Cordeiro, Shayan Noei, Ying Zou

entry.summary: Analyzes why LLM-generated Java refactorings break behavior and fail unit tests, then builds an agent that iteratively validates and repairs the refactorings across ten open-source projects with native test suites. Targets the functional-correctness gap that blocks practical adoption.

entry.title: Hierarchical Solomonoff Induction: An Unbounded Machine Learning Model

author.name: Nathan Young

entry.summary: Extends Solomonoff induction with a hyperprior over Solomonoff priors using de Finetti exchangeability, to model extrapolation from a training dataset the way LLMs do. Proves the hierarchical version is equivalent to standard Solomonoff induction and bounds its excess error relative to the true generator.

entry.title: Stop When Memory Suffices: Evidence-Conditioned Progressive Execution for LLM Agents

author.name: Yidan Lin, Kaixiang Wang, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: Router-Mem is an evidence-conditioned progressive execution framework for long-horizon agent memory that first tries cheap structured retrieval and escalates to deeper trajectory research only when evidence is insufficient. Aims to keep deep-research answer quality at low online latency.

entry.title: The Label Defines the Timescale: Trait-State Limits of Temporal-Aggregate Learning

author.name: Xizhe Zhang

entry.summary: Shows formally that when a label aggregates a long temporal horizon but inputs come from one short observation window, apparent performance ceilings may be acquisition-protocol limits rather than model-capacity limits. Decomposes label variance into a constant trait component and a component shrinking with horizon length, explaining why snapshots predict cross-sectional differences but track within-person change poorly.

entry.title: WorldDynCache: Risk-Controlled Latent Dynamics Approximation for Diffusion World Model

author.name: Leyang Chen, Junyi Wu, Shaoqiu Zhang, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: WorldDynCache accelerates diffusion world-model inference by approximating latent dynamics with a risk-controlled cache: a lightweight estimator tracks accumulated error from skipped denoising steps and calibrates when reuse is safe. The goal is large speedups in rollout generation without the drift accumulation of existing feature-reuse caches.

entry.title: SCOPE: Entanglement Frontier Escape for Source-Free Class Unlearning

author.name: Junhao Cai, Dohun Kim, Sung Il Choi, Juhyun Park, Chengjun Jin, Dowon Kim, Changhee Joo

entry.summary: Analyzes source-free class unlearning and proves a frontier result: any fixed feature-space projection that erases a class must pay a retain-accuracy cost lower-bounded by the retained energy along the forget-discriminant subspace, which binds all leading fixed-projection erasers. SCOPE escapes the bound by making the erasure input-conditional via spectral conditional projection.

entry.title: Empowering Credit Risk Detection in Weixin Pay with Billion-Scale Deep Graph Learning

author.name: Xin Liu, Xiyuan Chen, Chenglong Wu, Xuan Zong, Jun Zhou, Dawei Cheng

entry.summary: Describes a billion-scale distributed graph learning system for credit fraud detection deployed on Weixin Pay, arguing that common load-balancing partitioning destroys topological structure critical for risk signals and proposing a partitioning strategy that preserves it. Reports industrial-scale results on heterogeneous user-risk graphs.

entry.title: Z-PEFT: Zero-shot Backdoor Detection in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Canonical Spectral Signatures

author.name: Nicola Pitzalis, Donald Shenaj, Giacomo Cignoni, Andrea Cossu, Davide Bacciu, Antonio Carta

entry.summary: Z-PEFT detects backdoored parameter-efficient fine-tuned adapters directly from weights using canonical spectral signatures, and importantly evaluates in an open-world setting with previously unseen attack types and datasets rather than the usual matched train-test attack regime. This supports lightweight safety screening of models downloaded from public hubs.

entry.title: CRISP: Critical Step Perception for Training Efficient Deep Search Agents

author.name: Haosi Mo, Zihao Yan, Ruiqing Zhang, Zhongli Li, Hexuan Deng, Xuebo Liu, Min Zhang

entry.summary: CRISP trains deep search agents to be efficient by distinguishing critical evidence-gathering tool calls from redundant ones, rather than uniformly penalizing tool use as prior efficiency methods do. The goal is shorter trajectories without suppressing the steps that actually gather necessary evidence.

entry.title: The Role of Disfluencies in Speech Translation

author.name: Maike Z\"ufle, Maria Teleki, Fabian Retkowski, Vil\'em Zouhar, Oliver Grabner, Alexander Waibel, James Caverlee, Jan Niehues

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of human-translated, disfluency-annotated conversational speech into eight target languages and shows that current speech translation systems, including speech LLMs, drop meaning-bearing disfluencies. False starts and self-repairs, not filled pauses, account for most quality loss, and failures manifest as omission rather than mistranslation.

entry.title: LiveLight: Real-time Streaming Video Relighting with Interactive Control

author.name: Yue Ma, Jiangming Wang, Yucheng Wang, Xilai Wang, Zhiyuan Li, Xinyu Wang, Hongyu Liu, Ruofan Liang, Songchun Zhang, Yuxuan Xue, Qifeng Chen

entry.summary: LiveLight claims the first diffusion framework for real-time streaming video relighting with interactive 3D light control, injecting depth-aware irradiance maps through a lightweight adapter. It targets very few denoising steps and continuous streaming generation for interactivity.

entry.title: Stipple: Real-Time Incremental Gaussian Splatting with Visual-Inertial Tracking

author.name: Kilian Northoff, Mateo de Mayo, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Stipple couples an efficient visual-inertial tracking frontend with a new incremental Gaussian splatting backend to reconstruct photorealistic scenes in real time, avoiding the heavy preprocessing and per-scene optimization that keep 3DGS out of robotics and XR loops. Simultaneous tracking and mapping gives immediate feedback in unseen environments.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Price Competitively? A Dynamic Multi-Attribute Auction Benchmark for Agentic Commerce

author.name: Shimaa Ahmed, Yiwei Cai, Mohsen Minaei, Rahul Rachuri

entry.summary: Bazaar is a dynamic sealed-bid multi-attribute auction benchmark with closed-form customer utilities, used to test whether frontier LLM agents can price competitively when preferences are hidden and rivals adapt. Across eleven models, agents that win the most customers are not necessarily the most profitable.

entry.title: When Does LLM Orchestration Pay Off? A Controlled Evaluation of Accuracy, Cost, and Task Difficulty

author.name: Nicolas Leins, Nico Pelleriti, Jana Gonnermann-M\"uller, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: Runs a controlled comparison of Self-Refine, Best-of-N, and Debate against single-call and chain-of-thought baselines across five model backbones and three domains, equalizing prompt-optimization effort with GEPA under matched budgets. Finds orchestration gains are moderate, benchmark-dependent, and often not worth the extra inference cost.

entry.title: The Graph Language: How Knowledge Graphs Speak to Large Language Models

author.name: Giuseppe Pirr\`o

entry.summary: GRALAN trains a lightweight language mediator that turns knowledge-graph structure into relational tokens living in a frozen LLM's embedding space, then reframes knowledge-graph question answering as entity classification over question-focused subgraphs. Reported gains are largest on multi-hop reasoning where text serialization of graphs usually breaks down.

entry.title: G-ReAct: Graph-Guided Deep Search via Structure-State Co-Evolution

author.name: Shaoxiong Yang, Mengyuan Zhang, Shaojun Lin, Chao Li, Wei Liu, Kun Shao, Jian Luan

entry.summary: G-ReAct restructures deep search agents so reasoning is state evolution over a fixed-topology query graph instead of a linear chain, letting the graph explicitly carry intermediate findings and constraints across long multi-hop searches. The aim is to reduce context forgetting, search drift, and redundant exploration.

entry.title: Loud or Silent? A Reusable Framework for Per-Modality Failure Analysis in Multimodal Clinical AI

author.name: Quang Bui, Shlok Jaiswal, Samuel Paik-Heintz, Kevin Zhou, Kaushik Madapati, Krittaphas Chaisutyakorn, Noah Dane Hebdon, Dimitrios Proios, Sebasti\'an Andr\'es Cajas Ord\'o\~nez, Kacper Dobek, Boya Zhang, Aly Dhedhi, Ahram Han, Kushul Reddy Palakala, Rahul Gorijavolu, Jacques Kpodonu, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: Provides a model-agnostic framework for analyzing which modality caused a multimodal clinical model to fail when inputs are missing, and crucially whether the model fails loudly with reduced confidence or silently with confident errors. It outputs a per-example failure taxonomy and per-modality complementarity structure reusable across models.

entry.title: GISAgentBench: A Practitioner-Sourced Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on GIS Tasks

author.name: Abhinav Pothuri, Zhe Jiang, Zelin Xu, Di Yang

entry.summary: GISAgentBench is a practitioner-sourced benchmark of realistic multi-step geospatial analysis workflows with actual ground-truth outputs, unlike prior GIS agent benchmarks drawn from tutorials and scored by code or trajectory similarity. It enables end-to-end correctness evaluation of tool-using agents on urban planning, disaster response, and environmental tasks.

entry.title: CoNav-UAV: Cooperative Dual-Altitude Aerial Navigation via Stackelberg Learning

author.name: Junru Song, Wenhao Zhang, Yang Yang, Xuekai Qiu, Feifei Wang, Weien Zhou, Tingsong Jiang, Ying Wen, Yang Li, Wen Yao

entry.summary: CoNav-UAV coordinates two drones at complementary altitudes for target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation, using Stackelberg learning so a high-altitude explorer leads and a low-altitude approacher follows without relying on privileged information. It separates global exploration and grounding from collision-free close-range approach, which are hard to reconcile in one agent.

entry.title: ReasonCast: Towards Explainable Time Series Forecasting with Reasoning

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Jaehoon Lee, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: ReasonCast argues for time-series models that fuse forecasting and explanation into one response rather than routing numeric prediction and text understanding through separate task-specific paths. The authors introduce a setup for systematically studying joint prediction with self-explanation for interpretable forecasting.

entry.title: Beyond Solution-Centric Search: Adaptive Inquiry and Knowledge Revision for Autonomous ML Engineering

author.name: Shaokang Fu, Yulong Tao, Linbo Jin, Jiarong Zhao, Qiming Shi, Tianjun Pan, Haonan Li, Chengyu Wang, Jia Wu, Chengfu Huo

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous ML engineering agents should be organized around an evolving information state rather than a tree or graph search over candidate solutions, and instantiates this as Iris, an inquiry-revision loop using epistemic actions. Aims to spend limited compute budget on reducing uncertainty rather than blind solution search.

entry.title: From Simple QA to Deep Research: A Verifiable Benchmark Constructed through Iterative Task Evolution

author.name: Can Wang, Haoran Chen, Haowen Gao, Hao Ding, Zhaoyang Liu, Zhiying Tu

entry.summary: Builds a 500-task verifiable deep research benchmark automatically via an Explorer-Formalizer-Challenger loop that evolves simple questions into expert-level tasks, representing each as a DAG for traceable verification. Spans 31 topics and three query forms.

entry.title: Cooperative Coevolution for Resource-Constrained Agentic LLM Post-Training

author.name: Zhiyuan Wang, Shengcai Liu, Jiahao Wu, Ning Lu, Hui Ouyang, Shaofeng Zhang, Haoze Lv, Ke Tang

entry.summary: CoPES makes evolution-strategy post-training of tool-using LLM agents feasible on a few GPUs by decomposing the full parameter space into lower-dimensional subspaces searched cooperatively. Targets the memory advantage of backprop-free training without its prohibitive GPU-hour cost.

entry.title: Agentic Commerce World: An Auditable and Verifiable Environment for Vibe Commerce

author.name: Shicheng Fan, Mingdai Yang, Duohao Wang, Canyu Chen, Yongfeng Zhang, Hua Wei, Manling Li, Julian McAuley, Kun Zhang, Philip S. Yu, Kejing Yu, Zhiwei Liu

entry.summary: ACWorld is a simulated marketplace for evaluating buyer and merchant agents that pursue private objectives through natural-language delegated commerce, with a protocol that validates actions before updating shared transaction state. The design makes agent behavior auditable and evaluations reproducible across ongoing transactions.

entry.title: Role Steering of Language Models for Social Simulations

author.name: Isaac Song, Mohammed Rehan Parwani, Glenn Matlin, Emile Anand, Akhil Theerthala, Arjun Chatterjee, Maria Kostylew, Yonadav G. Shavit, Sebastien Krier, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: Presents an activation-steering screening workflow for role-conditioned agents in social simulations: extract a role-specific direction, sweep steering strengths, judge role-profile alignment, then pass or flag each configuration before deployment in a population. Applied to an open 7B instruct model over 275 roles with LLM-judged evaluation, outperforming an assistant-axis directional control.

entry.title: Exploring More to Solve More: Boosting Diversity in Text Diffusion Models via Entropy-Based Guidance

author.name: Jingwei Zhang, Haoyu Lei, Zijin Feng, Jiacheng Sun, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: SAKE is a training-free guidance method for text diffusion models that computes order-2 Renyi entropy over a kernel Gram matrix capturing cross-token semantic interactions and relative positions, then steers sampling to improve diversity without sacrificing fidelity. Increased diversity is shown to help solve more problems.

entry.title: LLM-OSDA: An Optimal-Stopping Dynamic Auction for Native Advertising in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations

author.name: Yan Fang, Jialin Chen, Chun Gan, Hang Yu, Mingjun Nie, Yeyu Zhang, Fengxiang He, Ching Law

entry.summary: LLM-OSDA designs an auction mechanism for advertising natively embedded in multi-turn LLM conversations, where the seller must choose not just who wins but when to insert the ad. It combines Bellman optimal stopping with envelope pricing and a bid-independent LLM layer estimating contextual click quality, aiming to retain truthfulness when timing and allocation are coupled.

entry.title: ORCA: ORgan-Centroid Aggregation for Training-Free 3D CT Visual Token Compression

author.name: Renjie Liang, Zijian Xu, Jinqian Pan, Chengkun Sun, Zhengkang Fan, Shawn Li, You Qin, Mei Liu, Jie Xu

entry.summary: ORCA is a training-free visual token compressor for 3D CT volumes that merges adjacent tokens using organ segmentation guidance and adds sinusoidal encodings of region centroids to preserve spatial layout. It addresses the fact that a single CT volume can produce tens of thousands of visual tokens and that naive grid pooling blends distinct anatomy, lesion and air into one token.

entry.title: Verifiable Checks for Business Rule Consistency

author.name: Joseph Tafese, Milad Hooshyar, Sam Bayless, Nick Feng, Arie Gurfinkel

entry.summary: SIRNA checks consistency between natural-language business-rule documentation and evolving code implementations by having an LLM translate documentation into candidate SMT formulas, validating those translations, and then formally comparing them to SMT encodings of the implemented rules. It is demonstrated on tax cost-calculation rules.

entry.title: CeQe: Grounding Lexical Retrieval in Semantic Evidence

author.name: Adam Kahirov, Umesh Deshpande, Swaminathan Sundararaman

entry.summary: CE-QE expands BM25 queries with terms taken from the per-token relevance attributions of a cross-encoder applied to semantic search results, so lexical retrieval can bridge the vocabulary gap it otherwise cannot cross. Unlike classical pseudo-relevance feedback it seeds expansion from dense retrieval rather than BM25's own possibly wrong top results.

entry.title: RadYOLO: Computationally Efficient 3D Object Detection and Segmentation in CT and MRI

author.name: Kai Geissler, Laurens M\"uller-Groh, Hans Meine

entry.summary: RadYOLO extends YOLO11 to three-dimensional medical images for joint detection and segmentation, and is compared with nnU-Net and nnDetection across five CT and MRI datasets with varying object sizes. It surpasses nnDetection on four of five datasets and beats nnU-Net on lesion detection while remaining fast enough for resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: From Chasing Ghosts to Missed Attacks: Perspectives and Perceptions of SOC Practitioners on LLM Integration, Risks, and Readiness

author.name: Jonas Thurner, Nadine Jost, Stefan Albert Horstmann, Fabian Ising, Lea Groeber, Alena Naiakshina, Sebastian Schinzel

entry.summary: Twenty-five semi-structured interviews with security operations center practitioners who have hands-on LLM experience, plus interactive scenarios, yield fifteen LLM use cases grouped into six functional categories along with practitioner concerns about risk and organizational readiness. It grounds claims about LLMs in security operations in what analysts actually experience.

entry.title: Coverage-Driven Adaptive Keyframe Selection for Video Understanding

author.name: Junyang Zhang, Puhan Luo, Chen Tang, Yuxi Shi, Xiang-Yang Li

entry.summary: CSES is a training-free keyframe selector for long-video understanding that adaptively decides how many frames to score and how many keyframes to keep by estimating the prominence of the frame-query relevance profile, instead of scoring hundreds or thousands of frames uniformly. It cuts large vision-language model inference cost when relevant-frame distributions vary sharply by query.

entry.title: Less Is More: Tuning Configurable Systems with Imperfect Fidelity

author.name: Yulong Ye, Miqing Li, Tao Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that configuration tuning for highly configurable systems improves substantially when part of the budget is spent measuring in a cheaper imperfect-fidelity environment rather than only in the expensive target environment, formalizing a fidelity framework for configurable systems. The empirical claim is that less measurement in the right place can yield more performance.

entry.title: Who Belongs in the Eval Set? A Capability-Taxonomy-Driven Pipeline for Curating Regression Eval Sets in Agent-Extensibility Platforms

author.name: Tezan Sahu, Aritra Das, Pankaj Mittal, Sudipta Das

entry.summary: Describes an industrial pipeline at Microsoft 365 Copilot for curating platform-side regression evaluation sets when every onboarding customer contributes its own domain evals but the platform has a hard query budget. Queries are projected into a capability taxonomy to select a compact representative set.

entry.title: CallScreenBench: Benchmarking On-Device Models as Phone Secretaries

author.name: Simiao Ren

entry.summary: CallScreenBench evaluates quantized on-device models acting as phone secretaries handling unknown, possibly adversarial inbound callers, where there is no task to complete and no cooperative user. Scores five quality dimensions each paired with a counter-metric to expose gaming.

entry.title: Talking to Digital Twins: Selective Disclosure and Belief Measurement in Financial Social Media

author.name: Boone Bowles, Raymond Duch, Sorin Sorescu

entry.summary: Constructs LLM digital twins of monitored financial influencers on X and interviews them repeatedly in real time to recover stock-level beliefs even when no public post is made, archiving answers before the return window to avoid look-ahead bias. Reports that twin-elicited beliefs predict cross-sectional large-cap returns.

entry.title: AdaHAT: Adaptive Hard Attention to the Task in Task-Incremental Learning

author.name: Pengxiang Wang, Hongbo Bo, Jun Hong, Weiru Liu, Kedian Mu

entry.summary: AdaHAT extends hard-attention-to-the-task continual learning with an adaptive mechanism that allows controlled updates to parameters previously frozen for earlier tasks, mitigating capacity exhaustion over long task sequences. Trades a small amount of stability for sustained plasticity.

entry.title: Auditing Semantic Gains in Sequential Recommendation: A Lightweight Recovery Test

author.name: Kong Wang, Zhongke He, Xiang Chen, Hongwei Zeng, Kai Deng, Long Wang, Kehua Yang

entry.summary: LIME-Rec is an auditable recovery test that fuses a sequential recommender, a co-occurrence expert, and frozen text-embedding item semantics to check whether reported gains from semantic and generative-retrieval recommenders actually require language-model reasoning. It attributes improvements to specific components via transparent score-level fusion.

entry.title: Weights or Skills? A Survey of Robot-Learning Techniques: from Action-Predicting Weights to Robots that Write their Own Skills

author.name: Gaytri Jena, Kapil Wanaskar, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Vasu Sharma, Amitava Das

entry.summary: This survey organizes robot learning along an axis of frozen-weight vision-language-action policies versus agents that write and refine their own executable skills as code, and grades code-as-policy methods by degree of self-improvement. It highlights that few systems combine execution feedback, persistent skill memory, and evolutionary search into one open-ended loop.

entry.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Tingyu Song, Mingxin Li, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Pengjun Xie, Zhijie Nie, Yilun Zhao, Shu Wu

entry.summary: UEmbed is a decoder-only multimodal embedding model that produces both learned sparse lexical and dense vectors in a single causal forward pass, using learnable special tokens mapped to disjoint vocabulary partitions. It extends learned sparse retrieval beyond bidirectional encoders and into multimodal inputs without extra cross-modal modules.

entry.title: Plasticity of Growing and Elastic Neural Networks in Online Continual Learning

author.name: Jeong Min Kong, Richard S. Sutton

entry.summary: Studies whether neural networks that grow, or grow and shrink, retain plasticity in online continual learning rather than only avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Builds on the finding that incrementally adding randomly initialized hidden units helps preserve a network's continuing ability to learn.

entry.title: GraphIR: Architecture-Level Search States for LLM-Guided Neural Architecture Evolution

author.name: Zhen Liu, Wanqi Zhou, Shuanghao Bai, Yuhan Liu, Jinjun Wang, Jingwen Fu

entry.summary: GraphIR gives LLM-driven neural architecture search an architecture-aware intermediate representation with three views: a tensor-flow skeleton, an explicit mutation surface of editable modules, and a validity envelope of interface constraints. The aim is to stop the LLM from having to infer editability and compatibility from raw code, making mutations more targeted and valid.

entry.title: Augmented Inverse Hybrid Weighting: Robust Inference under Deterministic and Random Distribution Shifts

author.name: Ying Jin, Ying Jin, Dominik Rothenh\"ausler

entry.summary: Introduces an estimator for generalizing evidence across populations when the shift includes both learnable covariate differences and residual random perturbations that no reweighting can capture. The method combines inverse weighting with an augmentation term and provides inference that remains valid under this hybrid shift model.

entry.title: SoniSpeech: A Large-Scale Open-Vocabulary Tri-Modal Dataset for Wearable Silent Speech Interfaces

author.name: Ruidong Zhang, Jiacheng Liu, Fran\c{c}ois Guimbreti\`ere, Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: Releases a 34-hour trimodal corpus for silent speech interfaces using acoustic-sensing eyewear, pairing ultrasound echo profiles with voiced audio and frontal video across 18,000 conversational utterances. A CTC ResNet baseline achieves 26.3 percent word error rate on open-vocabulary silent speech, reportedly the first such result for unobtrusive wearable hardware.

entry.title: RestoreKV: Recovering Full-Cache Behavior Under Aggressive Query-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction

author.name: Changwoo Baek, Seungjun Shin, Kyeongbo Kong

entry.summary: Complements query-agnostic KV cache eviction with a learned restoration step: after prefill, a small set of restore tokens attends to the full cache through a LoRA-adapted pass to produce a compact context-conditioned complement within the same total budget. The insight is that while lost information is context-specific, the mechanism for regenerating a compact substitute can be shared.

entry.title: Bole: Efficient Tree Speculation for Hybrid-Attention Language Models

author.name: Li Wang, Yi Su, Xiabao Wu, Chiran You, Yongchao Liu, Zhan Qiu, Juelu Zhang, Jiajun Zheng, Fangxin Liu, Jie Zhang, Chen Tian, Chengying Huan

entry.summary: Builds a kernel and runtime co-design that makes tree speculative decoding practical for hybrid attention LLMs that mix full attention with recurrent linear attention. It rewrites the linear-attention recurrence into a tree-structured form so verification avoids materializing a full recurrent state per proposal node.

entry.title: A Few Neurons Reveal When LLMs Misuse Tools: Sparse Detection and Selective Steering for Reliable Tool Use

author.name: Yutong Ke, Ming Yin, Chongwen Zhao, Kaizhu Huang

entry.summary: Finds that small failure-specific sets of MLP neurons linearly separate three agentic tool-use failure modes: invalid arguments, unnecessary calls, and omitted calls. Builds a closed-loop framework that shares this neuron basis between sparse detection and activation steering across six models from three families.

entry.title: Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance

author.name: Zhuowen Han, Jinwei Xiao, Zhengxi Lu, Renren Jin, Zhiyuan Yao, Yuxin Liu, Hongyan Hao, Yueqing Sun, Yu Yang, Qi GU, Xunliang Cai, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: Addresses the case where all sampled responses in a GRPO group receive identical rewards and gradients vanish, by selectively injecting on-policy teacher distillation only where it helps. Diagnoses three failure modes of naively combining verifiable-reward RL with distillation and proposes adaptive corrections.

entry.title: Opt.Gear Technical Report

author.name: Juneyoung Park, Youngwook Kwon

entry.summary: Technical report on a family of small on-device foundation models from 1 million to 1 billion parameters with a 64K context, using a hybrid convolutional key-value gated mixer plus local-global attention to curb KV cache growth. Claims up to nearly five times faster prefill and decode on NPUs and strong data efficiency from a curated half-trillion-token subset.

entry.title: Beyond Token-Level Cross-Entropy: Fr\'echet Distributional Post-Training for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Jinhua Zhang, Yisong Lin, Wei Long, Shuhang Gu

entry.summary: This work replaces token-level cross-entropy fine-tuning of autoregressive image generators with a post-training objective based on Frechet distance in representation space, using detached rollout contexts plus differentiable replay and a straight-through estimator. The goal is to close the gap between the training loss and the distributional metrics actually used to evaluate generated images.

entry.title: StreamSplat: Streaming Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Changhao Song, Yuxuan Wang, Qibiao Li, Youcheng Cai, Ligang Liu

entry.summary: StreamSplat performs feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting in a streaming, causal fashion, updating a persistent scene state as calibrated views arrive rather than processing a fixed view set jointly. A voxel-aligned causal cache bounds memory growth by explored geometry instead of stream length.

entry.title: Decoupling semantics from vision: A framework for faithful visual-text compression evaluation

author.name: Yonghan Gao, Zehong Chen, Lijian Xu, Jingzhi Chen, Jingwei Guan, Xingyu Zeng

entry.summary: Argues that current evaluations of visual-text compression, where long text is rendered as images to save tokens, are confounded by the language priors of multimodal models. Proposes an evaluation framework that decouples model capabilities plus a benchmark of semantically low-correlation samples to measure true text preservation.

entry.title: EOVSAM: Efficient Open-Vocabulary Segmentation with SAM 3 in One Pass

author.name: Haomin Peng, Yongkang Li, Zhaoxiang Liu, Xiaojie Jin, Shiguo Lian, Yunchao Wei, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: EOVSAM adapts a promptable segmentation foundation model for open-vocabulary segmentation in one forward pass, removing the need to iterate over every candidate noun phrase. It replaces multi-stage pipelines with an end-to-end attentional aggregation classifier over generated masks.

entry.title: Token Radius Attention for Efficient Video Generation

author.name: Jiayu Chen, Zhikun Jiang, Maoliang Li, Jiayi Luo, Jiawei Yang, Zihao Zheng, Hengyi Zhang, Guojie Luo, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Token Radius Attention is a training-free sparse attention method for video diffusion transformers that maps each query token attention entropy to a per-token compute budget, then converts that budget into a temporally decaying neighborhood radius rather than ranking keys explicitly. It exploits the observed log-linear relation between retained attention density and entropy to avoid uniform sparsity budgets.

entry.title: First Deployable Dynamic-CoM: A Unified Policy and Method-Agnostic Benchmark for Humanoid Single-Leg Balance

author.name: Yikai Zhou, Xingyun Wang, Jieming Cui, Bozhou Chen, Yikai Fan, Yixin Zhu, Wenxin Li

entry.summary: This paper reports that eight state-of-the-art unified humanoid policies fail to hold a clean single-leg stance on all 90 test motions in a new benchmark, surviving only by stepping or hopping. It introduces a deployable dynamic center-of-mass observation, showing that the capture point expressed relative to the support foot cancels the unmeasurable base linear velocity and is reconstructible from encoders and IMU alone.

entry.title: Toward Geometry-Scalable Whole-Body Touch for Humanoids: A 3D-Printed Conformal EIT Skin

author.name: Haofeng Chen, Carson Kohlbrenner, Jiri Kubik, Lukas Rustler, Alexander Dickhans, Karel Bartunek, Alessandro Roncone, Hyosang Lee, Matej Hoffmann

entry.summary: A 3D-printed conformal tactile skin uses electrical impedance tomography over a continuous conductive TPU layer instead of discrete taxel arrays, reconstructing contact from boundary voltages. The additive-manufacturing workflow adapts to arbitrary robot curvature, addressing wiring and scaling bottlenecks for whole-body humanoid touch.

entry.title: Fast-Mixing Markov Chains without Gradients

author.name: Robert Kutri, Robert Scheichl

entry.summary: DART is a Metropolis-Hastings sampling scheme where a regularized and tempered surrogate proposal implicitly captures Langevin-like gradient information without ever evaluating target or surrogate gradients. The authors prove the expected proposal displacement matches Langevin drift up to controlled error and derive mixing-rate bounds.

entry.title: Approximate Message Passing with Random Initialization for Phase Retrieval

author.name: Yuchen Chen, Yandi Shen, Xingyu Xu

entry.summary: The authors analyze approximate message passing with random Gaussian initialization for noiseless phase retrieval, where the tiny initial overlap requires a growing number of iterations and breaks fixed-time state evolution. They prove a Gaussian trajectory decomposition and establish that random initialization attains the weak-recovery threshold.

entry.title: AXRP Episode 50 - Eli Lifland on AI 2027

author.name: DanielFilan

entry.summary: An AXRP podcast transcript in which Eli Lifland discusses the AI 2027 forecasting scenario, covering time-horizon growth extrapolation, effective compute forecasts, the path from superhuman coders to superintelligence, misalignment dynamics, and the reception of the scenario. It is a long retrospective on the methodology behind a widely discussed forecast.

entry.title: 402Pilot: An x402 Decision Layer for Autonomous Agent Micropayments

author.name: Yin Li, Yanbo He, Boo-Ho Yang, Rav Lawana, Ziyue Li, Wei Zeng, Jing Tang, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: 402Pilot adds a buyer-side decision layer above per-request micropayment protocols so an autonomous agent can choose which paid service to purchase under a finite wallet, using a payment-aware discounted contextual Thompson sampling policy. It formalizes agent purchasing as contextual bandits with chosen-only paid feedback and nonstationary markets.

entry.title: CRAFTS: Collaborative Role-Adaptive Fine-Tuning of LLM Agents for Chemical Process Simulation

author.name: Ziyun Zhang, Yuxin Lin, Eldin Wee Chuan Lim, Xinghao Ding

entry.summary: CRAFTS decomposes chemical process simulation building into seven bounded LLM agent roles mirroring engineering workflow stages, with deterministic IDAES and Pyomo checks gating each stage transition. It consumes natural-language requests plus process flow diagrams to produce executable, degree-of-freedom-consistent flowsheet models.

entry.title: MemSIF: From Structured Interactions to Dual-Track Fact Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: YuFei Luo, Xiucheng Xu, Zhen Yang

entry.summary: MemSIF attributes long-term agent memory failures to two misalignments, temporal proximity not matching topical relatedness and write-time salience not predicting later query utility, and builds a dual-track memory that segments raw interactions topically while separately maintaining distilled facts. The design aims to decouple when information arrived from when it becomes useful.

entry.title: VLAGuard: A Framework for Evaluating and Mitigating Physical Attention Hijacking in Vision-Language-Action Robots within Wireless Sensor Networks

author.name: Dongfu Yin, Jinquan Zhang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that printable adversarial patches can hijack the action-conditioned cross-attention of vision-language-action robots, then proposes attention-protective fine-tuning that stabilizes spatiotemporal attention with no inference overhead. Evaluated in simulated and physical edge-robot settings.

entry.title: DynActiveGS: Active Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Hongbo Duan, Pengting Luo, Chengzhi Zhao, Yuanhao Chiang, Fangming Liu, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: DynActiveGS performs active 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction in dynamic scenes by separating structural uncertainty from motion-induced uncertainty, then using those fields for viewpoint selection and path planning. Suppresses motion-corrupted observations during incremental mapping.

entry.title: ACE-GraphRAG: Agentic Context Engineering for Hierarchical GraphRAG

author.name: Yongfeng Huang, Yuren Lai, Ruiying Chen, Haoyu Huang, Mingming Zhao, James Cheng

entry.summary: ACE-GraphRAG adds an inference-time context policy layer to hierarchical GraphRAG, identifying a representation-inference gap where fixed context construction fails to convert multi-resolution graph knowledge into query-appropriate context. It uses parallel depth-oriented and breadth-oriented retrieval branches plus task-conditioned adaptation.

entry.title: Upper-Expectile Multi-Step Q-Learning for Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Abdelghani Ghanem, Mounir Ghogho

entry.summary: Expectile n-step Q-learning replaces the symmetric temporal-difference loss with an asymmetric expectile loss to counter the pessimistic bias that multi-step returns inherit from suboptimal logged actions. The authors prove a contraction property and show that at the extreme expectile the bias vanishes on covered state-action pairs under deterministic dynamics.

entry.title: Convex Neural Energy Elements: Monolithic Finite-Element Assembly of Geometry-Parameterized Neural Operators with Stability and Error Guarantees

author.name: Hongyue Jiang, Jianjiang Zhan, Chenzhuo Zhang, Fan Wang
