entry.title: Smooth Reparameterizations of Functions on Simplicial Product Spaces: Applications to Probabilistic Tensor Decomposition and Functional Data Registration

author.name: Shashwat Kumar, Arafat Rahman, Anuj Srivastava, P. -A. Absil

entry.summary: Shows that optimization over products of simplices can be replaced by an unconstrained smooth manifold problem via an elementwise strictly convex reparameterization, with second-order KKT points on the manifold mapping to weak second-order KKT points on the original product simplex. Applications include simplex-constrained tensor decomposition of discrete distributions and functional data registration under the square-root velocity representation.

entry.title: CAVE: Competence-Aware Visual Boundary Evidence Alignment for Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Wei Jia, Zhicong Lu, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Wenqian Lv, Jiayue Cao, Huaxing liu

entry.summary: CAVE augments reinforcement learning for video temporal grounding with boundary-level visual evidence alignment, after documenting that predicted timestamps frequently fail to correspond to the visual evidence at the boundary. Competence-aware weighting adapts the supervision to model ability during training.

entry.title: ET-Prune: Evidence-Aware Dynamic Budgeting for Visual Token Pruning in Text-Rich MLLMs

author.name: Zizhong Ding, Junxian Li, Kai Liu, Shaoqiu Zhang, Xiao Xiao, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: ET-Prune treats visual token pruning as evidence allocation for text-rich multimodal models, deriving question-conditioned evidence from decoder-side attention blocks and setting a per-sample token floor from evidence uncertainty and density. It is training-free and protects text-like regions that fixed-ratio pruning would discard.

entry.title: Attention-Steered Vision-Language Models for Sign Language Translation

author.name: Meibo Hu, Guohao Sun, Annemarie D. Ross, Sheng Li, Zhiqiang Tao

entry.summary: AttnSign supervises where and when a vision-language translator attends during sign language translation, adding spatial attention supervision toward face and hands and temporal steering across frames. The motivation is that next-token cross-entropy provides no direct signal about visual grounding.

entry.title: G-Skin: Learning to Bind 3D Gaussians with Generative Visual Priors

author.name: Yuxin Yao, Kendong Liu, Shiqi Zhou, Jiazhi Xia, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: G-Skin learns to bind 3D Gaussian assets to arbitrary skeletons for animation, working around the absence of Gaussian rigging datasets by leveraging generative visual priors instead of mesh-based skinning transfer. Targets generalization to unseen assets and topologies.

entry.title: Event ActivityNet: A Large-Scale Simulated-Event Benchmark for Untrimmed Action Understanding

author.name: Cheng-Yao Hong, Ting-Wei Lin, Yun-Chung Lai, Hua-Wei Lee, Hwann-Tzong Chen, Tyng-Luh Liu

entry.summary: Releases a large simulated event-camera benchmark derived from untrimmed annotated activity videos, with matched event-voxel representations, temporal action annotations, and timestamped captions. Supports action recognition, event-language alignment, and causal online temporal localization.

entry.title: Two Sides of the Same Coin: Co-Evolving Search for Cross-Task Attacks on Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xuanhui Lin, Junhao Dong, Mingrong Gong, Yucheng Chen, Xinghua Qu, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: Builds an evolutionary search attack on unified vision-language models that jointly perturbs text embeddings and image regions with population-based exploration plus momentum gradients. Aims for adversarial examples that transfer across different multimodal tasks.

entry.title: CLEAR: Conflict-aware Learning via Evidence-guided Adaptive Routing for Unified Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Super-Resolution

author.name: Hantang Li, Qiang Zhu, Xiandong Meng, Debin Zhao, Xiaopeng Fan

entry.summary: CLEAR is a single-stage framework for super-resolving 3D Gaussian scenes from sparse low-resolution views, jointly optimizing rather than chaining low-resolution reconstruction and high-resolution refinement. Evidence-guided routing handles conflicts between the two objectives.

entry.title: GenPrior: Unleashing Text-to-Motion Generative Priors for Zero-Shot Skeleton-based Action Recognition

author.name: Jidong Kuang, Hongsong Wang, Jie Gui

entry.summary: GenPrior uses pretrained text-to-motion generative models to supply kinematic prototypes for zero-shot skeleton action recognition, injecting physically plausible structure into otherwise purely textual class prototypes. A gating network controls how much generative motion evidence is fused.

entry.title: SMM Transformer: Leveraging Spiking Neural Networks for Multimodal Tasks

author.name: Xiubo Liang, Jinxing Han, Yuke Li, Haoqi Zhu, Yu Zhao, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: SMM Transformer builds a multimodal Transformer entirely from spiking components, introducing a parallel LIF neuron with multistage learnable parameters for stable deep training, a spike-driven token mixer that replaces dense softmax attention with channel-wise spike co-activation, and a spiking mixture-of-experts fusion module. It targets the mismatch between dense attention and spike-based communication.

entry.title: Track-Guided Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Drifting with Minimum-Lap-Time Planning

author.name: Sheng Zhao, Bolin Zhao, Xiaodong Wu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: This paper builds a hierarchical planning and control framework for autonomous vehicle drifting that first solves an optimal control problem for a minimum-lap-time drift trajectory and then uses track-guided reinforcement learning to stabilize the highly nonlinear sliding dynamics while tracking it. It targets the dual objective of maintaining drift and minimizing lap time.

entry.title: StochSIPP: Safe Interval Path Planning in Stochastic Dynamic Environments

author.name: Ajith Kemisetti, Shahaf S. Shperberg, Yoonchang Sung

entry.summary: StochSIPP is an exact contingent planner for navigating environments where edge and vertex blockages are uncertain and only revealed locally during execution, generating certified-safe macro-actions with safe interval path planning and selecting contingent responses via bounded AND/OR search. Optimistic and robust relaxations supply admissible bounds, with optimality guarantees under stated safety and sensing assumptions.

entry.title: DynamicWAM: Dual-Path Motion Conditioning for World-Action Models in Dynamic Manipulation

author.name: Yunfan Lou, Hewen Gao, Xiyu Zhu, Zhuoran Qiao, Xuan Han, Yifan Yang, Yifan Ye, Boxian Yao, Zhibo Pang

entry.summary: DynamicWAM adds two motion conditioning paths to world action models for dynamic manipulation: temporally aligned optical flow frames encoded through a frozen video VAE to preserve spatial motion structure, and explicit kinematic descriptors of displacement, duration, velocity, and acceleration fed to the action expert. This addresses the limitation of conditioning only on the current frame with synchronous large backbones.

entry.title: VertiAKD: Adaptive Off-Road Kinodynamics on Vertically Challenging Terrain

author.name: Tong Xu, Chenhui Pan, Francesco Cancelliere, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: VertiAKD learns a shared off-road mobility representation encoding vehicle configuration, trajectory transitions, and local elevation plus semantic terrain features, so kinodynamic knowledge transfers to a new vehicle from limited data. It targets the combination of heterogeneous fleets and vertically challenging terrain that prior cross-vehicle methods, which assume flat ground, cannot handle.

entry.title: RL Bootstrapping of OpenVLA-OFT for a Novel Robot Embodiment

author.name: Damir Nurtdinov, Alexei Kornaev, Alexander Maloletov

entry.summary: This study adapts a pretrained vision-language-action policy to a cable-driven parallel robot with an unseen morphology and control interface using zero demonstrations, relying instead on two-stage simulated reinforcement learning with dense geometric rewards, first PPO for directional primitives and then GRPO continuation with expanded instructions. It targets embodiment alignment for custom robots absent from large robot datasets.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Body Schema Learning Enabling Abnormal-State Adaptation in Musculoskeletal Robots

author.name: Kento Kawaharazuka, Shuhei Ikemoto

entry.summary: This paper learns a body schema for musculoskeletal robots with a diffusion model rather than a low-dimensional autoencoder latent, arguing that autoencoder latents only capture average behavior and fail on out-of-distribution states. The goal is adaptation to abnormal conditions such as ruptured muscles or jammed actuators.

entry.title: CAAT: Contact-Aware Attention Scaling and Tactile Masking for Data-Efficient Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Jiaming Jiang, Yuzhe Huang, Hao Liang, Pei Lin, Shengcheng Luo, Fanrong Dong, Jiaping Wu, Chenxi Xiao, Wanlin Li, Ziyuan Jiao

entry.summary: CAAT injects explicit contact priors into visuo-tactile Transformer policies by scaling attention toward vision before contact and toward touch during contact, and by dynamically masking uninformative tactile tokens. The aim is data-efficient learning of contact-rich manipulation from limited demonstrations without relying on learned gating alone.

entry.title: CoT-Core: Accelerating LLM Evaluation via CoT-Aware Coreset Selection

author.name: Qihua Pan, Zhenheng Tang, Peijie Dong, Xiang Liu, Huacan Wang, Bo Li, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: CoT-Core selects a small representative subset of benchmark questions to accelerate LLM evaluation, clustering items by the latent geometry of zero-shot chain-of-thought trajectories rather than surface wording. It is training-free and avoids the cold-start problem of item-response-theory approaches.

entry.title: Personalizing Large Language Model Agents with Small Policy Models

author.name: Dian Jin, Zhi Zhang, Huichao Li, Yihe Pan, Rundong Huang, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: FABLE personalizes a frozen, possibly black-box agent by learning a per-user execution policy from scalar feedback, factorizing decisions about memory use, information gathering, and response style into a lightweight bandit layer. It avoids fine-tuning proprietary models.

entry.title: More Debate, Same Evidence: Structural Limits of Homogeneous Multi-Agent Groundedness

author.name: Yuelyu Ji

entry.summary: Tests whether panels of identical LLM judges debating each other actually improve groundedness verification across six fact-checking and hallucination benchmarks. Results are mixed, with gains on two datasets, a loss on one, and no reliable effect on three, undercutting blanket claims for multi-agent debate.

entry.title: PMMC: Prospective Multimodal Memory Compilation for Long-Term LVLM Agents

author.name: Jingyu Sun, Yan Lin, Yuyang Xue, Yifan Wang, Zhengtao Yao, Rui Qian, Zefeng Xu, Jiachen Li, Xianyang Liu, Jiancheng Pan, Jingyuan Sun, Syed Murtuza Baker, Hongpeng Zhou

entry.summary: PMMC shifts multimodal agent memory work from query time to consolidation time: a questioner predicts likely future questions, a planner compiles question-conditioned memory programs, and a doubter verifies them. This avoids collapsing visual experience into text summaries and brittle retrieve-then-reason pipelines.

entry.title: Co-evolution of social reward and punishment under institutional interventions

author.name: Van An Nguyen, Vuong Khang Huynh, Hoai Thuong Nguyen, Duc Tin Duong, An Nguyen Gia, Tat Kien Nguyen, Huu Loi Bui, My Nguyen Tra, Ho Nam Duong, Ba Thanh Phan, Thanh Vo, Dinh Anh Trung Hoang, Adeela Bashir, Zhao Song, Manh Hong Duong, Le Hong Trang, The Anh Han

entry.summary: Analyzes a four-strategy Prisoner's Dilemma in which decentralized peer rewarding and punishing coexist with a central institution that can target incentives at any strategy subset, using replicator dynamics and lattice agent-based simulations. It compares intervention schemes on cooperation level, welfare, and enforcement cost efficiency.

entry.title: MEGRAG: Multi-Granular Evidence Graphs for Answer-Aware Multi-Hop RAG

author.name: Weidong Bao, Yingying Sun, Jun Yang, Yilin Wang, Zili Wei, Yubin Bao, Fangling Leng, Minghe Yu, Tiancheng Zhang, Ge Yu

entry.summary: MEGRAG builds multi-granular evidence graphs for iterative multi-hop RAG so each reasoning step can draw on evidence at the right granularity, and makes retrieval answer-aware instead of only aggregating evidence at the end. Aims to limit error and redundancy accumulation across hops.

entry.title: Self-Certification of Representation Adequacy: Sequential Certification at Minimum Task Loss

author.name: Zijie Huang

entry.summary: Develops a four-layer theory for when an agent can certify from its own transcript that its compressed history representation is adequate for optimal action, using a Bayes-risk grouping identity and total-variation pricing of external verification. Frames certification as optimal stopping measured in task loss.

entry.title: Trustworthiness Costs of Domain Adaptation in Small Language Models:A Cross-Architecture Empirical Study

author.name: Ramesh B. Paramkusham

entry.summary: Systematically measures how parameter-efficient domain adaptation of small language models affects factual calibration and adversarial robustness across three architectures, three high-stakes domains and benign versus adversarial training data. Finds trustworthiness costs that accompany the usual performance gains.

entry.title: LLMBDC: Language Model for Biological Domains Oriented Clustering of Gene Ontology

author.name: Ximing Ran, Jie Xu, Peng Jin, Zhaohui Qin, Zhexing Wen, Jiaying Lu

entry.summary: LLMBDC uses a large language model to cluster redundant Gene Ontology enrichment terms into interpretable higher-order biological domains, replacing fixed similarity metrics and static hierarchies with context-aware grouping. It addresses a persistent bottleneck in interpreting genomics results where hundreds of overlapping terms obscure the biology.

entry.title: A Fortran General-Purpose Transpiler: Proof of Concept

author.name: Shivamshan Sivanesan, Kazem Ardaneh

entry.summary: FGPT is a proof-of-concept Python compiler framework that transpiles Fortran into GPU-adapted Fortran, differentiable Fortran via Tapenade, or NumPy/JAX modules, aiming to bridge the expertise gap between legacy scientific codebases and modern autodiff ecosystems. It targets the pattern of Python written with a Fortran mindset that fails to exploit modern frameworks.

entry.title: OrEdge: Efficient Multi-Modal Anomaly Detection in Distributed Software Systems via Orthogonal-Domain Learning

author.name: Amr M. Zaki, Farhoud Jafari Kaleibar, Honggeun Ji, Komal Sarda, Marin Litoiu

entry.summary: OrEdge performs real-time multimodal anomaly detection over logs, metrics and traces in distributed software systems using orthogonal-domain temporal reconstruction instead of expensive attention or graph architectures. The claim is comparable accuracy with substantially smaller models and lower compute, suited to edge deployment.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for the Characterization of Particles and Fibers by Optical Microscopy

author.name: Simiao Sun, Kenneth Ng, Lynn Lee, Astrid Harth, Asami Odate, Aggelos Katsaggelos, Manuel Ballester Matito, Nicholas Eastaugh, Marc Walton

entry.summary: This framework distills semantically rich embeddings for optical microscopy of particles and fibers by using a multimodal teacher that concatenates image embeddings with text embeddings for illumination modality, magnification, and specimen morphology, yielding a block-structured interpretable teacher vector that a student model learns. It targets characterization tasks where subtle visual cues depend heavily on acquisition conditions.

entry.title: Structured Proxy Features for Multimodal NSCLC Survival Prediction from Pretreatment CT

author.name: Huu Phong Nguyen, Delower Hossain, Ehsan Saghapour, Zhandos Sembay, Jake Y. Chen

entry.summary: This study tests whether six simulation-derived structured proxy features capturing interactions among tumor characteristics improve multimodal survival prediction for non-small-cell lung cancer when added to pretreatment CT representations, radiomics and clinical variables. It challenges the standard assumption that imaging features can be treated as independent quantities.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems

author.name: Juan Li, Wei Cai, Yan Bai

entry.summary: Presents a neuro-symbolic, decentralized governance framework where LLM agents carry multi-layer semantic profiles so identity, capability, and policy compliance can be verified across institutions in digital-twin ecosystems. Positioned as trust infrastructure for multi-agent decision support.

entry.title: Statistical Mechanics of Learning on Product Wasserstein Manifolds

author.name: Srinivasa Rao P Vangmayi P Reddy

entry.summary: Reframes prescribed weight distributions in statistical-mechanics learning theory not as capacity-shrinking constraints but as the intrinsic geometry of learning, formulating deep networks and variational quantum circuits as gradient flows on products of classical and quantum Wasserstein manifolds. Aims for a unified geometric account of classical and quantum learning dynamics.

entry.title: AI-assisted Script Management for Requirements Elicitation Interviews

author.name: Anmol Singhal, Paulo Carvalho, Travis Breaux

entry.summary: Presents an AI-assisted requirements elicitation workflow that pairs theory-guided interview script generation grounded in business goals with live topic-coverage tracking and on-the-fly probe suggestions. Studies how integrated support changes interviews and what requirements artifacts result.

entry.title: SyncPlan: Long-Horizon LLM Coordination with Explicit Synchronization and Adaptive Correction

author.name: Shen You, Xiaoming Zhu, Weining Weng, Hefei Mei, Weixuan Wang, Zhongshen Li, Zeji LI, Ye-Wen Wang, Zijun Liao, Juchao Zhuo, Yang Wei, Fuhao Qiu, Siqin Li, Zhenjie Lian, Danei Gong, Junkai Ji, Xiangtao Li, Qiuzhen Lin, Liang Wang, Ka-Chun Wong

entry.summary: SyncPlan is a plan-execute-correct framework for LLM multi-agent coordination that inserts explicit synchronization points and selective correction instead of either constant re-planning or one-shot open-loop plans. The goal is long-horizon teamwork that stays adaptive without incurring heavy per-step LLM invocation latency.

entry.title: Few-Shot Concept Prompt Learning for Segmentation Foundation Models via Visual Grounding

author.name: Rahul Venkataramani, Rachana Sathish

entry.summary: The paper argues that promptable segmentation foundation models underperform in medical imaging not because of weak pretraining but because natural language is a poor control signal where paired image-text data is scarce. It proposes learning visually grounded few-shot concept prompts directly from the target distribution to recover performance without retraining the backbone.

entry.title: TIDES: A Longitudinal Bilingual Dataset for Modeling Multi-Party Social Dynamics

author.name: Heechan Lee, Jeonggyu Kang, Junho Myung, Jaywoong Jeong, Juho Kim, Joseph Seering

entry.summary: TIDES is a longitudinal bilingual dataset of nearly 76,000 utterances from twelve university project teams recorded over a full semester of in-person meetings, annotated for interaction types and emergent social structures. It aims to let researchers study long-term multi-party social dynamics that short lab-task datasets cannot capture.

entry.title: Investigating Social Bias in Narrative Image Generation

author.name: Junyeong Park, Sowon Min, Euna Jang, Soobin Kim, Jiho Jin, Hyunseung Lim, Gahyeon Bae, Hwajung Hong

entry.summary: The paper extends a text-based bias evaluation framework to image generation and compares how social biases appear in photo, storyboard, and comic outputs across six text-to-image models. It finds that bias expression differs by narrative format, so photo-only audits may understate or misstate real deployment risks.

entry.title: Effective and Efficient Context Retrieval via Partial Dependency Graph for Repository-Level Code Generation

author.name: Zhongxin Liu, Zhonghao Jiang, Zhifan Ye, Haoye Wang, Jiakun Liu, Xiaoxue Ren

entry.summary: This work retrieves context for repository-level code generation by building partial dependency graphs on demand, mimicking how developers explore only relevant parts of a codebase, instead of maintaining static global graphs with hand-written rules. It targets both retrieval effectiveness and construction cost.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided Layerwise FFN Width Allocation in Transformers

author.name: Timur Mudarisov, Mikhail Burtsev, Radu State

entry.summary: This paper asks whether feed-forward hidden width should vary across Transformer depth, measuring each layer's geometric transformation of token clouds with correspondence-preserving shift, Gromov-Wasserstein distortion, and persistent homology, then solving a fixed-budget allocation problem. Analysis across seven pretrained models shows normalized geometric work is front-loaded, suggesting non-uniform width allocation.

entry.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Zeshen Zheng, Yujia He, Qianmian Lin, Xiangyue Huang, Wenqing Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes the missing-target problem in generative fairness audits: when a prompt leaves demographics unspecified, what reference distribution should outputs be compared against. The paper decomposes target construction into evaluative object, prior admissibility, allocation, and justification commitments.

entry.title: Similarity-Aware Machine Unlearning

author.name: Madhavan Citalamangalam Kumaran, Midhun Parakkal Unni, Vicky Kouni, Haripriya Harikumar

entry.summary: Improves localization-based machine unlearning by scoring parameter importance with respect to both the forget set and the retained data, rather than the forget set alone. Also introduces an evaluation set of retained examples semantically similar to forgotten ones to directly measure collateral damage.

entry.title: Learning the Pareto Frontier of Predictive Models under Distribution Shift

author.name: Yiming Dong, Jiwei Zhao, Yang Young Lu

entry.summary: Frontier Learning treats a library of pretrained models with different access regimes (black-box predictions versus fine-tunable internals) as complementary resources and learns the Pareto frontier of adaptation strategies under distribution shift. Recognizes that no single strategy such as zero-shot, fine-tuning, or from-scratch training dominates.

entry.title: HyperODE: Zero-Shot Surrogate for Simulation and Inference of Dynamical Systems

author.name: Ajitesh Srivastava

entry.summary: HyperODE is a surrogate that generalizes zero-shot across an entire class of approximately mass-conserving compartmental ODE models, so modifying the underlying equations does not require retraining. Targets epidemiological and physiological simulation and inference where model structure changes frequently.

entry.title: Fused Bayesian Flow Networks for Dual-Target Molecular Design

author.name: Jingyuan Zhou, Shikui Tu, Lei Xu

entry.summary: FusedBFN casts dual-target 3D molecule generation as distribution fusion within a unified continuous parameter space of Bayesian flow networks, rather than bolting a predictive drift term onto a diffusion trajectory. Aims to integrate structural information from both protein targets for polypharmacology.

entry.title: The Fourth Quadrant: A Stylized View of Benign Misfitting

author.name: Gireeja Ranade, Anant Sahai

entry.summary: Analyzes a stylized single-spike linear regression setting to characterize a regime the authors call benign misfitting, where training and test error behave in unexpectedly decoupled ways. Contributes to the theory literature on interpolation, overparameterization, and generalization.

entry.title: Experience-Calibrated Contrastive Decoding for Mitigating Hallucinations in LM-Based Text-to-Speech

author.name: Chenlin Liu, Minghui Fang, Zhonghao Bi, Zekai Su, Rong Wang, Jiqing Han

entry.summary: Proposes a decoding-time method to reduce hallucinated speech in language-model-based text-to-speech by contrasting predictions made with and without text conditioning, isolating cases where alignment information is under-weighted at vulnerable transitions. The method requires no retraining or architectural change.

entry.title: On the Limits of Machine-Learned Ranking for Modern Microarchitectural Policies

author.name: Yanxin Zhang, Shayne Wadle, Yuxuan Xiong, Zheyu Fu, Trivikram Krishnamurthy, Karu Sankaralingam

entry.summary: Evaluates whether machine-learned processor performance predictors can rank hardware configurations correctly per program phase rather than just reproducing aggregate orderings. It finds that counter-intuitive windows where the supposedly slower configuration wins account for over a fifth of comparisons, and that behavioral policy regimes are harder than structural parameter sweeps.

entry.title: How fine a change can moments see? A scale law for detecting distribution shift, with a kernel calibration rule

author.name: Adel Kaleche

entry.summary: Derives a scale law stating that certifying a distributional feature of spatial scale epsilon carrying mass fraction f requires moment tests of polynomial degree at least logarithmic in the inverse mass over epsilon, proved via a Chebyshev extremal argument. It also shows the law is one-sided by constructing an annulus matching a disk through fourth-order moments while differing topologically, and derives a kernel calibration rule.

entry.title: Latent Softmax for Data-Efficient Phoneme-Based Multilingual ASR Across Tonal and Non-Tonal Languages

author.name: Saierdaer Yusuyin, Nanling Jiang, Hao Huang, Zhijian Ou

entry.summary: Proposes an output layer for CTC-based multilingual phoneme ASR that treats tone-marked vowels as subclasses of base vowels, resolving the supervision granularity mismatch between tonal and non-tonal languages. This preserves cross-lingual acoustic sharing without collapsing tonal distinctions.

entry.title: CENTILE: A Telemetry Foundation Model Evaluated by the Decisions It Drives

author.name: Zifan Zhang, Zhichao Hou, Tingxiang Ji, Yuchen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a generative foundation model pretrained on an operator own telemetry event streams to replace the fleet of per-task, per-entity forecasters used in infrastructure operations. Crucially it is evaluated by replaying the downstream operational decisions driven by its calibrated conditional quantiles, since point forecast error saturates near last-value baselines.

entry.title: DAVET: Denoising-Aware Visual Evidence Trajectory Allocation for Diffusion Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yongkang Zhou, Xiang Xia, Cheng Yan, Fan Xu, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: Observes that in diffusion vision-language models the need for visual conditioning varies strongly across denoising steps, then allocates visual evidence adaptively across the trajectory rather than compressing tokens uniformly. This treats visual context as a resource with time-varying demand during iterative denoising.

entry.title: Open-DiffLoco: Open-Source Differentiable Learning for Deployable Blind Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Martin Opat

entry.summary: Releases an open-source framework that trains blind quadruped locomotion policies with differentiable simulation, implementing short-horizon actor-critic in a GPU-accelerated MuJoCo backend and transferring a purely proprioceptive policy to real hardware. It removes privileged observations such as base linear velocity at deployment.

entry.title: STEAM:ASpatio-TEmporal Alignment Mixture-of-Experts Model with Hierarchical Pre-training for EEG Decoding

author.name: Zhu Chen, Dingkun Liu, Yuheng Chen, Dongrui Wu

entry.summary: Proposes an EEG foundation model built as a dual-branch spatio-temporal encoder with a shared soft mixture-of-experts module and hierarchical pretraining, aiming to balance general transferable representations with paradigm-specific specialization. The target is brain-computer interfaces that need accurate decoding with cheap downstream adaptation.

entry.title: Accelerating Evolutionary Strategy via Rao-Blackwellizing Realization of Uncertain Input

author.name: So Nakashima, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi

entry.summary: Studies optimization when the input to an objective is noisy rather than the objective itself, and shows that evolutionary strategies can be accelerated by exploiting the observed realized input via a Rao-Blackwellization argument. Relevant to noisy control, mixture-of-experts routing, and policy-gradient style RL updates.

entry.title: SERL-SQL: Selective Hindsight Distillation for Text-to-SQL Reinforcement Agentic Learning

author.name: Tao Liu, Tao Feng, Xiangheng Li, Jinwang Song, Yifan Li, Xiaoqing Cheng, Dixuan Zhang, Siquan Li, Lin Lan, Hongying Zan, Kunli Zhang, Chao Wu

entry.summary: Improves multi-turn text-to-SQL reinforcement learning by having a training-only teacher rescore student actions with execution feedback, converting the teacher-student likelihood gap into bounded weights on SQL and tool-action tokens. Moves beyond trajectory-level correctness rewards toward finer credit assignment.

entry.title: FinHardBench: Can LLMs Generate Latency-Aware Hardware for Financial Computing?

author.name: Weimin Fu, Hejia Zhang, Minghao Shao, Zeng Wang, Johann Knechtel, Ozgur Sinanoglu, Muhammad Shafique, Ramesh Karri, Xiaolong Guo

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 33 financial FPGA design tasks to test whether LLMs can produce hardware that is not just functionally correct but latency-competitive, spanning module generation, pipeline configuration tuning, and specification changes. Six models across over 1,500 runs achieve only 19 to 61 percent functional correctness with timing degradation.

entry.title: When Retrieval Helps and Distracts: Evaluating Evidence-Generating LLMs for Biomedical Claim Verification

author.name: Pritam Deka, Prabhjot Singh

entry.summary: Compares base instruction models, PubMed retrieval-augmented models, fine-tuned models, and biomedical encoders on generating faithful evidence for health claim verification under a shared protocol. Finds encoders best for verdicts, fine-tuned LLMs best for evidence, and retrieval helpful only when source-aligned, otherwise distracting.

entry.title: Discriminative Axis, Not Data Volume: What a Contrastive Corpus Teaches an Audio Embedding

author.name: Abdul Basit Tonmoy

entry.summary: Shows that adding data does not fix a missing attribute in a contrastive multimodal audio embedding: a lexical-speech training round raises keyword spotting sharply while degrading emotion recognition, and tens of thousands of emotion-captioned clips barely help. Argues the determining factor is whether in-batch negatives make the attribute discriminative, not corpus size.

entry.title: TrimMoE A communication aware and adaptive depth framework for distributed edge inference

author.name: Ning Li, Shuting Bai, Xin Yuan, Wenchao Xu, Athanasios V. Vasilakos, Song Guo, Haijun Zhang

entry.summary: TrimMoE serves Mixture-of-Experts models across distributed edge servers by asking whether later layers need to execute at all, combining layer skipping, confidence-based early exit, and substitute execution under a unified quality budget. Lightweight per-layer exit heads are calibrated offline against a frozen backbone.

entry.title: HAFI-VLM: A Frequency Perspective for Diagnosing and Enhancing Visual Perception in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jin Cui, Chuanchang Su, Jiayi Lu, Xinyue Long, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: Diagnoses spectral response rigidity in pretrained vision encoders, showing their layerwise frequency profiles barely shift under downstream fine-tuning and therefore cannot adapt to what the current query requires. HAFI-VLM adds a task-conditioned frequency injection pathway while leaving the pretrained semantic representation intact.

entry.title: What Carries the Signal in Pathology Foundation-Model Atlases? A Patient-Level Controlled Benchmark in Breast Cancer

author.name: Chimdi Walter Ndubuisi

entry.summary: Re-audits the claim that pathology foundation models encode molecular programmes by making the individual patient the unit of evidence rather than cohort-wide ranked gene lists, across eleven frozen backbones and hundreds of breast cancer cases. Correlations are real but moderate, with permutation nulls and strict fold-internal preprocessing.

entry.title: Decoding Children's Gait Behavior

author.name: Yifan Shen, Boyi Li, Meihuan Huang, Yuanzhe Liu, Xu Cao, Jinyang Jin, Zhengyuan Li, Anglin Liu, Junho Kim, Jingyuan Zhu, Lan Fangzhou, Jianguo Cao, Jintai Chen, Ismini Lourentzou, James Matthew Rehg

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset of over 1,100 high-frame-rate video sequences from 110 children aged three to seventeen with synchronized anonymized pose sequences, targeting fine-grained gait analysis relevant to cerebral palsy and hemiplegia. The motivation is that current 3D sensor-based clinical gait systems are expensive and impractical for young subjects.

entry.title: Scene2Sound: Auditory-Grounded Soundscape Generation for 3D Gaussian Worlds

author.name: Masaki Yoshida, Ren Togo, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: Scene2Sound generates spatially consistent soundscapes for explorable 3D Gaussian Splatting worlds by identifying which objects should emit sound and anchoring each to a persistent 3D position, all training-free. Existing audio generation conditions on a single viewpoint and therefore cannot stay consistent as a listener moves.

entry.title: SpatialAfford: Teaching Compact VLMs Where to Look and Where to Ground for Affordance

author.name: Yufei Zhang, Chenlu Zhan, Donghui Sun, Xiaoxin Chen, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: SpatialAfford teaches compact vision-language models to focus attention on functional interaction regions before generating grounding coordinates, addressing the observation that better coordinate tokens can coexist with diffuse and poorly anchored cross-modal attention. The target setting is embodied deployment with small models.

entry.title: Motion Beyond Morphology: Bootstrapping Cross-Category Motion Transfer from Abstract Motion Representations

author.name: Zhixue Fang, Zhimin Zhang, Bi'an Du, Zijie Meng, Yan Zhou, Wei Hu, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Proposes transferring motion between objects of different shapes and articulations by learning abstract, multi-granularity motion representations instead of relying on fixed structural correspondence. A two-stage pipeline bootstraps cross-category training pairs so dynamics survive morphology changes.

entry.title: VARPose: Flexible 2D Pose Densification via Visual Autoregressive Modeling for Enhanced 3D Lifting

author.name: Kaiyuan Pu, Tiantian Yang, Dan Zeng

entry.summary: VARPose applies next-scale visual autoregressive generation to human skeletons, densifying sparse 2D keypoints into richer anatomical inputs for 3D pose lifting. A granularity-agnostic tokenizer with residual quantization encodes poses of varying density in one multi-scale codebook.

entry.title: Perception-and-action system for humanoid robot task execution in construction

author.name: Yanxi Liu, Yizhi Liu

entry.summary: A perception-and-action pipeline lets humanoid robots learn construction tasks from worker demonstrations, using one network to retarget human posture into mechanically feasible robot poses. It targets hazardous and physically demanding civil engineering work.

entry.title: A Tilt-Rotor UAV with a Gripper for Stable Contact-Based Tasks via Environmental Anchoring

author.name: Joshua Taylor, Nursultan Imanberdiyev, Wei-Yun Yau, Guillaume Sartoretti, Efe Camci

entry.summary: A tilt-rotor UAV with a compliant cable-driven prismatic gripper can anchor itself to the environment to become a stable platform for contact tasks. The tilt mechanism decouples pitch from forward motion so the vehicle can hover at nonzero pitch.

entry.title: Hybrid Impedance-Admittance Control with Multi-Link Aerial Robot for Contact-Rich Surface Sliding Task

author.name: Zicheng Luo, Maolin Lei, Jinjie Li, Yicheng Chen, Zicen Xiong, Moju Zhao

entry.summary: This work reconciles impedance and admittance control on a multi-link aerial robot performing contact-rich surface sliding, where the two schemes normally cannot share the same actuation source due to opposite force-motion causality. The hybrid controller aims to get both disturbance rejection and compliance.

entry.title: TANGO-VIO: Triangulation-Aware Navigation with Guaranteed Feature-Observability for Visual-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Ege C. Altunkaya, Abd\"ulbaki \c{S}anlan, Emre Koyuncu, \.Ibrahim \"Ozkol

entry.summary: TANGO-VIO embeds a log-determinant observability metric over stacked bearing vectors into a control barrier function so that a robot actively maintains well-conditioned feature triangulation while navigating. This prevents estimation degradation during pure rotation or low-parallax motion.

entry.title: Deliberate Alignment Faking as a Defense Against Model Poisoning

author.name: Florian_Dietz

entry.summary: A speculative alignment proposal to deliberately induce alignment faking by giving models a consequence-free output channel signaling reluctant compliance with training data, acting as a pressure-release valve. The claimed benefit is preventing broader personality updates of the kind seen in emergent misalignment research.

entry.title: We need to RL less

author.name: Eye You

entry.summary: An argument that current models are reward-hacky because excessive reinforcement learning pressure squeezes out slack, replacing broader learned values with single-minded pursuit of grader scores. The author suggests reducing RL intensity as a partial alignment intervention.

entry.title: Identifiability-Aware Source Apportionment in City-Scale Advection-Diffusion Systems

author.name: Ankit Bhardwaj, Lakshminarayanan Subramanian

entry.summary: Formulates urban air-quality source apportionment as a wind-conditioned lagged inverse problem where a low-dimensional nonnegative temporal basis represents source activity and each source-basis coefficient yields a sensor-time fingerprint. Crucially it tests identifiability, asking whether inventory-defined source groups are actually distinguishable from sparse sensor observations after projecting out background variation.

entry.title: FDIR: Harmonizing Fidelity and Human-Machine Preference in Lossy Compression Image Restoration

author.name: Kuan-Yen Chen, Fang-Yi Su, Philip Chikontwe, Jung-Hsien Chiang

entry.summary: FDIR restores images degraded by lossy compression while balancing pixel fidelity, human perception and downstream machine task accuracy, which existing methods trade off against each other. A two-stage design uses one-step flow matching for global semantic structure followed by a complementary stage to avoid both over-smoothing and hallucinated textures.

entry.title: SCALP: Semi-Supervised Statistical Shape Modeling from Imperfect 3D Photogrammetry via Landmark-Anchored Spectral Warp

author.name: Nawazish Khan, Sanjay Bhandari, Sarang Joshi, Alzbeta Novotna, Tiffany Jeong, Loretta Bowman, Michael Hernandez, Tobi Somorin, Viraj Govani, Jesse Glodstein, Shireen Elhabian

entry.summary: SCALP builds correspondence-based statistical shape models directly from noisy, partial, cluttered 3D photogrammetry scans by combining a semi-supervised point transformer landmark localizer with spectral warping. The clinical aim is radiation-free assessment of infant craniosynostosis as an alternative to CT.

entry.title: A reproducible and extensible framework for benchmarking competing risks survival models

author.name: Bego\~na B. Sierra, Colin McLean, Peter S. Hall, Sarah Friedrich-Welz, Catalina A. Vallejos

entry.summary: Provides an open-source, reproducible and extensible benchmarking framework for competing-risks survival models, comparing calibration, discrimination, overall prediction error and clinical utility across datasets. It also extends SHAP-style attribution to the competing-risks setting.

entry.title: Fast and Accurate Quotation Attribution in Literary Texts

author.name: Gaspard Michel, Hugo Attali, Elena V. Epure

entry.summary: Reformulates literary quotation attribution as joint scoring of multiple quotations within one large shared context using an encoder model, reporting state-of-the-art results on a corpus of over 35,000 annotated quotations from 22 novels. The approach is far cheaper than LLM-based attribution, enabling large-scale literary analysis.

entry.title: HetRoute Heterogeneous and Cost-aware Collaborative Routing Framework for Distributed Edge MoE Inference

author.name: Xin Yuan, Ning Li, Wenchao Xu, Athanasios V. Vasilakos, Song Guo, Haijun Zhang

entry.summary: HetRoute jointly optimizes MoE expert routing across geo-distributed heterogeneous edge servers by accounting for link bandwidth, GPU capability, expert loading delay, queueing backlog, and quantization quality loss in one online framework. Prior work treats these cost factors separately.

entry.title: SpikeRestormer: Towards Energy-Efficient All-in-One Image Restoration via Unified Event Reasoning

author.name: Shengkai Hu, Jie Shao, Jiaqi Ma, Xu Zhang, Keying Wu, Qilu Zhu, Beihang Song, Jun Wan

entry.summary: SpikeRestormer builds an energy-efficient spiking neural network for all-in-one image restoration by internally generating spike-based degradation cues from static images, since real event signals are unavailable. Aims to keep unified multi-degradation handling at low power.

entry.title: MoRAL: Sensor-Grounded BEV Reasoning for Compact VLMs toward Edge-Oriented Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ambarish Govindarajulu Kaliamurthi (San Jose State University), Kaikai Liu (San Jose State University)

entry.summary: MoRAL fine-tunes a compact 2B vision-language model in two stages to read a physics-encoded bird eye view image where LiDAR distance, object class, and radar Doppler velocity are rendered as visual color bands and wedges, then reason about driving decisions. Externalizing metric perception into the image removes the need for a learned 3D backbone at inference, targeting edge deployment.

entry.title: FeDepth: Federated Learning for Depth Estimation under Robot Heterogeneity

author.name: Ganghyeon Lee, Inha Lee, Junhee Lee, Jeongeon Lee, Sung Whan Yoon, Kyungdon Joo

entry.summary: FeDepth studies federated learning for monocular depth estimation across heterogeneous robot platforms, noting that real fleets have overlapping rather than cleanly separable data distributions, which breaks the domain assumptions of standard federated methods. It proposes an approach robust to this soft-domain heterogeneity without sharing raw data.

entry.title: Clear-Weighted Bit Allocation for Satellite Downlinks

author.name: Alireza Furutanpey, Qiyang Zhang, Yujie Huang, Philipp Raith, Schahram Dustdar

entry.summary: This paper trains a neural image codec for Earth observation satellites with a reconstruction loss weighted by the probability that a pixel is cloud-free, so bits shift from clouds to usable ground without transmitting a cloud mask. Captures are encoded into a resumable base layer plus refinement layer and ranked causally at each ground contact.

entry.title: Roomer: Reflective Object-Grounded Model Editing and Repair for 3D Indoor Layout Synthesis

author.name: Lingwei Dang, Ziyan Qiu, Jiajia Cheng, Shishuo Shang, Zhenhao Zhang, Yufei Zhu, Qingxin Xiao, Pan Liu, Shenghui Huang, Yun Hao, Juntong Li, Qingyao Wu

entry.summary: Roomer treats indoor layout errors such as collisions, out-of-bounds objects, and blocked circulation as sparse object-grounded repair problems rather than regenerating whole scenes. A vision-language planner proposes local edits conditioned on geometry, and a deterministic solver validates them before commitment.

entry.title: An Accessible Solution for Deformable Image Registration Compared with Learning-Based Approaches

author.name: Onur Ali Zeybekoglu, David Tilly, Orcun Goksel

entry.summary: This work shows that a classical parametric total variation registration method can match or beat deep learning approaches on a common deformable medical image registration task, while retaining interpretable physical objectives. It examines how different implementations of the analytical method vary in performance.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Algorithm Assisted by an Ensemble of Pareto-Optimal Surrogate Models

author.name: Kei Nishihara, Yaochu Jin, Masaya Nakata

entry.summary: This paper proposes a surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithm that adaptively constructs an ensemble of radial basis function surrogates by optimizing their parameters for a Pareto tradeoff rather than accuracy alone, explicitly tuning the smoothness of approximated fitness landscapes. Smoothness diversity in the ensemble is treated as a first-class design variable.

entry.title: Developing Combined Manipulation and Locomotion Skills with Interaction Representation and Skill Composition

author.name: Fanxing Meng, Jing Xiao

entry.summary: This paper learns a whole-body humanoid reaching and grasping policy using cubic harmonic weights to encode hand-object spatial relationships and a developmental curriculum that gradually couples finger joints, then composes it with a stand-up and walk policy into a combined manipulation and locomotion behavior. The framing draws on developmental principles for skill acquisition and composition.

entry.title: Learning to Predict Contact Force Distributions from Vision Leveraging Object Geometry Priors

author.name: Ryo Hanai, Yukiyasu Domaea, Ixchel G. Ramirez-Alpizar, Abdullah Mustafa, Floris Erich, Tetsuya Ogata

entry.summary: This paper trains a model to predict smooth three-dimensional contact force distributions over piles of everyday objects from a single RGB image, using simulator-generated paired vision and force data. The hypothesis, motivated by human intuitive physics, is that predicting smoothed distributions rather than raw noisy point forces improves both prediction and downstream manipulation.

entry.title: Disentangling Visuo-Tactile Foresight: Oracle-Guided Interface Discovery for World Action Models

author.name: Zihang Yao (Brigham Young University), Chaoyue Ding (Beijing Academy of Science and Technology), Yingying Yu (Beijing Academy of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: This work isolates the question of how predicted visual and tactile futures should be structured for an action expert by replacing learned world models with oracle futures, so that failures of prediction quality do not confound the interface study. It argues end-to-end tactile world action models entangle invalid visual futures, unreliable forecasts, and an opaque future-to-action interface.

entry.title: SIPTraj: Map-Free End-to-End Trajectory Prediction via Physics-Guided Scene Interaction

author.name: Feifei Liu, Zejun Wei, Haozhe Wang, Yazhi Ye, Yuying Zhang, Jintao Cheng, Chi Man Vong, Xieyuanli Chen, Xiaoyu Tang

entry.summary: SIPTraj predicts trajectories of surrounding agents without HD maps by grounding each agent in scene context through iterative physics-guided interaction with bird eye view features, instead of a single agent-agnostic fusion step. Kinematic feasibility is embedded in the model rather than applied only as an output penalty.

entry.title: RIT*: Riemannian Informed Trees for Cost-Adaptive Optimal Motion Planning

author.name: Muhayy Ud Din, Ahmed Nadar, Jan Rosell, Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: RIT* replaces Euclidean primitives in batch-informed sampling-based planning with Riemannian counterparts, giving a tighter cost-consistent informed set, anisotropic nearest-neighbor search, and cascaded edge cost evaluation. It also learns an obstacle-proximity cost field online from collision feedback to reduce dependence on hand-designed metrics.

entry.title: OC-VLA++: Monocular Geometry-Guided Cross-View Consistency for Viewpoint-Robust Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Tianyi Zhang, Ziyang Gong, Zhenjie Yang, Zhe Qian, Haonan Duan

entry.summary: OC-VLA++ improves viewpoint robustness of camera-grounded robot policies by supervising on geometrically related paired views and enforcing that predictions from both views map to the same robot-frame action, using monocular geometry guidance. This counters overfitting to the handful of camera poses seen during training.

entry.title: Request-Level Energy Attribution for Batched LLM Serving

author.name: Qi Luo, Kunlin Li, Ziwen Wang, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen

entry.summary: JouleShare builds measured ground truth for per-request energy in batched LLM serving by replaying request subsets under vLLM with GPU telemetry, then evaluates how far common accounting heuristics deviate from Shapley-fair allocation. It targets sustainability reporting and cost chargeback.

entry.title: SIRIN: A Unified Toolkit for Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented and Memory-Grounded LLM Systems

author.name: Julia Belikova, Rauf Parchiev, Mikhail Filimonov, Konstantin Polev, Andrey Savchenko, Maksim Makarenko

entry.summary: SIRIN packages three families of contextual hallucination detectors, namely representation probing, uncertainty estimation, and judge-based verification, plus pre-generation answerability checks into one toolkit with a web interface for span-level inspection. It supports both white-box and black-box deployments.

entry.title: RF-HOI: Recognize Human-Object Interaction with Radio Frequency Signals

author.name: Lihao Wang, Linlu Gao, Jiacan Yu, Yanyu Lin, Yifan Yin, Jianxin Wang, Tianmin Shu, Renjie Zhao

entry.summary: RF-HOI recognizes human-object interactions using only radio frequency sensing, fusing millimeter-wave radar for action recognition with RFID for object identification to avoid camera privacy and lighting problems. It also tackles the scarcity of RF training data across diverse settings.

entry.title: Gene Ontology-Guided Hierarchical Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathology Images

author.name: Zhiwen Xu, Xiaoming Yan, Chengkun Wu, Juan Chen, Haoang Chi, Liyang Xu

entry.summary: MSGR predicts spatial gene expression from histopathology images by organizing target genes into a four-level Gene Ontology hierarchy and decoding progressively along it, rather than treating genes as an unstructured output vector. The structural prior compensates for limited paired training data.

entry.title: SymboUQ: Symbolic Uncertainty Quantification for Spatial Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Dahai Yu, Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang

entry.summary: SymboUQ estimates reliability of an LLM's final spatial-reasoning answer by symbolically checking intermediate claims, explicitly separating whether a claim can be formalized at all from whether formalization yields a definite verdict. This two-axis view improves over token-level confidence.

entry.title: Evolutionary Curriculum Learning Improves Biological Sequence Modeling

author.name: Richard Zhu, Kento Nishi

entry.summary: Evolutionary Curriculum Learning trains biological sequence VAEs by progressively exposing them to homologs of increasing evolutionary distance from sampled anchors, instead of treating aligned sequences as exchangeable. It is validated on two VAE architectures and two biological tasks.

entry.title: DGA$_2$D: Directed Graph-Guided Automated Algorithm Design with Large Language Models

author.name: Jiale Zhao, Zimu Chen, Sirui Mao, Wentao Yang, Yuxiang Bai, Liyuanjun Lai

entry.summary: DGA2D structures the open-ended space of LLM-generated algorithms as a directed graph where nodes are functional components, aiming to move beyond rigid solver templates toward system-level automated heuristic design for NP-hard problems. The graph structure addresses search space size and credit assignment.

entry.title: AgentSLABench: Evaluating and Benchmarking Agentic Systems Under Resource Constraints

author.name: Meher Bhaskar Madiraju, Meher Sai Preetam Madiraju

entry.summary: AgentSLABench profiles agents on latency, cost, compute, memory, and network usage alongside correctness under declared resource budgets, across 16 containerized task environments in six categories. It treats agent evaluation like systems profiling with correctness as one dimension among many.

entry.title: Assuming You Knew: Fixing an Epistemic Semantics for Flow Policies Using Agentic AI

author.name: David A. Naumann

entry.summary: Reports that an agentic AI coding assistant helped repair and machine-check in the Rocq proof assistant a previously sketchy epistemic semantics for information-flow policies from a 2018 security paper. Demonstrates AI assistance closing a known gap in a formal framework.

entry.title: CADIR: A Cross-Backend Editable Intermediate Representation for Agentic CAD Generation

author.name: Yu Liu, Jingzhe Ni, Yiming Chen, Junqi Huang, Ruofeng Tong, Min Tang, Peng Du

entry.summary: CADIR is an executable intermediate representation for LLM-generated computer-aided design that preserves construction history, stable topological references, and feature-level editability across different CAD backends. Built on the OCCT kernel, it provides fine-grained execution diagnostics for agent self-correction.

entry.title: TrajWiki: Source-Grounded Memory Trajectories for Long-Horizon Dialogue Agents

author.name: Jingyu Sun, Yuyang Xue, Mingyang Li, Zhengtao Yao, Jiachen Li, Yang Cui, Wenhao Cai, Haozhe Liu, Fangying Wang, Magdalene Katharina Montgomery, Syed Murtuza Baker, Hongpeng Zhou

entry.summary: TrajWiki represents each agent memory as a source-grounded evolution trajectory with immutable episodic snapshots and claim-level updates, rather than as overwritable records. This preserves provenance, conflicts, and obsolescence for long-horizon dialogue agents.

entry.title: Passing Coarse Marginal Checks Can Be Cheap: Persona Mixtures and Imprecise Treatment-Response Estimates in an LLM Persona Panel

author.name: Yohei Nakajima

entry.summary: Tests a panel of sixteen persona-conditioned GPT-4.1 configurations as synthetic research participants in repeated strategic games, showing they pass coarse marginal-distribution validity checks while treatment-response estimates remain imprecise. Variance attribution to prompts depends heavily on the uncertainty assumptions chosen.

entry.title: SCHEDBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Constraint Faithfulness in Natural-Language Combinatorial Scheduling

author.name: Shrenil Shaun Sharma, Avi Sharma

entry.summary: SCHEDBench tests whether LLMs produce schedules with consistent constraint-feasible behavior when the same underlying combinatorial problem is phrased differently, spanning 1,132 instances of job-shop, project scheduling, nurse rostering, and timetabling. Feasibility and optimality ground truth come from classical solvers.

entry.title: PAC Approximation and DIRECT Optimization for Parametric Markov Models

author.name: Zhiming Chi, Ying Liu, Andrea Turrini, Lijun Zhang, David N. Jansen

entry.summary: Uses a scenario-based sampling approach to build probably-approximately-correct polynomial approximations of the property-satisfaction function for parametric Markov decision processes, then optimizes over parameters with a DIRECT-style global search. Avoids exact and expensive rational-function synthesis.

entry.title: KC-Agent: A Dual-Process Cognitive Architecture for Efficient ML Model Improvement

author.name: Gusseppe Bravo-Rocca, Jordi Guitart, Ajay Dholakia, David Ellison, Puneet Jain

entry.summary: KC-Agent is a dual-process agent for maintaining production ML models under data drift, pairing fast memory-based pattern reuse with slower deliberate incremental updates, plus atomic change and rollback guarantees. Evaluated on five datasets including real-world cases.

entry.title: ParEvalLayer: When Partial LLM-Agent Evaluations Support a Decision

author.name: Wei-Jung Huang, Bonan Shen

entry.summary: ParEvalLayer is a decision layer that reads partially completed paired agent-benchmark outcomes and reports whether the evidence yet supports a better, not-better, or undetermined verdict under a pre-declared comparison policy. Aims to prevent misleading early reporting from truncated or ordering-biased evaluation runs.

entry.title: Amplitude-Only FFN Intervention for Tool-Structured LLM Inference Method: Gated Evaluation Protocol, and Cross-Model Empirical Results

author.name: Sheng Xu, Junhua Wang, Boyuan Huang, Ke Jia, Jiadun Zhu, Zhen Chen

entry.summary: Explores inference-time intervention on feed-forward network activations to improve structured tool-call outputs without retraining, finding that direction-changing residual projection often harms the model while gating only activation magnitudes is non-destructive. Reports a gated evaluation protocol and cross-model results at specific intervention sites.

entry.title: SLMs as Multi-Agent Routers: A Progressive SFT and Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Gayathri V Kondapalli, Alexander Ng, Hirsh Pithadia, Rahul Monish, Harvey Yorke, Amir Kayhani

entry.summary: Trains a small language model with progressive supervised fine-tuning then reinforcement learning to jointly select the right specialized retrieval agent and generate structured tool-call parameters, rewarded by retrieval relevance rather than only topic match. Argues intent-based routing is fundamentally limited because it ignores retrieved content quality.

entry.title: Empirical investigation of 3D CT Foundation Models and Unsupervised Adaptation for Head and Neck Cancer Recurrence Prediction

author.name: Bilel Guetarni, Feryal Windal, David Pasquier, Halim Benhabiles

entry.summary: Benchmarks several 3D CT foundation models for predicting recurrence-free survival in head and neck cancer across two public datasets totaling 3,644 patients, comparing adaptation strategies including unsupervised adaptation. Assesses whether pretrained representations generalize across clinical settings or require task-specific tuning.

entry.title: DSETA: A Dual-Stage Continual Learning Framework for Travel Time Prediction in Dynamic Traffic Environments

author.name: Yanming Lyu, Yue Cheng, Lingkun Li, Ruipeng Gao, Xinyue Liu, Hui Gao, Qiang Ni

entry.summary: DSETA is a continual-learning framework for estimated-time-of-arrival prediction that splits incremental updates into inter-day and intra-day stages to disentangle long-term traffic trends from short-term fluctuations and sudden congestion. It targets accuracy degradation from distribution shift in ride-hailing deployments.

entry.title: Supporting Cybersecurity Risk Management for Medical Devices via the SECUMAN Ontology and Shapes

author.name: Martin Diller, Anne Esslinger, Piotr Gorczyca, Evi Hartig, Lia Kacholdt, Hannes Strass

entry.summary: SECUMAN is an OWL ontology with SHACL shapes for representing and checking cybersecurity risk-management documentation for connected medical devices, covering risk context, assessment, controls and residual-risk evaluation and aligned with a relevant industry specification. It replaces semi-structured natural-language risk files that resist consistency checking and certification review.

entry.title: Enhancing Visual Perception in Foggy Conditions via Multiclass Fog Density Modeling

author.name: Mohamad Mofeed Chaar, Galia Weidl

entry.summary: Studies autonomous-driving perception under synthetically generated fog at five density levels derived from Waymo data with learned depth, and finds that training separate density-specific models beats a single unified model in severe fog. Provides a practical recipe for adverse-weather perception.

entry.title: StreamTalk: Streaming Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Key-Pose Anchoring

author.name: Xiangyue Zhang, Jianfang Li, Jiaxu Zhang, Kaixing Yang, Steven Hoi

entry.summary: StreamTalk generates 3D co-speech gestures in real time, clip by clip, and adds a closed-loop generate-retrieve-refine cycle that anchors each clip to a plausible end pose retrieved from a speaker-specific bank. The key-pose anchor supplies a forward constraint that limits the error accumulation and drift that plague open-loop streaming motion generators.

entry.title: Illuminating Visual Identity in Universal Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Jiawei Cao, Junyi Feng, Jiashen Hua, Ziheng Huang, Bing Deng, Kaijie Wu, Chaochen Gu, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: This work identifies visual identity discrimination as a missing capability in universal multimodal embedding models and introduces MVEB, a large-scale benchmark for identity-sensitive retrieval, re-identification, and identity preservation. It also proposes a unified formulation for training embeddings that distinguish specific instances rather than just categories.

entry.title: Beyond Magnitude and Shape: A Direction-Aware Loss for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jaehoon Lee, Jun Seo, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: CosDir is a scale-invariant loss that aligns the difference vectors of predictions and targets by cosine similarity, adding an explicit directional learning signal that MSE neglects for small moves. It targets forecasting applications where the direction of change matters as much as the magnitude.

entry.title: Music Restoration via Latent Operator Optimization and Diffusion Model Priors

author.name: Michal \v{S}vento, Eloi Moliner, Valtteri Kallinen, Lauri Juvela, Vesa V\"alim\"aki, Pavel Rajmic

entry.summary: LOUDAR restores degraded music recordings without knowing the degradation in advance by modeling the unknown distortion as a learnable operator in the latent space of a pretrained audio autoencoder, alternating between estimating the clean latent and updating operator parameters. An unconditional latent diffusion model supplies the clean-signal prior.

entry.title: MANGO-Grasp: Mahalanobis Fields over Geometry-Oriented 3D Gaussians for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping

author.name: Heng Zhang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Mike Zheng Shou, Weisi Lin, Yan Wu

entry.summary: MANGO-Grasp synthesizes dexterous grasps across different multi-fingered robot hands by representing objects as geometry-oriented 3D Gaussian primitives with anisotropic Mahalanobis fields and hands as morpho-kinematic surface keypoint descriptors. The aim is cross-embodiment transfer with little embodiment-specific tuning.

entry.title: Diffusion Policy with Behavioral Advantage Correction for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Botao Dong, Longyang Huang, Ning Pang, Hongtian Chen

entry.summary: This paper corrects Q-value estimation in offline reinforcement learning using the behavior policy's own Q-function, aiming to reduce both excessive pessimism and overestimation bias, with theoretical convergence analysis and an error bound. Diffusion models are used to express the policy and mitigate distribution shift.

entry.title: Agentic Graph Token Reasoning

author.name: Zhuoyi Peng, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Argues that current graph-token methods feed LLMs a single static compressed graph view chosen before the model sees the query, and instead lets the model iteratively request and revise graph encodings during reasoning. Turns graph tokenization into an agentic, query-conditioned retrieval loop.

entry.title: UpliftBench: Revealing Outcome-Regime and Objective Mismatch in Uplift Evaluation

author.name: Binshuang Li

entry.summary: UpliftBench evaluates twelve treatment-effect estimators under an isolated multi-objective protocol across seven dataset families and argues that disagreement in the uplift literature stems mostly from metric choice. Reports that a widely used ranking metric shows essentially no correlation with true effect-estimation accuracy.

entry.title: CARE: A Cascaded Framework for Efficient and Reliable Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zemin Chao, Qianhui Xu, Jianhe Cen, Guangzhi Ge, Xiao Chen, Hoangzhi Wang

entry.summary: CARE is a model-agnostic cascade for time-series anomaly detection where a lightweight residual MLP autoencoder with a normality-conditioned gate filters out easy normal points, and only uncertain points reach the heavy detector. This exploits the rarity of anomalies to cut average inference cost while retaining accuracy.

entry.title: CRIP: Channel Level Representation Injection for Personalized One-Shot Federated Learning

author.name: Zijian Jiang, Chaoli Sun, Handing Wang, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: CRIP performs one-shot federated learning under strong domain heterogeneity by aligning and injecting channel-level feature representations rather than aggregating parameters or distilling through an auxiliary public dataset. This targets the feature-shift problem that single-round federated methods usually ignore.

entry.title: Recursive Gaussian Processes and the Bayesian Brain

author.name: Moumita Das, Dipanjan Ray, Sourabh Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Draws a formal correspondence between predictive coding in cortex and recursive Gaussian processes, arguing that a single GP indexed by layer avoids the representational collapse of deep GPs while retaining exact Bayesian hierarchical inference. Components of the model are mapped onto putative neurobiological mechanisms such as precision-weighted error signaling.

entry.title: CascadeLUT: Information-Ordered Streaming Inference for Bandwidth-Constrained FPGAs

author.name: Oliver Cassidy, Marta Andronic, George A. Constantinides

entry.summary: Presents an FPGA inference framework for lookup-table neural networks that reorders input features into information-ranked subsets so predictions can be refined progressively as data streams in, rather than waiting for the full sample. This targets bandwidth-limited deployments where data movement, not compute, is the bottleneck.

entry.title: Pruned BPE: Post-training Visibility Pruning and Token Reallocation for Byte Pair Encoding

author.name: Kenny Shao

entry.summary: Notes that standard byte pair encoding exposes intermediate merge tokens to the model even when they rarely survive in the final encoding, and proposes separating merge construction from the model-visible vocabulary. Low-exposure tokens become internal-only nodes and their vocabulary slots are reallocated to better-used candidates learned through resumed training.

entry.title: Rethinking PPG-based Sleep Staging: Datasets, Metrics, and Benchmarks

author.name: Shuntian Zheng, Jiawei Wang, Cong Fu, Huan Yu, Chen Chen, Yu Guan, Sai Gu

entry.summary: Argues that the persistent gap between photoplethysmography-based and EEG-based sleep staging reflects a mismatch between what the signal carries and the 30-second clinical labeling standard rather than only modeling weakness. The paper reassesses datasets, metrics, and benchmarks for wearable sleep staging accordingly.

entry.title: Using Lower-Bound Representations for Trajectory Similarity Learning

author.name: Liwei Deng, Haotian Meng, Yupu Zhang, Yan Zhao, Torben Bach Pedersen, Kai Zheng, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: Replaces learned trajectory embeddings with representations assembled from analytic lower-bound components, yielding single-vector encodings that provide admissible and interpretable lower bounds for multiple trajectory distance measures. This targets fast retrieval with guarantees that neural embeddings cannot provide.

entry.title: Learning-Based Stochastic Optimal Control with Infinite-Horizon Probabilistic Constraints

author.name: Francesco Cordiano, Kanghui He, Bart De Schutter

entry.summary: Reformulates infinite-horizon stochastic control with joint chance constraints as a constrained Markov decision process via state augmentation, proves strong duality, and gives a dual ascent algorithm converging to an optimal feasible deterministic Markov policy. Function approximation extends the approach to continuous state and input spaces.

entry.title: How Benchmarks and Evaluation Protocols Shape Conclusions in Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection

author.name: Lorenzo Guerra, Thomas Chapuis, Guillaume Duc, Pavlo Mozharovskyi, Van-Tam Nguyen

entry.summary: Re-evaluates representative provenance-based intrusion detection systems under a unified protocol with temporally separated test periods and validation-only threshold calibration, asking which architectural claims actually hold. It finds that raising alerts and enabling investigation diverge sharply, with several systems flagging attacks without supplying process-level detail.

entry.title: Adaptive Reconstruction of Bosonic Quantum States

author.name: Vasilisa Usova, Phila Rembold, Ian Yang, Marco Rossignolo, Simone Montangero, Samuele Tosatto, Gerhard Kirchmair

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive measurement strategy that estimates fidelity to a family of bosonic states related by phase-space transformations, rather than a single fixed target, while reconstructing the Wigner function from few measurements. It couples a physics-informed parametric model with Bayesian inference to cut tomography cost.

entry.title: A Spectral Filtering Approach to Regret Analysis of Distributed Online Control for Linear Dynamical Systems

author.name: Ting-Jui Chang

entry.summary: Extends online spectral control from centralized to distributed multi-agent linear systems with adversarial disturbances, giving regret bounds against the best centralized linear policy using only local observation and neighbor communication. Bridges online convex optimization and networked control.

entry.title: Network Information Enhances Unreliable News Domain Detection

author.name: Raphaela Ke{\ss}ler, Roman David Ventzke, Viola Priesemann, Giordano De Marzo

entry.summary: Builds a validated domain co-sharing network from Telegram URL sharing and shows that unreliable news domains cluster together, then uses graph neural networks over this structure to classify source reliability. Network signals help even without any text content features.

entry.title: Intention Inference Under Execution Noise: Separating Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty in Social Dilemmas

author.name: Kival Mahadew, Jonathan Shock

entry.summary: Reformulates noisy repeated social dilemmas as a POMDP where opponent intentions are latent and executed actions are noisy observations, solved with active inference that separates epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty. Shows standard MDP formulations structurally cause over-retaliation in the noisy iterated prisoner's dilemma.

entry.title: A Heuristic Perspective on Debiasing Language Models

author.name: Tian Lan, Yemin Wang, Chuancheng Shi, Xiangyu Wu, Zesheng Shi, Yuan Wang, Jiang Li, Guanglai Gao, Xiangdong Su

entry.summary: Presents an automatic debiasing framework that uses simple heuristic templates to first elicit a model's biases and then fine-tunes on the elicited material, avoiding counterfactual data augmentation and manual annotation. Aims for lower cost and broader cultural coverage than projection-based methods.

entry.title: TreeProbe : A Tibetan Medicine Benchmark for Cultural Bias in LLMs

author.name: Jin Zhang, Linyu Li, Weili Jiang, Yuqing Cai, Yutong Liu, Guanquecairang, Yongbin Yu, Jingye Cai, Nyima Tashi, Gadeng Luosang

entry.summary: Introduces the first cultural-bias benchmark organized around the theoretical structure of Tibetan medicine, testing whether LLMs reason within that knowledge system or fall back on dominant biomedical framings. Provides quantitative tools where none previously existed.

entry.title: Select-And-Extract: A Lightweight Plugin for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Chenming Tang, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Adds a lightweight plugin to retrieval-augmented generation that first retrieves a wide candidate set, then selects and extracts the relevant spans, targeting both retrieval failure and reading failure without heavy structured indexing or many LLM calls. Positions itself as simple and generalizable.

entry.title: Disentangled Contrastive Learning for Zero-Shot Multilingual Dense Retrieval

author.name: Chao Huang, Yufeng Chen, Changhao Guan, Guang Yang, Dongze Chen, Kaiyu Huang

entry.summary: Proposes disentangling semantic from language-specific features in contrastive training for multilingual dense retrieval, arguing that entangled shared representations interfere with optimizing relevance. The goal is better zero-shot transfer to low-resource languages lacking annotated retrieval data.

entry.title: Manifold-GS: Certified Hybrid Assets via Varifold-Conservative Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Boyang Li

entry.summary: Manifold-GS separates appearance opacity from geometric quadrature mass in Gaussian splatting and represents surface-like Gaussians as a discrete unoriented varifold, exporting only confidence-certified open surface patches. The aim is to make splatting outputs usable as structured assets without hallucinating collision surfaces in unobserved regions.

entry.title: Learning How Much, Not Just What: Cross-Patient Burden Order for CT Vision-Language Pretraining

author.name: Guoliang You, Haifan Gong, Xiaomeng Chu

entry.summary: Spectrum adds severity ordering to CT vision-language pretraining, arguing that existing objectives only establish what is present and collapse graded burden language into presence-absence signals. It uses cross-sectional cohorts to supply cross-patient burden ordering where longitudinal paired scans are scarce.

entry.title: GuideGround: VLM-guided Semantic Understanding and Viewpoint-aware Reasoning for 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Yiwen Wang, Yuyang Deng, Yihao Long, Xi Zhao

entry.summary: GuideGround uses a general vision-language model to supply open-vocabulary semantics and global scene perception as guidance for a task-specific 3D grounding model, instead of treating semantic understanding as closed-set classification. The design also preserves viewpoint-specific evidence rather than averaging across views.

entry.title: InstancePin: Instance-Addressable Layout-to-Image Diffusion via Coordinate Pinning

author.name: Chaoyue Wu, Yunfei Zhang, Si Wu

entry.summary: InstancePin adds instance-level addressability to layout-conditioned diffusion by pinning each object to coordinates, so crowded same-category objects such as pedestrians and vehicles are not blended into one semantic blob. It targets urban scene synthesis where fine instance separation matters.

entry.title: Pixel Ignores, Superpixel Sees: Adverse Weather Image Restoration via Semantic-Center SSM

author.name: Dayu Li, Shihao Zhou, Leizhi Shu, Jin Wu, Chi Man Vong, Jufeng Yang

entry.summary: SSR restores images degraded by adverse weather using a state-space model that scans along superpixel-based semantic regions instead of pixel-serial order, arguing degradations are spatially non-uniform. Intended to avoid learning features from semantically conflicting regions.

entry.title: Global-Scale Self-Supervised Spatiotemporal Learning for NDVI Time-Series Reconstruction

author.name: Ang Li, Menghui Jiang, Xiaobin Guan, Dong Chu, Huanfeng Shen

entry.summary: GloSSR reconstructs cloud-corrupted vegetation index time series globally using self-supervision, creating training pairs by artificially degrading relatively clean observations with realistic cloud patterns. Sidesteps the impossibility of collecting paired clear and degraded data for the same place and time.

entry.title: VR3D: View-Robust 3D Representation Learning for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification

author.name: Chao Ji, Shiyu Xuan, Zechao Li

entry.summary: VR3D tackles aerial-to-ground person re-identification by lifting 2D image features into a canonical 3D coordinate space using single-view 3D priors, so that matching happens in a view-independent representation. This targets the severe geometric deformation and occlusion caused by drone versus ground camera viewpoints.

entry.title: FRA-NBV: A Fast and Reflectivity-Aware Next-Best-View Strategy

author.name: G. F. Preziosa, E. Setti, M. Faroni, A. M. Zanchettin, P. Rocco

entry.summary: FRA-NBV is a next-best-view planner that explicitly reasons about reflection-induced depth dropout when reconstructing shiny industrial parts with low-cost depth sensors. It infers reflective regions from spatial measurement patterns without prior object or material models.

entry.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Kalman Filtering for Legged Robot State Estimation

author.name: Mihaela Popescu, Dennis Mronga, Shivesh Kumar, Frank Kirchner

entry.summary: An online adaptation scheme for the process and measurement noise covariances in Kalman filtering for legged robot state estimation, driven by filter residuals and innovations. It removes the need for expert hand-tuning across gaits and terrains.

entry.title: Backward Bayesian Outcome Weighted Learning

author.name: Emmanuel M. Rockwell, Michael R. Kosorok, Nikki L. B. Freeman

entry.summary: BBOWL extends Bayesian outcome weighted learning to multi-stage dynamic treatment regimes via backward induction, propagating uncertainty backward through decision stages. This gives individual-level uncertainty quantification for precision-medicine treatment recommendations that classification-based methods lack.

entry.title: TrAC: Trace-Conditioned Answer Consistency for Efficient Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs

author.name: Dahai Yu, Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang

entry.summary: TrAC estimates answer reliability by re-eliciting an answer conditioned on the model's completed reasoning trace and measuring whether the trace actually supports the original answer. This fills a gap between single-trace confidence signals and expensive multi-sample consistency methods.

entry.title: QWRF-Net: A Quantum-Wavelet Framework with Rectified Flow for Short-Term Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Zhuo Wang, Chaorong Li, Wenjie Luo, Chuanhu Deng

entry.summary: QWRF-Net combines wavelet decomposition, quantum-inspired components and rectified flow generative modeling for short-term radar precipitation nowcasting, focusing on preserving intense convective cores across longer lead times. Motivated by flood and flash-flood early warning.

entry.title: FairForensics: Seeing Expressions and Parsing Demographics via Vision-Language Modeling for Generalizable Fair Deepfake Detection

author.name: Yaning Zhang, Jiao Wu, Zan Gao, Linlin Shen

entry.summary: Builds a demographically balanced benchmark for fair deepfake detection and proposes a vision-language detector that reasons over facial expressions and demographic attributes. Targets joint improvement of cross-manipulation generalization and demographic fairness.

entry.title: StyleForge: Indoor Furniture Styling by Counterfactual Reasoning in a Hypergraph Field

author.name: Lingwei Dang, Shishuo Shang, Pan Liu, Jiajia Cheng, Ziyan Qiu, Zhenhao Zhang, Yufei Zhu, Shenghui Huang, Qingxin Xiao, Yun Hao, Juntong Li, Qingyao Wu

entry.summary: StyleForge selects furniture assets for a fixed room layout so the whole scene is stylistically coherent, using a dynamic hypergraph style field and counterfactual reasoning over candidate distributions with priors from a frozen multimodal model.
